The script\n  is fetched by moai itself, not by curl; install.sh then downloads the\n  release with curl or wget and checks it against the release checksums.\n\n  The repository is `buzzni/moai` unless your user config says otherwise -\n  `repo = \\\"owner/name\\\"` under [update] - and MOAI_REPO wins over both. The\n  repository's own .moai/config.toml is never read for it: what it names is\n  piped into a shell, and a repository you cloned must not choose that. A\n  value that is not owner/name is refused, not replaced with the default.\n\n  Nothing is fetched where it cannot work, and it stops with one line:\n  a binary cargo built (target/ or cargo install - rebuild from source\n  instead), a binary not named moai, a directory you cannot write (run it as a\n  user who can, or reinstall with install.sh --dir), and a machine the releases\n  do not cover. A directory outside your home is fine when you can write it.\n\n  --dry-run fetches nothing and runs nothing. --json prints {repo, script,\n  dir, command, dry_run} and, after a run, `code` - sh's exit code; install.sh's\n  own output then goes to stderr so stdout stays one JSON value.\")]\n    Update(UpdateArgs),\n\n    /// Put a .moai/ into this repository (safe to run again)\n    #[command(after_help = \"  Run again where it is already installed and only the attached files\n  (.gitattributes, .gitignore, AGENTS.md) are brought back in line. Issues\n  and the journal are not touched.\n\n  The prefix is decided once - every id already issued carries it.\n\n  **In a terminal the first init asks.** It shows the prefix and each choice\n  with its default picked, and Enter plants. A flag picks its row and locks\n  it; give every row a flag and nothing is asked. --yes asks nothing and\n  uses the old defaults - committed, with the guide block - for choices that\n  neither a flag nor existing git rules and guide files settle. Nothing is\n  asked where a script or an agent calls it - stdin or stdout is not a\n  terminal, TERM=dumb, or --json - and there init plants the same as --yes.\n  Running it again where .moai already stands never asks. Esc stops with nothing\n  written. Even a first run reads existing git ignore rules and the moai\n  guide block. A later run also recognizes installed moai hooks when no block\n  stands. If git fails, init refuses rather than guessing commit mode.\n\n  **Optional skills** (moai-tmux and moai-cmux, the supervisor's hands on\n  tmux panes and cmux tabs) get a row each under hooks · skills, shown while\n  that row installs. The screen checks one when it is already planted here,\n  or when your shell says you use it ($TMUX set for moai-tmux,\n  $CMUX_SURFACE_ID for moai-cmux); Enter passes the checked ones on\n  to `moai skill install --with`, and unchecking one already planted passes\n  --without. --with <skill> (repeatable, or names with a comma) checks and\n  locks that row and turns installing on; it cannot go with --no-skill.\n\n... [68 lines truncated] ...\n\n  there are no empty updates.\n\n  The two Korean text plugins an earlier moai installed alongside\n  (korean-skills and humanize-korean) are **removed**, once per scope: only\n  where this repository's moai stands as an earlier version (its installed\n  skill still teaches them), and only when their marketplace is the one an\n  earlier moai added. Once that scope holds this version, nothing there is\n  removed again. Where that earlier version stands at a scope other than\n  --scope, install first brings it up to this version there (claude plugin\n  update --scope <that scope>), so the next install does not remove from it\n  again; if that fails, nothing is removed there and the next install tries\n  again. Nothing is removed or brought up when moai's own registration\n  fails. A user-scope install is left behind when another repository's moai\n  stands there, and then the command to remove it is printed in one line;\n  that scope is not brought up either, so it is removed once that moai is\n  gone. The marketplaces are left behind. If one cannot be removed, moai's own\n  registration still stands and the command to remove it by hand is printed.\n\n  At project scope an earlier moai also declared their marketplaces in the\n  committed .claude/settings.json, which kept offering them to the team. moai\n  deletes those entries itself - only theirs, only when they point where an\n  earlier moai pointed them, and only when nothing in that file still enables\n  a plugin from them. The rest of the file stays as it was; commit the\n  change. `claude plugin marketplace remove --scope project` is not used: with\n  no other declaration in sight it removes the marketplace from the whole\n  machine. If the entry cannot be deleted, where to delete it is printed.\n\n  moai skill install                  just me (the default. settings.local.json)\n  moai skill install --scope user     every repository on this machine\n  moai skill install --scope project  with the team (committed settings.json)\n  moai skill install --dry-run        only show what would be done\n  moai skill install --agent codex    .agents/skills/ for Codex and Antigravity\n  moai skill install --agent auto     whichever agent is on PATH\n  moai skill install --with moai-tmux     plant the tmux skill too\n  moai skill install --without moai-tmux  take it out again\n  moai skill install --with moai-cmux     plant the cmux skill\n\n  A Claude session already open keeps the old version - reopen it to pick\n  this one up.\")]\n    Install {\n        // 값과 기본값은 `--color` 처럼 글로 적는다 — clap 이 붙이는 괄호가 `-h` 에서\n        // 98칸이 됐다(moai-x18p).\n        //\n        // **기본값을 clap 에 안 맡긴다**(moai-xs2h.ylx) — 준 값인지 알아야 `--agent codex --scope user` 에 \"범위는\n        // Claude 의 것\" 한 줄을 낸다. 기본값 `local` 은 부르는 쪽이 채운다.\n        /// Where to register: local (default), project, user\n        #[arg(long, value_name = \"scope\", hide_possible_values = true)]\n        scope: Option<Scope>,\n\n        /// Agent: claude (default), codex, antigravity, auto","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

길은 하나다: 플래그와 선택 상자가 저마다 [`Choices`] 를 만들고, 같은 [`resolve`] 를 지나 [`Plan`] 이\n//! 된다. `init::run` 은 `Plan` 만 받는다 — 그래서 화면으로 고른 것과 플래그로 준 것이 다른 결과를 낼\n//! 길이 구조로 없다.\n//!\n//! **저장하는 것은 사람이 고른 값뿐이다.** 칸마다 `Option` 이고 `None` 은 \"기본값을 따른다\" 다.\n//! 건드린다 — 그래서 [`resolve`] 는 그 차례로 한 번 훑으면 답이 난다. 거스르는 규칙이 필요해지면\n//! 그때가 설계를 다시 볼 때다.\n//!\n//! 사람이 고른 값이 앞 칸 때문에 무효가 되면 **지우지 않는다**. 화면은 그 칸을 숨기거나 잠그고 실제\n//! 값은 `resolve` 가 정한다 — 앞 칸을 되돌리면 고른 값이 그대로 돌아온다.\n\nuse crate::skill::OPTIONAL;\nuse clap::ValueEnum;\nuse ratatui::crossterm::event::{KeyCode, KeyEvent, KeyModifiers};\n\n/// 선택 스킬의 수([`crate::skill::OPTIONAL`]) — 칸 하나가 스킬 하나다.\nconst N: usize = OPTIONAL.len();\n\n/// 트래커를 git 이 추적하는가(moai-zynt.own).\n///\n/// **`--tracking` 의 값은 clap 이 이 열거형에서 푼다**(moai-8gwh.86j) — 낱말 목록을 손으로 적고 `parse` 로 다시\n/// 풀던 판은 두 목록이 갈리면 맞지 않는 값을 말없이 버렸다. 플래그의 낱말은 [`Tracking::word`] 와 같다.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, ValueEnum)]\npub enum Tracking {\n    /// 커밋해서 공유한다 — 지금까지의 `init` 이다.\n    Commit,\n    /// 이 클론에만 둔다. 무시 규칙을 `.git/info/exclude` 에 적는다 — 커밋되는 파일이 하나도 안 바뀐다.\n    Exclude,\n    /// 이 클론에만 둔다. 무시 규칙을 `.gitignore` 에 적는다 — 그 줄은 커밋되어 남에게도 보인다.\n    Gitignore,\n}\n\nimpl Tracking {\n    pub const ALL: [Tracking; 3] = [Tracking::Commit, Tracking::Exclude, Tracking::Gitignore];\n\n    /// 플래그와 `--json` 이 쓰는 낱말.\n    pub fn word(self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Tracking::Commit => \"commit\",\n            Tracking::Exclude => \"exclude\",\n            Tracking::Gitignore => \"gitignore\",\n        }\n    }\n\n... [40 lines truncated] ...\n\npub struct Choices {\n    /// id 접두어. `None` 이면 `run` 이 디렉터리 이름에서 짓는다 — 파일 시스템을 알아야 해서 여기서\n    /// 셈하지 않는다.\n    pub prefix: Option<String>,\n    pub tracking: Option<Tracking>,\n    /// `--guide`, 그리고 `--no-agents` 는 `--guide none` 이다.\n    pub guide: Option<Guide>,\n    /// 끝에 `moai skill install --scope local` 을 부르는가(moai-785q). `--skill`·`--no-skill`.\n    pub skill: Option<bool>,\n    /// `.git/config` 에 머지 드라이버를 심는가. `--driver`·`--no-driver` — 칸마다 짝 플래그가 선다. 켜는 쪽이\n    /// 없던 판은 커밋하는 트래커에서 이 칸만 플래그로 못 잠가, 모든 칸에 플래그를 줘도 화면이 열렸다(리뷰\n    /// moai-zynt.63u).\n    pub driver: Option<bool>,\n    /// 끝에 `moai project add` 로 사용자 설정의 프로젝트 목록에 올리는가(moai-785q). `--register`·`--no-register`.\n    pub project: Option<bool>,\n    /// 선택 스킬([`crate::skill::OPTIONAL`] 의 차례)마다 심는가(moai-3r7l.ocn). `--with <이름>` 이 `Some(true)` 다 —\n    /// 끄는 플래그는 없다(빼는 것은 `moai skill install --without`). 칸은 설치 칸이 켜졌을 때만 선다.\n    pub optional: [Option<bool>; N],\n}\n\nimpl Choices {\n    /// `self` 가 고른 칸은 `self` 의 것, 나머지는 `under` 의 것. 플래그(`self`)를 화면(`under`) 위에 얹는다.\n    pub fn over(&self, under: &Choices) -> Choices {\n        Choices {\n            prefix: self.prefix.clone().or_else(|| under.prefix.clone()),\n            tracking: self.tracking.or(under.tracking),\n            guide: self.guide.or(under.guide),\n            skill: self.skill.or(under.skill),\n            driver: self.driver.or(under.driver),\n            project: self.project.or(under.project),\n            optional: std::array::from_fn(|i| self.optional[i].or(under.optional[i])),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 묻지 않아도 되는가 — 화면에 서는 칸이 모두 골라졌다. **접두어도 센다**: 나중에 못 바꾸는 값이라\n    /// 기본값(디렉터리 이름)을 그대로 쓰더라도 한 번 보이는 값어치가 있다. 숨는 칸은 안 센다 — 추적하지\n    /// 않으면 드라이버는 묻지 않는다.\n    pub fn complete(&self, d: &Defaults) -> bool {\n        let plan = resolve(self, d);\n        FIELDS.iter().filter(|f| shown(**f, &plan)).all(|f| match f {\n            Field::Prefix => self.prefix.is_some(),\n            Field::Tracking => self.tracking.is_some(),\n            Field::Guide => self.guide.is_some(),\n            // 훅으로 알리면 설치는 이미 정해졌다 — 물을 것이 없다.\n            Field::Skill => self.skill.is_some() || plan.guide == Guide::Hook,\n            Field::Driver => self.driver.is_some(),\n            Field::Project => self.project.is_some(),\n            // **선택 스킬 칸은 혼자 화면을 열지 않는다** — 다른 칸을 다 플래그로 준 사람은 묻지 말라는 것이고, 그때 심는\n            // 것은 `--with` 와 이미 심긴 것뿐이다([`PLAIN`]). 화면이 서면 그 칸도 함께 묻는다.\n            Field::Optional(_) => true,","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 2831,3050p src/guide.rs","description":"Read the full recover() function in HEAD"},"toolOutput":"pub fn recover() -> String {\n    format!(\n        r#\"---\nname: moai-recover\ndescription: Use in Claude Code when the person asks to bring back the sessions of this repository that died — after a restart, an OOM kill or a crash — so the supervisor and its workers carry on where they stopped. Finds the dead sessions, draws the state each was in, points out background work that never returned and broken target links, and resumes each one in a new tmux pane or cmux tab, or prints the command to type. Triggers on \"recover the sessions\", \"bring the sessions back\", \"resume the dead sessions\", \"되살려\", \"세션 복구\", \"이어 가게 해\".\n---\n\n# moai-recover — bring back the sessions that died\n\nUse this when the person asks for it: the sessions of this repository — a supervisor, its\nworkers — died together, after a restart, an OOM kill or a crash, and the person wants them\nto carry on. **Their asking is the yes:** inside tmux or cmux you open the panes without asking\nagain.\nNone of this is a moai command; it is you reading Claude Code's own records and typing where\nthe person can watch.\n\n## What never happens\n\n- **No headless run.** A session you bring back is an ordinary interactive `claude --resume`\n  the person can see and type into. Never `claude -p`, never a `--dangerously-*` flag, never\n  `--permission-mode`\n- **Nothing is killed.** Never `kill-server`, `kill-session` or `kill-pane`, never `pkill`\n  or `killall` aimed at tmux (hook rule 4); inside cmux never `close-surface`, `close-workspace`\n  or `close-window`, and never `--force`. A session that is alive is left alone\n- **Only the panes you opened.** Type only into a pane this skill opened, by the `%N` that\n  `split-window` printed — every call names it, `-t <pane>`. Inside cmux it is the surface UUID\n  `new-split` printed, `--surface <surface>`\n- **Never over the person's words.** Paste only into an empty input box (\"Is the input box\n  empty\" below); otherwise tell the person\n- **No polling.** Every look is one look; the next comes after your next step, as its own\n  call — never a loop, never a `sleep`\n- **Their work stays as it is.** No commit, no checkout, no stash, no build, no `moai` write —\n  what a dead session left is for that session to pick up\n\n## Is the input box empty\n\nInside tmux:\n\n{EMPTY_BOX}\n\nInside cmux:\n\n{CMUX_EMPTY_BOX}\n\n**When it is not empty, do not paste.** Tell the person which pane holds what — the words in it\nare theirs.\n\n## 1. Find the dead\n\nClaude Code keeps one record per process under `~/.claude/sessions/`, and a process that dies\n\n... [120 lines truncated] ...\n\n\n**No other flag.** It prints `OK surface:<n> (<UUID>) workspace:<n> (<UUID>)` — the first UUID\nis the new tab, the second your workspace. The command is typed into the tab's shell, so the\nshell stays when `claude` exits, and the split does not take focus. When all are open, even\nthe splits out once:\n\n    cmux rpc workspace.equalize_splits '{{\"workspace_id\":\"<workspace UUID>\"}}'\n\nThen, as a separate call per tab, look once: when its box is empty (\"Is the input box empty\"\nabove), paste the block:\n\n    cmux paste --surface <surface> --submit -- - < <file>\n\nIf cmux refuses — someone's words or a dialog in the box — do not try again; tell the person.\nIf the box has not shown yet, look again after your next step. A prompt in the tab (trusting\nthe folder, say) is the person's to answer — tell them which tab. When all are open, tell the\nperson which tab is which session.\n\n## 7. Outside tmux and cmux — say what to type\n\nNeither way above stands: open nothing. Print, per session in the same order, the line the\nperson types in a terminal of their own, and under it the block to paste once its box shows:\n\n    cd <cwd> && claude --resume <sessionId>\n\"#\n    )\n}\n\n/// 되짚기(7-1)가 에픽 목적에 걸리는 backlog 를 선 에픽의 멤버로 되찾는 줄(moai-l288).\n/// **이것도 promote 다**(moai-f3ml) — `add` 와 손 닫기로 적었던 판은 \"backlog 를 일감으로 바꾸는\n/// 길은 promote 하나\" 를 어겼고, 그것을 지키던 시험에서 이 줄을 빼야 했다.\n///\n/// **`-C <루트>` 를 줄에 박는다.** 7-1 은 워크트리에서 치는데, 글로만 \"4-1 대로\" 라고 적고 줄을\n/// 맨 `moai` 로 두면 그대로 옮겨 친 줄이 워크트리의 `.moai` 에 멤버를 세운다 — 병합에서 스냅샷이\n/// 부딪히거나, 4-1 이 시키는 `git checkout -- .moai` 로 그 멤버가 사라진 채 에픽이 닫힌다.\n/// `<루트>` 는 감독이 채우는 자리라 받은 줄에 실제 자리가 박혀 온다. 다른 자리 이름은 그 목록과\n/// 겹치지 않는다 — 겹치면 맡긴 backlog 의 값이 이 줄에 미리 박힌다(`<등급>` 와 같은 덫).\nconst RECALL: &str = \"moai -C <root> backlog promote <backlog id> -e <epic> --from -\";\n\n/// 7 에서 리뷰 이슈를 세우며 멤버를 `review` 칸에 세우는 줄(사용자 결정 2026-10-03, moai-vxld).\n/// 리뷰가 도는 동안 아무도 손대지 않는 멤버가 보드에서 `in_progress` 로 \"하는 중\" 을 말했고,\n/// 브리프가 칸을 말하지 않아 창마다 옮기기도 두기도 했다.\n///\n/// **`--from in_progress` 가 첫 칸의 멤버를 거른다.** 4-3·7-1 로 남긴 멤버는 이 리뷰가 안 본\n/// 일이라 `review` 에 서면 안 되는데, 글로 \"빼라\" 고만 하면 옮겨 친 줄이 그것까지 세운다 —\n/// 본 칸이 다르면 옮기지 않는 `--from` 이 그 판단을 대신 한다.\nconst TO_REVIEW: &str = \"moai -C <root> mv <member> review --from in_progress\";\n\n/// `review` 칸이 없는 저장소에서 [`TO_REVIEW`] 가 받는 거절의 머리. 칸 이름은 config 가\n/// 정하는데, 브리프는 2 에서 이미 `in_progress`·`todo` 를 이름으로 박았다 — 그래서 칸이 있는지","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

The workers merge. Overlapping\nmerges are prevented by splitting the files when the supervisor sends (1), and where\nthey still collide the worker goes back into its worktree and resolves them.\n\n**This skill is for Claude Code, and moai carries no messaging.** The supervisor and its\nworkers talk with Claude Code's own tools:\n\n- `ListAgents` lists the live sessions, and subagents too — each row's name, its kind\n  (`interactive`, `bg`), whether it is busy or idle, and its tmux pane if it has one\n- `SendMessage(to: <name>, message: …)` sends to one session. With `notify_when_idle: true`\n  you also get one notice when that session goes idle; leave `message` out and it only\n  subscribes\n- A reply comes in as a cross-session message. Answer it by copying its `from` as `to`\n\n**Every session here is an interactive one the person can see.** The moai binary never\nlaunches or drives an agent, and nothing here runs headless. Outside tmux the supervisor\nlaunches nothing either; inside tmux or cmux it may open a worker pane, only after the person\nsays yes (`moai-tmux` or `moai-cmux`, below). **A worker is every idle session of this\nrepository in `ListAgents`, except you** — a row whose name starts with the root\ndirectory's slug and a `-` (2). Nobody registers and nobody is asked which windows count.\nThe message you send is the whole assignment, and it names the file of the worker's steps,\nwhich the worker reads (3).\n\n**One supervisor per repository.** A supervisor waiting for reports reads `idle` in\n`ListAgents` like any worker, so a second one sends it backlog, and the two keep separate\nbooks of what was sent — one backlog, or one worker, gets two jobs. Before the first round,\nask the person whether another window here runs `moai-supervise`; if one does, stop. A\nsession that refuses work because it is a supervisor comes out of the candidates. **You\nrefuse too:** a message that hands you backlog to work on came from another supervisor — do\nnothing of it, reply to its `from` that you are a supervisor, and tell the person.\n\nFive things about the messaging, one line each:\n\n- A session in a different permission mode holds an incoming message for its person's\n  approval — a worker that stays idle after you sent may be waiting on that\n- `notify_when_idle` answers only for a session on this machine — one reason a worker is a\n  session on this machine (2)\n\n... [12 lines truncated] ...\n\nstep below goes through messages and the person, as written. `moai-tmux` is an optional skill:\nit stands only where it was chosen (`moai skill install --with moai-tmux`, or its row in `moai\ninit`). Inside tmux without it, tell the person that one line plants it, and carry on as if\noutside tmux.\n\n**Inside cmux, load `moai-cmux` instead.** When `CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set in your shell and\n`$TMUX` is not, `moai-cmux` gives you the same hands on the workers' cmux tabs, at the same\nfive points, and reads the same session map. It needs cmux 0.65.0 or later and says so itself.\nWhen both are set you run in tmux inside a cmux tab — what you type goes to tmux, so it is\n`moai-tmux`. **With neither, nothing of either applies.** `moai-cmux` is optional the same\nway (`moai skill install --with moai-cmux`); inside cmux without it, tell the person that one\nline plants it, and carry on as if outside cmux.\n\n**When sessions died** — a restart or an OOM kill took the workers or a supervisor down —\nand the person asks to bring them back, load `moai-recover`, inside tmux or not.\n\n**Work you send out is always done in a worktree** — even if the repository has no\nworktree convention. Several workers share one root checkout, so fixing things in the\nroot mixes their edits and commits together. Worktrees stand in\n`<root>/.worktrees/`, and `moai init` writes that path into the gitignore.\n\n**Read the root branch once, at the start of the round.** Workers commit the tracker in\nthe root checkout and branch their worktrees from the local branches there, so that\ncheckout's current branch is the root branch — the remote's default branch may differ from\nthe root and may be stale. A worker that answered your message by refusing\nthe work is not a delivery that failed — it comes out of the candidates (the supervisor's 2).\n\n## When a worker stalls\n\nWhen a `notify_when_idle` notice comes with no report, or the person asks about a worker that\nhas read `busy` far longer than its work should take, look at its pane once:\n\n    tmux capture-pane -p -t <pane> -S -40\n\nand read why it stopped — a permission prompt, a question (`AskUserQuestion`), an API or\nrate-limit error, or a process that ended (a shell prompt where the box was). **Tell the\nperson** what the pane shows and which pane it is. Do not answer the prompt, do not press a\nkey, and do not look again in a loop. A process that ended is a dead session: bringing it\nback is `moai-recover`, once the person asks for it.\n\n## No idle worker left\n\nWhen the supervisor's 2 finds no worker, ask the person **once** whether to open new worker\npanes, and how many — one question covers several panes. Open a pane only on their yes, or\nwhen they asked you for it. On a yes, for each pane:\n\n    tmux split-window -P -F '#{{pane_id}}' -t \"$TMUX_PANE\" -c <root> 'claude --model <model>; exec bash'\n    tmux select-layout -t \"$TMUX_PANE\" tiled\n\n`<root>` is the `root dir` of the supervisor's 2 and `<model>` the model picked in 2-1. **No\nother flag.** The first line prints the new pane's id; `exec bash` keeps a shell in the pane\nwhen `claude` exits, so what it said stays readable. The pane belongs to the same person —\nit is their interactive session like any other.\n\nOnce it has started (a separate call: `capture-pane` of the new pane shows the `❯` box), look\nat `ListAgents` once more. The new row is a worker like any other (the supervisor's 2) — send\nto it as in 3. If it does not show yet, look once more after your next step; if a prompt\nstands in the new pane (trusting the folder, say), tell the person — it is theirs to answer.\n\"#\n    )\n}\n\n/// cmux 의 빈 입력 칸 잣대 — `moai-cmux` 와 `moai-recover` 가 `format!` 으로 같은 글을 싣는다([`EMPTY_BOX`] 와 같은\n/// 까닭이다, moai-o9je). 사람 결정(2026-10-10)대로 cmux 의 `surface.input_state` 가 읽은 것을 그대로 쓴다 — cmux 가\n/// 화면에서 Claude Code 의 입력 줄(`❯` 와 `─` 두 줄 사이)을 읽고, 흐린 자리글을 초안과 가른다. tmux 처럼 `-e` 로 색을\n/// 받아 손으로 가르는 글은 cmux 에 없다(`read-screen` 은 색을 안 낸다).\n///\n/// **초안 가드에 기대지 않는다.** `paste`·`send` 는 초안 앞에서 스스로 멈추지만, 그 거절은 `blocks_typing` 에 서고 그것은\n/// cmux 의 Claude 훅이 `agent` 를 채운 surface 에서만 참이다(v0.65.0 소스) — 훅 없이 띄운 `claude` 는 `state` 가 `draft`\n/// 여도 막히지 않는다. 그래서 `state` 를 스스로 읽는다. 가드는 둘째 울타리다.\npub const CMUX_EMPTY_BOX: &str = r#\"    cmux rpc surface.input_state '{\"surface_id\":\"<surface>\"}'","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

}","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"/tmp/cargo-target/moai-p5sz/debug/moai skill install --help 2>&1 | sed -n '1,60p'","description":"Show skill install help rendering"},"toolOutput":"Plant the skills for each agent; register Claude's with `claude`\n\nUsage: moai skill install [OPTIONS]\n\nOptions:\n      --scope <scope>        Where to register: local (default), project, user\n      --agent <agent>        Agent: claude (default), codex, antigravity, auto\n      --with <skill>         Also plant this optional skill (repeatable)\n      --without <skill>      Remove this optional skill (repeatable)\n      --dry-run              Change nothing; only say what would be done\n      --json                 Machine-readable output. Every human line goes away\n      --no-color             Turn colour off (same as `--color never`)\n      --color <how>          auto|always|never (auto by default, off when piped)\n  -C, --dir <path>           Run in this directory (same as `git -C`)\n      --user <name (email)>  Who is doing this (from `git config` when absent)\n  -h, --help                 Print help\n\n  Which agents: --agent claude (the default), codex, antigravity or auto -\n  repeat it for several. auto takes whichever of claude, codex and agy is on\n  PATH, and claude when none is.\n\n  Codex and Antigravity read the same `.agents/skills/` in this repository, so\n  naming either plants it for both. There is nothing to register: commit the\n  directory and the team has it. --scope is Claude's registration only. The\n  text is the one Claude gets; the steps that differ per agent are in the\n  `moai` skill's \"Words per agent\" table. The supervisor (moai-supervise),\n  its hands on tmux panes and cmux tabs (moai-tmux, moai-cmux) and the\n  recovery of sessions that died\n  (moai-recover) are planted for Claude Code only — Codex and Antigravity get\n  no supervisor.\n\n  Optional skills are planted only where you choose them: moai-tmux and\n  moai-cmux, the supervisor's hands on tmux panes and on cmux tabs (cmux\n  0.65.0 or later). --with <skill> plants one and\n  --without <skill> removes it; both repeat, and a comma separates names.\n  What you chose is not written down anywhere - a skill planted in the tree\n  is the answer. So a plain install refreshes the optional skills already\n  planted and plants no new one, and a first install plants none. Naming a\n  skill that is always planted, or one name in both, is refused.\n\n  The hooks are each agent's own: --agent codex plants `.codex/hooks.json`,\n  --agent antigravity plants `.agents/hooks.json` - commit them too. Codex\n  runs project hooks only once you trust them: open /hooks in a codex session\n  in this repository, and again whenever they change. A hooks file moai did\n  not write is left as it is - merge moai's in by hand, or move it aside. Codex\n  sends hooks only for its shell, apply_patch and MCP calls.\n\n  For Claude, skills and hooks are installed into `.claude/moai-plugin/` and\n  registered with `claude`. Your settings.json is not touched - putting the\n  two keys in is `claude`'s job. The one exception is the old declarations\n  below.\n\n  **Running again only overwrites.** Deleting a hook file a running session\n  holds would block every tool call of that session. The one thing deleted\n  is a skill directory an earlier moai planted in the same tree and this one\n  no longer plants (skills/moai-work/, and skills/moai-supervise/ in\n  .agents/skills/), or an optional skill left out with --without, and only\n  while it holds nothing but the files moai planted there; one with a file\n  of yours in it is left, and one line names it.","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"/tmp/cargo-target/moai-p5sz/debug/moai"}}

Issues\n  and the journal are not touched.\n\n  The prefix is decided once - every id already issued carries it.\n\n  **In a terminal the first init asks.** It shows the prefix and each choice\n  with its default picked, and Enter plants. A flag picks its row and locks\n  it; give every row a flag and nothing is asked. --yes asks nothing and\n  uses the old defaults - committed, with the guide block - for choices that\n  neither a flag nor existing git rules and guide files settle. Nothing is\n  asked where a script or an agent calls it - stdin or stdout is not a\n  terminal, TERM=dumb, or --json - and there init plants the same as --yes.\n  Running it again where .moai already stands never asks. Esc stops with nothing\n  written. Even a first run reads existing git ignore rules and the moai\n  guide block. A later run also recognizes installed moai hooks when no block\n  stands. If git fails, init refuses rather than guessing commit mode.\n\n  **Optional skills** (moai-tmux and moai-cmux, the supervisor's hands on\n  tmux panes and cmux tabs) get a row each under hooks · skills, shown while\n  that row installs. The screen checks one when it is already planted here,\n  or when your shell says you use it ($TMUX set for moai-tmux,\n  $CMUX_SURFACE_ID for moai-cmux); Enter passes the checked ones on\n  to `moai skill install --with`, and unchecking one already planted passes\n  --without. --with <skill> (repeatable, or names with a comma) checks and\n  locks that row and turns installing on; it cannot go with --no-skill.\n  Where nothing is asked, only what --with names is planted - nothing by\n  what your shell says - and optional skills already planted are refreshed.\n\n  A new prefix is up to 8 characters - you type it with every id. A longer\n  one is refused with shorter candidates. Without one it is made from the\n  directory name: dropping hyphens if that fits (moa-issue becomes moaissue),\n  else the initials of the hyphenated words (my-company-backend becomes mcb),\n  and with a single word the first 8 characters. A repository already\n  installed with a longer prefix is read and written as it is.\n\n  **It installs the merge driver too.** The repository declares merge=moai in\n  `.gitattributes`, and the command that word names lives in .git/config,\n  which is not committed - so init writes both. It picks the `moai` on PATH\n  when that is the same build, else the binary running now, and says which.\n  Run it again and a path that has gone dead is replaced. A clone of a\n  repository that already has a .moai never runs init: there the one line\n  from `moai status` is what asks for `moai merge-driver --install`.\n\n  --no-driver leaves .git/config alone. A repository that wants no driver at\n  all says so in `.gitattributes` - a line for the snapshot that settles\n  merge itself (`.moai/issues.jsonl   text eol=lf -merge`) is read as the\n  decision and init leaves it alone. An explicit --driver with --tracking\n  exclude or gitignore is refused.\n\n  --json reports gitignore=true only when .gitignore was written; exclude=true\n  means the ignore lines were written to .git/info/exclude. Its driver is\n  planted, current (already the same line), off (the repository declares no\n  driver, or is not a git repository), failed (driver_trouble says why),\n  skipped (--no-driver, this run only) or untracked (a tracker kept out of\n  git - git never merges it, so there is nothing to drive).\n\n  --check writes nothing and only answers whether the AGENTS.md block is\n  current, stale or missing, and where the merge driver stands. It is\n  non-zero when a file cannot be read or git cannot determine tracking.\n\n  --print only prints that block. That is where to copy it from when the file\n  the agent reads is not AGENTS.md - --print and init write the same text.\")]\n    Init {\n        /// id prefix (up to 8). [])\n    }\n\n    /// Splits a surface's TTY population into processes cmux can prove it owns and\n    /// processes that merely share the TTY device.\n    ///\n    /// Sharing a TTY is not ownership: a process reparented to launchd keeps the\n    /// controlling TTY of the terminal it was launched from, so a detached REPL or dev\n    /// server would otherwise be summed into the surface's memory.\n    /// See https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/issues/11004.\n    ///\n    /// - Parameters:\n    ///   - ttyPIDs: every PID sharing the surface's TTY device.\n    ///   - surfaceID: the surface being annotated, when it has an identifier.\n    ///   - cmuxOwnedPIDs: the window's app processes and their descendants, used as launch\n    ///     evidence for a process whose parent sits off the TTY.\n    ///   - provenPIDs: PIDs already proven through the cmux-scoped process tree.\n    /// - Returns: the proven set, the unattributed set, and the reason for each PID.\n    func ttyOwnership(\n        ttyPIDs: Set<Int>,\n        surfaceID: UUID?,\n        cmuxOwnedPIDs: Set<Int>,\n        provenPIDs: Set<Int> = []\n    ) -> CmuxTopTTYOwnership {\n        var ownershipProcesses: [Int: CmuxTopTTYOwnershipProcess] = [:]\n        ownershipProcesses.reserveCapacity(ttyPIDs.count)\n        for pid in ttyPIDs {\n            guard let process = processesByPID[pid] else { continue }\n            ownershipProcesses[pid] = CmuxTopTTYOwnershipProcess(\n                pid: process.pid,\n                parentPID: process.parentPID,\n                processGroupID: process.processGroupID,\n                cmuxSurfaceID: process.cmuxSurfaceID","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"cd"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 6076,6155p src/guide.rs","description":"Read the recover skill test"},"toolOutput":"    /// 없음, 빈 입력 칸에만 붙이기. tmux 밖이면 칠 줄을 내기만 한다. 차례는 일꾼 먼저, 감독 마지막이다 — 감독의\n    /// `ListAgents` 가 일꾼을 봐야 한다. 짝에 없는 것은 대화 기록에서 읽고, 둘째 짝은 적지 않는다.\n    #[test]\n    fn the_recover_skill_resumes_into_its_own_panes() {\n        let text = recover();\n        let calls = tmux_calls(&text);\n        assert!(calls >= 5, \"되살리기 스킬의 tmux 명령을 못 셌다 — {calls}\");\n        let calls = cmux_calls(&text);\n        assert!(calls >= 4, \"되살리기 스킬의 cmux 명령을 못 셌다 — {calls}\");\n        never_kills_nor_runs_headless(&text);\n        // 짝은 하나다 — `~/.claude/sessions` 를 읽는 둘째 파이썬이 서면 기록의 꼴이 바뀌는 날 한쪽만 고쳐진다.\n        assert_eq!(text.matches(\"~/.claude/sessions/*.json\").count(), 1, \"세션 기록을 읽는 짝이 둘이다\");\n        // 띄우는 줄은 셋 — tmux 칸, cmux 탭(moai-p5sz.kfi), 둘 밖에서 사람이 칠 줄. 깃발은 `--resume` 하나다. 코드 줄에서\n        // `claude ` 를 든 줄을 다 센다 — `--resume` 앞에 다른 깃발(`--model …`)을 끼운 줄도 걸려야 한다.\n        let launches: Vec<&str> = text.lines().filter(|l| l.starts_with(\"    \") && l.contains(\"claude \")).collect();\n        assert_eq!(\n            launches,\n            [\n                \"    tmux split-window -P -F '#{pane_id}' -t \\\"$TMUX_PANE\\\" -c <cwd> 'claude --resume <sessionId>; exec bash'\",\n                \"    cmux --id-format both new-split right --surface \\\"$CMUX_SURFACE_ID\\\" --command 'cd <cwd> && claude --resume <sessionId>'\",\n                \"    cd <cwd> && claude --resume <sessionId>\",\n            ],\n            \"claude 를 띄우는 줄이 셋이 아니거나 다른 깃발이 섰다\"\n        );\n        for flag in [\"claude -p\", \"--dangerously\", \"--permission-mode\"] {\n            assert_eq!(text.matches(flag).count(), 1, \"{flag} 가 하지 않는 것 밖에도 섰다\");\n        }\n        let open = section(&text, \"## 5. Inside tmux — open a pane each\");\n        let tabs = section(&text, \"## 6. Inside cmux — open a tab each\");\n        let outside = section(&text, \"## 7. Outside tmux and cmux — say what to type\");\n        assert!(open.contains(\"paste-buffer -p -d -b moai-recover -t <pane>\"), \"여러 줄을 붙이기로 안 싣는다\");\n        assert!(outside.contains(\"open nothing\"), \"tmux·cmux 밖에서도 칸을 연다\");\n        // cmux 의 판은 제 글이 잰다 — `moai-cmux` 는 고른 사람에게만 서서 그 절을 대면 없는 글을 가리킨다.\n        assert!(tabs.contains(\"`cmux capabilities` lists `surface.input_state`\"), \"되살리기가 cmux 의 판을 안 잰다\");\n        assert!(\n            tabs.contains(\"    cmux paste --surface <surface> --submit -- - < <file>\"),\n            \"cmux 탭에 한 덩이로 안 붙인다\"\n        );\n        assert!(tabs.contains(\"(\\\"Is the input box empty\\\"\\nabove)\"), \"cmux 탭에 붙이기 전에 입력 칸을 안 본다\");\n        assert!(!text.contains(\"`moai-cmux`\"), \"되살리기가 심기지 않았을 수 있는 moai-cmux 를 댄다\");\n        // 빈 입력 칸의 잣대는 제 글 안에 선다 — `moai-tmux` 는 고른 사람에게만 심기니(moai-3r7l) 그 절을 대면 없는\n        // 글을 가리킨다(moai-o9je). 잣대는 `moai-tmux` 와 한 상수다.\n        assert!(!text.contains(\"`moai-tmux`, \\\"Is the\"), \"되살리기가 심기지 않았을 수 있는 moai-tmux 의 절을 댄다\");\n        let rule = &text[text.find(\"\\n## Is the input box empty\\n\").expect(\"되살리기에 빈 입력 칸의 절이 없다\")..];\n        let rule = &rule[..rule.find(\"\\n## 1. [`Scratch::fenced`] 는 그래서 남는다 — **자리를 고르는 시험**(`layer`·`worktree`·`git`)이 제\n//! 자리를 저장소 꼭대기로 세울 때 쓴다. 울타리는 자리째 `Drop` 이 치운다 — 체크아웃 안에 커밋\n//! 없는 저장소가 남으면 그 체크아웃의 `git add -A` 가 거기서 멈춘다([`fence`]).\n\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\n/// 시험 하나가 쓰는 디렉터리. 놓을 때 지운다.\n///\n/// 이름에 pid·스레드·셈을 함께 넣는다 — pid 만으로는 한 판 안의 스레드 둘이 같은 자리를\n/// 잡고, 한쪽의 `Drop` 이 다른 쪽이 쓰는 자리를 지운다.\npub struct Scratch(PathBuf);\n\nimpl Scratch {\n    /// `<자리>/moai-<이름>-<pid>-<스레드>-<셈>` 을 만든다. 이미 있으면 지우고 새로 만든다.\n    ///\n    /// **울타리는 없다.** [`base`] 가 체크아웃 밖임을 보장하므로 위에 잡힐 `.git` 도 `.moai` 도\n    /// 없다(moai-izeo). 울타리를 골라 치던 자리다 — 그것은 `.git` 훑기만 세웠고, `.moai` 를\n    /// 찾아 오르는 쪽은 그대로 바깥 트래커를 잡았다.\n    pub fn new(name: &str) -> Scratch {\n        Scratch::in_place(&base(), name)\n    }\n\n    /// 자리를 받아 세운다. 이름 짓는 법은 [`Scratch::new`] 와 같다. 울타리는 없다 —\n    /// [`Scratch::fenced_in`] 이 이것 위에 세우고, 울타리가 실제로 일하는지 견주는\n    /// 시험이 대조군으로 쓴다.\n    pub fn in_place(base: &Path, name: &str) -> Scratch {\n        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, Ordering};\n        static NTH: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);\n        let dir = base.join(format!(\n            \"moai-{name}-{}-{:?}-{}\",\n            std::process::id(),\n            std::thread::current().id(),\n            NTH.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed),\n        ));\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!(\"{}: {e}\", dir.display()));\n        Scratch(dir)\n    }\n\n    /// 링크를 푼 자리. macOS 의 `/tmp` 는 `/private/tmp` 로 가는 링크라, 도구가 내는\n    /// 철자와 시험이 든 철자가 다르면 견주는 시험이 헛돈다.\n    pub fn real(name: &str) -> Scratch {\n        let mut s = Scratch::new(name);\n        // **여기만 터진다** — 방금 지은 디렉터리라 못 푸는 것은 시험 자리가 성치 않다는 뜻이고,\n        // 받은 철자로 떨어지면([`crate::path::real`]) 견주는 시험이 까닭 없이 붉어진다.\n        s.0 = std::fs::canonicalize(&s.0).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!(\"{}: {e}\", s.0.display()));\n        s\n    }\n\n    /// 아무것도 없는 저장소를 울타리로 세운 자리(moai-46xz). **위로 새지 않는다.**\n    ///\n    /// `worktree` 의 파일로 읽는 반쪽은 `Path::ancestors()` 를 타고 올라가 `.git` 을 처음\n    /// 만나는 곳을 저장소 꼭대기로 읽는다. 자리가 어느 체크아웃 **안**이면 그 체크아웃이\n92:[profile.release]","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

|at: usize| {\n        if at < seen.0 {\n            return lines(&body[..at]);\n        }\n        seen = (at, seen.1 + lines(&body[seen.0..at]));\n        seen.1\n    };\n    let ids = |s: &str, {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 425,470p docs/agents.md; echo ----; sed -n 505,550p docs/agents.md","description":"Read In tmux section of docs/agents.md"},"toolOutput":"**When the person steps away**, they tell the supervisor, and its messages say\n`Person: away`. The worker then settles a design question by its own\nrecommendation and leaves `Decided alone: …` on the issue instead of waiting,\nand stops at anything that cannot be undone.\n\n### In tmux\n\nWhen the supervisor runs inside tmux (`$TMUX` is set) and the `moai-tmux`\nskill is planted ([optional skills](#optional-skills) — `moai skill install\n--with moai-tmux`), it also loads that skill and works on the workers' panes of\nyour own tmux server (moai-u99i). Without tmux, or without the skill, nothing of\nthis happens.\n\n- **Which pane is which worker.** Claude Code keeps a record per process under\n  `~/.claude/sessions/`; the skill reads the live ones (the pid alive and its\n  start time matching) and pairs each `ListAgents` name with its pane `%N`.\n  Every tmux call names that pane\n- **A label on the pane.** When it sends work, it writes `<worker> <id>` into the\n  pane option `@moai`, and removes it once the report is checked. Once a round\n  it asks whether you want the labels on the pane borders; on a yes it puts\n  `#{@moai}` in front of the running server's `pane-border-format`. Your tmux\n  config file is never edited\n- **Clearing a reported worker.** After the report is checked, while the worker\n  reads idle and its input box is empty, it types `/clear` into that pane before\n  sending the next work\n- **A message that did not arrive.** When `SendMessage` fails, it pastes the\n  message into the worker's empty input box and tells you. A message held for\n  your approval is not pasted — it waits for you, and it tells you so\n- **A stalled worker.** When a worker goes idle with no report, it reads the\n  pane once and tells you what stands there — a permission prompt, a question,\n  an error. It never answers in your place\n- **No idle worker.** It asks you whether to open new worker panes; on a yes it\n  splits a pane running `claude --model <model>` in the root — an ordinary\n  interactive session you can see and type into\n\n**If anything stands in a worker's input box, or you are scrolling that pane\n(copy mode), it does not type** — it tells you.\nIt never kills a pane, a session or the server, and never runs `claude -p` or a\n`--dangerously-*` flag.\n\n**On a Mac** the same works: the session records there carry the process start\ntime in another form (`ps -o lstart`), and a pane is matched to a session by its\nterminal (`#{pane_tty}`), never by reading another process's environment\n(moai-p5sz.7q3).\n\n### In cmux\n----\n### Bring back sessions that died\n\nWhen the supervisor and its workers died together — the machine restarted, the\ncontainer was OOM-killed — open one Claude Code session in the root and ask it\nto bring them back (\"recover the sessions\", \"되살려\"). It loads `moai-recover`\n(moai-uqf7); your asking is the yes.\n\n- **Which died.** It reads the same records under `~/.claude/sessions/` and\n  takes the dead ones standing in the root or a worktree, leaving out any that\n  is already back and older crashes you did not name. When several stand in one\n  directory it asks you once which to bring back\n- **What each was doing.** From each session's transcript under\n  `~/.claude/projects/` it reads its role (supervisor or worker), the issue it\n  held and what it was waiting for, adds the uncommitted files and the issue's\n  `Next:` note, and shows you one table\n- **What died with it.** A background subagent or command that never reported\n  back, and a `target` link whose `/tmp/cargo-target/<name>` was wiped — it\n  makes that directory again; the build output is gone, so the session rebuilds\n- **Bringing them back, workers first and the supervisor last.** Inside tmux it\n  splits a pane per session running `claude --resume <id>` and pastes a short\n  note on what happened once the input box is empty; the supervisor is told its\n  workers' names may have changed. Inside cmux (0.65.0 or later) it does the\n  same with a split tab per session. Outside both it prints, per session,\n  `cd <dir> && claude --resume <id>` and the note to paste\n\nIt changes nothing in the sessions' work — no commit, no build, no `moai` write.\n\n## Work the queue from a session\n\nEvery command takes `--json`. Three are enough for a session to take its next row:\n\n- `moai ready --json` — `ready` is yours to pick up, `others` is ready work that\n  belongs to someone else or nobody (ask first), `held` is what is deferred or\n  blocked and where to pick it up again\n- `moai mv <id> in_progress --from todo` — picks up one id only if it still\n  stands where you saw it. A session that lost the race gets `stale` and a\n  non-zero exit, and moves on to the next row. Pass one id per call\n- `moai prime` — what this session holds and what is next, short enough to load\n  into a prompt\n\nThe moai binary never launches a session or runs one headless. A person opens\neach one — or, inside tmux or cmux, says yes to the supervisor opening one — and the\nsession reads these the way that person would.\n\n**Name the AI that did the work** before closing an issue — one note, the\n[model line](glossary.md#model-line), one line per issue, read back as `work` in","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

[`Scratch::fenced`] 는 그래서 남는다 — **자리를 고르는 시험**(`layer`·`worktree`·`git`)이 제\n//! 자리를 저장소 꼭대기로 세울 때 쓴다. 울타리는 자리째 `Drop` 이 치운다 — 체크아웃 안에 커밋\n//! 없는 저장소가 남으면 그 체크아웃의 `git add -A` 가 거기서 NUL)?\nUses only its own throwaway servers under a short base dir, killed with the same -S.\"\"\"\nimport os, subprocess, sys, shutil\n\nbase = \"/private/tmp/claude-501/mrv-sun\"  # short, outside the repo, owned by this user\nos.makedirs(base, exist_ok=True)\nenv = dict(os.environ)\nenv.pop(\"TMUX\", None)\nfor total in (102, 103, 104, 105):\n    # pad a directory name so that <dir>/tmux.sock has exactly `total` chars\n    fixed = len(base) + 1 + len(\"/tmux.sock\")\n    d = os.path.join(base, \"d\" * (total - fixed))\n    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)\n    sock = os.path.join(d, \"tmux.sock\")\n    assert len(sock) == total, (len(sock), total)\n    p = subprocess.run([\"tmux\", \"-S\", sock, \"new-session\", \"-d\", \"-s\", \"probe\", \"sleep 5\"],\n                       capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)\n    print(total, \"chars -> exit\", p.returncode, (p.stderr.strip() or \"ok\")[:120])\n    subprocess.run([\"tmux\", \"-S\", sock, \"kill-server\"], capture_output=True, env=env)\nshutil.rmtree(base, ignore_errors=True)\n"},"toolOutput":"#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Does tmux refuse a -S socket path of 104 chars on macOS (sun_path is 104 incl. {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 40,70p src/scratch.rs","description":"Read Scratch::new implementation"},"toolOutput":"impl Scratch {\n    /// `<자리>/moai-<이름>-<pid>-<스레드>-<셈>` 을 만든다. 이미 있으면 지우고 새로 만든다.\n    ///\n    /// **울타리는 없다.** [`base`] 가 체크아웃 밖임을 보장하므로 위에 잡힐 `.git` 도 `.moai` 도\n    /// 없다(moai-izeo). 울타리를 골라 치던 자리다 — 그것은 `.git` 훑기만 세웠고, `.moai` 를\n    /// 찾아 오르는 쪽은 그대로 바깥 트래커를 잡았다.\n    pub fn new(name: &str) -> Scratch {\n        Scratch::in_place(&base(), name)\n    }\n\n    /// 자리를 받아 세운다. 이름 짓는 법은 [`Scratch::new`] 와 같다. 울타리는 없다 —\n    /// [`Scratch::fenced_in`] 이 이것 위에 세우고, 울타리가 실제로 일하는지 견주는\n    /// 시험이 대조군으로 쓴다.\n    pub fn in_place(base: &Path, name: &str) -> Scratch {\n        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, Ordering};\n        static NTH: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);\n        let dir = base.join(format!(\n            \"moai-{name}-{}-{:?}-{}\",\n            std::process::id(),\n            std::thread::current().id(),\n            NTH.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed),\n        ));\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!(\"{}: {e}\", dir.display()));\n        Scratch(dir)\n    }\n\n    /// 링크를 푼 자리. macOS 의 `/tmp` 는 `/private/tmp` 로 가는 링크라, 도구가 내는\n    /// 철자와 시험이 든 철자가 다르면 견주는 시험이 헛돈다.\n    pub fn real(name: &str) -> Scratch {\n        let mut s = Scratch::new(name);","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 1,80p src/scratch.rs; echo \"TMPDIR=$TMPDIR\"","description":"Read scratch helper and check TMPDIR"},"toolOutput":"//! 시험이 쓰는 임시 디렉터리 한 벌(moai-shgx). **시험에서만 선다.**\n//!\n//! ## 왜 한 벌인가\n//!\n//! 같은 것이 다섯 벌 있었다 — `tui/register.rs`·`tui/layer.rs`·`tui/mod.rs`·\n//! `user_config.rs` 와 통합 시험의 것. 앞의 넷과 `cmd/tui.rs` 의 편집기 시험 자리는\n//! 이것으로 모았다. **통합 시험(`tests/cli.rs`)의 `Scratch` 는 아직 따로다** — 따로 된\n//! 크레이트라 `use` 로는 못 가져가고, 뿌리([`base`])만 `#[path]` 로 이 파일을\n//! 읽어 함께 쓴다. 울타리는 안 쓴다(moai-izeo 뒤로 그쪽에서 [`fence`] 를 부르지 않는다).\n//! 그래서 **이 파일의 단위 시험은 그쪽에서도 컴파일돼 돈다** — 여기 더하는 시험은 `crate::` 의\n//! 다른 모듈을 쓰지 못한다(그쪽 크레이트에는 없다). 그리고 **모으지 않은 자리**(`git.rs`·\n//! `store.rs`·`worktree.rs`)는 끝에서 `remove_dir_all` 을 부르는 식이라, 시험이\n//! 패닉하면 그 줄에 닿지 못해 `/tmp/moai-git-<pid>` 가 그대로 남는다. 이름에 pid 가\n//! 들어 다음 판이 그것을 치우지도 않는다 — 이 기계에 죽은 pid 의 것 셋이 남아 있었다.\n//!\n//! `Drop` 은 패닉으로 풀릴 때도 돈다. 그래서 치우는 일은 **놓을 때** 한다.\n//!\n//! ## 자리\n//!\n//! `std::env::temp_dir()` 다 — **그것이 어느 체크아웃 안이면 밖으로 옮긴다**([`base`], moai-izeo).\n//! **`CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` 은 여기서 못 쓴다** — cargo 는\n//! 그것을 통합 시험·벤치 타깃에만 주고, 이 모듈은 바이너리 타깃의 단위 시험으로\n//! 컴파일되므로 `option_env!` 가 늘 `None` 이었다(`tests/cli.rs` 는 통합 시험이라\n//! `env!` 로 그것을 곧바로 읽는다). 있는 척하는 갈래는 걷어냈다.\n//!\n//! 일부러 저장소 안(`target/` 밑)으로 옮기지는 않는다 — 위의 `.git` 이 꼭대기로 잡혀 moai-46xz 가\n//! 통째로 돌아오고, 위의 `.moai` 는 그보다 나쁘다(moai-izeo: 시험이 바깥 트래커에 실제로 썼다).\n//! [`Scratch::fenced`] 는 그래서 남는다 — **자리를 고르는 시험**(`layer`·`worktree`·`git`)이 제\n//! 자리를 저장소 꼭대기로 세울 때 쓴다. 울타리는 자리째 `Drop` 이 치운다 — 체크아웃 안에 커밋\n//! 없는 저장소가 남으면 그 체크아웃의 `git add -A` 가 거기서 멈춘다([`fence`]).\n\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\n/// 시험 하나가 쓰는 디렉터리. 놓을 때 지운다.\n///\n/// 이름에 pid·스레드·셈을 함께 넣는다 — pid 만으로는 한 판 안의 스레드 둘이 같은 자리를\n/// 잡고, 한쪽의 `Drop` 이 다른 쪽이 쓰는 자리를 지운다.\npub struct Scratch(PathBuf);\n\nimpl Scratch {\n    /// `<자리>/moai-<이름>-<pid>-<스레드>-<셈>` 을 만든다. 이미 있으면 지우고 새로 만든다.\n    ///\n    /// **울타리는 없다.** [`base`] 가 체크아웃 밖임을 보장하므로 위에 잡힐 `.git` 도 `.moai` 도\n    /// 없다(moai-izeo). 울타리를 골라 치던 자리다 — 그것은 `.git` 훑기만 세웠고, `.moai` 를\n    /// 찾아 오르는 쪽은 그대로 바깥 트래커를 잡았다.\n    pub fn new(name: &str) -> Scratch {\n        Scratch::in_place(&base(), name)\n    }\n\n    /// 자리를 받아 세운다. 이름 짓는 법은 [`Scratch::new`] 와 같다. 울타리는 없다 —\n    /// [`Scratch::fenced_in`] 이 이것 위에 세우고, 울타리가 실제로 일하는지 견주는\n    /// 시험이 대조군으로 쓴다.\n    pub fn in_place(base: &Path, name: &str) -> Scratch {\n {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 2546,2566p src/guide.rs; echo .....; sed -n 2975,3025p src/guide.rs","description":"Compare tmux and recover open-pane sections"},"toolOutput":"## No idle worker left\n\nWhen the supervisor's 2 finds no worker, ask the person **once** whether to open new worker\npanes, and how many — one question covers several panes. Open a pane only on their yes, or\nwhen they asked you for it. On a yes, for each pane:\n\n    tmux split-window -P -F '#{{pane_id}}' -t \"$TMUX_PANE\" -c <root> 'claude --model <model>; exec bash'\n    tmux select-layout -t \"$TMUX_PANE\" tiled\n\n`<root>` is the `root dir` of the supervisor's 2 and `<model>` the model picked in 2-1. **No\nother flag.** The first line prints the new pane's id; `exec bash` keeps a shell in the pane\nwhen `claude` exits, so what it said stays readable. The pane belongs to the same person —\nit is their interactive session like any other.\n\nOnce it has started (a separate call: `capture-pane` of the new pane shows the `❯` box), look\nat `ListAgents` once more. The new row is a worker like any other (the supervisor's 2) — send\nto it as in 3. If it does not show yet, look once more after your next step; if a prompt\nstands in the new pane (trusting the folder, say), tell the person — it is theirs to answer.\n\"#\n    )\n}\n.....\n## 5. Inside tmux — open a pane each\n\n`$TMUX` is set in your shell. For each session, in that order:\n\n    tmux split-window -P -F '#{{pane_id}}' -t \"$TMUX_PANE\" -c <cwd> 'claude --resume <sessionId>; exec bash'\n    tmux select-layout -t \"$TMUX_PANE\" tiled\n\n**No other flag.** The first line prints the new pane's `%N`; `exec bash` keeps a shell there\nwhen `claude` exits. Then, as a separate call, look once: when its `❯` box shows and is empty\n(\"Is the input box empty\" above), paste the block:\n\n    tmux load-buffer -b moai-recover <file>\n    tmux paste-buffer -p -d -b moai-recover -t <pane>\n    tmux send-keys -t <pane> Enter\n\nIf the box has not shown yet, look again after your next step. A prompt in the pane (trusting\nthe folder, say) is the person's to answer — tell them which pane. When all are open, tell the\nperson which pane is which session.\n\n## 6. Inside cmux — open a tab each\n\n`CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set in your shell and `$TMUX` is not — and the cmux is 0.65.0 or later:\n`cmux capabilities` lists `surface.input_state` in its `methods`. On an older cmux, tell the\nperson that this way needs cmux 0.65.0, and go to 7. For each session, in that order:\n\n    cmux --id-format both new-split right --surface \"$CMUX_SURFACE_ID\" --command 'cd <cwd> && claude --resume <sessionId>'\n\n**No other flag.** It prints `OK surface:<n> (<UUID>) workspace:<n> (<UUID>)` — the first UUID\nis the new tab, the second your workspace. The command is typed into the tab's shell, so the\nshell stays when `claude` exits, and the split does not take focus. When all are open, even\nthe splits out once:\n\n    cmux rpc workspace.equalize_splits '{{\"workspace_id\":\"<workspace UUID>\"}}'\n\nThen, as a separate call per tab, look once: when its box is empty (\"Is the input box empty\"\nabove), paste the block:\n\n    cmux paste --surface <surface> --submit -- - < <file>\n\nIf cmux refuses — someone's words or a dialog in the box — do not try again; tell the person.\nIf the box has not shown yet, look again after your next step. A prompt in the tab (trusting\nthe folder, say) is the person's to answer — tell them which tab. When all are open, tell the\nperson which tab is which session.\n\n## 7. Outside tmux and cmux — say what to type\n\nNeither way above stands: open nothing. Print, per session in the same order, the line the\nperson types in a terminal of their own, and under it the block to paste once its box shows:\n\n    cd <cwd> && claude --resume <sessionId>\n\"#","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

Finds the dead sessions, draws the state each was in, points out background work that never returned and broken target links, and resumes each one in a new tmux pane or cmux tab, or prints the command to type. Triggers on \"recover the sessions\", \"bring the sessions back\", \"resume the dead sessions\", \"되살려\", \"세션 복구\", \"이어 가게 해\".\n---\n\n# moai-recover — bring back the sessions that died\n\nUse this when the person asks for it: the sessions of this repository — a supervisor, its\nworkers — died together, after a restart, an OOM kill or a crash, and the person wants them\nto carry on. **Their asking is the yes:** inside tmux or cmux you open the panes without asking\nagain.\nNone of this is a moai command; it is you reading Claude Code's own records and typing where\nthe person can watch.\n\n## What never happens\n\n- **No headless run.** A session you bring back is an ordinary interactive `claude --resume`\n  the person can see and type into. Never `claude -p`, never a `--dangerously-*` flag, never\n  `--permission-mode`\n- **Nothing is killed.** Never `kill-server`, `kill-session` or `kill-pane`, never `pkill`\n  or `killall` aimed at tmux (hook rule 4); inside cmux never `close-surface`, `close-workspace`\n  or `close-window`, and never `--force`. A session that is alive is left alone\n- **Only the panes you opened.** Type only into a pane this skill opened, by the `%N` that\n  `split-window` printed — every call names it, `-t <pane>`. Inside cmux it is the surface UUID\n  `new-split` printed, `--surface <surface>`\n- **Never over the person's words.** Paste only into an empty input box (\"Is the input box\n  empty\" below); otherwise tell the person\n- **No polling.** Every look is one look; the next comes after your next step, as its own\n  call — never a loop, never a `sleep`\n- **Their work stays as it is.** No commit, no checkout, no stash, no build, no `moai` write —\n  what a dead session left is for that session to pick up\n\n## Is the input box empty\n\nInside tmux:\n\n{EMPTY_BOX}\n\nInside cmux:\n\n{CMUX_EMPTY_BOX}\n\n**When it is not empty, do not paste.** Tell the person which pane holds what — the words in it\nare theirs.\n\n## 1. Find the dead\n\nClaude Code keeps one record per process under `~/.claude/sessions/`, and a process that dies\n\n... [60 lines truncated] ...\n\n  `\"run_in_background\": true` differs by version and the timeout case carries nothing, so read\n  the result; when it ends, a later user line carries a\n  `<task-notification>` whose `<task-id>` is that id. A launch with no such line after it died\n  with the session — the resumed session will never hear from it, and what it\n  changed is uncommitted in that session's `cwd`\n- **A broken target link.** In the root and each worktree, `target` may be a link to\n  `/tmp/cargo-target/<name>`, and a restart can empty `/tmp`:\n\n      readlink <cwd>/target\n      test -e <cwd>/target || echo dangling\n\n  Make the directory again, `mkdir -p /tmp/cargo-target/<name>`, so builds land there. The\n  build output is gone: `./target/release/moai` needs `cargo build --release` before anything\n  calls it. Do not build it yourself — the resumed session does\n\n## 4. The text each one gets\n\nOne block per session, written to a file in your scratchpad:\n\n    Recovery: this session died at <time> (<what happened>) and was resumed.\n    - Background work that never returned: <each launch and what it was for>. It is dead,\n      do not wait for it; what it changed is uncommitted in <cwd>.\n    - git status --short in <cwd>: <files, or clean>.\n    - target -> /tmp/cargo-target/<name> was gone and is made again; build before you\n      call ./target/release/moai.\n    Go on from where you stopped: <work id>, <what it was waiting for>.\n\nLeave out a line that does not hold. The supervisor's block adds one line: **the workers are\nback in new sessions and their names may have changed — run `ListAgents` again** before you\nsend or wait for a report.\n\n**Workers first, the supervisor last**, in every way below — the supervisor's `ListAgents`\nhas to see the workers when it starts.\n\n## 5. Inside tmux — open a pane each\n\n`$TMUX` is set in your shell. For each session, in that order:\n\n    tmux split-window -P -F '#{{pane_id}}' -t \"$TMUX_PANE\" -c <cwd> 'claude --resume <sessionId>; exec bash'\n    tmux select-layout -t \"$TMUX_PANE\" tiled\n\n**No other flag.** The first line prints the new pane's `%N`; `exec bash` keeps a shell there\nwhen `claude` exits. Then, as a separate call, look once: when its `❯` box shows and is empty\n(\"Is the input box empty\" above), paste the block:\n\n    tmux load-buffer -b moai-recover <file>\n    tmux paste-buffer -p -d -b moai-recover -t <pane>\n    tmux send-keys -t <pane> Enter\n\nIf the box has not shown yet, look again after your next step. The command is typed into the tab's shell, so the\nshell stays when `claude` exits, and the split does not take focus. Outside tmux and cmux — say what to type\n\nNeither way above stands: open nothing. Wait.** End your turn. The report comes back as a cross-session message from the\nworker, `report: <epic>` at its head, and it wakes you. The idle notice that\n`notify_when_idle` sends is not a report: a worker goes idle whenever its turn ends — while\nit waits on its person's answer, say — and one that asked its person something sends nothing\nuntil it is answered. **Do not poll `ListAgents`** — the report comes to you. Inside tmux, an\nidle notice with no report is the moment to read that worker's pane once (`moai-tmux`, \"When a\nworker stalls\") and tell the person what it shows — inside cmux, its tab (`moai-cmux`, \"When a\nworker stalls\").\n\n**A report reaches only the name it was sent to.** A supervisor that started again —\nrestarted, or resumed with `claude --resume` — stands under a new name, and a worker whose\nreport to the old one fails leaves it on the epic as a note with `report: <epic>` at its\nhead. So when you start or resume, before waiting, read what the tracker holds:\n\n    moai show -s in_progress,review        the work sent and picked up, not done\n    moai show -g 'Sent:'                   sent and not done — a backlog not unfolded yet, or an\n                                           epic not picked up yet; neither is a candidate\n....\nreason it was left (a person's decision, a file held beside it).\n\n`<epic>` is the epic id carried in the report. A backlog item is already done once it is\nunfolded and it does not show its members, so `moai show <id>` cannot tell you whether\nthe work finished — when the report does not carry it, read it from that backlog's history\nline about being unfolded.\n\nIf the three hold, mark the report checked on the epic and take it into the root with a\ncommit with a path — a supervisor that starts again reads that line, not this conversation (4).\n\n    moai note <epic> 'Report-checked: <merge hash>'\n\nThen send the next backlog to an idle worker. **Outside tmux and cmux, clearing a window is\nthe person's** — the supervisor never types into a window. The report ends with the worker\ntelling its person when its window can be cleared, so a message you send to that same window\nright away can be erased by a clear that comes after it, and that backlog then waits for a\nreport that never comes. Send to that window once the person has cleared it or said they will\nnot — a clear does not show from here, so ask the person — or send to another idle worker.\n**Inside tmux or cmux you may clear it yourself** — only after the report is checked and the note\nabove is written, only while `ListAgents` and its session record read `idle`, and only when its\ninput box is empty (`moai-tmux`, \"Clear a worker's window\"; `moai-cmux`, \"Clear a worker's\nwindow\"). If any of these fails, do as the paragraph above says. Remove that pane's label once the report is checked (`moai-tmux`), or\nthat tab's (`moai-cmux`).\n\nIf they do not hold, ask that worker with a message what is left, and do not finish it in\nits place.\n\n## The shared root\n\nThe root checkout is **shared by every session.** While one session has a merge open\n(`MERGE_HEAD`), another session committing a tracker note seals that merge with its own","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"git diff f891f00f0cd898de17ab71f327b56da6377b4b0a HEAD -- CHANGELOG.md; sed -n 1,30p CHANGELOG.md | cut -c1-160","description":"Show CHANGELOG diff and head"},"toolOutput":"diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md\nindex d92a0965..02f29a24 100644\n--- a/CHANGELOG.md\n+++ b/CHANGELOG.md\n@@ -12,6 +12,33 @@ does not tag — see `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n \n ## [Unreleased]\n \n+### Added\n+\n+- **A second optional Claude Code skill, `moai-cmux`, for a supervisor running\n+  inside [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux).** It is `moai-tmux` for\n+  cmux tabs: it finds each worker's surface (`cmux top` says which surface a\n+  session runs in), labels its tab once you say labels are wanted, clears a\n+  reported worker's window, pastes a message `SendMessage` could not deliver\n+  (`cmux paste --submit`), reads why a worker stalled, and — only after asking —\n+  opens new worker splits running an ordinary interactive `claude`. It reads the\n+  input box through cmux's own `surface.input_state` and never types over\n+  anything in it, never closes a tab, never moves focus and never passes\n+  `--force`. **It needs cmux 0.65.0 or later** and checks that itself; on an\n+  older cmux it says so and does nothing. Running tmux inside a cmux tab stays\n+  `moai-tmux`'s case. Plant it with `moai skill install --with moai-cmux`, or\n+  its row in the first `moai init` (checked when `$CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set).\n+  `moai-recover` opens a tab per session inside cmux the same way. (moai-p5sz)\n+\n+### Fixed\n+\n+- **`moai-tmux` and `moai-recover` found no session on a Mac.** Their session\n+  map read the process start time from `/proc`, which macOS does not have, so\n+  every session read as dead. It now compares the start time Claude Code writes\n+  on a Mac (`ps -o lstart`), and matches a session to a tmux pane by its\n+  terminal (`#{pane_tty}`) instead of reading the process's environment — which\n+  also no longer trips Claude Code's auto-mode guard against reading other\n+  processes' environments. Plant it with `moai skill install --with moai-cmux`, or\n  its row in the first `moai init` (checked when `$CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set).\n  `moai-recover` opens a tab per session inside cmux the same way. let text = |k: &str| input.get(k).and_then(|v| v.as_str());\n        match tool {\n            Some(\"Bash\") => Call::Shell(text(\"command\").unwrap_or_default()),\n            Some(\"Edit\" | 거기서 돈다. `command_at` 이 감싸는\n        // 명령을 넘게 된 뒤로 이 자가 보이기 시작했고, 안 가리던 판은 남의 리뷰를 두고 **여기**\n        // 트래커에 리뷰 이슈를 세우라고 막았다 — `moai` 축을 닫은 것과 같은 까닭이다.\n        let read = command_at(&seg.words);\n        match read.words.split_first() {\n            Some((first, rest)) if !trackerless(&read, seg) => {\n                let head = first.trim_start_matches('/');\n                head == REVIEW_CMD\n                    || (head.ends_with(\"claude\")\n                        && rest.first().is_some_and(|w| w.trim_start_matches('/') == REVIEW_CMD))\n            }\n            _ => false,\n        }\n    })\n}\n\n/// 이 토막이 **셸에 넘기는 글** — [`handed_text`] 가 읽은 그것이되, **렉서가 이미 읽은 글은\n/// 빼고** 낸다(moai-6qkc).\n///\n/// `eval \"$( … )\"` 가 돌리는 것은 그 치환의 **값**이지 그 글이 아니다. 그 글은 렉서가 낱말의\n/// 치환으로 읽어 제 토막을 이미 하나**의 것이라,\n/// 엉뚱한 치환 하나가 안 읽힌 글을 읽은 것으로 덮었다. 규칙 넷이 다 샜다 —\n/// `bash -c '$(쓰기)' \"$(echo hi)\"` 도, `eval '$(tmux kill-server)' > \"$(mktemp)\"` 도 지나갔다.\nfn shell_text(words: &[String], eaten: {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 425,470p docs/agents.md","description":"Read the In tmux section of docs/agents.md"},"toolOutput":"**When the person steps away**, they tell the supervisor, and its messages say\n`Person: away`. The worker then settles a design question by its own\nrecommendation and leaves `Decided alone: …` on the issue instead of waiting,\nand stops at anything that cannot be undone.\n\n### In tmux\n\nWhen the supervisor runs inside tmux (`$TMUX` is set) and the `moai-tmux`\nskill is planted ([optional skills](#optional-skills) — `moai skill install\n--with moai-tmux`), it also loads that skill and works on the workers' panes of\nyour own tmux server (moai-u99i). Without tmux, or without the skill, nothing of\nthis happens.\n\n- **Which pane is which worker.** Claude Code keeps a record per process under\n  `~/.claude/sessions/`; the skill reads the live ones (the pid alive and its\n  start time matching) and pairs each `ListAgents` name with its pane `%N`.\n  Every tmux call names that pane\n- **A label on the pane.** When it sends work, it writes `<worker> <id>` into the\n  pane option `@moai`, and removes it once the report is checked. Once a round\n  it asks whether you want the labels on the pane borders; on a yes it puts\n  `#{@moai}` in front of the running server's `pane-border-format`. Your tmux\n  config file is never edited\n- **Clearing a reported worker.** After the report is checked, while the worker\n  reads idle and its input box is empty, it types `/clear` into that pane before\n  sending the next work\n- **A message that did not arrive.** When `SendMessage` fails, it pastes the\n  message into the worker's empty input box and tells you. A message held for\n  your approval is not pasted — it waits for you, and it tells you so\n- **A stalled worker.** When a worker goes idle with no report, it reads the\n  pane once and tells you what stands there — a permission prompt, a question,\n  an error. It never answers in your place\n- **No idle worker.** It asks you whether to open new worker panes; on a yes it\n  splits a pane running `claude --model <model>` in the root — an ordinary\n  interactive session you can see and type into\n\n**If anything stands in a worker's input box, or you are scrolling that pane\n(copy mode), it does not type** — it tells you.\nIt never kills a pane, a session or the server, and never runs `claude -p` or a\n`--dangerously-*` flag.\n\n**On a Mac** the same works: the session records there carry the process start\ntime in another form (`ps -o lstart`), and a pane is matched to a session by its\nterminal (`#{pane_tty}`), never by reading another process's environment\n(moai-p5sz.7q3).\n\n### In cmux","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 1,60p .claude/moai-plugin/skills/moai-cmux/SKILL.md","description":"Read top of generated moai-cmux SKILL.md"},"toolOutput":"---\nname: moai-cmux\ndescription: Use in Claude Code together with moai-supervise when the supervisor runs inside cmux (CMUX_SURFACE_ID is set and $TMUX is not) — to find a worker's surface from its ListAgents name, label its tab, clear a reported worker's window, deliver a message SendMessage could not, read why a worker stalled, and open new worker splits once the person says yes. Triggers on \"worker surface\", \"worker tab\", \"open a worker\", \"clear the worker\", \"일꾼 탭\", \"일꾼 창 열어\", \"탭 비워\".\n---\n\n# moai-cmux — the supervisor's hands on the workers' surfaces\n\nThis is the supervisor's (`moai-supervise`) companion **when it runs inside cmux** —\n`CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set in its shell and `$TMUX` is not. Inside tmux — tmux running in a cmux\ntab included — what you type goes to tmux: that is `moai-tmux`, and none of this applies.\nWithout `CMUX_SURFACE_ID` none of this applies either: the supervisor works through messages and\nthe person alone. The cmux app here is **the person's own**: every workspace they have lives in\nit, and every surface you touch is a tab they are looking at.\n\ncmux's words: a window holds workspaces (the rows of its sidebar), a workspace holds panes (its\nsplits), and a pane holds surfaces (the tabs of that split). A surface is one terminal — what you\nread and what you type into.\n\n## First, the version\n\nThis needs cmux 0.65.0 or later. Look once, at the start of the round:\n\n    cmux capabilities\n\nIf its `methods` do not list `surface.input_state`, the cmux here is older: tell the person once\nthat `moai-cmux` needs cmux 0.65.0 or later, and go on as if this skill were not here. Updating\nrestarts cmux, and with it every session inside — yours too — so when is theirs to choose.\n\n## What never happens\n\n- **No headless run.** A worker you open is an ordinary interactive `claude` the person can\n  see and type into. Never `claude -p`, never a `--dangerously-*` flag, never\n  `--permission-mode`. The moai binary launches and drives nothing; this skill is you\n  typing cmux commands where the person can watch\n- **Nothing is closed.** Never `close-surface`, `close-workspace` or `close-window`, never\n  `respawn-pane`, never `pkill` or `killall` aimed at cmux. A worker that is done stays open;\n  closing a tab is the person's\n- **Never `--force`.** cmux refuses to type into a Claude Code box that holds someone's words or a\n  dialog, and `--force` skips that refusal. A refusal is an answer — tell the person\n- **Only a worker's surface.** Type only into a surface found through the session map below for\n  a worker of this repository — never your own (`$CMUX_SURFACE_ID`), never a session of another\n  repository. Every call names its surface by UUID, `--surface <surface>`: left out, cmux types\n  into your own tab, and a `surface:N` name is handed out as asked for and does not outlive a\n  restart\n- **What the person looks at stays theirs.** No `focus-*`, no `select-workspace`, no\n  `--focus true` — a split you open does not take focus\n- **Never over the person's words.** If a worker's input box holds anything, do not type into\n  it — tell the person\n- **Never in their place.** A permission prompt or a question in a worker's tab is the\n  person's to answer — you read it and tell them; you press no key\n- **No polling.** Every look below is one look. A second one comes after your next step, as\n  its own call — never a loop, never a `sleep`, never `wait-for`\n- **The person's cmux settings stay theirs.** No `reload-config`, `themes`, `set-hook` or\n  `bind-key`\n\n## Which surface is which worker\n\n`ListAgents` names a session; cmux needs a surface. Claude Code keeps one record per process\nunder `~/.claude/sessions/`, and the lines below print one row per record, tab-separated:","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

bool {\n        self == Tracking::Commit\n    }\n}\n\n/// 에이전트에게 moai 를 어떻게 알리는가(moai-cbfz). `--guide` 의 값도 [`Tracking`] 처럼 clap 이 푼다.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, ValueEnum)]\npub enum Guide {\n    /// AGENTS.md 에 안내 전문을 블록으로 쓴다 — 지금까지의 `init` 이다.\n/// 고른 값과 기본값으로 계획을 낸다. 머리글의 차례(추적 → 안내 → 설치 → 드라이버)로 적는다 — 앞 칸을\n/// 먼저 정하고, 뒤 칸은 이미 정한 앞 칸만 읽는다.\npub fn resolve(c: &Choices, d: &Defaults) -> Plan {\n    let tracking = c.tracking.unwrap_or(d.tracking);\n    let guide = c.guide.unwrap_or(if tracking.tracked() { d.guide_tracked } else { d.guide_local });\n    // 훅으로 알리면 훅이 깔려야 한다 — 설치를 켠다. 끄는 플래그와 부딪히면 [`conflict`] 가 잡는다.\n    let skill = guide == Guide::Hook || c.skill.unwrap_or(d.skill);\n    // 추적하지 않으면 머지 드라이버는 할 일이 없다 — git 이 그 파일을 병합할 일이 없다. 고른 값은 두고 끈다.\n    let driver = tracking.tracked() && c.driver.unwrap_or(d.driver);\n    let project = c.project.unwrap_or(d.project);\n    // 선택 스킬은 설치 칸만 읽는다 — 설치를 안 하면 건넬 것이 없다.\n    let (mut with, mut without) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());\n    for (i, o) in OPTIONAL.iter().enumerate().filter(|_| skill) {\n        match (c.optional[i], d.optional[i]) {\n            (Some(true), _) | (None, Some(true)) => with.push(o.name),\n            (Some(false), Some(true)) => without.push(o.name),\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n    Plan { prefix: c.prefix.clone(), tracking, guide, skill, driver, project, with, without }\n}\n\n/// 플래그로 준 것이 계획과 부딪히는가 — 뒤 칸에 준 플래그가 앞 칸이 정한 것을 뒤집으려 할 때다. 화면은 그 칸을\n/// 잠가 못 고르게 하지만 플래그는 이미 와 있다. **조용히 한쪽을 이기게 하지 않는다**: 부르는 쪽이 거절한다.\npub fn conflict(fixed: &Choices, plan: &Plan) -> Option<Conflict> {\n    if fixed.skill == Some(false) && plan.guide == Guide::Hook {\n        Some(Conflict::HookWithoutSkill)\n    } else if fixed.driver == Some(true) && !plan.tracking.tracked() {\n        Some(Conflict::DriverWithoutTracking)\n    } else {\n        None\n    }\n}\n\n/// [`conflict`] 의 갈래.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum {\n        controlCommandCoordinator.resolveRef(handle)\n    }\n\n    nonisolated func v2Ref(kind: ControlHandleKind, uuid: UUID?) -> Any {\n        guard let uuid else { return NSNull() }\n        return v2MainSync { v2EnsureHandleRef(kind: kind, uuid: uuid) }\n    }\n\n    func v2WorkspaceRefs(for ids: [UUID]) -> [UUID: String] {\n        var refs: [UUID: String] = [:]\n        refs.reserveCapacity(ids.count)\n        for id in ids {\n            refs[id] = v2EnsureHandleRef(kind: .workspace, uuid: id)\n        }\n        return refs\n    }\n\n    func v2WorkspacePaneAndSurfaceRefs(\n        workspaceId: UUID,\n        paneId: UUID?,\n        surfaceId: UUID\n    ) -> (workspaceRef: String, paneRef: String?, surfaceRef: String) {\n        return (\n            workspaceRef: v2EnsureHandleRef(kind: .workspace, uuid: workspaceId),\n            paneRef: paneId.map { v2EnsureHandleRef(kind: .pane, uuid: $0) },\n            surfaceRef: v2EnsureHandleRef(kind: .surface, uuid: surfaceId)\n        )\n    }\n\n    func v2TabRef(uuid: UUID?) -> Any {\n        guard let uuid else { return NSNull() }\n        let surfaceRef = v2EnsureHandleRef(kind: .surface, uuid: uuid)\n        return surfaceRef.replacingOccurrences(of: \"surface:\", with: \"tab:\")\n    }\n\n    // Internal (not private): the `controlResolveOnMain` seam conformance in\n    // TerminalControllerControlCommandContext.swift runs this refresh inside\n    // the worker-lane resolution hop, mirroring the main-lane dispatch\n    // preamble.\n    func v2RefreshKnownRefs() {\n        guard let app = AppDelegate.shared else { return }\n\n        // #2751: skip the pre-mint pass until session restore has settled.\n        // Refreshing here is only an optimization (refs otherwise mint lazily\n        // on the first list/create); iterating the half-built window/tab tree\n        // while restore is pending or in flight faults (EXC_BAD_ACCESS / arm64e\n        // ptrauth). A v2 socket command arriving within ~1s of launch can\n        // re-enter this on the main actor mid-restore, so degrade gracefully.\n        guard app.didCompleteInitialSessionRestore else { return }\n\n        let windows = app.listMainWindowSummaries()\n        for item in windows {\n            _ = v2EnsureHandleRef(kind: .window, uuid: item.windowId)\n            if let tm = app.tabManagerFor(windowId: item.windowId) {\n                for ws in tm.tabs {\n                    _ = v2EnsureHandleRef(kind: .workspace, uuid: ws.id)\n                    v2RefreshRemoteTmuxAwarePaneAndSurfaceRefs(workspace: ws)\n                }\n                // Mint workspace_group refs for groups that exist before any\n                // workspace.group.* call so callers can pass `workspace_group:N`\n                // immediately after restore (otherwise the first ref hand-off\n                // happens only on `list`/`create`).\n                for group in tm.workspaceGroups {\n                    _ = v2EnsureHandleRef(kind: .workspaceGroup, uuid: group.id)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        controlCommandCoordinator.markHandleTopologyRefreshCompleted()\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - V2 Context Resolution\n\n    nonisolated func v2ResolveTabManager(params: [String: Any]) -> TabManager? {\n        // Prefer explicit window_id routing. {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"cat /Applications/cmux.app/Contents/Resources/shell-integration/.zshenv | head -80","description":"Read cmux's injected .zshenv loader"},"toolOutput":"# vim:ft=zsh\n#\n# cmux ZDOTDIR bootstrap for zsh.\n#\n# GhosttyKit already uses a ZDOTDIR injection mechanism for zsh (setting ZDOTDIR\n# to Ghostty's integration dir). cmux also needs to run its integration, but\n# we must restore the user's real ZDOTDIR immediately so that:\n# - /etc/zshrc sets HISTFILE relative to the real ZDOTDIR/HOME (shared history)\n# - zsh loads the user's real .zprofile/.zshrc normally (no wrapper recursion)\n#\n# We restore ZDOTDIR from (in priority order):\n# - GHOSTTY_ZSH_ZDOTDIR (set by GhosttyKit when it overwrote ZDOTDIR)\n# - CMUX_ZSH_ZDOTDIR (set by cmux when it overwrote a user-provided ZDOTDIR)\n# - unset (zsh treats unset ZDOTDIR as $HOME)\n\nif [[ -n \"${GHOSTTY_ZSH_ZDOTDIR+X}\" ]]; then\n    builtin export ZDOTDIR=\"$GHOSTTY_ZSH_ZDOTDIR\"\n    builtin unset GHOSTTY_ZSH_ZDOTDIR\nelif [[ -n \"${CMUX_ZSH_ZDOTDIR+X}\" ]]; then\n    builtin export ZDOTDIR=\"$CMUX_ZSH_ZDOTDIR\"\n    builtin unset CMUX_ZSH_ZDOTDIR\nelse\n    builtin unset ZDOTDIR\nfi\n\n{\n    # zsh treats unset ZDOTDIR as if it were HOME. We do the same.\n    builtin typeset _cmux_file=\"${ZDOTDIR-$HOME}/.zshenv\"\n    [[ ! -r \"$_cmux_file\" ]] || builtin source -- \"$_cmux_file\"\n\n    if [[ -o interactive \\\n       && -z \"${ZSH_EXECUTION_STRING:-}\" \\\n       && \"${CMUX_SHELL_INTEGRATION:-1}\" != \"0\" \\\n       && -n \"${CMUX_SHELL_INTEGRATION_DIR:-}\" \\\n       && -r \"${CMUX_SHELL_INTEGRATION_DIR}/cmux-zsh-integration.zsh\" \\\n       && \"${TERM:-}\" == \"xterm-256color\" \\\n       && -z \"${CMUX_ZSH_RESTORE_TERM:-}\" ]]; then\n        # Keep startup TERM-compatible prompt/theme selection during shell init,\n        # then restore the managed xterm-256color identity before the first\n        # interactive command executes.\n        builtin export CMUX_ZSH_RESTORE_TERM=\"$TERM\"\n        builtin export TERM=\"xterm-ghostty\"\n    fi\n} always {\n    if [[ -o interactive ]]; then\n        # We overwrote GhosttyKit's injected ZDOTDIR, so manually load Ghostty's\n        # zsh integration if available.\n        #\n        # We can't rely on GHOSTTY_ZSH_ZDOTDIR here because Ghostty's own zsh\n        # bootstrap unsets it before chaining into this cmux wrapper.\n        if [[ \"${CMUX_LOAD_GHOSTTY_ZSH_INTEGRATION:-0}\" == \"1\" ]]; then\n            if [[ -n \"${CMUX_SHELL_INTEGRATION_DIR:-}\" ]]; then\n                builtin typeset _cmux_ghostty=\"$CMUX_SHELL_INTEGRATION_DIR/ghostty-integration.zsh\"\n            fi\n            if [[ ! -r \"${_cmux_ghostty:-}\" && -n \"${GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR:-}\" ]]; then\n                builtin typeset _cmux_ghostty=\"$GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR/shell-integration/zsh/ghostty-integration\"\n            fi\n            [[ -r \"$_cmux_ghostty\" ]] && builtin source -- \"$_cmux_ghostty\"\n        fi\n\n        # Load cmux integration (unless disabled)\n        if [[ \"${CMUX_SHELL_INTEGRATION:-1}\" != \"0\" && -n \"${CMUX_SHELL_INTEGRATION_DIR:-}\" ]]; then\n            builtin typeset _cmux_integ=\"$CMUX_SHELL_INTEGRATION_DIR/cmux-zsh-integration.zsh\"\n            [[ -r \"$_cmux_integ\" ]] && builtin source -- \"$_cmux_integ\"\n        fi\n    fi\n\n    builtin unset _cmux_file _cmux_ghostty _cmux_integ\n}","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"cat"}}
