Defaults follow the\n/// debounce shape proven by community prior art (manaflow-ai/cmux#2043)\n/// and are expected to be tuned from dogfood feedback.\nstruct AutoNamingConfig: Sendable {\n    /// Minimum transcript line growth since the last naming before another\n    /// summarization call is considered.\n    var minLineGrowth: Int = 6\n    /// Minimum seconds between summarization calls for one session.\n    var minInterval: TimeInterval = 180\n    /// Transcripts shorter than this are skipped entirely (subagent or\n    /// trivial sessions).\n    var minTranscriptLines: Int = 12\n    /// Hard deadline for the summarizer subprocess.\n    var llmTimeout: TimeInterval = 60\n    /// Extra slack on top of `llmTimeout` before an in-flight marker is\n    /// considered stale: covers the termination grace window and the socket\n    /// apply, so a pass still finishing cannot be doubled by a concurrent\n    /// Stop, while a crashed pass cannot block naming forever.\n    var inFlightExpiryGrace: TimeInterval = 15\n\n    /// Total lifetime of an in-flight marker before a new pass may start.\n    var inFlightExpiry: TimeInterval { llmTimeout + inFlightExpiryGrace }\n    /// Maximum title length after sanitization.\n    var maxTitleLength: Int = 50\n    /// Leading user messages included in the summarization context.\n    var contextHeadUserMessages: Int = 2\n    /// Trailing user/assistant messages included in the context.\n    var contextTailMessages: Int = 4\n    /// Per-message truncation applied to context excerpts.\n    var contextMessageMaxChars: Int = 240\n}\n\n/// Projection of one session's persisted auto-naming state, read from the\n/// agent hook session store under its lock.\nstruct AutoNamingSessionSnapshot: Sendable {\n    var lastTitle: String?\n    var lastLineCount: Int?\n    var lastNamedAt: TimeInterval?\n    var inFlightAt: TimeInterval?\n    /// Last attempt time, success or failure (see the record field of the same\n    /// purpose). Drives the failure cooldown in ``throttleDecision``.\n    var lastAttemptAt: TimeInterval?\n\n    init(\n        lastTitle: String? = nil,\n        lastLineCount: Int? = nil,\n        lastNamedAt: TimeInterval? = nil,\n        inFlightAt: TimeInterval? = nil,\n        lastAttemptAt: TimeInterval? = nil\n    ) {\n        self.lastTitle = lastTitle\n        self.lastLineCount = lastLineCount\n        self.lastNamedAt = lastNamedAt\n        self.inFlightAt = inFlightAt\n        self.lastAttemptAt = lastAttemptAt\n    }\n}\n\n/// Outcome of the throttle evaluation that gates a summarization call.\nenum AutoNamingThrottleDecision: Equatable, Sendable {\n    /// Run the summarizer; on success the baseline advances to this count.\n    case proceed(baseline: Int)\n    /// The transcript shrank (compaction or resume rewrite): record the new\n    /// baseline without naming so future growth measures from it.\n    case reseedBaseline(to: Int)\n    case skipShortTranscript\n    case skipInFlight\n    case skipTooSoon\n    case skipInsufficientGrowth\n}","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"cd"}}

When an existing owner records its normal\nlifecycle change, that ordinary CMUX projection reflects it. The execution\ntransport, machine placement, physical attempt, and recovery truth remain with\ntheir existing owners rather than being duplicated into a second CMUX ledger.\n\n## Draft Guard\n\nBefore writing, `send`, `send-panel` and `paste` (and `send --paste`) ask the\napp for `surface.input_state` and refuse when an agent's prompt holds text\nsomeone is typing, or when a question or permission dialog is open in an\nagent. `send-key` and `send-key-panel`, and `send` of text that only presses\nEnter, refuse only for an open dialog: `cmux send \"text\"` followed by\n`cmux send-key enter` leaves the sent text in the prompt, and the key has to\ngo through. Surfaces without an agent are never blocked. A refusal writes nothing, prints the reason on stderr\nand exits non-zero. `--force`, before the text or key, skips the check. When\nthe app can't answer `surface.input_state` (an older build, or a `cmux ssh`\nrelay, which doesn't forward it) the commands write as before.\n\n`surface.input_state` is a v2 worker-lane socket method. It takes\n`surface_id`, or the usual workspace selectors for that workspace's focused\nsurface, and returns:\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| `state` | `empty`, `draft`, `dialog`, or `unknown` when no agent prompt is on screen. Read from the active screen (not the scrolled viewport): Claude Code's and Codex's input rows, ignoring faint placeholder text, and key hints such as \"Esc to cancel\" below the input row. |\n| `draft_length` | Characters in the draft, when `state` is `draft`. The text itself is not returned. |\n| `agent` | Whether an agent reports lifecycle state for the surface. |\n| `lifecycle` | The agent's lifecycle: `unknown`, `running`, `idle` or `needsInput`. |\n| `waiting_on_human` | `lifecycle` is `needsInput`. Informational: it can stay set after an interrupt or an API error, so it does not block on its own. |\n| `blocks_typing` | Typing text now could disturb a human: a draft or a dialog, on a surface that runs an agent. |\n| `terminal` | Whether the surface is a terminal. |\n\n191:| `paste` | Paste text from an argument or stdin into a terminal surface through the Cmd+V paste path (`terminal.paste`). The CLI sends the text unchanged; Ghostty brackets it when the program enabled bracketed paste (otherwise newlines become Enter) and replaces unsafe control bytes with spaces. `--submit` presses the agent-aware submit key afterwards. Refuses to paste over an agent prompt draft or into an open dialog unless `--force`. Authenticated remote-workspace relays may use `terminal.paste` only with an exact owned workspace/surface and `submit_key` `none` or `return`; the relay cannot use window/focus fallback selectors or arbitrary submit keys. |","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"SCRATCH=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-raven-Works-Projects2-moai/fa832c96-fa4b-42be-96a4-d574a5501beb/scratchpad;"}}

comes from stdin (no positional\n        /// text, or a lone `-` before any `--` separator).\n        var text: String?\n    }\n\n    func parsePasteCommandArguments(_ commandArgs: [String]) throws -> PasteCommandArguments {\n        let (workspace, rem0) = parseOption(commandArgs, name: \"--workspace\")\n        let (surface, rem1) = parseOption(rem0, name: \"--surface\")\n        let (window, readsStandardInput = false\n        var pastTerminator = false\n        for arg in rem2 {\n            if pastTerminator {\n                positional.append(arg)\n                continue\n            }\n            switch arg {\n            case \"--\":\n                pastTerminator = true\n            case \"--submit\":\n                parsed.submit = true\n            case \"--force\":\n                parsed.force = true\n            case \"-\":\n                readsStandardInput = true\n            default:\n                // Everything here lands in an agent prompt, so a mistyped String) == \"queued\" else { return summary }\n        let suffix = String(\n            localized: \"cli.send.queuedSuffix\",\n            defaultValue: \"queued (terminal starting; input will be sent when its PTY is ready)\"\n        )\n        return \"\\(summary) \\(suffix)\"\n    }\n\n    private static var pasteMissingTextMessage: String {\n        String(\n            localized: \"cli.paste.error.missingText\",\n            defaultValue: \"paste requires text as an argument or on stdin\"\n        )\n    }\n\n    private func pasteTextFromStandardInput() throws -> String {\n        switch CLIStandardInputText.shared.read() {\n        case .success(let text):\n            return text\n        case .failure(.interactive):\n            // An interactive stdin with no text argument is almost always a\n            // mistake; fail instead of silently waiting for EOF.\n            throw CLIError(message: Self.pasteMissingTextMessage)","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"cd"}}

2] = [\n    Optional { name: \"moai-tmux\", sign: |var| var == \"TMUX\" },\n    Optional { name: \"moai-cmux\", sign: |var| var == \"CMUX_SURFACE_ID\" },\n];\n\n/// 고를 수 있는 스킬 하나 — 이름과 표식.\npub struct Optional {\n    pub name: &'static str,\n    /// 그 스킬을 쓰는 사람이라는 환경 변수의 이름인가 — 그 이름의 변수가 **비지 않게** 하나라도 서면 쓰는 사람이다\n    /// ([`detected`]). tmux 는 제 안에서 도는 셸에 `$TMUX` 를 세운다.\n    pub sign: fn(&str) -> bool,\n}\n\n/// `name` 이 고를 수 있는 스킬인가([`OPTIONAL`]).\npub fn is_optional(name: &str) -> bool {\n    OPTIONAL.iter().any(|o| o.name == name)\n}\n\n/// 고를 수 있는 스킬의 이름 — [`OPTIONAL`] 의 차례로.\npub fn optional_names() -> impl Iterator<Item = &'static str> {\n    OPTIONAL.iter().map(|o| o.name)\n}\n\n/// 환경 `vars` 가 쓰는 사람이라고 이르는 선택 스킬 — [`OPTIONAL`] 의 차례로. **환경을 받기만 한다** — 이 모듈은 글만\n/// 짓고, 환경을 읽는 것은 부르는 쪽이다(`init` 의 고르는 상자).\npub fn detected(vars: &[(String, String)]) -> Vec<&'static str> {\n    detected_in(&OPTIONAL, vars)\n}\n\n/// [`detected`] 의 몸통 — 목록을 받아, 아직 목록에 없는 꼴의 표식(머리로 재는 cmux)도 시험이 잰다.\nfn detected_in(list: &[Optional], vars: &[(String, String)]) -> Vec<&'static str> {\n    list.iter().filter(|o| vars.iter().any(|(k, v)| (o.sign)(k) && !v.is_empty())).map(|o| o.name).collect()\n}\n\n/// 이번에 심을 선택 스킬 — **(지금 심긴 것 ∪ `with`) − `without`**, [`OPTIONAL`] 의 차례로(moai-3r7l). 맨 `install` 은 둘이\n/// 비어 심긴 것만 다시 심고 새것은 안 심는다. 처음 심는 저장소는 심긴 것이 없어 하나도 안 심는다.\npub fn kept(planted: &[&str], with: &[&str], without: &[&str]) -> Vec<&'static str> {\n    optional_names().filter(|n| (planted.contains(n) || with.contains(n)) && !without.contains(n)).collect()\n}\n\n/// `--with`·`--without` 에 준 이름이 안 서는 까닭 — 처음 걸린 이름 하나로 댄다.\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]\npub enum Misnamed<'a> {","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

The execution\ntransport, machine placement, physical attempt, and recovery truth remain with\ntheir existing owners rather than being duplicated into a second CMUX ledger.\n\n## Draft Guard\n\nBefore writing, `send`, `send-panel` and `paste` (and `send --paste`) ask the\napp for `surface.input_state` and refuse when an agent's prompt holds text\nsomeone is typing, or when a question or permission dialog is open in an\nagent. `send-key` and `send-key-panel`, and `send` of text that only presses\nEnter, refuse only for an open dialog: `cmux send \"text\"` followed by\n`cmux send-key enter` leaves the sent text in the prompt, and the key has to\ngo through. Surfaces without an agent are never blocked. A refusal writes nothing, prints the reason on stderr\nand exits non-zero. `--force`, before the text or key, skips the check. When\nthe app can't answer `surface.input_state` (an older build, or a `cmux ssh`\nrelay, which doesn't forward it) the commands write as before.\n\n`surface.input_state` is a v2 worker-lane socket method. It takes\n`surface_id`, or the usual workspace selectors for that workspace's focused\nsurface, and returns:\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| `state` | `empty`, `draft`, `dialog`, or `unknown` when no agent prompt is on screen. Read from the active screen (not the scrolled viewport): Claude Code's and Codex's input rows, ignoring faint placeholder text, and key hints such as \"Esc to cancel\" below the input row. |\n| `draft_length` | Characters in the draft, when `state` is `draft`. The text itself is not returned. |\n| `agent` | Whether an agent reports lifecycle state for the surface. |\n| `lifecycle` | The agent's lifecycle: `unknown`, `running`, `idle` or `needsInput`. |\n| `waiting_on_human` | `lifecycle` is `needsInput`. Informational: it can stay set after an interrupt or an API error, so it does not block on its own. |\n| `blocks_typing` | Typing text now could disturb a human: a draft or a dialog, on a surface that runs an agent. |\n| `terminal` | Whether the surface is a terminal. |\n\n## Surface Selection Contract\n\n`surface.read_selection` is a v2 worker-lane socket method advertised by\n`system.capabilities` and printed by `cmux capabilities`. It accepts the usual\nsurface routing selectors (`window_id`, `workspace_id`, `surface_id`,\n`terminal_id`, `tab_id`, and `pane_id`) without focusing a window, workspace,\npane, or surface.\n\nSuccessful responses use one shape across surface kinds:\n\n191:| `paste` | Paste text from an argument or stdin into a terminal surface through the Cmd+V paste path (`terminal.paste`). The CLI sends the text unchanged; Ghostty brackets it when the program enabled bracketed paste (otherwise newlines become Enter) and replaces unsafe control bytes with spaces. `--submit` presses the agent-aware submit key afterwards. Refuses to paste over an agent prompt draft or into an open dialog unless `--force`. Authenticated remote-workspace relays may use `terminal.paste` only with an exact owned workspace/surface and `submit_key` `none` or `return`; the relay cannot use window/focus fallback selectors or arbitrary submit keys. |","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"cd"}}

A session a person opened reads that shape to choose its next row —\nthe moai binary never launches or drives a session itself. Only the supervisor skill, inside\ntmux or cmux, may clear a worker's pane, paste into it, or open one once the person says yes.\n\n**A key that cannot be absent is never absent.** `kind` and `priority` hold a default,\nassignment (`SendMessage`) with a line naming the file of the worker's steps to read, and\nthe worker reports the same way. moai carries no messaging, and the moai binary never\nlaunches or drives a session. When the supervisor runs inside tmux, its companion skill\n`moai-tmux` lets it clear a worker's pane, paste a message into it, and open new worker\npanes — an ordinary interactive `claude` the person sees, opened only after the person says\nyes. Inside cmux (0.65.0 or later) `moai-cmux` does the same with cmux's tabs. Each is planted\nonly where it is chosen: `moai skill install --with moai-tmux` plants it and `--without`\ntakes it out. Nothing runs headless. The supervisor picks, sends and checks; it does not fix and it\ndoes not merge.\n\n### The wiki\nit stands only where it was chosen (`moai skill install --with moai-tmux`, or its row in `moai\ninit`). Inside tmux without it, tell the person that one line plants it, and carry on as if\noutside tmux.\n\n**Inside cmux, load `moai-cmux` instead.** When `CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set in your shell and\n`$TMUX` is not, `moai-cmux` gives you the same hands on the workers' cmux tabs, at the same\nfive points, and reads the same session map. It needs cmux 0.65.0 or later and says so itself.\nWhen both are set you run in tmux inside a cmux tab — what you type goes to tmux, so it is\n`moai-tmux`. **With neither, nothing of either applies.** `moai-cmux` is optional the same\nway (`moai skill install --with moai-cmux`); inside cmux without it, tell the person that one\nline plants it, and carry on as if outside cmux.\n\n**When sessions died** — a restart or an OOM kill took the workers or a supervisor down —\n  sent to is gone from `ListAgents` with its report unchecked, a name you have not sent to\n  may be that worker — ask the person before sending to it\n- **If no row is left, nobody is free here.** Tell the person, and stop — do not send to a\n  session of another repository. Inside tmux, ask the person first whether to open new worker\n  panes (`moai-tmux`, \"No idle worker left\"); inside cmux, whether to open new worker tabs\n  (`moai-cmux`, \"No idle worker left\"). On a no, stop\n- **A worker that refused the work comes out of the candidates and is not sent to\nanswers it, or `permissions.additionalDirectories` in their settings holding that plugin\ndirectory lets it through. The settings are theirs — do not write them.\nInside tmux, label the worker's pane as you send and, if the message does not arrive, deliver\nit into the pane — `moai-tmux`, \"Label the pane\" and \"When a message does not arrive\".\nInside cmux, label the worker's tab as you send and, if the message does not arrive, deliver it\ninto the tab — `moai-cmux`, \"Label the tab\" and \"When a message does not arrive\".\nFill in `<id>`, `<title>`, `<steps file>`, `<root branch>`, `<base branch>`, `<milestone>`, `<model>`, `<difficulty>`, `<why>`, `<other work>`, `<root>`, `<person>` and — only for a subdirectory project — `<subdir>`.\n`notify_when_idle` sends is not a report: a worker goes idle whenever its turn ends — while\nit waits on its person's answer, say — and one that asked its person something sends nothing\nuntil it is answered. **Do not poll `ListAgents`** — the report comes to you. Inside tmux, an\nidle notice with no report is the moment to read that worker's pane once (`moai-tmux`, \"When a\nworker stalls\") and tell the person what it shows — inside cmux, its tab (`moai-cmux`, \"When a\nworker stalls\").\n\n    moai note <epic> 'Report-checked: <merge hash>'\n\nThen send the next backlog to an idle worker. **Outside tmux and cmux, clearing a window is\nthe person's** — the supervisor never types into a window. Shell stays after command exits.\n- cmux send [--surface] [--paste] [--force] -- <text>   (\\n \\r = Enter, \\t Tab; keystrokes)\n- cmux send-key [--surface] [--force] -- <key>  (enter, escape, ctrl+c, ctrl+u ...)\n- cmux paste [--surface] [--submit] [--force] [-- text | -]  (stdin with -, bracketed, 15MiB, --submit presses return)\n- Draft guard: send/paste refuse (non-zero, nothing written) when Claude input row holds a human draft or a dialog is open; send-key refuses on dialog only; --force skips. NEVER pass --force.\n- cmux rpc surface.input_state '{\"surface_id\":\"<uuid>\"}' -> state empty|draft|dialog|unknown, lifecycle running|idle|needsInput, waiting_on_human, blocks_typing\n- cmux read-screen --surface <id> [--lines N]  (alias capture-pane)\n- cmux rename-tab --surface <id> --title '<t>' ; rename-workspace ; set-description\n- cmux notify --title ... ; trigger-flash --surface\n- equalize: cmux rpc workspace.equalize_splits '{\"workspace_id\":\"<uuid>\",\"orientation\":\"vertical\"}' (no CLI verb)\n- close-surface (--force kills) — never\n- focus-* change what user sees — never unless asked\n- cmux agent message <surface> [--from name] -- <text|-> : delivers via Claude hooks (32KiB) no typing; needs cmux Claude integration\nSocket: default mode cmuxOnly admits processes descending from cmux (a supervisor inside a pane is fine).\n\n... The workers merge. Overlapping\nmerges are prevented by splitting the files when the supervisor sends (1), and where\nthey still collide the worker goes back into its worktree and resolves them.\n\n**This skill is for Claude Code, and moai carries no messaging.** The supervisor and its\nworkers talk with Claude Code's own tools:\n\n- `ListAgents` lists the live sessions, and subagents too — each row's name, its kind\n  (`interactive`, `bg`), whether it is busy or idle, and its tmux pane if it has one\n- `SendMessage(to: <name>, message: …)` sends to one session. With `notify_when_idle: true`\n  you also get one notice when that session goes idle; leave `message` out and it only\n  subscribes\n- A reply comes in as a cross-session message. Answer it by copying its `from` as `to`\n\n**Every session here is an interactive one the person can see.** The moai binary never\nlaunches or drives an agent, and nothing here runs headless. Outside tmux the supervisor\nlaunches nothing either; inside tmux or cmux it may open a worker pane, only after the person\nsays yes (`moai-tmux` or `moai-cmux`, below). **A worker is every idle session of this\nrepository in `ListAgents`, except you** — a row whose name starts with the root\ndirectory's slug and a `-` (2). Nobody registers and nobody is asked which windows count.\nThe message you send is the whole assignment, and it names the file of the worker's steps,\nwhich the worker reads (3).\n\n**One supervisor per repository.** A supervisor waiting for reports reads `idle` in\n`ListAgents` like any worker, so a second one sends it backlog, and the two keep separate\nbooks of what was sent — one backlog, or one worker, gets two jobs. Before the first round,\nask the person whether another window here runs `moai-supervise`; if one does, stop. A\nsession that refuses work because it is a supervisor comes out of the candidates. **You\nrefuse too:** a message that hands you backlog to work on came from another supervisor — do\nnothing of it, reply to its `from` that you are a supervisor, and tell the person.\n\nFive things about the messaging, one line each:\n\n- A session in a different permission mode holds an incoming message for its person's\n  approval — a worker that stays idle after you sent may be waiting on that\n- `notify_when_idle` answers only for a session on this machine — one reason a worker is a\n  session on this machine (2)\n- A subagent sends under its parent session's address — a message can come from a session\n  that did not write it itself\n- `@path` in a message attaches nothing — a file the worker has to read is named by its\n  absolute path, and the worker reads it itself (3)\n- Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop — the report comes to you (4)\n\n**Inside tmux, load `moai-tmux` too.** When `$TMUX` is set in your shell, the skill\n`moai-tmux` gives you hands on the workers' panes, at five points of the round: offer new\nworker panes when no worker is idle (2), label the pane you send to and deliver a message\n`SendMessage` could not (3), read a stalled worker's pane (4), and clear a reported worker's\nwindow before its next work (5). It finds each worker's pane from its `ListAgents` name, and\nnever types into a box that holds anything. **Without `$TMUX` nothing of it applies** — every\nstep below goes through messages and the person, as written. `moai-tmux` is an optional skill:\nit stands only where it was chosen (`moai skill install --with moai-tmux`, or its row in `moai\ninit`). Inside tmux without it, tell the person that one line plants it, and carry on as if\noutside tmux.\n\n**Inside cmux, load `moai-cmux` instead.** When `CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set in your shell and\n`$TMUX` is not, `moai-cmux` gives you the same hands on the workers' cmux tabs, at the same\nfive points, and reads the same session map. It needs cmux 0.65.0 or later and says so itself.\nWhen both are set you run in tmux inside a cmux tab — what you type goes to tmux, so it is\n`moai-tmux`. **With neither, nothing of either applies.** `moai-cmux` is optional the same\nway (`moai skill install --with moai-cmux`); inside cmux without it, tell the person that one\nline plants it, and carry on as if outside cmux.\n\n**When sessions died** — a restart or an OOM kill took the workers or a supervisor down —\nand the person asks to bring them back, load `moai-recover`, inside tmux or not.\n\n**Work you send out is always done in a worktree** — even if the repository has no\nworktree convention. Several workers share one root checkout, so fixing things in the\nroot mixes their edits and commits together. Worktrees stand in\n`<root>/.worktrees/`, and `moai init` writes that path into the gitignore.","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

resourcesByPID[pid] : process\n            // A process that exited after the listing is absent, not unreadable:\n            // only a live process we failed to read leaves the census incomplete.\n            // A reused PID is still live and still counts as missing.\n            guard let resources else {\n                if !reader.processHasExited(pid: pid) { missingCount += 1 }\n                continue\n            }\n            let key = CmuxTopProcessSnapshot.scopeCacheKey(from: bsd)\n            guard !readsIdentitySensitiveData || reader.matches(pid: pid, key: key) else {\n                if !reader.processHasExited(pid: pid) { missingCount += 1 }\n                continue\n            }\n            let name = missing.contains(.details)\n                ? reader.processName(pid: pid, fallback: process.name) : process.name\n            let path = missing.contains(.details) ? reader.processPath(pid: pid) : process.path\n            let scope = missing.contains(.scope) ? reader.scope(for: pid, key: key) : nil\n            guard !readsIdentitySensitiveData || reader.matches(pid: pid, key: key) else {\n                if !reader.processHasExited(pid: pid) { missingCount += 1 }\n                continue\n            }\n            records.append(CmuxTopProcessInfo(\n                pid: pid, processIdentity: process.processIdentity,\n                parentPID: process.parentPID, name: name, path: path,\n                ttyDevice: process.ttyDevice,\n                cmuxWorkspaceID: missing.contains(.scope) ? scope?.workspaceID : process.cmuxWorkspaceID,\n                cmuxSurfaceID: missing.contains(.scope) ? scope?.surfaceID : process.cmuxSurfaceID,\n                cmuxAttributionReason: missing.contains(.scope) ? scope?.attributionReason : process.cmuxAttributionReason,\n                processGroupID: process.processGroupID, terminalProcessGroupID: process.terminalProcessGroupID,\n                cpuPercent: resources.cpuPercent, memoryBytes: resources.memoryBytes, memorySource: resources.memorySource,\n                residentBytes: resources.residentBytes, residentMemorySource: resources.residentMemorySource,\n                virtualBytes: resources.virtualBytes, threadCount: resources.threadCount\n            ))\n        }\n        let combined = capture.fields.union(missing)\n        let snapshot = CmuxTopProcessSnapshot(\n            processes: records, sampledAt: capture.snapshot.sampledAt,\n            includesProcessDetails: combined.contains(.details), includesCMUXScope: combined.contains(.scope),\n            includesResources: combined.contains(.resources),\n            enumerationIsComplete: capture.snapshot.enumerationIsComplete && missingCount == 0,\n            enumerationMissingProcessCount: missingCount\n        )\n        return CmuxTopProcessCapture(listing: capture.listing, snapshot: snapshot, fields: combined)\n    }\n}","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"cd"}}

[`Scratch::fenced`] 는 그래서 남는다 — **자리를 고르는 시험**(`layer`·`worktree`·`git`)이 제\n//! 자리를 저장소 꼭대기로 세울 때 쓴다. 울타리는 자리째 `Drop` 이 치운다 — 체크아웃 안에 커밋\n//! 없는 저장소가 남으면 그 체크아웃의 `git add -A` 가 거기서 멈춘다([`fence`]).\n\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\n/// 시험 하나가 쓰는 디렉터리. 놓을 때 지운다.\n///\n/// 이름에 pid·스레드·셈을 함께 넣는다 — pid 만으로는 한 판 안의 스레드 둘이 같은 자리를\n/// 잡고, 한쪽의 `Drop` 이 다른 쪽이 쓰는 자리를 지운다.\npub struct Scratch(PathBuf);\n\nimpl Scratch {\n    /// `<자리>/moai-<이름>-<pid>-<스레드>-<셈>` 을 만든다. 이미 있으면 지우고 새로 만든다.\n    ///\n    /// **울타리는 없다.** [`base`] 가 체크아웃 밖임을 보장하므로 위에 잡힐 `.git` 도 `.moai` 도\n    /// 없다(moai-izeo). 울타리를 골라 치던 자리다 — 그것은 `.git` 훑기만 세웠고, `.moai` 를\n    /// 찾아 오르는 쪽은 그대로 바깥 트래커를 잡았다.\n    pub fn new(name: &str) -> Scratch {\n        Scratch::in_place(&base(), name)\n    }\n\n    /// 자리를 받아 세운다. 이름 짓는 법은 [`Scratch::new`] 와 같다. 울타리는 없다 —\n    /// [`Scratch::fenced_in`] 이 이것 위에 세우고, 울타리가 실제로 일하는지 견주는\n    /// 시험이 대조군으로 쓴다.\n    pub fn in_place(base: &Path, name: &str) -> Scratch {\n        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, Ordering};\n        static NTH: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);\n        let dir = base.join(format!(\n            \"moai-{name}-{}-{:?}-{}\",\n            std::process::id(),\n            std::thread::current().id(),\n            NTH.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed),","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"cd"}}

Parameters:\n        ///   - jsonOutput: Whether JSON output was requested.\n        ///   - idFormat: The optional identifier format.\n        ///   - remaining: Arguments that are not presentation options.\n        public init(jsonOutput: Bool, idFormat: String?, remaining: [String]) {\n            self.jsonOutput = jsonOutput\n            self.idFormat = idFormat\n            self.remaining = remaining\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Errors produced while parsing presentation options.\n    public enum ParseError: Error, Equatable, Sendable, CustomStringConvertible {\n        /// `--id-format` did not have a following value.\n        case missingIDFormatValue\n\n        /// A stable CLI-facing description for this parse failure.\n        public var description: String {\n            switch self {\n            case .missingIDFormatValue:\n                \"--id-format requires a value (refs|uuids|both)\"\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    private static let commandOptionsWithValues: Set<String> = [\n        \"--action\", \"--after-workspace\", \"--agent\", \"--amount\", \"--arch\",\n        \"--attr\", \"--before-workspace\", \"--body\", \"--color\", \"--command\",\n        \"--config\", \"--cwd\", \"--description\", \"--direction\", \"--domain\",\n        \"--dx\", \"--dy\", \"--email\", \"--event\", \"--expires\", \"--focus\",\n        \"--function\", \"--id\", \"--image\", \"--index\", \"--key\", \"--kind\",\n        \"--label\", \"--layout\", \"--lines\", \"--load-state\", \"--max-depth\", \"--name\", \"--os\",\n        \"--order\", \"--out\", \"--pane\", \"--panel\", \"--path\", \"--profile\", \"--property\",\n        \"--provider\", \"--relay-port\", \"--script\", \"--selector\", \"--session\",\n\n... [40 lines truncated] ...\n\n    /// - Returns: The presentation flags and the command arguments to forward.\n    /// - Throws: ``ParseError/missingIDFormatValue`` when `--id-format` has no value.\n    public func parse(_ commandArgs: [String]) throws -> Result {\n        var jsonOutput = false\n        var idFormat: String?\n        var remaining: [String] = []\n        var index = 0\n        var pastTerminator = false\n        while index < commandArgs.count {\n            let arg = commandArgs[index]\n            if pastTerminator {\n                remaining.append(arg)\n                index += 1\n                continue\n            }\n            if arg == \"--\" {\n                pastTerminator = true\n                remaining.append(arg)\n                index += 1\n                continue\n            }\n            if arg == \"--json\" {\n                jsonOutput = true\n                index += 1\n                continue\n            }\n            if arg == \"--id-format\" {\n                guard index + 1 < commandArgs.count else {\n                    throw ParseError.missingIDFormatValue\n                }\n                idFormat = commandArgs[index + 1]\n                index += 2\n                continue\n            }\n            if !arg.hasPrefix(\"-\") {\n                remaining.append(arg)\n                index += 1\n                continue\n            }\n            remaining.append(arg)\n            if Self.commandOptionsWithValues.contains(arg), index + 1 < commandArgs.count {\n                remaining.append(commandArgs[index + 1])\n                index += 2\n                continue\n            }\n            index += 1\n        }\n        return Result(jsonOutput: jsonOutput, idFormat: idFormat, remaining: remaining)\n    }\n}","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"cat"}}

Deleting the two keys from your\n  settings is `claude`'s job - we do not touch someone else's JSON, except\n  the old declarations below.\n\n  **`.claude/moai-plugin/` is not deleted.** Deleting a file a running\n  session holds can block that session's tool calls. That skill's\n  directory goes (only while it holds nothing but moai's files) and the\n  plugin is planted again; the registration and the other skills stay.\n  A tree moai has not planted is left alone - no file and no hooks file\n  is made there. The workers merge. Overlapping\nmerges are prevented by splitting the files when the supervisor sends (1), and where\nthey still collide the worker goes back into its worktree and resolves them.\n\n**This skill is for Claude Code, and moai carries no messaging.** The supervisor and its\nworkers talk with Claude Code's own tools:\n\n- `ListAgents` lists the live sessions, and subagents too — each row's name, its kind\n  (`interactive`, `bg`), whether it is busy or idle, and its tmux pane if it has one\n- `SendMessage(to: <name>, message: …)` sends to one session. With `notify_when_idle: true`\n  you also get one notice when that session goes idle; leave `message` out and it only\n  subscribes\n- A reply comes in as a cross-session message. Answer it by copying its `from` as `to`\n\n**Every session here is an interactive one the person can see.** The moai binary never\nlaunches or drives an agent, and nothing here runs headless. Outside tmux the supervisor\nlaunches nothing either; inside tmux or cmux it may open a worker pane, only after the person\nsays yes (`moai-tmux` or `moai-cmux`, below). **A worker is every idle session of this\nrepository in `ListAgents`, except you** — a row whose name starts with the root\ndirectory's slug and a `-` (2). Nobody registers and nobody is asked which windows count.\nThe message you send is the whole assignment, and it names the file of the worker's steps,\nwhich the worker reads (3).\n\n**One supervisor per repository.** A supervisor waiting for reports reads `idle` in\n`ListAgents` like any worker, so a second one sends it backlog, and the two keep separate\nbooks of what was sent — one backlog, or one worker, gets two jobs. Before the first round,\nask the person whether another window here runs `moai-supervise`; if one does, stop. A\nsession that refuses work because it is a supervisor comes out of the candidates. **You\nrefuse too:** a message that hands you backlog to work on came from another supervisor — do\nnothing of it, reply to its `from` that you are a supervisor, and tell the person.\n\nFive things about the messaging, one line each:\n\n- A session in a different permission mode holds an incoming message for its person's\n  approval — a worker that stays idle after you sent may be waiting on that\n- `notify_when_idle` answers only for a session on this machine — one reason a worker is a\n  session on this machine (2)\n- A subagent sends under its parent session's address — a message can come from a session\n  that did not write it itself\n- `@path` in a message attaches nothing — a file the worker has to read is named by its\n  absolute path, and the worker reads it itself (3)\n- Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop — the report comes to you (4)\n\n**Inside tmux, load `moai-tmux` too.** When `$TMUX` is set in your shell, the skill\n`moai-tmux` gives you hands on the workers' panes, at five points of the round: offer new\nworker panes when no worker is idle (2), label the pane you send to and deliver a message\n`SendMessage` could not (3), read a stalled worker's pane (4), and clear a reported worker's\nwindow before its next work (5). It finds each worker's pane from its `ListAgents` name, and\nnever types into a box that holds anything. **Without `$TMUX` nothing of it applies** — every\nstep below goes through messages and the person, as written. `moai-tmux` is an optional skill:\nit stands only where it was chosen (`moai skill install --with moai-tmux`, or its row in `moai\ninit`). Inside tmux without it, tell the person that one line plants it, and carry on as if\noutside tmux.\n\n**Inside cmux, load `moai-cmux` instead.** When `CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set in your shell and\n`$TMUX` is not, `moai-cmux` gives you the same hands on the workers' cmux tabs, at the same\nfive points, and reads the same session map. It needs cmux 0.65.0 or later and says so itself.\nWhen both are set you run in tmux inside a cmux tab — what you type goes to tmux, so it is\n`moai-tmux`. **With neither, nothing of either applies.** `moai-cmux` is optional the same\nway (`moai skill install --with moai-cmux`); inside cmux without it, tell the person that one\nline plants it, and carry on as if outside cmux.\n\n**When sessions died** — a restart or an OOM kill took the workers or a supervisor down —\nand the person asks to bring them back, load `moai-recover`, inside tmux or not.\n\n**Work you send out is always done in a worktree** — even if the repository has no\nworktree convention. Several workers share one root checkout, so fixing things in the\nroot mixes their edits and commits together. Worktrees stand in\n`<root>/.worktrees/`, and `moai init` writes that path into the gitignore.\n\n**Read the root branch once, at the start of the round.** Workers commit the tracker in\nthe root checkout and branch their worktrees from the local branches there, so that","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 60,175p /Users/raven/Works/Projects2/moai/.worktrees/moai-p5sz/CONTRIBUTING.md","description":"Read CONTRIBUTING.md commit and docs sections"},"toolOutput":"listed under `[lints.clippy]` in `Cargo.toml`, each with the reason it is there.\nAdd the reason when you add a line — an `allow` without one cannot be judged\nlater.\n\n`cargo fmt --all --check` runs in CI, before clippy and the tests. The width is\nset in `rustfmt.toml`, which also records why that value and not the default.\n\n**The toolchain is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`**, so rustup builds this\nrepository — and formats and lints it — with the version written there, and your\n`cargo fmt` gives what CI sees. Without the pin CI ran on whatever stable the\nrunner shipped that week, and rustfmt moving a line it has never touched turned\nsomeone else's pull request red. Bumping the pin is its own commit: change the\nchannel and carry the `cargo fmt --all` it causes in the same commit, never\nmixed with a change to the code. `rust-version` in `Cargo.toml` is a separate\nclaim, and the `msrv` job proves it: that job reads the line and builds the\ncrate with exactly that toolchain, so bumping the line moves what CI walks.\n\nThe whole repository was formatted in one commit. `git blame` can step over it\nso that it points at the commit that actually wrote each line, but git only\nreads that list from config, and config is not committed — so turn it on once\nper clone, the same as the `.moai` merge driver:\n\n```sh\ngit config blame.ignoreRevsFile .git-blame-ignore-revs\n```\n\nA clone that skips this is no worse off than before; `blame` just stops at the\nformatting commit.\n\n## If you change a command's help\n\n`docs/cli.md` is generated from `--help`, and a test compares the two. When you\nchange help text, or add or remove a command, regenerate and commit it:\n\n```sh\ncargo build --release && scripts/gen-cli-docs.sh\n```\n\nA reference written by hand drifts from the binary, and a reference that has\ndrifted is worse than none at all — a reader trusts it and types what it says.\nSo the words live in one place and that file is a copy of them.\n\n## What a change looks like\n\nWork is tracked in `.moai/issues.jsonl`, in this repository, with this tool.\nThese commands write to it, so they are for maintainers with push access — from\na fork, describe the issue in the pull request instead and a maintainer will\nfile it:\n\n```sh\n\n... [15 lines truncated] ...\n\n\n## Pull requests\n\n- Say what changed, why, and how you verified it.\n- Do not include changes to `.moai/` — that directory is this repository's own\n  tracker, and CI rejects external pull requests that touch it. Describe the\n  issue in the pull request instead and a maintainer will file it.\n- New commands are caught by the tests that sweep every command for `--json`\n  support, so add the command and let the test tell you what it wants.\n- **Open it against `develop`.** `main` takes no direct push and no pull request\n  from anywhere but `develop` — a ruleset holds the first, and a step in\n  `ci-gate` holds the second, because GitHub has no rule that pins the source\n  branch of a pull request. `main` carries one commit per release that way, and\n  its history reads as the distance between two releases.\n\n## Releasing\n\n```sh\ngit -C .worktrees/milestone-<id> merge --no-ff develop -m \"merge: take develop into milestone/<id>\"\ncargo test                                        # in .worktrees/milestone-<id>\ngit merge --no-ff milestone/<id> -m \"merge: <milestone title> (<id>)\"   # in the root, on develop\nmoai archive --dry-run                            # preview closed bundles eligible to move\nmoai archive                                      # refresh .moai/archive/<year>.jsonl\ngit add .moai/issues.jsonl .moai/archive\ngit commit -m \"chore(tracker): archive closed bundles\"\nscripts/bump-version.sh --next                    # prints 0.2.0 and why; writes nothing\nscripts/bump-version.sh auto                      # Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, CHANGELOG.md\ngit commit -m \"chore(release): 0.2.0\" -- Cargo.toml Cargo.lock CHANGELOG.md\ngit push origin develop\ngh pr create --base main --head develop --title \"v0.2.0\"   # merge it, no squash\ngit fetch origin && git tag v0.2.0 origin/main\ngit push origin v0.2.0\ngit worktree remove .worktrees/milestone-<id>     # once the release is out\ngit branch -d milestone/<id>\nrm -rf /tmp/cargo-target/milestone-<id>\n```\n\n**A milestone's work waits on its own branch until the release** (moai-nvju,\n2026-10-08). Work inside a milestone branches from `milestone/<id>` and merges\nback into it, not into `develop`. The branch is raised from the local `develop`\nwhen the milestone's first epic is sent, by the worker that receives it, and it\nis checked out in a long-lived worktree at `.worktrees/milestone-<id>` because\nthe root stays on `develop`:\n\n```sh\ngit worktree add -b milestone/<id> .worktrees/milestone-<id> develop   # no branch yet\ngit worktree add .worktrees/milestone-<id> milestone/<id>               # branch, no worktree\ngit worktree add -b worktree-<epic> .worktrees/<epic> milestone/<id>    # an epic of it\ngit -C .worktrees/milestone-<id> merge --no-ff worktree-<epic> -m \"merge: … (<epic>)\"\n```","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

In a\n  worktree, also drop it when a live row other than your own stands in that same `cwd`. The\n  root is not such a place — several live sessions stand there at once, and one of them being\n  alive says nothing about the dead one\n- **Drop old crashes.** Records of earlier deaths stay too. Keep the candidates whose\n  transcript (below) last moved around the same time; name an older one to the person apart,\n  and bring it back only if they say so\n- When several candidates stand in the same `cwd`, ask the person **once** — one question\n  for all of them — which to bring back\n\n**A session's transcript** is `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<sessionId>.jsonl`, one JSON object\nper line. Draw the state each was in\n\nRead each candidate's transcript from the end — the last user line and the last assistant\nline — and look at where it stood:\n\n- **Role.** The supervisor's transcript runs `moai-supervise`; a worker's holds the\n  supervisor's message naming `references/worker.md`. {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 1,140p /Users/raven/Works/Projects2/moai/.worktrees/moai-p5sz/CHANGELOG.md","description":"Read the top of the CHANGELOG"},"toolOutput":"# Changelog\n\nAll notable changes to this project are documented here. The format follows\n[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and this project uses\n[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).\n\n`scripts/bump-version.sh auto` moves whatever has accumulated under\n`[Unreleased]` into a new release section and leaves `[Unreleased]` empty for the\nnext one. The headings pick the version: before 1.0, `Fixed` and `Security` alone\nmake a patch release and anything else a minor one. It does not commit and it\ndoes not tag — see `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\n## [Unreleased]\n\n### Added\n\n- **A second optional Claude Code skill, `moai-cmux`, for a supervisor running\n  inside [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux).** It is `moai-tmux` for\n  cmux tabs: it finds each worker's surface (`cmux top` says which surface a\n  session runs in), labels its tab once you say labels are wanted, clears a\n  reported worker's window, pastes a message `SendMessage` could not deliver\n  (`cmux paste --submit`), reads why a worker stalled, and — only after asking —\n  opens new worker splits running an ordinary interactive `claude`. It reads the\n  input box through cmux's own `surface.input_state` and never types over\n  anything in it, never closes a tab, never moves focus and never passes\n  `--force`. **It needs cmux 0.65.0 or later** and checks that itself; on an\n  older cmux it says so and does nothing. Running tmux inside a cmux tab stays\n  `moai-tmux`'s case. Plant it with `moai skill install --with moai-cmux`, or\n  its row in the first `moai init` (checked when `$CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set).\n  `moai-recover` opens a tab per session inside cmux the same way. (moai-p5sz)\n\n### Fixed\n\n- **`moai-tmux` and `moai-recover` found no session on a Mac.** Their session\n  map read the process start time from `/proc`, which macOS does not have, so\n  every session read as dead. It now compares the start time Claude Code writes\n  on a Mac (`ps -o lstart`), and matches a session to a tmux pane by its\n  terminal (`#{pane_tty}`) instead of reading the process's environment — which\n  also no longer trips Claude Code's auto-mode guard against reading other\n  processes' environments. (moai-p5sz.7q3)\n\n## [0.13.0] - 2026-10-10\n\n### Added\n\n- **A fourth Claude Code skill, `moai-tmux`, planted only where you choose it.**\n  When the supervisor runs inside tmux it finds each worker's pane from\n  `~/.claude/sessions/`, labels it (pane option `@moai`), clears a reported\n  worker's window, pastes a message `SendMessage` could not deliver, reads why a\n  worker stalled and tells the person, and — only after asking — opens new\n\n... [39 lines truncated] ...\n\n  `:asc`/`:desc` keeps the direction it always had (newest first for created\n  and updated, urgent first for priority), so `--sort id` and every one-word\n  `--sort` order exactly as before. `--reverse` still turns the whole order\n  around, and `-n`/`--after` page through a multi-field order the same way. An\n  unknown field or direction, an empty field, or a field given twice is refused\n  with the words that are allowed. (moai-r170.9es)\n- **The explorer keeps its sort per project, as a list of fields** — a sort\n  picked inside a project is written for that project alone, as\n  `order = [...]` under `[tui.project.\"<project root>\"]` in the user config —\n  the root the project's tracker lives in, so a linked worktree shares its\n  project's sort — and one picked in the all-projects list (`0`) is written as `order` under\n  `[tui]`, the default for every project without its own. Entering a project\n  puts its own sort back; one sort no longer follows you from project to\n  project. `order` takes the words of `moai show --sort` (`\"updated:asc\"`)\n  except `id`, which the explorer does not sort by.\n  Where `order` is absent the older `sort`/`sort_reversed` pair is read as\n  before, and every write of `[tui] order` also writes that pair from its\n  first field, so an older moai on the same config shows the nearest order.\n  An `order` that cannot be read is named in one line and the older pair\n  stands. (moai-r170.8dz)\n- **The explorer sorts by several fields** — `SPC s P`, `C`, `U`, `S`, `A`\n  and `T` (uppercase) add that field at the end of the order with its own\n  direction, and pressing the same key again turns that field around; the\n  lowercase keys still make the order that one field. `SPC s e` opens a sort\n  window with all six fields, the ones in the order numbered and marked\n  `↑ asc` or `↓ desc`: `j`/`k` move, `J`/`K` move a field down or up the order,\n  `SPC` puts a field in or takes it out, `d` turns its direction, `Enter`\n  applies it where you stand, `D` also keeps it as the default (`[tui] order`)\n  even inside a project, and `Esc` leaves without a change. The path line\n  names the whole order, every field with `↑` or `↓`\n  (`sort priority↑, updated↓`). (moai-r170.x22)\n\n### Changed\n\n- **Where picked-up work stands is read from worktree names and pick-up marks\n  only, the way the hook reads it.** The `Place` line of `moai show` (`place`\n  and `workplaces` under `--json`) and the `stranded` warning of `moai status`\n  no longer read sibling worktrees' `.moai/issues.jsonl` — those are stale\n  copies, since every write goes to the main checkout. A worktree counts for a\n  row when its name points at the row or when `moai mv` picked the row up\n  inside it, and the explorer's `⎇` beside a row someone else holds now names\n  such a worktree too. A row picked up in\n  the main checkout and carried into a worktree whose name is not its id now\n  shows `none` and stands under `stranded`. `place` has three values — `at`,\n  `fresh`, `lost`; `unknown` no longer appears, and neither does\n  `unreadable_worktrees` under `status --json` or `tui --json`: a broken\n  sibling snapshot is still named by `broken_worktrees` but no longer hides a\n  verdict, and the explorer's project layer gives the number of such\n  worktrees without saying they hid places from the count. (moai-jn4d.ewm,\n  moai-bl4d)","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

Only topology collection visits MainActor.\nextension TerminalController {\n    #if compiler(>=6.2)\n    @concurrent\n    #else\n    @Sendable\n    #endif\n    nonisolated func v2SystemTopAsync(_ request: ControlRequest) async throws -> String {\n        let base = try await v2MainAsync {\n            let foundationParams = request.params.mapValues(\\.foundationObject)\n            return Self.controlCallResult(\n                fromLegacy: self.v2SystemTopBasePayload(params: foundationParams)\n            )\n        }\n        guard case .ok(let basePayload) = base,\n              case .object(let baseObject) = basePayload,\n              case .bool(let includeProcesses)? = baseObject[\"include_processes\"],\n              case .array(let rawWindows)? = baseObject[\"windows\"] else {\n            return Self.v2Encoder.response(id: request.id, base)\n        }\n        let processPayload = await processTopPayload(\n            windows: .array(rawWindows), includeProcesses: includeProcesses\n        )\n        let payload = baseObject.merging(processPayload) { _, incoming in incoming }\n        return Self.v2Encoder.response(id: request.id, .ok(.object(payload)))\n    }\n\n    #if compiler(>=6.2)\n    @concurrent\n    #else\n    @Sendable\n    #endif\n    nonisolated func processTopPayload(windows: JSONValue, includeProcesses: Bool) async -> [String: JSONValue] {\n        guard let windowsObject = windows.foundationObject as? [[String: Any]] else { return [:] }\n        let processSnapshot = await CmuxTopProcessSnapshot.captureCached(\n            includeProcessDetails: includeProcesses, maximumAge: 2\n        )\n        var windows = windowsObject\n        let browserPIDOccurrences = v2TopBrowserPIDOccurrences(in: windows)\n        let totalPIDs = v2AnnotateTopWindows(\n            &windows,\n            processSnapshot: processSnapshot,\n            browserPIDOccurrences: browserPIDOccurrences,\n            includeProcesses: includeProcesses\n        )\n        let aggregates = processAggregates(\n            from: processSnapshot,\n            totalPIDs: totalPIDs\n        )\n        let memoryDiagnostic = v2TopMemoryDiagnosticPayload(\n            processSnapshot: processSnapshot,\n            annotatedWindows: windows\n        )\n\n        var payload: [String: JSONValue] = [:]\n        payload[\"sample\"] = JSONValue(\n            foundationObject: processSnapshot.samplePayload()\n        ) ?? .object([:])\n        payload[\"totals\"] = JSONValue(\n            foundationObject: processSnapshot.summaryPayload(for: totalPIDs)\n        ) ?? .object([:])\n        payload[\"memory_diagnostic\"] = JSONValue(\n            foundationObject: memoryDiagnostic\n        ) ?? .object([:])\n        payload[\"program_totals\"] = JSONValue(\n            foundationObject: aggregates.programs\n        ) ?? .array([])\n        payload[\"coding_agents\"] = JSONValue(\n            foundationObject: aggregates.codingAgents\n        ) ?? .array([])\n        payload[\"windows\"] = JSONValue(\n            foundationObject: windows\n        ) ?? .array([])\n        return payload\n    }\n\n}","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

Prints the sessions dir.\n\nUsage: python3 -I mkrecords.py <dir> <tmux -L name> <dead count>\n\"\"\"\nimport json, os, subprocess, sys\n\nd, name, dead = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])\nos.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)\nfor f in os.listdir(d):\n    os.remove(os.path.join(d, f))\nenv = dict(os.environ)\nenv.pop(\"TMUX\", None)\npanes = subprocess.run([\"tmux\", \"-L\", name, \"list-panes\", \"-a\", \"-F\", \"#{pane_id} #{pane_pid}\"],\n                       capture_output=True, text=True, env=env).stdout.split(\"\\n\")\nn = 0\nfor line in panes:\n    if not line.strip():\n        continue\n    pane, pid = line.split()\n    start = subprocess.run([\"ps\", \"-p\", pid, \"-o\", \"lstart=\"], capture_output=True, text=True,\n                           env=dict(os.environ, LC_ALL=\"C\", TZ=\"UTC\")).stdout.strip()\n    rec = {\"pid\": int(pid), \"procStart\": start, \"pidDomain\": \"darwin\", \"status\": \"idle\",\n           \"name\": f\"w{n}\", \"tmux\": f\"map:@0.{pane}\", \"cwd\": \"/repo\", \"sessionId\": f\"s{n}\"}\n    with open(os.path.join(d, f\"{pid}.json\"), \"w\") as f:\n        json.dump(rec, f)\n    n += 1\n# dead records: pids that are not running (probe with kill 0)\npid = 90000\nmade = 0\nwhile made < dead:\n    pid += 7\n    try:\n        os.kill(pid, 0)\n        continue  # alive, skip\n    except ProcessLookupError:\n        pass\n    except PermissionError:\n        continue\n    rec = {\"pid\": pid, \"procStart\": \"Mon Oct  5 10:00:00 2026\", \"pidDomain\": \"darwin\", \"status\": \"idle\",\n           \"name\": f\"dead{made}\", \"tmux\": f\"old:@1.%{made + 50}\", \"cwd\": \"/repo\", \"sessionId\": f\"d{made}\"}\n    with open(os.path.join(d, f\"{pid}.json\"), \"w\") as f:\n        json.dump(rec, f)\n    made += 1\nprint(d, \"alive:\", n, \"dead:\", made)\n"},"toolOutput":"\"\"\"Write fake ~/.claude/sessions records into a scratch dir: one alive record per pane of the private\ntmux server, plus `dead` records whose pids are not running. {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"cat -n .claude/moai-plugin/skills/moai-recover/SKILL.md | sed -n 1,70p","description":"Read recover skill first part"},"toolOutput":"     1\t---\n     2\tname: moai-recover\n     3\tdescription: Use in Claude Code when the person asks to bring back the sessions of this repository that died — after a restart, an OOM kill or a crash — so the supervisor and its workers carry on where they stopped. Finds the dead sessions, draws the state each was in, points out background work that never returned and broken target links, and resumes each one in a new tmux pane or cmux tab, or prints the command to type. Triggers on \"recover the sessions\", \"bring the sessions back\", \"resume the dead sessions\", \"되살려\", \"세션 복구\", \"이어 가게 해\".\n     4\t---\n     5\t\n     6\t# moai-recover — bring back the sessions that died\n     7\t\n     8\tUse this when the person asks for it: the sessions of this repository — a supervisor, its\n     9\tworkers — died together, after a restart, an OOM kill or a crash, and the person wants them\n    10\tto carry on. **Their asking is the yes:** inside tmux or cmux you open the panes without asking\n    11\tagain.\n    12\tNone of this is a moai command; it is you reading Claude Code's own records and typing where\n    13\tthe person can watch.\n    14\t\n    15\t## What never happens\n    16\t\n    17\t- **No headless run.** A session you bring back is an ordinary interactive `claude --resume`\n    18\t  the person can see and type into. Never `claude -p`, never a `--dangerously-*` flag, never\n    19\t  `--permission-mode`\n    20\t- **Nothing is killed.** Never `kill-server`, `kill-session` or `kill-pane`, never `pkill`\n    21\t  or `killall` aimed at tmux (hook rule 4); inside cmux never `close-surface`, `close-workspace`\n    22\t  or `close-window`, and never `--force`. A session that is alive is left alone\n    23\t- **Only the panes you opened.** Type only into a pane this skill opened, by the `%N` that\n    24\t  `split-window` printed — every call names it, `-t <pane>`. Inside cmux it is the surface UUID\n    25\t  `new-split` printed, `--surface <surface>`\n    26\t- **Never over the person's words.** Paste only into an empty input box (\"Is the input box\n    27\t  empty\" below); otherwise tell the person\n    28\t- **No polling.** Every look is one look; the next comes after your next step, as its own\n    29\t  call — never a loop, never a `sleep`\n    30\t- **Their work stays as it is.** No commit, no checkout, no stash, no build, no `moai` write —\n    31\t  what a dead session left is for that session to pick up\n    32\t\n    33\t## Is the input box empty\n    34\t\n    35\tInside tmux:\n    36\t\n    37\t    tmux display -p -t <pane> '#{pane_in_mode}'\n    38\t    tmux capture-pane -p -e -t <pane>\n    39\t\n    40\tThe first line prints `1` while the person is scrolling the pane (copy mode) — keys you send\n    41\tthen go to tmux's copy mode, not to Claude Code, so a pane in a mode is theirs: do not type.\n    42\tClaude Code's input box is the line that starts with `❯`, under the conversation, between two\n    43\t`─` rules. **Empty** is `❯` followed by nothing, or by Claude Code's dim placeholder — `-e`\n    44\tkeeps the colours, and the placeholder is drawn dim (SGR `2`, or a grey foreground) where the\n    45\tperson's text is not. Anything else — a word, a pasted block, a half-typed command — is the\n    46\tperson's, and if you cannot tell the placeholder from their draft, it is theirs. A pane with\n    47\tno `❯` box at all (a shell prompt, a dialog) is not a box to type into either.\n    48\t\n    49\tInside cmux:\n    50\t\n    51\t    cmux rpc surface.input_state '{\"surface_id\":\"<surface>\"}'\n    52\t\n    53\tcmux reads Claude Code's input box off that surface's screen. The box is **empty** only when\n    54\tthe answer reads `\"state\": \"empty\"` and `\"waiting_on_human\": false`. `draft` is text someone\n    55\ttyped or pasted — the person's, even a half-typed word. `dialog` is a prompt or a menu standing\n    56\twhere the box was. `unknown` is a screen cmux cannot read as Claude Code's — a shell prompt, a\n    57\tprocess that ended. `waiting_on_human` is a permission prompt or a question waiting for the\n    58\tperson. None of these is a box to type into, and neither is an error or an answer without\n    59\t`state`.\n    60\t\n    61\t**When it is not empty, do not paste.** Tell the person which pane holds what — the words in it\n    62\tare theirs.\n    63\t\n    64\t## 1. Find the dead\n    65\t\n    66\tClaude Code keeps one record per process under `~/.claude/sessions/`, and a process that dies\n    67\tleaves its record behind. The lines below print one row per record, tab-separated:\n    68\t\n    69\t    state  name  pane  status  cwd  sessionId\n    70","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"cat"}}

\"-\":\n                readsStandardInput = true\n            default:\n                // Everything here lands in an agent prompt, so a mistyped flag\n                // (`--sumbit`, `-s`) or an Installed files stay\n\nUsage: moai skill uninstall [OPTIONS]\n\nOptions:\n      --agent <agent>        Agent: claude (default), codex, antigravity, auto\n      --only <skill>         Remove only this optional skill (repeatable)\n      --dry-run              Call nothing; only say what would be called\n      --json                 Machine-readable output. Every human line goes away\n      --no-color             Turn colour off (same as `--color never`)\n      --color <how>          auto|always|never (auto by default, off when piped)\n  -C, --dir <path>           Run in this directory (same as `git -C`)\n      --user <name (email)>  Who is doing this (from `git config` when absent)\n  -h, --help                 Print help\n\n  This repository's install is removed per scope with\n  `claude plugin uninstall`, and the marketplace with\n  `claude plugin marketplace remove`. Deleting the two keys from your\n  settings is `claude`'s job - we do not touch someone else's JSON, except\n  the old declarations below.\n\n  **`.claude/moai-plugin/` is not deleted.** Deleting a file a running\n  session holds can block that session's tool calls. Delete it after closing\n  the session.\n\n  The two Korean plugins an earlier moai installed alongside are removed **at\n  the scope moai was removed from**, under the same conditions as install: an\n  earlier version of moai stands there and the marketplace is the one it\n  added. The marketplace is left behind - the name is global to one machine\n  and another repository's install uses it. A user-scope install is also left\n  behind when another repository's moai stands there, and then the command to\n  remove it is printed in one line. At project scope the marketplace's\n  declaration in the committed .claude/settings.json goes, as with install.\n\n  A Claude session already open keeps calling the old hook - reopen it for\n  the removal to land.\n\n  For codex and antigravity (--agent) there is no registration to remove,\n  and no file is deleted either: the `rm -r` lines for moai's skills in\n  `.agents/skills/`, and the `rm` line for that agent's hooks file when moai\n  wrote it, are printed, to run once no session holds them. Without that\n  --agent, one line says when moai's skills are still there.\n\n  --only <skill> removes one optional skill and nothing else: it is\n  `moai skill install --without <skill>` under another name. That skill's\n  directory goes (only while it holds nothing but moai's files) and the\n  plugin is planted again; the registration and the other skills stay.\n  A tree moai has not planted is left alone - no file and no hooks file\n  is made there. Where this repository's moai is registered, that scope is\n  brought up to the new version; where it is registered nowhere, only the\n  files change - no registration is made. A skill that is always planted\n  is refused.\n\n  moai skill uninstall --dry-run      only show what would be called\n  moai skill uninstall --agent codex  name what to delete in .agents/skills/\n  moai skill uninstall --only moai-tmux   take the tmux skill out","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"./target/debug/moai"}}

Find the dead\n\nClaude Code keeps one record per process under `~/.claude/sessions/`, and a process that dies\nleaves its record behind. The lines below print one row per record, tab-separated:\n\n\n```sh\npython3 - <<'PY'\nmine = os.environ.get(\"TMUX\")\ncmux = not mine and bool(os.environ.get(\"CMUX_SURFACE_ID\"))\nsurfaces = {}\nif cmux:\nfor path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.expanduser(\"~/.claude/sessions/*.json\"))):\nPY\n```\n\n- A **candidate** is a `dead` row with a `sessionId` whose `cwd` is the root or one of the\n  worktrees `git worktree list` names\n- **Drop it when it is back already** — a live row carries the same `sessionId` (`--resume`\n  keeps the id), **your own row included**: a session the person resumed first and then asked\n  for this is back already, and resuming it again puts one conversation in two windows. In a\n  worktree, also drop it when a live row other than your own stands in that same `cwd`. The\n  root is not such a place — several live sessions stand there at once, and one of them being\n  alive says nothing about the dead one\n- **Drop old crashes.** Records of earlier deaths stay too. Keep the candidates whose\n  transcript (below) last moved around the same time; name an older one to the person apart,\n  and bring it back only if they say so\n- When several candidates stand in the same `cwd`, ask the person **once** — one question\n  for all of them — which to bring back\n\n**A session's transcript** is `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<sessionId>.jsonl`, one JSON object\nper line. The slug is a directory with every character that is not a letter or a digit\nturned into `-` (`/home/me/repo/.worktrees/moai-ab12` is `-home-me-repo--worktrees-moai-ab12`).\nWhich directory is not fixed: a worker that entered its worktree from the root has kept its\ntranscript under the root's slug on one Claude Code version and under the worktree's on\nanother, so do not work the slug out — find it by id:\n\n\n**When the records are gone too**, look under the root's slug and under each worktree's slug\nfor every `*.jsonl` that last moved around the time they died — the root's slug may hold the\nsupervisor's and a worker's both, so not only the newest one. A line's `cwd` and `sessionId`\nsay where that session last stood and which id to resume; its `timestamp` says when it last\nmoved.\n\n## 2. Draw the state each was in\n\nRead each candidate's transcript from the end — the last user line and the last assistant\nline — and look at where it stood:\n\n- **Role.** The supervisor's transcript runs `moai-supervise`; a worker's holds the\n  supervisor's message naming `references/worker.md`. A session that is neither is brought\n  back the same way, as a worker\n- **Work.** The issue or epic id it held, and what it was doing or waiting for — a report,\n  a review, a person's decision, a build\n- **Died at** — the `timestamp` of its last line\n- `git -C <cwd> status --short` — what it left uncommitted\n- `moai show <id>` — a `Next:` note on that id says where the session meant to go on\n\nShow the person **one table**, a row per session: role, name, `cwd`, work id, what it was\nwaiting for, died at, uncommitted files. Then go on — they asked for recovery already.\n\n## 3. Point out what died with it\n\n- **Background work that never returned.** A background launch is an `Agent` or `Bash`\n  `tool_use` whose result reads `Async agent launched` (with its `agentId`), `Command running\n  in background with ID: <id>`, or — a command that ran past its timeout —\n  `moved to the background (ID: <id>)`. Whether the input carries\n  `\"run_in_background\": true` differs by version and the timeout case carries nothing, so read\n  the result; when it ends, a later user line carries a\n  `<task-notification>` whose `<task-id>` is that id. A launch with no such line after it died\n  with the session — the resumed session will never hear from it, and what it\n  changed is uncommitted in that session's `cwd`\n- **A broken target link.** In the root and each worktree, `target` may be a link to\n  `/tmp/cargo-target/<name>`, and a restart can empty `/tmp`:\n\n\n  Make the directory again, `mkdir -p /tmp/cargo-target/<name>`, so builds land there. The\n  build output is gone: `./target/release/moai` needs `cargo build --release` before anything\n  calls it. Do not build it yourself — the resumed session does\n\n## 4. The text each one gets\n\nOne block per session, written to a file in your scratchpad:\n\n\nLeave out a line that does not hold. The supervisor's block adds one line: **the workers are\nback in new sessions and their names may have changed — run `ListAgents` again** before you\nsend or wait for a report.\n\n**Workers first, the supervisor last**, in every way below — the supervisor's `ListAgents`\nhas to see the workers when it starts.\n\n## 5. Inside tmux — open a pane each","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

An older diagnostic census cannot authorize\n    /// lifecycle decisions merely because its enrichment finished more recently.\n    static func capture(\n        includeProcessDetails: Bool = false,\n        includeCMUXScope: Bool = true,\n        includeResources: Bool = true,\n        service: ProcessSnapshotService<CmuxTopProcessCapture, CmuxTopProcessFields>? = nil\n    ) async -> CmuxTopProcessSnapshot {\n        await capture(\n            fields: CmuxTopProcessFields(details: includeProcessDetails, scope: includeCMUXScope, resources: includeResources),\n            freshness: .afterRequest, service: service ?? defaultProcessSnapshotService()\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Permits diagnostic reuse only within the explicit age bound from census start.\n    static func captureCached(\n        includeProcessDetails: Bool = false,\n        includeCMUXScope: Bool = true,\n        includeResources: Bool = true,\n        maximumAge: TimeInterval,\n        service: ProcessSnapshotService<CmuxTopProcessCapture, CmuxTopProcessFields>? = nil\n    ) async -> CmuxTopProcessSnapshot {\n        await capture(\n            fields: CmuxTopProcessFields(details: includeProcessDetails, scope: includeCMUXScope, resources: includeResources),\n            freshness: .maximumAge(.seconds(max(0, maximumAge))), service: service ?? defaultProcessSnapshotService()\n        )\n    }\n\n    private static func capture(\n        fields: CmuxTopProcessFields, freshness: ProcessSnapshotFreshness,\n        service: ProcessSnapshotService<CmuxTopProcessCapture, CmuxTopProcessFields>\n    ) async -> CmuxTopProcessSnapshot {\n        do {\n            return try await service.snapshot(fields: fields, freshness: freshness).snapshot\n        } catch {\n            // Expiry, cancellation and admission failure are unavailable evidence,\n            // never a complete empty machine. resourcesByPID[pid] : process\n            // A process that exited after the listing is absent, not unreadable:\n            // only a live process we failed to read leaves the census incomplete.\n            // A reused PID is still live and still counts as missing.\n            guard let resources else {\n                if !reader.processHasExited(pid: pid) { missingCount += 1 }\n                continue\n            }\n            let key = CmuxTopProcessSnapshot.scopeCacheKey(from: bsd)\n            guard !readsIdentitySensitiveData || reader.matches(pid: pid, key: key) else {\n                if !reader.processHasExited(pid: pid) { missingCount += 1 }\n                continue\n            }\n            let name = missing.contains(.details)\n                ? reader.processName(pid: pid, fallback: process.name) : process.name\n            let path = missing.contains(.details) ? reader.processPath(pid: pid) : process.path\n            let scope = missing.contains(.scope) ? reader.scope(for: pid, key: key) : nil\n            guard !readsIdentitySensitiveData || reader.matches(pid: pid, key: key) else {\n                if !reader.processHasExited(pid: pid) { missingCount += 1 }\n                continue\n            }\n            records.append(CmuxTopProcessInfo(\n                pid: pid, processIdentity: process.processIdentity,\n                parentPID: process.parentPID, name: name, path: path,\n                ttyDevice: process.ttyDevice,\n                cmuxWorkspaceID: missing.contains(.scope) ? scope?.workspaceID : process.cmuxWorkspaceID,\n                cmuxSurfaceID: missing.contains(.scope) ? scope?.surfaceID : process.cmuxSurfaceID,\n                cmuxAttributionReason: missing.contains(.scope) ? scope?.attributionReason : process.cmuxAttributionReason,\n                processGroupID: process.processGroupID, terminalProcessGroupID: process.terminalProcessGroupID,\n                cpuPercent: resources.cpuPercent, memoryBytes: resources.memoryBytes, memorySource: resources.memorySource,\n                residentBytes: resources.residentBytes, residentMemorySource: resources.residentMemorySource,\n                virtualBytes: resources.virtualBytes, threadCount: resources.threadCount\n            ))\n        }\n        let combined = capture.fields.union(missing)\n        let snapshot = CmuxTopProcessSnapshot(\n            processes: records, sampledAt: capture.snapshot.sampledAt,\n            includesProcessDetails: combined.contains(.details), includesCMUXScope: combined.contains(.scope),\n            includesResources: combined.contains(.resources),\n            enumerationIsComplete: capture.snapshot.enumerationIsComplete && missingCount == 0,\n            enumerationMissingProcessCount: missingCount\n        )\n        return CmuxTopProcessCapture(listing: capture.listing, snapshot: snapshot, fields: combined)\n    }\n}","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 19803,19832p tests/cli.rs","description":"Read misnamed-skill test in tests/cli.rs"},"toolOutput":"/// **고른 이름은 무엇을 쓰기 전에 잰다**(moai-3r7l.5ja) — 늘 심는 이름은 \"늘 심는다\" 로, 모르는 이름은 고를 수 있는\n/// 이름을 대며, 한 이름을 심고 걷으라는 것은 그것대로 거절한다. 셋 다 `bad_input` 이고 아무것도 안 심는다.\n#[test]\nfn skill_install_refuses_a_pick_it_cannot_take() {\n    let s = init(\"skillwithbad\");\n    let c = Claude::new(\"skillwithbad-home\");\n    for (args, said) in [\n        (&[\"--with\", \"moai-wiki\"][..], \"늘 심는\"),\n        (&[\"--without\", \"moai-recover\"][..], \"늘 심는\"),\n        (&[\"--with\", \"tmux\"][..], \"moai-tmux\"),\n        (&[\"--with\", \"moai-tmux\", \"--without\", \"moai-tmux\"][..], \"--without\"),\n    ] {\n        let mut argv = vec![\"skill\", \"install\"];\n        argv.extend(args);\n        let out = c.run(s.path(), &argv, true);\n        assert!(!out.status.success(), \"{args:?} 를 받았다\\n{}\", text(&out));\n        assert!(text(&out).contains(said), \"{args:?}: 까닭을 안 댄다\\n{}\", text(&out));\n        argv.push(\"--json\");\n        let err = String::from_utf8(c.run(s.path(), &argv, true).stderr).unwrap();\n        assert!(err.contains(\"\\\"code\\\":\\\"bad_input\\\"\"), \"{args:?}\\n{err}\");\n    }\n    assert!(!s.path().join(\".claude/moai-plugin\").exists(), \"거절한 고르기에 심었다\");\n    assert_eq!(c.calls(), \"\", \"거절한 고르기에 claude 를 불렀다\");\n}\n\n/// **`uninstall --only` 는 `install --without` 이다**(2026-10-10 사용자 결정, moai-3r7l.xr1) — 그 스킬만 걷고 다른 스킬은\n/// 둔다. 등록이 선 범위는 새 판으로 올리기만 하고(`plugin update`), 등록을 세우는 걸음(`marketplace add`·`plugin install`)도\n/// 걷는 걸음(`plugin uninstall`)도 안 부른다. 어디에도 등록이 없으면 `claude` 를 아예 안 부르고 파일만 고친다.\n#[test]","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 1,40p scripts/bump-version.sh | head -60","description":"Read bump-version.sh header"},"toolOutput":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# `Cargo.toml` 과 `CHANGELOG.md` 의 버전을 한 번에 움직인다.\n#\n#     scripts/bump-version.sh auto      [Unreleased] 의 절을 읽고 판을 고른다\n#     scripts/bump-version.sh minor     한 칸을 손으로 고른다 (patch 도 같다)\n#     scripts/bump-version.sh 0.2.0     판을 그대로 준다 — 1.0 은 이 길로만 연다\n#     scripts/bump-version.sh --next    auto 가 고를 판만 찍는다. 아무것도 안 쓴다\n#\n# **태그는 사람이 단다.** 이 스크립트는 커밋도 태그도 하지 않고 파일만 고친다 —\n# 무엇이 바뀌었는지 사람이 보고 커밋하는 자리를 남긴다. 태그를 여기서 달면\n# `check-version.sh` 가 재는 두 값을 한 손이 같이 써, 어긋남을 잡을 눈이 없어진다.\n#\n# 날짜는 `MOAI_NOW` 가 서 있으면 그것을 쓴다 (시험이 시계를 고정하는 자리).\nset -euo pipefail\n\nroot=$(cd -- \"$(dirname -- \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")/..\" && pwd)\nmanifest=$root/Cargo.toml\nchangelog=$root/CHANGELOG.md\ncheck=$root/scripts/check-version.sh\n\ndie() {\n  printf 'bump-version: %s\\n' \"$1\" >&2\n  exit 2\n}\n\n# **판을 고르는 자는 `[Unreleased]` 의 절이다**(moai-ug3j, 2026-10-01 사용자 결정).\n# 1.0 전에는 Fixed·Security 만 있으면 patch, Added·Changed·Deprecated·Removed 가 하나라도\n# 있으면 minor 다 — 동작이 바뀌었으면 고친 것이 아니다. AI 든 사람이든 고르는 것은 줄을\n# 어느 절에 넣는가이고, 번호는 여기서 센다. 세션마다 손으로 셈하던 판은 0.1.1 부터\n# 내리 patch 였다 — 그 판들 대부분에 `### Added` 가 있었는데도.\n#\n# 모르는 절은 어느 칸인지 못 가르므로 고르지 않고 멈춘다. 어림으로 patch 를 주면 기능이\n# 든 판이 고친 판으로 나간다.\n#\n# **첫 절 앞의 머리글은 세지 않는다**(리뷰 moai-ug3j.rrc 4번). 0.1.2 는 깨지는 것 둘을\n# 머리글에 모아 두고 같은 것을 아래 절에 다시 적었다 — 그 꼴을 막으면 판을 다시 손으로\n# 주는 수밖에 없다. 대신 머리글만 있고 절이 비었으면 멈추고, 머리글을 건너뛰었다는 것을\n# 까닭 줄에 적는다. 항목은 절 안에 적는다.\npick() {\n  [ -f \"$changelog\" ] || die \"auto 는 CHANGELOG.md 의 [Unreleased] 를 읽는다 — 파일이 없다\"","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 515,540p src/held.rs","description":"Read existing unix socket test in held.rs"},"toolOutput":"    /// 기다리는데, 시험은 [`within`] 이 정한 때에 진다. 소켓은 `open` 에서 지는데(`ENXIO`), 그것도 같은 갈래로 선다.\n    #[cfg(unix)]\n    #[test]\n    fn a_fifo_a_socket_or_a_directory_is_not_read_and_does_not_hang() {\n        let s = Scratch::new(\"held-fifo\");\n        let fifo = s.join(\"f\");\n        let c = std::ffi::CString::new(fifo.as_os_str().as_encoded_bytes()).unwrap();\n        // SAFETY: 널로 끝나는 경로와 권한 비트만 넘긴다.\n        assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::mkfifo(c.as_ptr(), 0o600) }, 0, \"FIFO 를 못 지었다\");\n        let opened = fifo.clone();\n        assert!(matches!(within(\"FIFO\", move || read(&opened)), Err(Fell::Unheld(Unheld::NotAFile))));\n        assert!(matches!(read(s.path()), Err(Fell::Unheld(Unheld::NotAFile))));\n        assert!(matches!(read(&s.join(\"none\")), Err(Fell::Io(e)) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound));\n        let sock = s.join(\"s\");\n        let _listener = std::os::unix::net::UnixListener::bind(&sock).expect(\"소켓을 못 지었다\");\n        assert!(matches!(read(&sock), Err(Fell::Unheld(Unheld::NotAFile))), \"소켓을 io 실패로 댔다\");\n    }\n\n    /// **손잡이가 댄 크기까지만 읽는다.** `/proc/self/status` 는 `stat` 이 크기 0 이라 답하면서 글을 내는\n    /// 파일이라, 고침이 없으면 글이 읽히고 고치면 빈 것이다. 끝없이 읽는 파일로 재지 않는다 — 고침이 없으면\n    /// 시험이 메모리를 다 쓴다. 저널이 이 자를 지나는지는 `store` 의 시험이 따로 잰다.\n    #[cfg(target_os = \"linux\")]\n    #[test]\n    fn a_file_is_read_no_further_than_the_size_its_handle_gives() {\n        let status = Path::new(\"/proc/self/status\");\n        assert_eq!(std::fs::metadata(status).unwrap().len(), 0, \"procfs 가 크기를 대는 경우다 — 시험이 못 잰다\");","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

If you can see your own context usage, put that number in the line too.\n    **Say the opposite in the same line** — not to clear while a review is running in the\n    background, while a merge conflict is being resolved, while waiting on a person's answer,\n    or after the supervisor's next message has arrived in this window. Clearing (`/clear`) then\n    loses what is not yet moved into the tracker, or the message that arrived.\n    Then end the turn.
