{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 428,470p docs/agents.md","description":"Read docs/agents.md In tmux section"},"toolOutput":"and stops at anything that cannot be undone.\n\n### In tmux\n\nWhen the supervisor runs inside tmux (`$TMUX` is set) and the `moai-tmux`\nskill is planted ([optional skills](#optional-skills) — `moai skill install\n--with moai-tmux`), it also loads that skill and works on the workers' panes of\nyour own tmux server (moai-u99i). Without tmux, or without the skill, nothing of\nthis happens.\n\n- **Which pane is which worker.** Claude Code keeps a record per process under\n  `~/.claude/sessions/`; the skill reads the live ones (the pid alive and its\n  start time matching) and pairs each `ListAgents` name with its pane `%N`.\n  Every tmux call names that pane\n- **A label on the pane.** When it sends work, it writes `<worker> <id>` into the\n  pane option `@moai`, and removes it once the report is checked. Once a round\n  it asks whether you want the labels on the pane borders; on a yes it puts\n  `#{@moai}` in front of the running server's `pane-border-format`. Your tmux\n  config file is never edited\n- **Clearing a reported worker.** After the report is checked, while the worker\n  reads idle and its input box is empty, it types `/clear` into that pane before\n  sending the next work\n- **A message that did not arrive.** When `SendMessage` fails, it pastes the\n  message into the worker's empty input box and tells you. A message held for\n  your approval is not pasted — it waits for you, and it tells you so\n- **A stalled worker.** When a worker goes idle with no report, it reads the\n  pane once and tells you what stands there — a permission prompt, a question,\n  an error. It never answers in your place\n- **No idle worker.** It asks you whether to open new worker panes; on a yes it\n  splits a pane running `claude --model <model>` in the root — an ordinary\n  interactive session you can see and type into\n\n**If anything stands in a worker's input box, or you are scrolling that pane\n(copy mode), it does not type** — it tells you.\nIt never kills a pane, a session or the server, and never runs `claude -p` or a\n`--dangerously-*` flag.\n\n**On a Mac** the same works: the session records there carry the process start\ntime in another form (`ps -o lstart`), and a pane is matched to a session by its\nterminal (`#{pane_tty}`), never by reading another process's environment\n(moai-p5sz.7q3).\n\n### In cmux","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n '425,470p' /Users/raven/Works/Projects2/moai/.worktrees/moai-p5sz/docs/agents.md; sed -n '505,530p' /Users/raven/Works/Projects2/moai/.worktrees/moai-p5sz/docs/agents.md","description":"Read In tmux and recover sections of docs/agents.md"},"toolOutput":"**When the person steps away**, they tell the supervisor, and its messages say\n`Person: away`. The worker then settles a design question by its own\nrecommendation and leaves `Decided alone: …` on the issue instead of waiting,\nand stops at anything that cannot be undone.\n\n### In tmux\n\nWhen the supervisor runs inside tmux (`$TMUX` is set) and the `moai-tmux`\nskill is planted ([optional skills](#optional-skills) — `moai skill install\n--with moai-tmux`), it also loads that skill and works on the workers' panes of\nyour own tmux server (moai-u99i). Without tmux, or without the skill, nothing of\nthis happens.\n\n- **Which pane is which worker.** Claude Code keeps a record per process under\n  `~/.claude/sessions/`; the skill reads the live ones (the pid alive and its\n  start time matching) and pairs each `ListAgents` name with its pane `%N`.\n  Every tmux call names that pane\n- **A label on the pane.** When it sends work, it writes `<worker> <id>` into the\n  pane option `@moai`, and removes it once the report is checked. Once a round\n  it asks whether you want the labels on the pane borders; on a yes it puts\n  `#{@moai}` in front of the running server's `pane-border-format`. Your tmux\n  config file is never edited\n- **Clearing a reported worker.** After the report is checked, while the worker\n  reads idle and its input box is empty, it types `/clear` into that pane before\n  sending the next work\n- **A message that did not arrive.** When `SendMessage` fails, it pastes the\n  message into the worker's empty input box and tells you. A message held for\n  your approval is not pasted — it waits for you, and it tells you so\n- **A stalled worker.** When a worker goes idle with no report, it reads the\n  pane once and tells you what stands there — a permission prompt, a question,\n  an error. It never answers in your place\n- **No idle worker.** It asks you whether to open new worker panes; on a yes it\n  splits a pane running `claude --model <model>` in the root — an ordinary\n  interactive session you can see and type into\n\n**If anything stands in a worker's input box, or you are scrolling that pane\n(copy mode), it does not type** — it tells you.\nIt never kills a pane, a session or the server, and never runs `claude -p` or a\n`--dangerously-*` flag.\n\n**On a Mac** the same works: the session records there carry the process start\ntime in another form (`ps -o lstart`), and a pane is matched to a session by its\nterminal (`#{pane_tty}`), never by reading another process's environment\n(moai-p5sz.7q3).\n\n### In cmux\n### Bring back sessions that died\n\nWhen the supervisor and its workers died together — the machine restarted, the\ncontainer was OOM-killed — open one Claude Code session in the root and ask it\nto bring them back (\"recover the sessions\", \"되살려\"). It loads `moai-recover`\n(moai-uqf7); your asking is the yes.\n\n- **Which died.** It reads the same records under `~/.claude/sessions/` and\n  takes the dead ones standing in the root or a worktree, leaving out any that\n  is already back and older crashes you did not name. When several stand in one\n  directory it asks you once which to bring back\n- **What each was doing.** From each session's transcript under\n  `~/.claude/projects/` it reads its role (supervisor or worker), the issue it\n  held and what it was waiting for, adds the uncommitted files and the issue's\n  `Next:` note, and shows you one table\n- **What died with it.** A background subagent or command that never reported\n  back, and a `target` link whose `/tmp/cargo-target/<name>` was wiped — it\n  makes that directory again; the build output is gone, so the session rebuilds\n- **Bringing them back, workers first and the supervisor last.** Inside tmux it\n  splits a pane per session running `claude --resume <id>` and pastes a short\n  note on what happened once the input box is empty; the supervisor is told its\n  workers' names may have changed. Inside cmux (0.65.0 or later) it does the\n  same with a split tab per session. Outside both it prints, per session,\n  `cd <dir> && claude --resume <id>` and the note to paste\n\nIt changes nothing in the sessions' work — no commit, no build, no `moai` write.","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

Only topology collection visits MainActor.\nextension TerminalController {\n    #if compiler(>=6.2)\n    @concurrent\n    #else\n    @Sendable\n    #endif\n    nonisolated func v2SystemTopAsync(_ request: ControlRequest) async throws -> String {\n        let base = try await v2MainAsync {\n            let foundationParams = request.params.mapValues(\\.foundationObject)\n            return Self.controlCallResult(\n                fromLegacy: self.v2SystemTopBasePayload(params: foundationParams)\n            )\n        }\n        guard case .ok(let basePayload) = base,\n              case .object(let baseObject) = basePayload,\n              case .bool(let includeProcesses)? = baseObject[\"include_processes\"],\n              case .array(let rawWindows)? = baseObject[\"windows\"] else {\n            return Self.v2Encoder.response(id: request.id, base)\n        }\n        let processPayload = await processTopPayload(\n            windows: .array(rawWindows), includeProcesses: includeProcesses\n        )\n        let payload = baseObject.merging(processPayload) { _, incoming in incoming }\n        return Self.v2Encoder.response(id: request.id, .ok(.object(payload)))\n    }\n\n    #if compiler(>=6.2)\n    @concurrent\n    #else\n    @Sendable\n    #endif\n    nonisolated func processTopPayload(windows: JSONValue, includeProcesses: Bool) async -> [String: JSONValue] {\n        guard let windowsObject = windows.foundationObject as? [[String: Any]] else { return [:] }\n        let processSnapshot = await CmuxTopProcessSnapshot.captureCached(\n            includeProcessDetails: includeProcesses, maximumAge: 2\n        )\n        var windows = windowsObject\n        let browserPIDOccurrences = v2TopBrowserPIDOccurrences(in: windows)\n        let totalPIDs = v2AnnotateTopWindows(\n            &windows,\n            processSnapshot: processSnapshot,\n            browserPIDOccurrences: browserPIDOccurrences,\n            includeProcesses: includeProcesses\n        )\n        let aggregates = processAggregates(\n            from: processSnapshot,\n            totalPIDs: totalPIDs\n        )\n        let memoryDiagnostic = v2TopMemoryDiagnosticPayload(\n            processSnapshot: processSnapshot,\n            annotatedWindows: windows\n        )\n\n        var payload: [String: JSONValue] = [:]\n        payload[\"sample\"] = JSONValue(\n            foundationObject: processSnapshot.samplePayload()\n        ) ?? .object([:])\n        payload[\"totals\"] = JSONValue(\n            foundationObject: processSnapshot.summaryPayload(for: totalPIDs)\n        ) ?? .object([:])\n        payload[\"memory_diagnostic\"] = JSONValue(\n            foundationObject: memoryDiagnostic\n        ) ?? .object([:])\n        payload[\"program_totals\"] = JSONValue(\n            foundationObject: aggregates.programs\n        ) ?? .array([])\n        payload[\"coding_agents\"] = JSONValue(\n            foundationObject: aggregates.codingAgents\n        ) ?? .array([])\n        payload[\"windows\"] = JSONValue(\n            foundationObject: windows\n        ) ?? .array([])\n        return payload\n    }\n\n}","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"cd"}}

It carries the merge hash,\n    the unfolded epic's id, a line or two of summary, what you handed on and any new backlog,\n    the members reclaimed in 7-1 and left in the first column,\n    the members left in 4-3 because the work beside you held the file, with that other work\n    named, and the wiki pages 7-4 changed — or that it changed none — and anything still\n    running that 11 could not finish.\n    **If that send fails** — the supervisor restarted, so its old name is gone — the report\n    must not be lost: leave the same text, `report: <epic>` at its head, on the epic with\n    `moai note <epic> -b -` and take it into the root with a commit with a path as in 2. Tell\n    the person watching that the report is on the epic; the next supervisor reads it there.\n    Then **say when the window can be cleared**, in one line to the person watching. The\n    context lives in the tracker, not in the conversation: issue bodies, notes, review texts,\n    commit messages. If you can see your own context usage, put that number in the line too.\n    **Say the opposite in the same line** — not to clear while a review is running in the\n    background, while a merge conflict is being resolved, while waiting on a person's answer,\n    or after the supervisor's next message has arrived in this window. Clearing (`/clear`) then\n    loses what is not yet moved into the tracker, or the message that arrived.\n    Then end the turn. The supervisor's next message is the next work\n\n## Carrying on stalled work\n\nA session died holding a member of `<epic>`, the epic the message's first line names; that\nmember still stands picked up. {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n '1,60p' /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-raven-Works-Projects2-moai/fa832c96-fa4b-42be-96a4-d574a5501beb/scratchpad/cmux-src/v0.65.0/CLI/CMUXCLI+LocalZellij.swift","description":"Read how cmux integrates local zellij sessions"},"toolOutput":"import Darwin\nimport Foundation\n\n/// What zellij reports for a session this profile owns.\nenum LocalZellijSessionState: String {\n    /// Running in the private socket directory.\n    case live\n    /// Listed as stopped. cmux never attaches to it: a client's `zellij\n    /// attach` would resurrect it into a server started with that client's\n    /// environment.\n    case exited\n    /// zellij has no session by this name.\n    case stale\n}\n\n/// Registry, command builder, and process runner for one local-zellij command.\nstruct LocalZellijRuntime {\n    let registry: LocalTmuxSessionRegistry\n    let builder: LocalZellijCommandBuilder\n    let runner: LocalTmuxProcessRunner\n\n    /// Sessions zellij would attach to by name: live ones in the private\n    /// socket directory and exited ones it lists from its cache.\n    func sessions() throws -> [LocalZellijSessionListParser.Session] {\n        let result = try runner.run(arguments: builder.listSessionsArguments())\n        guard let sessions = LocalZellijSessionListParser().sessions(result) else {\n            throw CLIError(message: String(localized: \"cli.localZellij.error.listFailed\", defaultValue: \"local-zellij could not list sessions; liveness is unknown.\"))\n        }\n        return sessions\n    }\n\n    /// The single place that maps a record to zellij's view of its session.\n    func state(of record: LocalTmuxSessionRecord) throws -> LocalZellijSessionState {\n        Self.state(of: record, in: try sessions())\n    }\n\n    static func state(\n        of record: LocalTmuxSessionRecord,\n        in sessions: [LocalZellijSessionListParser.Session]\n    ) -> LocalZellijSessionState {\n        let zellijName = LocalZellijCommandBuilder.zellijSessionName(for: record)\n        guard let session = sessions.first(where: { $0.name == zellijName }) else { return .stale }\n        return session.exited ? .exited : .live\n    }\n}\n\nextension CMUXCLI {\n    /// Runs the opt-in local zellij profile. The ordinary terminal path never\n    /// enters this method. `client` is nil when the command runs without the\n    /// cmux app, which only actions that `canRunWithoutCmux` do.\n    func runLocalZellijCommand(\n        commandArgs: [String],\n        client: SocketClient?,\n        jsonOutput: Bool,\n        idFormat: CLIIDFormat,\n        windowOverride: String? = nil\n    ) throws {\n        var invocation = try LocalZellijInvocation.parse(commandArgs)\n        if let windowOverride,\n           invocation.attachRequest.window == nil,","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

On Linux the tty can come from /proc/<pid>/stat field 7 (tty_nr)\n   compared with os.stat(pane_tty).st_rdev.\n\n6. guide.rs:2308 (SESSIONS `out()`): `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, text=True, ...)` needs Python 3.7+; on 3.6\n   (RHEL/Alma/Rocky 8 /usr/bin/python3, Ubuntu 18.04) it raises TypeError, which `except OSError` does not catch, so the map dies\n   with a traceback partway through its rows (old script ran on 3.6).\n\n7. guide.rs:2336 (SESSIONS cmux `top` call) and the version gate prose (cmux() \"## First, the version\" ~2626-2631, recover() §6\n   ~2996-2998): when `cmux top` gives no JSON (socket unreachable, sandbox, old cmux) `except ValueError: pass` silently makes\n   every alive row `-` (\"not in a cmux tab of yours\"); and `cmux capabilities` failing with \"Socket not found\" reads as\n   \"methods do not list surface.input_state\" → the agent tells the person to update cmux (which restarts every session).\n\n8. guide.rs:2579 (CMUX_EMPTY_BOX): \"empty only when the answer reads `\\\"state\\\": \\\"empty\\\"` and `\\\"waiting_on_human\\\": false`\" —\n   `cmux rpc` prints Foundation pretty JSON with a space before the colon (`\"state\" : \"empty\"`), so a literal match never succeeds\n\n... [20 lines truncated] ...\n\n    planted, so this is a behaviour change for every cmux user (CLAUDE.md: \"동작 변경(Changed)도 minor 다\"; 0.13.0 filed the tmux\n    equivalent under ### Changed).\n\n## Tests\n\n13. guide.rs:5753 (the_session_map_reads_the_records): the private tmux socket `s.path().join(\"tmux.sock\")` under\n    $TMPDIR/moai-tmux-session-map-<pid>-ThreadId(<n>)-<nth>/ is measured at exactly 103 bytes in a full macOS run; macOS\n    sun_path allows 103; one more digit (Scratch counter ≥ 100, ThreadId ≥ 1000, longer TMPDIR) makes `tmux new-session` fail\n    (\"File name too long\") and the test panic.\n\n14. guide.rs:~5973 (the_cmux_skill_touches_only_named_surfaces): the supervisor-citation check asserts `named >= 1`, while\n    supervise() cites five moai-cmux sections (tmux's twin asserts `>= 5`) — four citations could break unnoticed.\n\n15. src/init_choice.rs:837: `assert!(f.plan().changes_optional(&[\"moai-tmux\"]), …)` — with OPTIONAL now 2 and\n    `pre = Defaults { optional: [Some(true); N], .. }`, `with` = [\"moai-cmux\"] makes changes_optional true via the `with`\n    clause alone; the assertion no longer tests the `without` clause it was written for.\n\n16. guide.rs:~5900-5912 and the recover test: recover's new never-clause (\"inside cmux never `close-surface`, `close-workspace`\n    or `close-window`, and never `--force`\", ~2853) is pinned by no test; `let version = &text[text.find(\"## First, the\n    version\")..]` runs to the end of the text instead of using `section()`.\n\n## Cleanup\n\n17. guide.rs:5842-5851: `cmux_calls` and its doc were inserted between the doc comment of `the_tmux_skill_touches_only_named_panes`\n    and its `#[test]`; the tmux test's doc (moai-u99i rationale) now prefixes cmux_calls's doc, and the tmux test has none.\n\n18. src/skill.rs:1618-1620 and the `detected_in` doc (~87): the test still builds `Optional { name: \"moai-cmux\", sign: |var|\n    var.starts_with(\"CMUX_\") }` and asserts CMUX_SOCKET_PATH alone yields [\"moai-cmux\"] — the opposite of the shipped sign\n    (`var == \"CMUX_SURFACE_ID\"`) and of the new OPTIONAL doc; the doc still says cmux is not yet in the list.\n\n19. Test duplication: cmux test re-types `never_kills_nor_runs_headless` slicing and its headless loop; the citation parser is a\n    verbatim copy of the tmux test's; `cmux_calls` re-implements `tmux_calls`; its `text.replace(SESSIONS, \"\")` + comment guard\n    nothing (only 4-space-indented lines count).\n\n20. Skill-text duplication: recover() §6 hand-copies cmux()'s version gate, new-split line + OK-line reading, equalize call;\n    cmux() copies tmux()'s clear gates / paste policy — the repo's rule for shared text is a const (`SESSIONS`, `EMPTY_BOX`,\n    `CMUX_EMPTY_BOX`).\n\n21. Efficiency: \"Label the tab\" has the agent print `cmux --json --id-format both tree --all` (~64 KB here) to read one title per\n    tab; capabilities prints the full method list for one yes/no; SESSIONS spawns ps/tmux per record.\n\n22. SESSIONS style: the two `if alive …` branches are mutually exclusive (`cmux = not mine and …`) but written as independent ifs;\n    `mine` no longer holds a socket; whitespace is folded on both sides separately.\n\n23. Commit 94b973a1 (subject moai-p5sz.lz0) also carries the regenerated plugin copies for the two moai-p5sz.7q3 commits\n    (CLAUDE.md \"한 커밋은 한 가지 일이다\").\n\n24. guide.rs:1205 (AGENTS block): \"Each is planted only where it is chosen: `moai skill install --with moai-tmux` plants it\" names\n    only moai-tmux; the block's \"Only the supervisor skill, inside tmux or cmux, may … open one\" contradicts moai-recover opening\n    panes/tabs (pre-existing for tmux).","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"cat"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"cat /Users/raven/Works/Projects2/moai/.worktrees/moai-p5sz/src/scratch.rs; echo \"TMPDIR=$TMPDIR\"; echo -n \"$TMPDIR\" | wc -c; tmux -V; id -u","description":"Read scratch helper and check TMPDIR, tmux version"},"toolOutput":"//! 시험이 쓰는 임시 디렉터리 한 벌(moai-shgx). **시험에서만 선다.**\n//!\n//! ## 왜 한 벌인가\n//!\n//! 같은 것이 다섯 벌 있었다 — `tui/register.rs`·`tui/layer.rs`·`tui/mod.rs`·\n//! `user_config.rs` 와 통합 시험의 것. 앞의 넷과 `cmd/tui.rs` 의 편집기 시험 자리는\n//! 이것으로 모았다. **통합 시험(`tests/cli.rs`)의 `Scratch` 는 아직 따로다** — 따로 된\n//! 크레이트라 `use` 로는 못 가져가고, 뿌리([`base`])만 `#[path]` 로 이 파일을\n//! 읽어 함께 쓴다. 울타리는 안 쓴다(moai-izeo 뒤로 그쪽에서 [`fence`] 를 부르지 않는다).\n//! 그래서 **이 파일의 단위 시험은 그쪽에서도 컴파일돼 돈다** — 여기 더하는 시험은 `crate::` 의\n//! 다른 모듈을 쓰지 못한다(그쪽 크레이트에는 없다). 그리고 **모으지 않은 자리**(`git.rs`·\n//! `store.rs`·`worktree.rs`)는 끝에서 `remove_dir_all` 을 부르는 식이라, 시험이\n//! 패닉하면 그 줄에 닿지 못해 `/tmp/moai-git-<pid>` 가 그대로 남는다. 이름에 pid 가\n//! 들어 다음 판이 그것을 치우지도 않는다 — 이 기계에 죽은 pid 의 것 셋이 남아 있었다.\n//!\n//! `Drop` 은 패닉으로 풀릴 때도 돈다. 그래서 치우는 일은 **놓을 때** 한다.\n//!\n//! ## 자리\n//!\n//! `std::env::temp_dir()` 다 — **그것이 어느 체크아웃 안이면 밖으로 옮긴다**([`base`], moai-izeo).\n//! **`CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` 은 여기서 못 쓴다** — cargo 는\n//! 그것을 통합 시험·벤치 타깃에만 주고, 이 모듈은 바이너리 타깃의 단위 시험으로\n//! 컴파일되므로 `option_env!` 가 늘 `None` 이었다(`tests/cli.rs` 는 통합 시험이라\n//! `env!` 로 그것을 곧바로 읽는다). 있는 척하는 갈래는 걷어냈다.\n//!\n//! 일부러 저장소 안(`target/` 밑)으로 옮기지는 않는다 — 위의 `.git` 이 꼭대기로 잡혀 moai-46xz 가\n//! 통째로 돌아오고, 위의 `.moai` 는 그보다 나쁘다(moai-izeo: 시험이 바깥 트래커에 실제로 썼다).\n//! [`Scratch::fenced`] 는 그래서 남는다 — **자리를 고르는 시험**(`layer`·`worktree`·`git`)이 제\n//! 자리를 저장소 꼭대기로 세울 때 쓴다. 울타리는 자리째 `Drop` 이 치운다 — 체크아웃 안에 커밋\n//! 없는 저장소가 남으면 그 체크아웃의 `git add -A` 가 거기서 멈춘다([`fence`]).\n\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\n/// 시험 하나가 쓰는 디렉터리. 놓을 때 지운다.\n///\n/// 이름에 pid·스레드·셈을 함께 넣는다 — pid 만으로는 한 판 안의 스레드 둘이 같은 자리를\n/// 잡고, 한쪽의 `Drop` 이 다른 쪽이 쓰는 자리를 지운다.\npub struct Scratch(PathBuf);\n\nimpl Scratch {\n    /// `<자리>/moai-<이름>-<pid>-<스레드>-<셈>` 을 만든다. 이미 있으면 지우고 새로 만든다.\n    ///\n    /// **울타리는 없다.** [`base`] 가 체크아웃 밖임을 보장하므로 위에 잡힐 `.git` 도 `.moai` 도\n    /// 없다(moai-izeo). 울타리를 골라 치던 자리다 — 그것은 `.git` 훑기만 세웠고, `.moai` 를\n    /// 찾아 오르는 쪽은 그대로 바깥 트래커를 잡았다.\n    pub fn new(name: &str) -> Scratch {\n        Scratch::in_place(&base(), name)\n    }\n\n    /// 자리를 받아 세운다. 이름 짓는 법은 [`Scratch::new`] 와 같다. 울타리는 없다 —\n\n... [269 lines truncated] ...\n\n    ///\n    /// 이 줄은 [`base`] 가 이미 본 것을 다시 보는 것이라 혼자서는 못 무너진다 — 무엇을 표식으로\n    /// 세는지는 [`a_tracker_above_counts_as_inside_too`] 가, 옮기는 갈래는\n    /// [`a_base_inside_a_checkout_moves_out_or_says_why`] 가 잰다. 여기서 재는 것은 그 셋이 실제\n    /// 기계에서 한 답으로 모이는가다.\n    #[test]\n    fn the_base_is_never_inside_a_checkout() {\n        assert!(!inside_checkout(&base()), \"임시 자리가 체크아웃 안이다 — {}\", base().display());\n        assert!(!inside_checkout(Scratch::new(\"outside\").path()));\n    }\n\n    /// **위의 `.moai` 도 \"안\" 이다**(moai-izeo). 울타리는 `.git` 만 세웠는데 moai 는 `.moai` 를\n    /// 찾아 오르므로, `.git` 만 보는 자는 git 아닌 moai 프로젝트 밑에 선 임시 자리를 \"밖\" 이라\n    /// 답한다 — 그 기계에서 시험이 그 사람의 트래커를 읽고 **쓴다**(moai-595o).\n    #[test]\n    fn a_tracker_above_counts_as_inside_too() {\n        let outer = Scratch::new(\"tracker-outer\");\n        let under = outer.join(\"tmp\");\n        std::fs::create_dir(&under).unwrap();\n        assert!(!inside_checkout(&under), \"표식이 하나도 없는데 안이라 했다\");\n        std::fs::create_dir(outer.join(\".moai\")).unwrap();\n        assert!(inside_checkout(&under), \"위의 .moai 를 못 봤다 — 시험이 바깥 트래커를 잡는다\");\n    }\n\n    /// **옮기는 갈래와 실패하는 갈래를 실제로 돌린다**(moai-izeo). [`base`] 는 `TMPDIR` 을 한\n    /// 판에 한 번만 보므로 뿌리로는 이 둘을 못 재고, 그래서 [`pick`] 이 자리를 받는다.\n    #[test]\n    fn a_base_inside_a_checkout_moves_out_or_says_why() {\n        let outer = Scratch::fenced_in(&base(), \"pick-outer\");\n        let inside = outer.join(\"tmp\");\n        std::fs::create_dir(&inside).unwrap();\n        let away = Scratch::new(\"pick-away\");\n\n        // 밖이면 준 자리를 그대로 쓴다 — 갈 곳을 안 줘도 그렇다.\n        assert_eq!(pick(away.path().to_path_buf(), &[]).unwrap(), away.path());\n        // 안이면 밖으로 옮긴다. **링크를 푼 철자로** 넘긴다.\n        let moved = pick(inside.clone(), &[away.path()]).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(moved, std::fs::canonicalize(away.path()).unwrap(), \"링크를 안 풀고 넘겼다\");\n        // 갈 곳이 못 쓰는 자리뿐이면 그 자리를 건너뛴다 — 있기만 한 것을 보고 옮기지 않는다.\n        let gone = outer.join(\"없다\");\n        assert!(pick(inside.clone(), &[gone.as_path()]).is_err(), \"못 쓰는 자리로 옮겼다\");\n        // 갈 곳이 다 체크아웃 안이면 크게 실패한다 — 조용히 눌러앉지 않는다.\n        let why = pick(inside.clone(), &[inside.as_path()]).unwrap_err();\n        assert!(why.contains(\"TMPDIR\"), \"고칠 길을 안 댄다 — {why}\");\n    }\n}\nTMPDIR=/var/folders/9f/83nfw03936q9kj62x1mnxwb00000gn/T/\n      49\ntmux 3.4\n501","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"cat"}}

exec bash' 몫). --focus 는 기본이 false 라 포커스를 안 뺏는다\n- --id-format both 로 새 surface 의 UUID 를 받는다 — 기본 refs 꼴은 UUID 를 지운다.\n  다 연 뒤 rpc workspace.equalize_splits 로 한 번 고르게 한다(tmux 의 tiled 몫, CLI\n  동사가 없다)\n- 감독의 2·4 가 cmux 갈래를 댄다\n\nRefs: moai-p5sz.vxb\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n\n8a7f3fb5 feat(skill): moai-cmux 가 일꾼 창을 비우고 닿지 않은 메시지를 붙인다 (moai-p5sz.cwj)\n- 비우기는 moai-tmux 의 세 조건(보고 확인·idle·빈 입력 칸)을 그대로 지킨다.\n  send 는 \\n 을 Enter 로 읽어 /clear 를 한 번에 치고 누른다 — 두 번에 나누면 둘째\n  send-key 앞의 입력 칸에 /clear 가 서서, 가드가 그것을 초안으로 읽을 자리가 생긴다\n- 붙이기는 사람 결정대로 cmux paste --surface --submit -- - < <file> 다. 한 덩이로\n  붙이고 cmux 가 150ms 뒤 제출 키를 따로 친다(v0.65.0 소스). 거절은 답이다 —\n  --force 로 밀지 않고 다시 치지 않는다\n\n... Claude Code 가 darwin 기록에 적는\n  procStart 는 LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC ps -o lstart= 의 글이라 그것과 견준다(2026-10-11\n  실제 기록 넷과 맞춰 봄). 날이 한 자리면 빈칸이 둘이라 빈칸을 접어 견준다\n- 다른 tmux 서버를 거르던 /proc/<pid>/environ 비교를 칸의 #{pane_tty} 와\n  프로세스 tty 비교로 바꾼다. macOS 에 그 파일이 없고, 남의 프로세스 환경을 읽는\n  일은 자동 모드 분류기가 비밀 뒤지기로 막는다 — 감독이 짝을 돌리다 막힐 자리였다.\n  tty 가 같으면 그 칸에서 도는 프로세스라 서버만 견주던 것보다 한 걸음 더 잰다\n- 시험이 macOS 에서도 돈다. 시험용 tmux 서버를 -S 소켓으로 따로 띄워, 부르는 쪽\n  서버의 칸에서 도는 세션이 그 칸을 받는지까지 잰다\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"cd"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"cd /Users/raven/Works/Projects2/moai/.worktrees/moai-p5sz; sed -n '1,80p' CHANGELOG.md","description":"Print the top of CHANGELOG.md"},"toolOutput":"# Changelog\n\nAll notable changes to this project are documented here. The format follows\n[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and this project uses\n[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).\n\n`scripts/bump-version.sh auto` moves whatever has accumulated under\n`[Unreleased]` into a new release section and leaves `[Unreleased]` empty for the\nnext one. The headings pick the version: before 1.0, `Fixed` and `Security` alone\nmake a patch release and anything else a minor one. It does not commit and it\ndoes not tag — see `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\n## [Unreleased]\n\n### Added\n\n- **A second optional Claude Code skill, `moai-cmux`, for a supervisor running\n  inside [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux).** It is `moai-tmux` for\n  cmux tabs: it finds each worker's surface (`cmux top` says which surface a\n  session runs in), labels its tab once you say labels are wanted, clears a\n  reported worker's window, pastes a message `SendMessage` could not deliver\n  (`cmux paste --submit`), reads why a worker stalled, and — only after asking —\n  opens new worker splits running an ordinary interactive `claude`. It reads the\n  input box through cmux's own `surface.input_state` and never types over\n  anything in it, never closes a tab, never moves focus and never passes\n  `--force`. **It needs cmux 0.65.0 or later** and checks that itself; on an\n  older cmux it says so and does nothing. Running tmux inside a cmux tab stays\n  `moai-tmux`'s case. Plant it with `moai skill install --with moai-cmux`, or\n  its row in the first `moai init` (checked when `$CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set).\n  `moai-recover` opens a tab per session inside cmux the same way. (moai-p5sz)\n\n### Fixed\n\n- **`moai-tmux` and `moai-recover` found no session on a Mac.** Their session\n  map read the process start time from `/proc`, which macOS does not have, so\n  every session read as dead. It now compares the start time Claude Code writes\n  on a Mac (`ps -o lstart`), and matches a session to a tmux pane by its\n  terminal (`#{pane_tty}`) instead of reading the process's environment — which\n  also no longer trips Claude Code's auto-mode guard against reading other\n  processes' environments. (moai-p5sz.7q3)\n\n## [0.13.0] - 2026-10-10\n\n### Added\n\n- **A fourth Claude Code skill, `moai-tmux`, planted only where you choose it.**\n  When the supervisor runs inside tmux it finds each worker's pane from\n  `~/.claude/sessions/`, labels it (pane option `@moai`), clears a reported\n  worker's window, pastes a message `SendMessage` could not deliver, reads why a\n  worker stalled and tells the person, and — only after asking — opens new\n  worker panes running an ordinary interactive `claude`. It never types over a\n  non-empty input box and never kills anything. Without `$TMUX` nothing\n  changes. It is the first *optional* skill: a plain `moai skill install`\n  plants it nowhere new, and only refreshes it where it is already planted.\n  (moai-u99i, moai-3r7l)\n- **Optional skills are chosen per repository.** `moai skill install --with\n  <skill>` plants one and `--without <skill>` removes it (both repeat, and take\n  names separated by commas); `moai skill uninstall --only <skill>` is the same\n  removal under the uninstall name, and brings up only the registrations that\n  already stand. `moai init --with <skill>` plants one with the rest, and the\n  first-init picker gets a row per optional skill under hooks · skills —\n  checked when it is already planted, or when your shell says you use it\n  (`$TMUX` for `moai-tmux`). Nothing records the choice: the planted skill is\n  the answer, and \"the planted skills differ\" no longer counts a left-out\n  optional skill as drift. (moai-3r7l)\n- **A fifth Claude Code skill, `moai-recover`, brings back the sessions that\n  died.** Asked by the person after a restart or an OOM kill, it finds the dead\n  sessions of the repository in `~/.claude/sessions/`, draws what each was doing\n  from its transcript, points out background work that never returned and a\n  `target` link whose `/tmp/cargo-target` directory was wiped, and resumes each\n  one — workers first, the supervisor last — in a new tmux pane running\n  `claude --resume <id>`, or, outside tmux, prints the line to type and the note\n  to paste. No new moai command. (moai-uqf7)\n\n### Changed\n\n- **The supervisor may type into worker panes inside tmux** where `moai-tmux`\n  is planted. This reverses the 0.9.0 rule that the supervisor types nothing\n  into a window; outside tmux, or without that skill, clearing a window is\n  still the person's. The AGENTS block now says the moai","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"cd"}}

(moai-u99i)\n\n## [0.12.0] - 2026-10-10\n\n### Added\n\n- **`moai show --sort` takes several fields, each with a direction, like\n  ORDER BY** — `--sort priority,updated:desc`, `--sort status:asc,title`. The\n  next field decides only where the ones before it tie; a field without\n  `:asc`/`:desc` keeps the direction it always had (newest first for created\n  and updated, urgent first for priority), so `--sort id` and every one-word\n  `--sort` order exactly as before. `--reverse` still turns the whole order\n  around, and `-n`/`--after` page through a multi-field order the same way. An\n  unknown field or direction, an empty field, or a field given twice is refused\n  with the words that are allowed. (moai-r170.9es)\n- **The explorer keeps its sort per project, as a list of fields** — a sort\n  picked inside a project is written for that project alone, as\n  `order = [...]` under `[tui.project.\"<project root>\"]` in the user config —\n  the root the project's tracker lives in, so a linked worktree shares its\n  project's sort — and one picked in the all-projects list (`0`) is written as `order` under\n  `[tui]`, the default for every project without its own. Entering a project\n  puts its own sort back; one sort no longer follows you from project to\n  project. `order` takes the words of `moai show --sort` (`\"updated:asc\"`)\n  except `id`, which the explorer does not sort by.\n  Where `order` is absent the older `sort`/`sort_reversed` pair is read as\n  before, and every write of `[tui] order` also writes that pair from its\n  first field, so an older moai on the same config shows the nearest order.\n  An `order` that cannot be read is named in one line and the older pair\n  stands. (moai-r170.8dz)\n- **The explorer sorts by several fields** — `SPC s P`, `C`, `U`, `S`, `A`\n  and `T` (uppercase) add that field at the end of the order with its own\n  direction, and pressing the same key again turns that field around; the\n  lowercase keys still make the order that one field. `SPC s e` opens a sort\n  window with all six fields, the ones in the order numbered and marked\n  `↑ asc` or `↓ desc`: `j`/`k` move, `J`/`K` move a field down or up the order,\n  `SPC` puts a field in or takes it out, `d` turns its direction, `Enter`\n  applies it where you stand, `D` also keeps it as the default (`[tui] order`)\n  even inside a project, and `Esc` leaves without a change. The path line\n  names the whole order, every field with `↑` or `↓`\n  (`sort priority↑, updated↓`). (moai-r170.x22)\n\n### Changed\n\n- **Where picked-up work stands is read from worktree names and pick-up marks\n  only, the way the hook reads it.** The `Place` line of `moai show` (`place`\n  and `workplaces` under `--json`) and the `stranded` warning of `moai status`\n  no longer read sibling worktrees' `.moai/issues.jsonl` — those are stale\n  copies, since every write goes to the main checkout. A worktree counts for a\n  row when its name points at the row or when `moai mv` picked the row up\n  inside it, and the explorer's `⎇` beside a row someone else holds now names","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"cd"}}

So a plain install refreshes the optional skills already\n  planted and plants no new one, and a first install plants none. Naming a\n  skill that is always planted, or one name in both, is refused.\n\n  The hooks are each agent's own: --agent codex plants `.codex/hooks.json`,\n----\n- **`moai-recover`** is what you call when the sessions died together — a\n  restart, an OOM kill — to bring them back where they stopped —\n  [Bring back sessions that died](#bring-back-sessions-that-died)\n- **`moai-tmux`** is what the supervisor loads when it runs inside tmux: it maps\n  a worker's `ListAgents` name to its pane and lets the supervisor label, clear\n  and paste into that pane, and open new worker panes once you say yes —\n  [In tmux](#in-tmux). It is planted only where you choose it\n- **`moai-cmux`** is the same for a supervisor running inside a\n  [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux) tab: it maps a worker to its cmux\n  surface, labels the tab, clears and pastes, and opens new worker splits once\n  you say yes — [In cmux](#in-cmux). Anything else — a word, a pasted block, a half-typed command — is the\nperson's, and if you cannot tell the placeholder from their draft, it is theirs. The execution\ntransport, machine placement, physical attempt, and recovery truth remain with\ntheir existing owners rather than being duplicated into a second CMUX ledger.\n\n## Draft Guard\n\nBefore writing, `send`, `send-panel` and `paste` (and `send --paste`) ask the\napp for `surface.input_state` and refuse when an agent's prompt holds text\nsomeone is typing, or when a question or permission dialog is open in an\nagent. `send-key` and `send-key-panel`, and `send` of text that only presses\nEnter, refuse only for an open dialog: `cmux send \"text\"` followed by\n`cmux send-key enter` leaves the sent text in the prompt, and the key has to\ngo through. Surfaces without an agent are never blocked. A refusal writes nothing, prints the reason on stderr\nand exits non-zero. `--force`, before the text or key, skips the check. When\nthe app can't answer `surface.input_state` (an older build, or a `cmux ssh`\nrelay, which doesn't forward it) the commands write as before.\n\n`surface.input_state` is a v2 worker-lane socket method. It takes\n`surface_id`, or the usual workspace selectors for that workspace's focused\nsurface, and returns:\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| `state` | `empty`, `draft`, `dialog`, or `unknown` when no agent prompt is on screen. Read from the active screen (not the scrolled viewport): Claude Code's and Codex's input rows, ignoring faint placeholder text, and key hints such as \"Esc to cancel\" below the input row. |\n| `draft_length` | Characters in the draft, when `state` is `draft`. The text itself is not returned. |\n| `agent` | Whether an agent reports lifecycle state for the surface. |\n| `lifecycle` | The agent's lifecycle: `unknown`, `running`, `idle` or `needsInput`. |\n| `waiting_on_human` | `lifecycle` is `needsInput`. Informational: it can stay set after an interrupt or an API error, so it does not block on its own. |\n| `blocks_typing` | Typing text now could disturb a human: a draft or a dialog, on a surface that runs an agent. |\n| `terminal` | Whether the surface is a terminal. |\n\n## Surface Selection Contract\n\n`surface.read_selection` is a v2 worker-lane socket method advertised by\n`system.capabilities` and printed by `cmux capabilities`. It accepts the usual\nsurface routing selectors (`window_id`, `workspace_id`, `surface_id`,\n`terminal_id`, `tab_id`, and `pane_id`) without focusing a window, workspace,\npane, or surface.\n\nSuccessful responses use one shape across surface kinds:","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"cd"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 6086,6116p src/guide.rs","description":"Read recover test pinning cmux lines"},"toolOutput":"        // 짝은 하나다 — `~/.claude/sessions` 를 읽는 둘째 파이썬이 서면 기록의 꼴이 바뀌는 날 한쪽만 고쳐진다.\n        assert_eq!(text.matches(\"~/.claude/sessions/*.json\").count(), 1, \"세션 기록을 읽는 짝이 둘이다\");\n        // 띄우는 줄은 셋 — tmux 칸, cmux 탭(moai-p5sz.kfi), 둘 밖에서 사람이 칠 줄. 깃발은 `--resume` 하나다. 코드 줄에서\n        // `claude ` 를 든 줄을 다 센다 — `--resume` 앞에 다른 깃발(`--model …`)을 끼운 줄도 걸려야 한다.\n        let launches: Vec<&str> = text.lines().filter(|l| l.starts_with(\"    \") && l.contains(\"claude \")).collect();\n        assert_eq!(\n            launches,\n            [\n                \"    tmux split-window -P -F '#{pane_id}' -t \\\"$TMUX_PANE\\\" -c <cwd> 'claude --resume <sessionId>; exec bash'\",\n                \"    cmux --id-format both new-split right --surface \\\"$CMUX_SURFACE_ID\\\" --command 'cd <cwd> && claude --resume <sessionId>'\",\n                \"    cd <cwd> && claude --resume <sessionId>\",\n            ],\n            \"claude 를 띄우는 줄이 셋이 아니거나 다른 깃발이 섰다\"\n        );\n        for flag in [\"claude -p\", \"--dangerously\", \"--permission-mode\"] {\n            assert_eq!(text.matches(flag).count(), 1, \"{flag} 가 하지 않는 것 밖에도 섰다\");\n        }\n        let open = section(&text, \"## 5. Inside tmux — open a pane each\");\n        let tabs = section(&text, \"## 6. Inside cmux — open a tab each\");\n        let outside = section(&text, \"## 7. Outside tmux and cmux — say what to type\");\n        assert!(open.contains(\"paste-buffer -p -d -b moai-recover -t <pane>\"), \"여러 줄을 붙이기로 안 싣는다\");\n        assert!(outside.contains(\"open nothing\"), \"tmux·cmux 밖에서도 칸을 연다\");\n        // cmux 의 판은 제 글이 잰다 — `moai-cmux` 는 고른 사람에게만 서서 그 절을 대면 없는 글을 가리킨다.\n        assert!(tabs.contains(\"`cmux capabilities` lists `surface.input_state`\"), \"되살리기가 cmux 의 판을 안 잰다\");\n        assert!(\n            tabs.contains(\"    cmux paste --surface <surface> --submit -- - < <file>\"),\n            \"cmux 탭에 한 덩이로 안 붙인다\"\n        );\n        assert!(tabs.contains(\"(\\\"Is the input box empty\\\"\\nabove)\"), \"cmux 탭에 붙이기 전에 입력 칸을 안 본다\");\n        assert!(!text.contains(\"`moai-cmux`\"), \"되살리기가 심기지 않았을 수 있는 moai-cmux 를 댄다\");\n        // 빈 입력 칸의 잣대는 제 글 안에 선다 — `moai-tmux` 는 고른 사람에게만 심기니(moai-3r7l) 그 절을 대면 없는","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

You set which files and network domains those commands can reach, and the limits apply to Bash, PowerShell, and Monitor commands and the processes they start. Because the operating system applies the limits while a command runs, Claude Code can [run sandboxed commands without asking you](#sandbox-modes) to approve each one.\n19:  * To compare other isolation approaches such as dev containers, custom containers, and virtual machines, see [Sandbox environments](/docs/en/sandbox-environments)\n25:While the sandbox is on, the shell commands Claude runs start inside its boundary, and so do the processes they start. The sandbox is off by default. These tools and processes run outside it:\n43:* **Other processes Claude Code starts**: command [hooks](/docs/en/hooks), local [MCP servers](/docs/en/mcp), [plugin monitors](/docs/en/plugins/components#monitors), [LSP servers](/docs/en/tools-reference#lsp-tool-behavior), and helper commands such as your [status line](/docs/en/statusline) command and `apiKeyHelper` run with your full access\n47:* **Commands you type yourself**: a command you enter at the [`!` shell-mode prompt](/docs/en/interactive-mode#shell-mode-with-prefix) runs unsandboxed in most sessions. [Strict sandbox mode](#turn-off-the-retry-with-strict-sandbox-mode) lists the sessions where a command you type runs sandboxed\n49:* **Unsandboxed retries**: Claude can [ask to run a command unsandboxed](#the-unsandboxed-retry-escape-hatch), usually after it fails in the sandbox\n51:To put the tools, processes, and commands in this section behind one boundary, run the Claude Code process itself in a [container, virtual machine, or the sandbox runtime](/docs/en/sandbox-environments).\n57:* **macOS**: sandboxing uses the built-in Seatbelt framework, so you can go straight to the steps\n58:* **Linux and WSL2**: the sandbox relies on `bubblewrap` and `socat`, covered in [Set up Linux and WSL2](#set-up-linux-and-wsl2). Even if you haven't installed them yet, you can start with `/sandbox`, because its panel shows whether anything is missing\n61:  <Step title=\"Run /sandbox\">\n62:    Start a Claude Code session and run the `/sandbox` command:\n65:    /sandbox\n74:    If the panel shows only a Dependencies tab, a required package is missing. Install it as described in [Set up Linux and WSL2](#set-up-linux-and-wsl2), restart Claude Code, and run `/sandbox` again.\n78:    On the Mode tab, select auto-allow or regular permissions. Auto-allow runs sandboxed commands without prompting, and regular permissions keeps the regular permission prompts even when commands are sandboxed. See [Sandbox modes](#sandbox-modes) for which commands still prompt in auto-allow mode.\n88:    If sandboxed commands fail with `Operation not permitted` inside a container, see [Bubblewrap fails to start inside a container](#bubblewrap-fails-to-start-inside-a-container).\n92:When you select a mode in the panel, Claude Code saves it to your project's local settings at `.claude/settings.local.json`, which apply to the current project. Claude Code adds that file to your global gitignore when it saves a setting there. To enable the sandbox across all of your projects, set [`sandbox.enabled`](/docs/en/settings-reference#sandbox-enabled) to `true` in your user settings at `~/.claude/settings.json`. To enforce sandboxing for every developer in an organization, use [managed settings](#enforce-sandboxing-with-managed-settings).\n94:To change the sandbox for one session without writing to a settings file, start Claude Code with [`--settings`](/docs/en/settings#change-a-setting-for-one-session). For example, this command starts a sandboxed session in which Claude can't retry a blocked command outside the sandbox:\n97:claude --settings '{\"sandbox\": {\"enabled\": true, \"allowUnsandboxedCommands\": false}}'\n110:| `touch ~/sandbox-probe` | Fails with `Operation not permitted` on macOS, or `Read-only file system` on Linux and WSL2 |\n113:If Claude asks to retry a failed command outside the sandbox, decline the retry. If `touch` succeeds and your home directory isn't one of the directories the sandbox lets c\n... [2133 characters truncated] ...\nexcludedCommands`](#run-commands-outside-the-sandbox-with-excludedcommands) or because Claude [retries it unsandboxed](#the-unsandboxed-retry-escape-hatch).\n204:#### The unsandboxed retry escape hatch\n206:The unsandboxed retry is an escape hatch for commands that fail inside the sandbox, such as tools that are incompatible with it. When the sandbox blocks a network connection, Claude Code names the denied host in the command's result, so Claude sees what was blocked. Claude analyzes the failure and may retry the command with the `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` parameter.\n210:* **`bypassPermissions` mode**: the retry runs without a prompt\n213:* **`dontAsk` mode**: Claude Code denies the retry\n216:These rules and settings change who approves the retry:\n218:* **A matching allow rule**: if an allow rule such as `Bash(curl *)` matches the command, it also approves the retry, so the command runs outside the sandbox with no prompt\n219:* **An ask rule for the parameter**: add an [ask rule](/docs/en/permissions#match-by-input-parameter) for `Bash(dangerouslyDisableSandbox:true)` to be prompted on Bash retries. You get the prompt in auto mode and `bypassPermissions` mode too, and the rule takes precedence over a matching allow rule\n222:#### Turn off the retry with strict sandbox mode\n224:You can disable the unsandboxed retry by setting `\"allowUnsandboxedCommands\": false` in your [sandbox settings](/docs/en/settings-reference#sandbox-settings). With the retry disabled, Claude Code ignores the `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` parameter. While the sandbox is running, commands Claude runs are then sandboxed unless they match an `excludedCommands` entry. To keep Claude Code from running commands unsandboxed when the sandbox can't start, also set [`failIfUnavailable`](/docs/en/settings-reference#sandbox-failifunavailable). The `/sandbox` **Overrides** tab shows this setting as **Strict sandbox mode**.\n228:If you or your administrator disable the retry in managed settings or with the `--settings` flag, the sandbox becomes admin-required. Claude Code then ignores the settings in a repository's files that loosen the sandbox, `excludedCommands` entries included. [Repository settings under an admin-required sandbox](#repository-settings-under-an-admin-required-sandbox) lists them.\n233:* **A Linux session with [`CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB`](/docs/en/env-vars#variables) set**: every command runs sandboxed, shell-mode commands included\n247:By default, sandboxed commands can write to the current working directory, the per-user temp directory, and any [directories you've added](/docs/en/permissions#additional-directories-grant-file-access-not-configuration) with `--add-dir`, `/add-dir`, or `permissions.additionalDirectories`. If subprocess commands like `kubectl`, `terraform`, or `npm` need to write outside those directories, use `sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite` to grant access to specific paths:\n252:    \"enabled\": true,\n260:These paths are enforced at the OS level, so all commands running inside the sandbox, including their child processes, respect them. The tests at guide.rs:5946 and 6111 assert exactly this string. Generated copies: .claude/moai-plugin/skills/moai-cmux/SKILL.md:211 and moai-recover/SKILL.md:251.\ncmux v0.65.0, CLI/CMUXCLI+Paste.swift parsePasteCommandArguments: `for arg in rem2 { if pastTerminator { positional.append(arg); continue } switch arg { case \"--\": pastTerminator = true ... case \"-\": readsStandardInput = true ...`, then `parsed.text = positional.isEmpty ? nil : positional.joined(separator: \" \")`. The struct doc says it directly: `/// Positional text, or nil when the text comes from stdin (no positional text, or a lone `-` before any `--` separator).`\nNothing upstream strips `--`. The presentation parser keeps it and everything after it (Packages/.../CmuxCLIArgumentParser.swift: `if arg == \"--\" { pastTerminator = true; remaining.append(arg) ...`), and parseOption also stops at `--`. So commandArgs is [--surface, <uuid>, --submit, --, -], and text is \"-\".\nprepareStandardInputBeforeSocket drains stdin only `if parsed.text == nil`, and runPasteCommand does `if let positional = parsed.text { text = positional } else { text = try pasteTextFromStandardInput() }`. The redirected file is never read.\ncmux's own test pins this behaviour: cmuxCLITests/CLIPasteCommandTests.swift pasteTreatsTextAfterTheSeparatorLiterally runs [\"paste\",\"--surface\",\"surface:11\",\"--\",\"--submit\",\"-\"] and expects text == \"--submit -\" and submit_key == \"none\". The help text agrees: \"With no text argument, or with - before --, the text is read from stdin.\"\nTrigger: every use of either line. One case: SendMessage failed and the worker's box is empty. The other: recover section 6, once a resumed tab's box shows empty.\nWrong output: ensureAgentPromptIsFree passes because the box is empty. terminal.paste then gets text \"-\" with submit_key \"return\". The worker, or the freshly resumed session, receives a submitted one-character prompt \"-\". The message or recovery block never arrives, yet the skill then tells the person it was delivered.''',\n\"fix_notes\": r'''Replace both skill lines with `cmux paste --surface <surface> --submit - < <file>`. Keep the 7-space list indent at guide.rs:2755 and the 4-space indent at 3012. Change the asserts at guide.rs:5946 and 6111 to match, then regenerate the plugin copies with `moai skill install`.\n`cmux paste --surface <surface> --submit < <file>` (no text argument at all) is equivalent.\nOrder is free as long as everything comes before any `--`. parseOption pulls `--surface <v>` (or `--surface=<v>`) from anywhere before the terminator, and the loop accepts `--submit`, `--force` and `-` in any position. So `- --surface S --submit`, `--submit - --surface S` and `--surface S --submit - --` all read stdin.\nOnly two forms go wrong: `-` after `--`, which becomes the text \"-\", and `-` together with other positional text, which errors with \"paste: pass text or -, not both\".''',\n})\n\nout.append({\n\"candidate\": 4,\n\"verdict\": \"CONFIRMED\",\n\"evidence\": r'''Skill lines: guide.rs:2699 `    cmux rename-tab --surface <surface> --title '<worker> <id>'` and guide.rs:2705 `    cmux tab-action --surface <surface> --action clear-name`. Tests 5926 and 5929 pin both.\nCLI side, how workspace_id gets filled (CLI/cmux.swift):\n- runRenameTab forwards `[\"--action\", \"rename\", \"--title\", title]` plus `[\"--surface\", surfaceOpt]` to runTabAction.\n- runTabAction (~10767) sets `let workspaceArg = workspaceOpt ?? (windowRaw == nil ? ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment[\"CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID\"] : nil)`.\n- normalizeWorkspaceHandle returns a UUID unchanged (`if isUUID(trimmed) { return trimmed }`). normalizeTabHandle hands off to normalizeSurfaceHandle, which also returns the UUID unchecked when no window is given.\n- Then `if let workspaceId { params[\"workspace_id\"] = workspaceId }`. The help text says the same: \"--workspace <id|ref|index>   Workspace context (default: current/$CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID)\".\nServer side:\n- ControlCommandCoordinator+SystemTabAction.tabAction passes routingSelectors(params) into controlTabAction (Sources/TerminalController+ControlSystemContext2.swift). resolveTabManager picks the window that owns workspace_id.\n- rename: resolveSurfaceWorkspace (Sources/TerminalController+ControlSurfaceContext.swift) checks `if let wsId = routing.workspaceID { ... return tabManager.tabs.first(where: { $0.id == wsId }) }` before it looks at surface_id. Then `guard let tabTarget = workspace.controlTabTarget(for: surfaceId) else { return .tabNotFound(surfaceID: surfaceId) }`, and controlTabTarget does `guard panels[surfaceID] != nil else { return nil }`.\n- clear_name: controlTabActionResolveWorkspace also checks `routing.workspaceID` first, then `guard workspace.panels[surfaceId] != nil else { return .tabNotFound(surfaceID: surfaceId) }`.\nTrigger: the worker's surface is in another workspace (another sidebar row) or another window than the supervisor's own tab. It also fires when a labelled tab was moved after labelling, or when the supervisor's own tab moved (CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID is then stale).\nWrong output: \"not_found: Tab not found\" and a non-zero exit. The label never lands, and a label written earlier cannot be taken off, so it stays over Claude Code's own titles until the person clears it by hand. On macOS, started() is `ps -p <pid> -o lstart=` (2313). Then `alive = bool(start) and start == \\\" \\\".join(str(r.get(\\\"procStart\\\")).split())` (2346). So an unreadable start time, a missing procStart (str(None) == 'None'), or a record from another pidDomain all print `dead`. REPRO (verify2/repro2.sh): records for the probe shell, its parent, and this Claude Code process itself (pid 56179). With the real ps: `alive parent`, `alive self-shell`, `alive grandparent`, `dead gone`. With a fake `ps` first on PATH that prints nothing and exits 1: all four rows `dead`, exit=0, stderr empty. Under `sandbox-exec -p '(version 1) (allow default)'`: all four `dead`, exit 0. Python sees `PermissionError [Errno 1] Operation not permitted: 'ps'`, because setuid /bin/ps cannot be exec'd inside any Seatbelt sandbox. Against the real ~/.claude/sessions (states only, verify2/real_states.py): normally 4 of 4 alive, including this session's own record; under sandbox-exec 4 of 4 dead. THE TRIGGER IS REAL: when the Bash sandbox is on, Claude Code 2.1.296 runs commands as `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec -p <profile>`, and the profile has `(deny default ...)` and `(allow process-info* (target same-sandbox))`. The docs say the sandbox is opt-in: 'The sandbox is off by default. To turn it on, run /sandbox ... or set sandbox.enabled'. It is off in this session. On Linux it is bwrap with `--unshare-pid` and a fresh /proc (docs: 'a fresh /proc mount would hide' process information), so every host pid gives ENOENT and reads dead. CLAUDE CODE'S OWN RULE IS THE OPPOSITE: `function jjn(e,n){if(n===void 0)return!0;return g(n,$$e(e))}` and `function g(e,n){return n===void 0||n===e||T(e,n)}`. A missing recorded start, or a current start it cannot read, counts as alive. RECOVER TEXT: 'A **candidate** is a `dead` row with a `sessionId` whose `cwd` is the root or one of the worktrees' (2889). Both drop rules need a live row ('a live row carries the same `sessionId` ... **your own row included**'; 'a live row other than your own stands in that same `cwd`'), and none exists. 'Drop old crashes ... Keep the candidates whose transcript last moved around the same time' then keeps exactly the live sessions, whose transcripts are moving now, and sets the real old crashes apart. The person is asked only when several candidates share a cwd. And '**Their asking is the yes:** inside tmux or cmux you open the panes without asking again' (2842). Result: each live worker alone in its worktree, and a lone live root session (possibly the caller itself), is resumed with `claude --resume` into a second window. The map exits 0 with nothing on stderr, so the sandbox's unsandboxed retry (which reacts to visible failures) never starts. moai-tmux and moai-cmux read only alive rows, so they fail closed.\",\n \"fix_notes\": \"The stopgap is sound and does not break the_session_map_reads_the_records. Replaying the test's records against a patched copy (verify2/stopgap_check.py) gives byte-identical output for run(None) and run(other server). The cmux and tmux runs also carry alive rows (`plain`, `here`, `worker`). An all-dead set gives exit 1, empty stdout and one stderr line. Add a test case that pins it: on macOS a fake ps on PATH; on Linux only the `reused` record. FALSE FIRES happen only when the caller has no alive record of its own while other records exist: (a) its records go elsewhere (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, while the script hard-codes ~/.claude/sessions); (b) the session comes from a Claude Code version before records or procStart existed; (c) the record was written while Claude Code's own 1 s `ps` call timed out, so procStart was left out (transient); (d) the snippet is run by hand after everything died. `claude --resume` in a fresh process writes its own new <pid>.json with the same sessionId, so that case is covered. All of these fail closed. GAP: the stopgap misses partial misreads, where some rows read alive and others cannot be read, for example records from a container or host that shares ~/.claude, or a procStart format change after an upgrade. Those rows still become recover candidates. STRONGER: (1) add a third state `unknown` for an unreadable start, a missing procStart, or a record pidDomain that differs from ours, and have recover never treat it as a candidate. This mirrors Claude Code's own fail-alive rule. On Linux, compare the record's pid-namespace part with readlink('/proc/self/ns/pid'), because a hidden pid and a dead pid both give ENOENT. (2) Add a self-probe: if started(os.getpid()) is empty, refuse. This catches the macOS sandbox and a missing ps without relying on records. The input-box gate reads the surface's visible screen (TerminalController+SurfaceInputState.swift:55 `Self.agentPromptInputState(of: panel.surface)`). AGENTS 블록은 언제나 읽히는 산문이라 길어도 되고, SKILL.md\\n//! 는 언제 부르는가가 frontmatter 에 있고 본문이 한 화면이어야 한다. 그래서\\n//! **조각을 한 군데 두고 표면마다 필요한 만큼 엮는다.** 조각 안의 문장은\\n//! 어느 표면에서 읽어도 뜻이 서야 한다 — \\\"위에서 말했듯\\\" 같은 말을 넣지 않는다.\\n//!\\n//! 순수 모듈이다. 파일을 쓰는 것은 `cmd/init.rs` 와 `cmd/skill.rs` 가 한다.\\n\\n/// 규칙 다섯의 이름. **스킬이 적은 규칙과 훅이 낸 거절문이 같은 이름을 댄다** —\\n/// 다르면 막힌 쪽이 무엇을 어겼는지 두 번 읽어야 한다.\\npub const RULES: [&str; 5] = [\\n    \\\"New issues stay inside what you picked up\\\",\\n    \\\"Pick something up before you change the repository\\\",\\n    \\\"A review is an issue too\\\",\\n    \\\"Never kill the person's tmux server\\\",\\n    \\\"Ask before you pick up someone else's work\\\",\\n];\\n\\n/// 거절문의 머리. 스킬의 규칙 제목과 글자가 같다.\\npub fn rule_head(n: usize) -> String {\\n    format!(\\\"Rule {n} — {}.\\\", RULES[n - 1])\\n}\\n\\n/// 리뷰 이슈를 세운 뒤의 세 걸음. **훅의 거절문과 스킬이 이것을 그대로 쓴다.**\\n///\\n/// **여기 적힌 명령은 그대로 쳐서 지나가야 한다.** `-m` 없는 `done` 을 일러\\n/// 줘 결과가 없다고 막은 적이 있다 — 규칙이 제가 일러 준 명령을 막는 자리는\\n/// 규칙이 아니라 덫이다.\\n// **줄 잇기(`\\\\`)를 쓰지 않는다.** 그것은 개행과 함께 다음 줄의 앞 공백까지\\n// 먹어, 첫 명령만 왼쪽 끝에 붙는다.\\npub const REVIEW_STEPS: &str = concat!(\\n    \\\"  moai mv <id> in_progress      when the review starts\\\\n\\\",\\n    \\\"  moai note <id> -b - < <review text>   the reviewer's own words (summarize past 64KB)\\\\n\\\",\\n    \\\"  moai mv <id> done -m '<what you took in, what you handed on>'\\\",\\n);\\n\\n/// 리뷰 원문이 한 번에 적는 상한([`crate::model::MAX_TEXT_BYTES`])을 넘을 때의 길\\n/// (moai-b8aj, 2026-09-19 사용자 결정). **요약하되 요약이라고 밝힌다.** 원문 노트와 판단 노트를\\n/// 가르는 까닭이 리뷰어가 한 말과 이쪽이 정한 것을 가르는 데 있으니, 줄인 글은 줄였다고 적혀\\n/// 있어야 읽는 쪽이 둘을 안 섞는다. 건의 번호와 자리를 두는 것은 판단 노트가 \\\"3번\\\" 으로 가리키기\\n/// 때문이다. 규칙 3 의 글·참고 문서·`note` 의 거절문이 이 글을 쓴다.\\n///\\n/// **울타리와 들여쓰기를 지키라는 말이 함께 선다**(리뷰 moai-4u6b.5hl). 리뷰 원문은 일한 AI 줄의\\n/// 꼴을 그대로 옮겨 적고, [`crate::model::work_of`] 는 울타리와 들여쓰기로 그것을 예로 읽는다 —\\n/// 줄이면서 울타리를 풀면 아무도 안 한 일이 토큰째 통계에 선다. 저널은 덧붙이기만 하니 되돌릴\\n/// 길도 없다.\\n///\\n/// **첫 줄이 원문을 가리킨다**(2026-09-19 사용자 결정, 리뷰 moai-4u6b.5hl 13번). 크기만 적던 판은\\n/// 줄인 글만 남기고 원문으로 돌아갈 길을 안 남겼다 — 대화록 파일 이름은 끝났다는 알림의 `task-id`\\n/// 에만 실려 온다. 긴 집 경로는 기계마다 달라 안 싣고 `task-id` 만 싣는다.\\n///\\n/// **두 줄이다.** 싣는 쪽이 제 들여쓰기를 붙인다 — 한 줄로 두면 AGENTS 블록과 참고 문서에\\n/// 옆 줄의 두 배가 넘는 줄이 서고, 낱말 하나를 고쳐도 그 줄이 통째로 diff 에 뜬다.\\npub const REVIEW_OVER_LIMIT: &str = concat!(\\n    \\\"If the text runs past 64KB, summarize it — put `Summary: original <size>KB agent-<task-id>` on\\\\n\\\",\\n    \\\"the first line, keep every finding's number and place, and shorten only the sentences. Leave fences and indentation alone\\\",\\n);\\n\\n/// 리뷰 이슈에 붙는 태그. 훅은 리뷰 줄을 이 글자로 가르고, 가르치는 글은 같은\\n/// 글자로 세우게 한다 — 둘이 다르면 시킨 대로 세운 리뷰를 규칙이 못 알아본다.\\npub const REVIEW_TAG: &str = \\\"review\\\";\\n\\n/// 리뷰 이슈를 세우는 줄. `anchor` 는 `--parent <id>` 나 `-e <에픽>` 이다 — 규칙\\n/// 셋의 글과 두 거절문이 이 한 줄에서 나온다.\\npub fn make_review(anchor: &str) -> String {\\n    format!(\\n        \\\"moai add 'review — <what you are looking at>' -t {REVIEW_TAG} {anchor} -b '<what you are looking for and why\n... Find the dead\\\").expect(\\\"빈 입력 칸의 절이 1 앞에 안 선다\\\")];\\n        assert!(rule.contains(EMPTY_BOX) && tmux().contains(EMPTY_BOX), \\\"두 스킬이 빈 입력 칸의 잣대를 따로 적는다\\\");\\n        assert!(rule.contains(CMUX_EMPTY_BOX) && cmux().contains(CMUX_EMPTY_BOX), \\\"cmux 의 빈 입력 칸 잣대가 갈렸다\\\");\\n        assert!(\\n            EMPTY_BOX.contains(\\\"#{pane_in_mode}\\\") && 안 본다\\\");\\n        assert!(text.contains(\\\"**Their asking is the yes:**\\\"), \\\"되살려 달라는 말을 허락으로 안 읽는다\\\");\\n        assert!(text.contains(\\\"**Workers first, the supervisor last**\\\"), \\\"일꾼 먼저·감독 마지막의 차례가 없다\\\");\\n        assert!(\\n            text.contains(\\\"their names may have changed — run `ListAgents` again**\\\"),\\n            \\\"감독에게 일꾼의 이름이 바뀌었을 수 있다고 안 이른다\\\"\\n        );\\n        // 이미 되살아난 것은 거른다 — 같은 세션을 두 칸에서 되살리면 두 창이 한 대화를 이어 쓴다.\\n        assert!(text.contains(\\\"**Drop it when it is back already**\\\"), \\\"이미 되살아난 세션을 안 거른다\\\");\\n        // 사람이 감독을 먼저 되살려 그 창에서 부르면 제 줄이 그 id 를 든다 — 제 줄을 빼면 제 대화를 한 번 더 연다.\\n        assert!(text.contains(\\\"**your own row included**\\\"), \\\"제 줄이 든 id 를 이미 되살아난 것으로 안 읽는다\\\");\\n        // 루트에는 산 세션이 여럿 선다 — 같은 에이전트에게 주는 글. **한 출처다** — `init` 이 AGENTS.md 에 쓰는 블록,\\n//! `skill install` 이 심는 SKILL.md 와 참고 문서, 훅이 내는 거절문, 그리고 쓰기가\\n//! 막을 때의 거절문(`model::check_text_size`)이 모두 여기서 조각을 가져간다.\\n//!\\n//! 마지막 하나는 훅이 아니다 — `add`·`edit`·`mv -m`·`note` 가 모두 지나는 쓰기 검사라,\\n//! 여기서 리뷰 얘기를 길게 붙이면 제목이 큰 것을 막을 때도 그 글이 함께 나온다.\\n//!\\n//! ## 왜 한 출처인가\\n//!\\n//! 같은 것을 두 벌로 두면 반드시 갈라지고, 갈라진 둘 중 어느 것이 참인지\\n//! 아무도 모른다. 실제로 AGENTS 블록에는 `tui`·`edit` 이 있고 스킬에는\\n//! 없었으며, 스킬에는 규칙 셋이 있고 AGENTS 블록에는 없었다.\\n//!\\n//! ## 왜 그대로 복사하지 않는가\\n//!\\n//! 모양이 다르다. AGENTS 블록은 언제나 읽히는 산문이라 길어도 되고, SKILL.md\\n//! 는 언제 부르는가가 frontmatter 에 있고 본문이 한 화면이어야 한다. 그래서\\n//! **조각을 한 군데 두고 표면마다 필요한 만큼 엮는다.** 조각 안의 문장은\\n//! 어느 표면에서 읽어도 뜻이 서야 한다 — \\\"위에서 말했듯\\\" 같은 말을 넣지 않는다.\\n//!\\n//! 순수 모듈이다. 파일을 쓰는 것은 `cmd/init.rs` 와 `cmd/skill.rs` 가 한다.\\n\\n/// 규칙 다섯의 이름. **스킬이 적은 규칙과 훅이 낸 거절문이 같은 이름을 댄다** —\\n/// 다르면 막힌 쪽이 무엇을 어겼는지 두 번 읽어야 한다.\\npub const RULES: [&str; 5] = [\\n    \\\"New issues stay inside what you picked up\\\",\\n    \\\"Pick something up before you change the repository\\\",\\n    \\\"A review is an issue too\\\",\\n    \\\"Never kill the person's tmux server\\\",\\n    \\\"Ask before you pick up someone else's work\\\",\\n];\\n\\n/// 거절문의 머리. 스킬의 규칙 제목과 글자가 같다.\\npub fn rule_head(n: usize) -> String {\\n    format!(\\\"Rule {n} — {}.\\\", RULES[n - 1])\\n}\\n\\n/// 리뷰 이슈를 세운 뒤의 세 걸음. **훅의 거절문과 스킬이 이것을 그대로 쓴다.**\\n///\\n/// **여기 적힌 명령은 그대로 쳐서 지나가야 한다.** `-m` 없는 `done` 을 일러\\n/// 줘 결과가 없다고 막은 적이 있다 — 규칙이 제가 일러 준 명령을 막는 자리는\\n/// 규칙이 아니라 덫이다.\\n// **줄 잇기(`\\\\`)를 쓰지 않는다.** 그것은 개행과 함께 다음 줄의 앞 공백까지\\n// 먹어, 첫 명령만 왼쪽 끝에 붙는다.\\npub const REVIEW_STEPS: &str = concat!(\\n    \\\"  moai mv <id> in_progress      when the review starts\\\\n\\\",\\n    \\\"  moai note <id> -b - < <review text>   the reviewer's own words (summarize past 64KB)\\\\n\\\",\\n    \\\"  moai mv <id> done -m '<what you took in, what you handed on>'\\\",\\n);\\n\\n/// 리뷰 원문이 한 번에 적는 상한([`crate::model::MAX_TEXT_BYTES`])을 넘을 때의 길\\n/// (moai-b8aj, 2026-09-19 사용자 결정). **요약하되 요약이라고 밝힌다.** 원문 노트와 판단 노트를\\n/// 가르는 까닭이 리뷰어가 한 말과 이쪽이 정한 것을 가르는 데 있으니, 줄인 글은 줄였다고 적혀\\n/// 있어야 읽는 쪽이 둘을 안 섞는다. 건의 번호와 자리를 두는 것은 판단 노트가 \\\"3번\\\" 으로 가리키기\\n/// 때문이다. 규칙 3 의 글·참고 문서·`note` 의 거절문이 이 글을 쓴다.\\n///\\n/// **울타리와 들여쓰기를 지키라는 말이 함께 선다**(리뷰 moai-4u6b.5hl). 리뷰 원문은 일한 AI 줄의\\n/// 꼴을 그대로 옮겨 적고, [`crate::model::work_of`] 는 울타리와 들여쓰기로 그것을 예로 읽는다 —\\n/// 줄이면서 울타리를 풀면 아무도 안 한 일이 토큰째 통계에 선다. 저널은 덧붙이기만 하니 되돌릴\\n/// 길도 없다.\\n///\\n/// **첫 줄이 원문을 가리킨다**(2026-09-19 사용자 결정, 리뷰 moai-4u6b.5hl 13번). 크기만 적던 판은\\n/// 줄인 글만 남기고 원문으로 돌아갈 길을 안 남겼다 — 대화록 파일 이름은 끝났다는 알림의 `task-id`\\n/// 에만 실려 온다. 긴 집 경로는 기계마다 달라 안 싣고 `task-id` 만 싣는다.\\n///\\n/// **두 줄이다.** 싣는 쪽이 제 들여쓰기를 붙인다 — 한 줄로 두면 AGENTS 블록과 참고 문서에\\n/// 옆 줄의 두 배가 넘는 줄이 서고, 낱말 하나를 고쳐도 그 줄이 통째로 diff 에 뜬다.\\npub const REVIEW_OVER_LIMIT: &str = concat!(\\n    \\\"If the text runs past 64KB, summarize it — put `Summary: original <size>KB agent-<task-id>` on\\\\n\\\",\\n    \\\"the first line, keep every finding's number and place, and shorten only the sentences. Leave fences and indentation alone\\\",\\n);\\n\\n/// 리뷰 이슈에 붙는 태그. 훅은 리뷰 줄을 이 글자로 가르고, 가르치는 글은 같은\\n/// 글자로 세우게 한다 — 둘이 다르면 시킨 대로 세운 리뷰를 규칙이 못 알아본다.\\npub const REVIEW_TAG: &str = \\\"review\\\";\\n\\n/// 리뷰 이슈를 세우는 줄. `anchor` 는 `--parent <id>` 나 `-e <에픽>` 이다 — 규칙\\n/// 셋의 글과 두 거절문이 이 한 줄에서 나온다.\\npub fn make_review(anchor: &str) -> String {\\n    format!(\\n        \\\"moai add 'review — <what you are looking at>' -t {REVIEW_TAG} {anchor} -b '<what you are looking for and why>'\\\"\\n    )\\n}\\n\\n/// 리뷰를 닫는 두 걸음 — `REVIEW_STEPS` 에서 시작 걸음을 빼고 **실제 id** 를 넣은\\n/// 것. 닫기 거절문과 세션을 닫을 때의 붙듦이 쓴다. 손으로 다시 적던 두 자리는\\n/// 이미 서로 다른 글을 내고 있었다.\\n///\\n/// **`moai` 는 겨눌 트래커를 단 머리로 받는다**(moai-j2vp) — 남의 트래커를 보는 판에서 규칙 1 은\\n/// `moai -C /other` 를 대는데 이 줄만 맨 `moai` 를 내던 판은, 옮겨 친 두 줄이 이 트래커를 겨눠\\n/// 거기 없는 리뷰를 닫으라고 했다. 이 자리의 트래커면 맨 `moai` 다.\\npub fn close_steps(id: &str, moai: &str) -> String {\\n    // 머리는 줄마다 같다 — `map` 안에서 짓던 판은 줄 수만큼 다시 지었다. 줄의 **첫** `moai ` 만\\n    // 바꾼다: `REVIEW_STEPS` 의 줄은 들여쓰기 뒤 곧바로 그 낱말로 시작한다\\n    // (`the_skill_names_each_rule_as_the_hook_does` 가 그것을 못박는다).\\n    let head = format!(\\\"{moai} \\\");\\n    REVIEW_STEPS\\n        .lines()\\n        .skip(1)\\n        .map(|l| l.replace(\\\"<id>\\\", id).re\n... AGENTS 블록은 언제나 읽히는 산문이라 길어도 되고, SKILL.md\\n//! 는 언제 부르는가가 frontmatter 에 있고 본문이 한 화면이어야 한다. 그래서\\n//! **조각을 한 군데 두고 표면마다 필요한 만큼 엮는다.** 조각 안의 문장은\\n//! 어느 표면에서 읽어도 뜻이 서야 한다 — \\\"위에서 말했듯\\\" 같은 말을 넣지 않는다.\\n//!\\n//! 순수 모듈이다. 파일을 쓰는 것은 `cmd/init.rs` 와 `cmd/skill.rs` 가 한다.\\n\\n/// 규칙 다섯의 이름. **스킬이 적은 규칙과 훅이 낸 거절문이 같은 이름을 댄다** —\\n/// 다르면 막힌 쪽이 무엇을 어겼는지 두 번 읽어야 한다.\\npub const RULES: [&str; 5] = [\\n    \\\"New issues stay inside what you picked up\\\",\\n    \\\"Pick something up before you change the repository\\\",\\n    \\\"A review is an issue too\\\",\\n    \\\"Never kill the person's tmux server\\\",\\n    \\\"Ask before you pick up someone else's work\\\",\\n];\\n\\n/// 거절문의 머리. 스킬의 규칙 제목과 글자가 같다.\\npub fn rule_head(n: usize) -> String {\\n    format!(\\\"Rule {n} — {}.\\\", RULES[n - {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 320,400p /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-raven-Works-Projects2-moai/fa832c96-fa4b-42be-96a4-d574a5501beb/scratchpad/cmux-src/v0.65.0/Sources/TerminalController+ControlWorkspaceContext.swift","description":"Read equalize_splits server handler"},"toolOutput":"    /// land in the current workspace; that still reports `not_found` so tmux\n    /// `-` targets never resolve to the current workspace.\n    func controlSelectLastWorkspace(routing: ControlRoutingSelectors) -> ControlWorkspaceNavigationResolution {\n        guard let tabManager = resolveTabManager(routing: routing) else {\n            return .tabManagerUnavailable\n        }\n        guard let before = tabManager.selectedTabId else { return .notFound }\n        if let windowId = AppDelegate.shared?.windowId(for: tabManager) {\n            _ = AppDelegate.shared?.focusMainWindow(windowId: windowId)\n            setActiveTabManager(tabManager)\n        }\n        guard tabManager.navigateToLastFocused(),\n              let after = tabManager.selectedTabId,\n              after != before else { return .notFound }\n        let windowId = AppDelegate.shared?.windowId(for: tabManager)\n        return .resolved(workspaceID: after, windowID: windowId)\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Equalize\n\n    func controlEqualizeWorkspaceSplits(\n        routing: ControlRoutingSelectors,\n        orientationFilter: String?\n    ) -> ControlWorkspaceEqualizeResolution {\n        guard let tabManager = resolveTabManager(routing: routing) else {\n            return .tabManagerUnavailable\n        }\n        guard let ws = resolveWorkspace(routing: routing, tabManager: tabManager) else {\n            return .notFound\n        }\n        let tree = ws.bonsplitController.treeSnapshot()\n        let equalizeResult = tabManager.paneLayout.equalizeSplits(\n            in: tree,\n            controller: ws.bonsplitController,\n            orientationFilter: orientationFilter\n        )\n        return .resolved(workspaceID: ws.id, equalized: equalizeResult.didFullyEqualize)\n    }\n\n    /// Mirrors the legacy `v2ResolveWorkspace(params:tabManager:)` precedence\n    /// using the pre-resolved routing selectors: workspace, then surface, then\n    /// pane (same TabManager), then the selected workspace.\n    private func resolveWorkspace(\n        routing: ControlRoutingSelectors,\n        tabManager: TabManager\n    ) -> Workspace? {\n        if let workspaceId = routing.workspaceID {\n            return tabManager.tabs.first(where: { $0.id == workspaceId })\n        }\n        if let surfaceId = routing.surfaceID {\n            return tabManager.tabs.first(where: { $0.panels[surfaceId] != nil })\n        }\n        if let paneId = routing.paneID,\n           let located = v2LocatePane(paneId) {\n            guard located.tabManager === tabManager else { return nil }\n            return located.workspace\n        }\n        guard let workspaceId = tabManager.selectedTabId else { return nil }\n        return tabManager.tabs.first(where: { $0.id == workspaceId })\n    }\n\n    // MARK: - Remote\n\n    func controlResolveRemoteWorkspaceID(\n        routing: ControlRoutingSelectors,\n        requestedWorkspaceID: UUID?\n    ) -> UUID? {\n        let fallbackTabManager = resolveTabManager(routing: routing)\n        return requestedWorkspaceID ?? fallbackTabManager?.selectedTabId\n    }\n\n    func controlDisconnectWorkspaceRemote(\n        workspaceID: UUID,\n        clearConfiguration: Bool\n    ) -> ControlWorkspaceRemoteResolution {\n        guard let owner = AppDelegate.shared?.tabManagerFor(tabId: workspaceID),\n              let workspace = owner.tabs.first(where: { $0.id == workspaceID }) else {\n            return .notFound(workspaceID: workspaceID)\n        }\n        workspace.disconnectRemoteConnection(clearConfiguration: clearConfiguration)\n        let windowId = AppDelegate.shared?.windowId(for: owner)","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

The box is **empty** only when\\nthe answer's `state` is `empty` and its `waiting_on_human` is `false`. `draft` is text someone\\ntyped or pasted — the person's, even a half-typed word. `dialog` is a prompt or a menu standing\\nwhere the box was. `unknown` is a screen cmux cannot read as Claude Code's — a shell prompt, a\\nprocess that ended. `waiting_on_human` is cmux's note that the agent last asked for the person —\\na permission prompt, a question — and it stays `true` after an API error or an interrupt too.\\nNone of these is a box to type into, and neither is an error or an answer without `state`.\\\"#;\",\"originalFile\":\"//! 에이전트에게 주는 글. **한 출처다** — `init` 이 AGENTS.md 에 쓰는 블록,\\n//! `skill install` 이 심는 SKILL.md 와 참고 문서, 훅이 내는 거절문, 그리고 쓰기가\\n//! 막을 때의 거절문(`model::check_text_size`)이 모두 여기서 조각을 가져간다.\\n//!\\n//! 마지막 하나는 훅이 아니다 — `add`·`edit`·`mv -m`·`note` 가 모두 지나는 쓰기 검사라,\\n//! 여기서 리뷰 얘기를 길게 붙이면 제목이 큰 것을 막을 때도 그 글이 함께 나온다.\\n//!\\n//! ## 왜 한 출처인가\\n//!\\n//! 같은 것을 두 벌로 두면 반드시 갈라지고, 갈라진 둘 중 어느 것이 참인지\\n//! 아무도 모른다. 실제로 AGENTS 블록에는 `tui`·`edit` 이 있고 스킬에는\\n//! 없었으며, 스킬에는 규칙 셋이 있고 AGENTS 블록에는 없었다.\\n//!\\n//! ## 왜 그대로 복사하지 않는가\\n//!\\n//! 모양이 다르다. AGENTS 블록은 언제나 읽히는 산문이라 길어도 되고, SKILL.md\\n//! 는 언제 부르는가가 frontmatter 에 있고 본문이 한 화면이어야 한다. 그래서\\n//! **조각을 한 군데 두고 표면마다 필요한 만큼 엮는다.** 조각 안의 문장은\\n//! 어느 표면에서 읽어도 뜻이 서야 한다 — \\\"위에서 말했듯\\\" 같은 말을 넣지 않는다.\\n//!\\n//! 순수 모듈이다. 파일을 쓰는 것은 `cmd/init.rs` 와 `cmd/skill.rs` 가 한다.\\n\\n/// 규칙 다섯의 이름. **스킬이 적은 규칙과 훅이 낸 거절문이 같은 이름을 댄다** —\\n/// 다르면 막힌 쪽이 무엇을 어겼는지 두 번 읽어야 한다.\\npub const RULES: [&str; 5] = [\\n    \\\"New issues stay inside what you picked up\\\",\\n    \\\"Pick something up before you change the repository\\\",\\n    \\\"A review is an issue too\\\",\\n    \\\"Never kill the person's tmux server\\\",\\n    \\\"Ask before you pick up someone else's work\\\",\\n];\\n\\n/// 거절문의 머리. 스킬의 규칙 제목과 글자가 같다.\\npub fn rule_head(n: usize) -> String {\\n    format!(\\\"Rule {n} — {}.\\\", RULES[n - 1])\\n}\\n\\n/// 리뷰 이슈를 세운 뒤의 세 걸음. **훅의 거절문과 스킬이 이것을 그대로 쓴다.**\\n///\\n/// **여기 적힌 명령은 그대로 쳐서 지나가야 한다.** `-m` 없는 `done` 을 일러\\n/// 줘 결과가 없다고 막은 적이 있다 — 규칙이 제가 일러 준 명령을 막는 자리는\\n/// 규칙이 아니라 덫이다.\\n// **줄 잇기(`\\\\`)를 쓰지 않는다.** 그것은 개행과 함께 다음 줄의 앞 공백까지\\n// 먹어, 첫 명령만 왼쪽 끝에 붙는다.\\npub const REVIEW_STEPS: &str = concat!(\\n    \\\"  moai mv <id> in_progress      when the review starts\\\\n\\\",\\n    \\\"  moai note <id> -b - < <review text>   the reviewer's own words (summarize past 64KB)\\\\n\\\",\\n    \\\"  moai mv <id> done -m '<what you took in, what you handed on>'\\\",\\n);\\n\\n/// 리뷰 원문이 한 번에 적는 상한([`crate::model::MAX_TEXT_BYTES`])을 넘을 때의 길\\n/// (moai-b8aj, 2026-09-19 사용자 결정). **요약하되 요약이라고 밝힌다.** 원문 노트와 판단 노트를\\n/// 가르는 까닭이 리뷰어가 한 말과 이쪽이 정한 것을 가르는 데 있으니, 줄인 글은 줄였다고 적혀\\n/// 있어야 읽는 쪽이 둘을 안 섞는다. 건의 번호와 자리를 두는 것은 판단 노트가 \\\"3번\\\" 으로 가리키기\\n/// 때문이다. 규칙 3 의 글·참고 문서·`note` 의 거절문이 이 글을 쓴다.\\n///\\n/// **울타리와 들여쓰기를 지키라는 말이 함께 선다**(리뷰 moai-4u6b.5hl). 리뷰 원문은 일한 AI 줄의\\n/// 꼴을 그대로 옮겨 적고, [`crate::model::work_of`] 는 울타리와 들여쓰기로 그것을 예로 읽는다 —\\n/// 줄이면서 울타리를 풀면 아무도 안 한 일이 토큰째 통계에 선다. 저널은 덧붙이기만 하니 되돌릴\\n/// 길도 없다.\\n///\\n/// **첫 줄이 원문을 가리킨다**(2026-09-19 사용자 결정, 리뷰 moai-4u6b.5hl 13번). 크기만 적던 판은\\n/// 줄인 글만 남기고 원문으로 돌아갈 길을 안 남겼다 — 대화록 파일 이름은 끝났다는 알림의 `task-id`\\n/// 에만 실려 온다. 긴 집 경로는 기계마다 달라 안 싣고 `task-id` 만 싣는다.\\n///\\n/// **두 줄이다.** 싣는 쪽이 제 들여쓰기를 붙인다 — 한 줄로 두면 AGENTS 블록과 참고 문서에\\n/// 옆 줄의 두 배가 넘는 줄이 서고, 낱말 하나를 고쳐도 그 줄이 통째로 diff 에 뜬다.\\npub const REVIEW_OVER_LIMIT: &str = concat!(\\n    \\\"If the text runs past 64KB, summarize it — put `Summary: original <size>KB agent-<task-id>` on\\\\n\\\",\\n    \\\"the first line, keep every finding's number and place, and shorten only the sentence\n... AGENTS 블록은 언제나 읽히는 산문이라 길어도 되고, SKILL.md\\n//! 는 언제 부르는가가 frontmatter 에 있고 본문이 한 화면이어야 한다. 그래서\\n//! **조각을 한 군데 두고 표면마다 필요한 만큼 엮는다.** 조각 안의 문장은\\n//! 어느 표면에서 읽어도 뜻이 서야 한다 — \\\"위에서 말했듯\\\" 같은 말을 넣지 않는다.\\n//!\\n//! 순수 모듈이다. 파일을 쓰는 것은 `cmd/init.rs` 와 `cmd/skill.rs` 가 한다.\\n\\n/// 규칙 다섯의 이름. **스킬이 적은 규칙과 훅이 낸 거절문이 같은 이름을 댄다** —\\n/// 다르면 막힌 쪽이 무엇을 어겼는지 두 번 읽어야 한다.\\npub const RULES: [&str; 5] = [\\n    \\\"New issues stay inside what you picked up\\\",\\n    \\\"Pick something up before you change the repository\\\",\\n    \\\"A review is an issue too\\\",\\n    \\\"Never kill the person's tmux server\\\",\\n    \\\"Ask before you pick up someone else's work\\\",\\n];\\n\\n/// 거절문의 머리. 스킬의 규칙 제목과 글자가 같다.\\npub fn rule_head(n: usize) -> String {\\n    format!(\\\"Rule {n} — {}.\\\", RULES[n - 1])\\n}\\n\\n/// 리뷰 이슈를 세운 뒤의 세 걸음. **훅의 거절문과 스킬이 이것을 그대로 쓴다.**\\n///\\n/// **여기 적힌 명령은 그대로 쳐서 지나가야 한다.** `-m` 없는 `done` 을 일러\\n/// 줘 결과가 없다고 막은 적이 있다 — 규칙이 제가 일러 준 명령을 막는 자리는\\n/// 규칙이 아니라 덫이다.\\n// **줄 잇기(`\\\\`)를 쓰지 않는다.** 그것은 개행과 함께 다음 줄의 앞 공백까지\\n// 먹어, 첫 명령만 왼쪽 끝에 붙는다.\\npub const REVIEW_STEPS: &str = concat!(\\n    \\\"  moai mv <id> in_progress      when the review starts\\\\n\\\",\\n    \\\"  moai note <id> -b -
