Triggers on \"worker pane\", \"open a worker\", \"clear the worker\", \"일꾼 칸\", \"일꾼 창 열어\", \"칸 비워\".\n.claude/moai-plugin/skills/moai-wiki/SKILL.md:3:description: Use when the repository's manual (its wiki) has to catch up with what the work changed — at the end of an epic, or when a person asks. \"update the wiki\", \"write the manual\", \"document this\", \"위키 갱신\", \"매뉴얼 써\", \"문서화해 줘\", \"wiki 정리\". {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 2440,2530p src/guide.rs","description":"Read tmux() skill intro and body start"},"toolOutput":"///\n/// **moai-obxm 의 두 결정을 tmux 쓰는 사람에게만 뒤집는다.** \"창을 비우는 것은 사람의 몫 — 감독은 칸에 아무것도 치지\n/// 않는다\" 와 \"감독도 에이전트를 띄우지 않는다\" 였다. 이제 `$TMUX` 가 서 있으면 감독이 칸을 비우고, 닿지 않은\n/// 메시지를 붙이고, 사람이 그러라고 한 뒤에 새 일꾼 칸을 연다. 참인 쪽은 그대로다 — **바이너리는 아무것도 띄우거나\n/// 몰지 않고**(이 글은 스킬의 말일 뿐 새 명령이 없다), 헤드리스·`-p`·`--dangerously-*`·권한 모드 바꾸기는 없다.\n///\n/// **치기 전의 잣대는 하나다 — 입력 칸에 무엇이든 있으면 안 친다.** 옛 5-1 은 사람이 쓰던 초안을 건지느라 480줄이\n/// 되었다. 초안인지 자리글(placeholder)인지 못 가르면 있는 것으로 읽고 사람에게 말한다.\n///\n/// **칸은 언제나 짝([`SESSIONS`])에서 찾은 `%id` 로 겨눈다.** 사람의 tmux 서버라, 맨 `kill-*` 하나가 그 서버의 모든\n/// 세션을 죽인다(2026-09-18). 감독 제 칸·다른 저장소의 칸·시험 서버의 칸에는 치지 않는다.\n///\n/// **칸 이름표는 칸 사용자 옵션 `@moai` 다.** Claude Code 가 `pane_title` 을 제 화제로 덮어 써서 제목은 못 쓴다.\n/// 보일지는 바퀴마다 사람에게 묻고, 그렇다고 하면 **도는 서버의** `pane-border-format` 앞에 붙인다 — 사람의 설정\n/// 파일은 안 고친다.\n///\n/// Claude Code 에만 심는다([`crate::skill::Skill::claude_only`]) — 감독 스킬과 같은 까닭이다.\npub fn tmux() -> String {\n    format!(\n        r#\"---\nname: moai-tmux\ndescription: Use in Claude Code together with moai-supervise when the supervisor runs inside tmux ($TMUX is set) — to find a worker's pane from its ListAgents name, label it, clear a reported worker's window, deliver a message SendMessage could not, read why a worker stalled, and open new worker panes once the person says yes. Triggers on \"worker pane\", \"open a worker\", \"clear the worker\", \"일꾼 칸\", \"일꾼 창 열어\", \"칸 비워\".\n---\n\n# moai-tmux — the supervisor's hands on the workers' panes\n\nThis is the supervisor's (`moai-supervise`) companion **when it runs inside tmux** — `$TMUX`\nis set in its shell. Without `$TMUX` none of this applies: the supervisor works through\nmessages and the person — or, inside cmux, through `moai-cmux`. Nor does it apply when `$TMUX`\nstarts with `/tmp/cmux-`: that is cmux's own stand-in (`cmux claude-teams` sets it), and its\n`tmux` is cmux in disguise — that is `moai-cmux`'s. The tmux server here is **the\nperson's own**: every session they have lives on it, and every pane you touch is one they are\nlooking at.\n\n## What never happens\n\n- **No headless run.** A worker you open is an ordinary interactive `claude` the person can\n  see and type into. Never `claude -p`, never a `--dangerously-*` flag, never\n  `--permission-mode`. The moai binary launches and drives nothing; this skill is you\n  typing tmux commands where the person can watch\n- **Nothing is killed.** Never `kill-server`, `kill-session` or `kill-pane`, never `pkill`\n  or `killall` aimed at tmux — one bare `kill-server` once took down every session the\n  person had (hook rule 4, and the person's own guard hook refuses it too). A worker that\n  is done stays open; closing a pane is the person's\n- **Only a worker's pane.** Type only into a pane found through the session map below for a\n  worker of this repository — never your own pane (`$TMUX_PANE`), never a session of another\n  repository, never a test server's pane. Every call names its pane, `-t <pane>`, as `%N`\n- **Never over the person's words.** If a worker's input box holds anything, do not type into\n  it — tell the person\n- **Never in their place.** A permission prompt or a question in a worker's pane is the\n  person's to answer — you read it and tell them; you press no key\n- **No polling.** Every look below is one look. A second one comes after your next step, as\n  its own call — never a loop and never a `sleep`\n- **The person's tmux config file stays theirs.** What you set is on the running server\n\n## Which pane is which worker\n\n`ListAgents` names a session; tmux needs a pane. Claude Code keeps one record per process\nunder `~/.claude/sessions/`, and the lines below print one row per record, tab-separated:\n\n    state  name  pane  status  cwd  sessionId\n\n```sh\n{SESSIONS}\n```\n\n- **Read only `alive` rows.** A `dead` row is a record a process left behind — its pid is gone,\n  or now belongs to another process (the start time differs)\n- `name` is the `ListAgents` name, `pane` the `%N` that `-t` takes — `-` when that session\n  is not in tmux or runs on another tmux server than yours (pane ids are counted per server,\n  so another server's `%4` is a different pane here), and then this skill has nothing for\n  that worker\n- `cwd` is where the session stands: the root, or one of the worktrees `git worktree list`\n  names — wherever they stand. A row standing elsewhere is not a worker of this repository, whatever its name\n- `status` is `idle`, `busy` or another word. It has to agree with `ListAgents` where a step\n  below asks for `idle`\n- Your own row is the one whose pane is `$TMUX_PANE`\n\nRun it when a step below needs a pane, once.\n\n## Is the input box empty\n\n{EMPTY_BOX}\n\n**Then do not type. Tell the person which pane holds what, and go on as if this skill were not\nhere.**\n\n## Label the pane\n\nWhen you send work (the supervisor's 3), write the worker and the work onto its pane:","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

The box is **empty** only when\nthe answer's `state` is `empty` and its `waiting_on_human` is `false`, and the session map, run\nagain just before, still reads that session `alive` in that tab — cmux reads the screen alone,\nand a tab whose Claude Code has ended can still show its last box, and read `empty`, while a\nshell has the keyboard. `draft` is text someone typed or pasted — the person's, even a half-typed\nword. `dialog` is a prompt or a menu standing where the box was. `unknown` is a screen cmux\ncannot read as Claude Code's — a shell prompt, a process that ended. `waiting_on_human` is cmux's\nnote that the session last asked the person something — a permission prompt, a question — and\nit can stay `true` after an API error or an interrupt. `new-split --command` 는 `OK surface:<n> (<UUID>) workspace:<n> (<UUID>)` 를 내고 포커스를 안 뺏으며 `cd` 가 먹는다.\n///   짝은 새 세션을 그 UUID 에 잇는다\n/// - 갓 뜬 Claude 의 흐린 자리글(`Try \"…\"`)이 선 칸과 `/clear` 뒤의 칸은 `state` 가 `empty`, 친 초안은 `draft` 다. 부분\n///   슬래시 명령(`/cle`)도 `draft` 라 `/clear` 를 두 번에 나눠 치면 둘째 앞에서 칸이 초안이 된다 — 한 번에 친다\n/// - `Permission denied` 로 넘어지고 아래의 한 줄은 그 까닭을 못 댄다.\n        if inside_checkout(&away) || !usable(&away) {\n            continue;\n        }\n        // **링크를 풀어 넘긴다** — macOS 의 `/tmp` 는 `/private/tmp` 로 Err(format!(\n        \"임시 자리({})가 체크아웃 안이고 밖에 쓸 자리도 없다 — \\\n         TMPDIR 을 체크아웃 밖에 두고 다시 돌린다\",\n        wanted.display()\n    ))\n}\n\n/// 그 자리에 **정말 만들 수 있는가.** `is_dir` 은 있는지만 답한다 — 있는데 못 쓰는 ws_col: 120, ws_xpixel: 0, ws_ypixel: 0 };\n    // SAFETY: openpty 가 쓰는 두 fd 와 읽는 크기는 살아 있는 값이며, 이름·설정은 필요 없다.\n    // 설정·크기는 `*mut` 로 넘긴다 — macOS 의 libc 는 둘을 `*mut` 로, 리눅스는 `*const` 로 받고 `*mut` 는 `*const` 로\n    // 저절로 바뀐다(moai-xpa8.f0b). openpty 는 둘을 읽기만 한다.\n    let (termp, winp) = (std::ptr::null_mut::<libc::termios>(), &size as *const libc::winsize as *mut libc::winsize);\n    assert_eq!(\n        unsafe { libc::openpty(&mut master_fd, &mut slave_fd, std::ptr::null_mut(), termp, winp) },\n        0,\n        \"{}\",\n        std::io::Error::last_os_error()\n    );\n    // SAFETY: openpty 가 만든 fd 를 File 에 한 번씩 넘겨 닫는 일을 맡긴다.\n    let (mut master, slave) = unsafe { (std::fs::File::from_raw_fd(master_fd), std::fs::File::from_raw_fd(slave_fd)) };\n    // 자식이 master 를 물려받으면 slave 가 닫혀도 EOF 가 안 선다. 읽기는 마감을 지키게 막히지 않는다.\n    for fd in [master.as_raw_fd(), slave.as_raw_fd()] {\n        assert_ne!(unsafe { libc::fcntl(fd, libc::F_SETFD, libc::FD_CLOEXEC) }, -1);\n    }\n    assert_ne!(unsafe { libc::fcntl(master.as_raw_fd(), libc::F_SETFL, libc::O_NONBLOCK) }, -1);\n    let mut command = c.command(Path::new(BIN), s.path(), &[\"init\", \"argos\"], true);\n    // tmux 안의 {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 1,80p .claude/moai-plugin/skills/moai-cmux/SKILL.md","description":"Read moai-cmux skill head"},"toolOutput":"---\nname: moai-cmux\ndescription: Use in Claude Code together with moai-supervise when the supervisor runs inside cmux (CMUX_SURFACE_ID is set and $TMUX is not) — to find a worker's surface from its ListAgents name, label its tab, clear a reported worker's window, deliver a message SendMessage could not, read why a worker stalled, and open new worker splits once the person says yes. Triggers on \"worker surface\", \"worker tab\", \"open a worker\", \"clear the worker\", \"일꾼 탭\", \"일꾼 창 열어\", \"탭 비워\".\n---\n\n# moai-cmux — the supervisor's hands on the workers' surfaces\n\nThis is the supervisor's (`moai-supervise`) companion **when it runs inside cmux** —\n`CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set in its shell and `$TMUX` is not. A `$TMUX` that starts with\n`/tmp/cmux-` counts as not set: it is cmux's own stand-in, which cmux's `claude-teams` sets for\nClaude Code's agent teams, and the `tmux` on that `PATH` is cmux in disguise — it passes\n`set-option` by and refuses `load-buffer`. Inside a real tmux — one running in a cmux tab\nincluded — what you type goes to tmux: that is `moai-tmux`, and none of this applies.\nOutside both tmux and cmux none of this applies either: the supervisor works through messages\nand the person alone. The cmux app here is **the person's own**: every workspace they have lives\nin it, and every surface you touch is a tab they are looking at.\n\ncmux's words: a window holds workspaces (the rows of its sidebar), a workspace holds panes (its\nsplits), and a pane holds surfaces (the tabs of that split). A surface is one terminal — what you\nread and what you type into.\n\n## First, the version\n\nThis needs cmux 0.65.0 or later. Look once, at the start of the round:\n\n    cmux capabilities\n\nIf its `methods` do not list `surface.input_state`, the cmux here is older: tell the person once\nthat `moai-cmux` needs cmux 0.65.0 or later, and go on as if this skill were not here. Updating\nrestarts cmux, and with it every session inside — yours too — so when is theirs to choose. If it\nprints an error instead of a `methods` list — a socket it cannot reach, a sandbox — that says\nnothing about the version: tell the person what it said, and go on as if this skill were not here.\n\n## What never happens\n\n- **No headless run.** A worker you open is an ordinary interactive `claude` the person can\n  see and type into. Never `claude -p`, never a `--dangerously-*` flag, never\n  `--permission-mode`. The moai binary launches and drives nothing; this skill is you\n  typing cmux commands where the person can watch\n- **Nothing is closed.** Never `close-surface`, `close-workspace` or `close-window`, never\n  `respawn-pane`, never `pkill` or `killall` aimed at cmux. A worker that is done stays open;\n  closing a tab is the person's\n- **Never `--force`.** cmux refuses to type into a Claude Code box that holds someone's words or a\n  dialog — but only for a session its own Claude hook knows, which is why you read the box\n  yourself first — and `--force` skips that refusal. A refusal is an answer — tell the person\n- **Only a worker's surface.** Type only into a surface found through the session map below for\n  a worker of this repository — never your own (`$CMUX_SURFACE_ID`), never a session of another\n  repository. Every call names its surface by UUID, `--surface <surface>`: left out, cmux types\n  into your own tab, and a `surface:N` name is handed out as asked for and does not outlive a\n  restart\n- **What the person looks at stays theirs.** No `focus-*`, no `select-workspace`, no\n  `--focus true` — a split you open does not take focus\n- **Never over the person's words.** If a worker's input box holds anything, do not type into\n  it — tell the person\n- **Never in their place.** A permission prompt or a question in a worker's tab is the\n  person's to answer — you read it and tell them; you press no key\n- **No polling.** Every look below is one look. A second one comes after your next step, as\n  its own call — never a loop, never a `sleep`, never `wait-for`\n- **The person's cmux settings stay theirs.** No `reload-config`, `themes`, `set-hook` or\n  `bind-key`\n\n## Which surface is which worker\n\n`ListAgents` names a session; cmux needs a surface. Claude Code keeps one record per process\nunder `~/.claude/sessions/`, and the lines below print one row per record, tab-separated:\n\n    state  name  pane  status  cwd  sessionId\n\n```sh\npython3 - <<'PY'\nimport glob, json, os, subprocess, sys\ndef out(*cmd, **env):\n    try:\n        return subprocess.run(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, universal_newlines=True, env=dict(os.environ, **env), timeout=10).stdout.strip()\n    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):\n        return \"\"\nlinux = os.path.isdir(\"/proc/self\")\ndef stat(pid):\n    try:\n        with open(f\"/proc/{pid}/stat\") as f:","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 2915,2965p src/cmd/merge_driver.rs","description":"Read merge_driver probe unit tests"},"toolOutput":"        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt as _;\n        // 자리는 `Scratch` 가 쥔다 — 끝에서 `remove_dir_all` 을 부르면 패닉한 판이 찌꺼기를 남긴다.\n        let scratch = crate::scratch::Scratch::new(\"probe\");\n        let dir = scratch.path();\n        // **돌릴 파일은 이 프로세스가 쓴 inode 를 안 쓴다**(리뷰 moai-vbmn.spv). 쓰기 fd 가 열린\n        // 동안 옆 스레드의 시험이 fork 하면 그 자식이 fd 를 물려받고, 자식이 exec 할 때까지 그\n        // inode 에 쓰는 이가 남아 Linux 가 이쪽 exec 을 ETXTBSY 로 거절한다 — `tests/cli.rs` 의\n        // `place_exe` 가 복사 2,400번으로 잰 것이 그것이다(`fs::copy` 345번, `cp` 0번). 여기가\n        // 쓴 것을 **이 프로세스에서 곧바로 부르는** 첫 자리라 같은 대처를 쓴다.\n        let write = |name: &str, body: &str| {\n            let src = dir.join(format!(\"{name}.src\"));\n            let p = dir.join(name);\n            std::fs::write(&src, body).unwrap();\n            std::fs::set_permissions(&src, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755)).unwrap();\n            let out = std::process::Command::new(\"cp\").arg(&src).arg(&p).output().unwrap();\n            assert!(out.status.success(), \"{}\", String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr));\n            p\n        };\n        let at = |cmd: &std::path::Path| probe(dir, &cmd.display().to_string());\n\n        // 이 명령을 아는 바이너리. `--help` 는 어느 갈래에서도 파일을 안 건드린다.\n        // **제 이름을 댄다**(moai-wwbi) — 0 으로 끝나는 것만으로는 `Runs` 가 아니다.\n        let ours = write(\n            \"moai\",\n            \"#!/bin/sh\\n[ \\\"$1\\\" = merge-driver ] && { echo 'Usage: moai merge-driver'; exit 0; }\\nexit 2\\n\",\n        );\n        assert!(matches!(at(&ours), Probe::Runs));\n\n        // **모르는 인자를 흘려 듣고 0 을 내는 래퍼**(moai-wwbi). 끝난 꼴만 보던 판이 그냥\n        // 지나가던 자리다 — 그 명령은 이 부명령을 모르고 매 병합이 말없이 내려앉는다.\n        let mute = write(\"삼킨다\", \"#!/bin/sh\\nexit 0\\n\");\n        assert!(matches!(at(&mute), Probe::Alien), \"흘려 듣는 래퍼가 지나갔다\");\n\n        // **그 이름의 다른 도구.** 파일도 있고 돌기도 도는데 이 명령을 모른다 — 모드를 읽던\n        // 판이 조용히 지나가던 자리다.\n        let alien = write(\"옛moai\", \"#!/bin/sh\\necho '모르는 부명령' >&2\\nexit 2\\n\");\n        assert!(matches!(at(&alien), Probe::Alien));\n\n        // 띄우지도 못하는 셋. 자리가 비었다, 실행 권한이 없다, 디렉터리다.\n        assert!(matches!(at(&dir.join(\"없다\")), Probe::Dead));\n        let dead = write(\"권한없다\", \"#!/bin/sh\\nexit 0\\n\");\n        std::fs::set_permissions(&dead, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o644)).unwrap();\n        assert!(matches!(at(&dead), Probe::Dead));\n        assert!(matches!(at(dir), Probe::Dead), \"디렉터리를 명령으로 읽었다\");\n\n        // 상대 경로는 프로세스의 자리가 아니라 뿌리에서 푼다.\n        assert!(matches!(probe(dir, \"./moai\"), Probe::Runs), \"뿌리에 있는 상대 경로를 못 찾았다\");\n        assert!(matches!(probe(Path::new(\"/\"), \"./moai\"), Probe::Dead), \"엉뚱한 뿌리에서 찾아 냈다\");\n\n        // **표준 입력을 끊는다.** 물려주면 stdin 을 읽는 명령 하나가 `moai status` 를 영영\n        // 붙든다. 읽은 것이 비었는지로 잰다 — 끊긴 자리는 곧바로 EOF 다.","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

아직 그 fd 를 쥐고 있어도 유닉스에서는 지워진다.\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&self.0);\n    }\n}\n\n/// [`PROBE_BUDGET`] 안에 끝나면 그 끝을, 아니면 죽이고 거둔 뒤 `None`.\n///\n/// **거두고 간다.** 죽이기만 하고 두면 `moai status` 가 좀비를 남긴 채 끝난다. 기다리는 자는\n/// [`crate::git::waited`] 와 한 벌이다 — 기다리는 간격을 늘려 가는 까닭도 거기 적혀 있다.\nfn reaped(child: &mut std::process::Child) -> Option<std::process::ExitStatus> {\n    crate::git::waited(child, PROBE_BUDGET).or_else(|| {\n        let _ = child.kill();\n        let _ = child.wait();\n        None\n    })\n}\n\n/// 아무도 안 주면 심을 명령 — **`PATH` 의 `moai` 가 같은 판이면 그쪽, 아니면 지금 이\n/// 바이너리**(moai-bq6w, 2026-09-21 사용자 결정).\n///\n/// 심는 자리(`--local`)는 클론이 함께 쓰는 `$GIT_COMMON_DIR/config` 인데, 이 저장소의 절차는\n/// 일을 모두 워크트리에서 하므로 지금 도는 바이너리는 대개 `<워크트리>/target/release/moai` 다.\n/// 그 워크트리를 지우는 날 **모든 체크아웃**이 죽은 경로를 든다 — \"한 번도 안 심었다\" 가\n/// \"전부 썩었다\" 로 바뀌는 자리고, `merge_driver_absent` 의 힌트를 그대로 친 사람이 밟는다.\n///\n/// **고르는 자리가 하나다.** 힌트에 경고를 적는 길은 버렸다 — 에이전트는 명령만 읽고 친다.\n/// 거절하는 **옛\n/// 빌드**가 같은 글을 내고 그대로 심겼다. 그러면 병합 알고리즘을 고친 사람이 `init` 을 친 뒤로\n/// 모든 병합이 **옛 알고리즘**으로 합쳐지는데 `status` 와 `init --check` 는 둘 다 \"제대로 섰다\"\n/// 고 말한다(이 컨테이너에서 두 번 재현했다). 판을 가릴 자가 글에 없으니 파일로 가른다: 크기가\n/// 다르면 거기서 끝이고, 같으면 바이트를 견준다. 심는 명령은 한 번 치는 것이라 그 값이 싸다.\n///\n/// **그래서 감싼 스크립트는 안 고른다.** `exec <진짜>` 하는 셸 래퍼는 바이트가 다르니 지금\n/// 바이너리가 심긴다 — 틀리는 값은 **덜 이르는 쪽**이라야 하고, 그쪽은 이 워크트리를 지울 때만\n/// 썩지만 {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 200,420p src/scratch.rs","description":"Read scratch.rs bottom half"},"toolOutput":"}\n\n/// `dir` 이 어느 체크아웃이나 트래커 안인가. **표식은 둘이다** — `.git` 과 `.moai`(moai-izeo).\n///\n/// `.git` 만 보던 자는 울타리([`fence`])가 못 막던 바로 그 자리를 놓친다: moai 는 `.git` 이 아니라\n/// `.moai` 를 찾아 위로 오르므로(`store::Repo::found_root`), git 이 아닌 moai 프로젝트 밑에 선\n/// 임시 자리를 \"밖\" 이라고 답하고, 그러면 시험이 그 사람의 트래커를 읽고 쓴다. 두 표식을 함께\n/// 봐야 [`base`] 의 말이 참이 된다.\n///\n/// **링크를 푼 자리로 잰다** — `TMPDIR` 이 체크아웃 안을 가리키는 링크면 글자로 된 조상에는\n/// `.git` 이 없는데 git 은 실제 자리(`getcwd`)로 위를 찾는다.\npub fn inside_checkout(dir: &Path) -> bool {\n    real(dir).ancestors().any(|d| d.join(\".git\").exists() || d.join(\".moai\").is_dir())\n}\n\n/// 디렉터리에 선 이름들, 이름 차례로 — 찌꺼기를 세는 시험들(`store`·`cmd::skill`)이 함께 쓴다. 저마다 베껴 두던 것을\n/// 모았다(리뷰 moai-dj4j.n9y) — 부르는 시험이 다 유닉스의 것이라 여기도 그렇다(밖에서는 쓰는 이가 없어 죽은 글이 된다).\n#[cfg(unix)]\npub fn names(d: &Path) -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut v: Vec<String> =\n        std::fs::read_dir(d).unwrap().map(|e| e.unwrap().file_name().into_string().unwrap()).collect();\n    v.sort();\n    v\n}\n\n/// [`crate::path::real`] 과 같은 자 — **여기만 제 몸으로 든다.**\n///\n/// 이 파일은 `tests/cli.rs` 가 `#[path]` 로 함께 들어(dev-dependency 0개, CLAUDE.md \"테스트\"),\n/// 그쪽에서는 `crate` 가 시험 크레이트라 `crate::path` 가 없다. 한 자로 모으는 결정(moai-8csx)이\n/// 닿지 못하는 한 자리고, 갈리면 시험 자리가 링크를 달리 푼다 — 그래서 글로 맨다.\nfn real(p: &Path) -> PathBuf {\n    std::fs::canonicalize(p).unwrap_or_else(|_| p.to_path_buf())\n}\n\n/// `dir` 에 아무것도 없는 저장소를 세운다([`Scratch::fenced`] 가 왜 세 개인지 적는다).\n///\n/// **울타리는 시험 자리마다 치고 그 자리와 함께 치운다.** 한때 판들이 나눠 쓰는 뿌리 하나\n/// (`moai-fence`)를 두었는데 주인이 없어 아무도 안 치웠고, 그 체크아웃에 커밋 없는 저장소가 남아\n/// `git add -A` 가 거기서 통째로 멈췄다(`does not have a commit checked out`, 에픽 리뷰\n/// moai-8mq9.1bw). 자리마다 치면 `Drop` 이 치우고, 남는 것은 판이 죽었을 때뿐이다.\n///\n/// 부르는 곳은 [`Scratch::fenced_in`] 하나다 — 통합 시험(`tests/cli.rs`)의 `Scratch` 는 moai-izeo\n/// 뒤로 [`base`] 만 읽고 울타리를 안 친다.\n///\n/// **막는 것은 `.git` 훑기뿐이다.** `.moai` 를 찾아 오르는 쪽([`inside_checkout`] 이 두 번째\n/// 표식으로 세는 그것)은 여기서 안 선다. 그러니 체크아웃 **안**에 세운 울타리 자리\n/// ([`Scratch::fenced_in`] 에 뿌리를 골라 주는 쓰임)에서 `Repo` 를 여는 시험을 쓰면, 그 훑기가\n/// 울타리를 지나쳐 돌리는 사람의 진짜 트래커를 잡는다 — moai-595o 가 났던 바로 그 길이다.\n/// 여기에 `.moai` 를 같이 심지 않는 것은 그것이 곧 설정을 읽히는 저장소가 되기 때문이고,\n/// 그래서 그런 시험은 뿌리를 [`base`] 로 두거나 제 `.moai` 를 손수 세워야 한다.\n\n... [70 lines truncated] ...\n\n\n    /// **뿌리는 어느 체크아웃 안도 아니다**(moai-izeo). 여기가 무너지면 시험이 바깥 저장소의\n    /// `.moai` 를 잡고, 쓰는 시험 하나가 그 트래커를 실제로 더럽힌다.\n    ///\n    /// 이 줄은 [`base`] 가 이미 본 것을 다시 보는 것이라 혼자서는 못 무너진다 — 무엇을 표식으로\n    /// 세는지는 [`a_tracker_above_counts_as_inside_too`] 가, 옮기는 갈래는\n    /// [`a_base_inside_a_checkout_moves_out_or_says_why`] 가 잰다. 여기서 재는 것은 그 셋이 실제\n    /// 기계에서 한 답으로 모이는가다.\n    #[test]\n    fn the_base_is_never_inside_a_checkout() {\n        assert!(!inside_checkout(&base()), \"임시 자리가 체크아웃 안이다 — {}\", base().display());\n        assert!(!inside_checkout(Scratch::new(\"outside\").path()));\n    }\n\n    /// **위의 `.moai` 도 \"안\" 이다**(moai-izeo). 울타리는 `.git` 만 세웠는데 moai 는 `.moai` 를\n    /// 찾아 오르므로, `.git` 만 보는 자는 git 아닌 moai 프로젝트 밑에 선 임시 자리를 \"밖\" 이라\n    /// 답한다 — 그 기계에서 시험이 그 사람의 트래커를 읽고 **쓴다**(moai-595o).\n    #[test]\n    fn a_tracker_above_counts_as_inside_too() {\n        let outer = Scratch::new(\"tracker-outer\");\n        let under = outer.join(\"tmp\");\n        std::fs::create_dir(&under).unwrap();\n        assert!(!inside_checkout(&under), \"표식이 하나도 없는데 안이라 했다\");\n        std::fs::create_dir(outer.join(\".moai\")).unwrap();\n        assert!(inside_checkout(&under), \"위의 .moai 를 못 봤다 — 시험이 바깥 트래커를 잡는다\");\n    }\n\n    /// **옮기는 갈래와 실패하는 갈래를 실제로 돌린다**(moai-izeo). [`base`] 는 `TMPDIR` 을 한\n    /// 판에 한 번만 보므로 뿌리로는 이 둘을 못 재고, 그래서 [`pick`] 이 자리를 받는다.\n    #[test]\n    fn a_base_inside_a_checkout_moves_out_or_says_why() {\n        let outer = Scratch::fenced_in(&base(), \"pick-outer\");\n        let inside = outer.join(\"tmp\");\n        std::fs::create_dir(&inside).unwrap();\n        let away = Scratch::new(\"pick-away\");\n\n        // 밖이면 준 자리를 쓴다 — 갈 곳을 안 줘도 그렇다. 그때도 **링크를 푼 철자로** 넘긴다(moai-xpa8.egv).\n        let kept = pick(away.path().to_path_buf(), &[]).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(kept, std::fs::canonicalize(away.path()).unwrap(), \"밖의 자리를 링크째 넘겼다\");\n        // 안이면 밖으로 옮긴다. **링크를 푼 철자로** 넘긴다.\n        let moved = pick(inside.clone(), &[away.path()]).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(moved, std::fs::canonicalize(away.path()).unwrap(), \"링크를 안 풀고 넘겼다\");\n        // 갈 곳이 못 쓰는 자리뿐이면 그 자리를 건너뛴다 — 있기만 한 것을 보고 옮기지 않는다.\n        let gone = outer.join(\"없다\");\n        assert!(pick(inside.clone(), &[gone.as_path()]).is_err(), \"못 쓰는 자리로 옮겼다\");\n        // 갈 곳이 다 체크아웃 안이면 크게 실패한다 — 조용히 눌러앉지 않는다.\n        let why = pick(inside.clone(), &[inside.as_path()]).unwrap_err();\n        assert!(why.contains(\"TMPDIR\"), \"고칠 길을 안 댄다 — {why}\");\n    }\n}","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 150,260p .claude/moai-plugin/skills/moai-cmux/SKILL.md","description":"Read moai-cmux session map usage section"},"toolOutput":"```\n\n- **Read only `alive` rows.** A `dead` row is a record a process left behind — its pid is gone,\n  or now belongs to another process (the start time differs)\n- `name` is the `ListAgents` name, `pane` the surface UUID that `--surface` takes. cmux itself\n  answers which processes run in which surface (`cmux top`). It is `-` when that session is not\n  in a cmux tab of yours — another terminal, or tmux, tmux inside a cmux tab included — when it\n  shares its tab with another live session, or when cmux gave no answer (a line on its own says\n  so), and then this skill has nothing for that worker\n- **No row at all, and a line saying no record reads alive:** this shell cannot tell live from\n  dead — act on no row, and tell the person what it said\n- `cwd` is where the session stands: the root, or one of the worktrees `git worktree list`\n  names — wherever they stand. A row standing elsewhere is not a worker of this repository, whatever its name\n- `status` is `idle`, `busy` or another word. It has to agree with `ListAgents` where a step\n  below asks for `idle`\n- Your own row is the one whose pane is `$CMUX_SURFACE_ID`\n\nRun it when a step below needs a surface, once.\n\n## Is the input box empty\n\n    cmux rpc surface.input_state '{\"surface_id\":\"<surface>\"}'\n\ncmux reads Claude Code's input box off that surface's screen. The box is **empty** only when\nthe answer's `state` is `empty` and its `waiting_on_human` is `false`, and the session map, run\nagain just before, still reads that session `alive` in that tab — cmux reads the screen alone,\nand a tab whose Claude Code has ended can still show its last box, and read `empty`, while a\nshell has the keyboard. `draft` is text someone typed or pasted — the person's, even a half-typed\nword. `dialog` is a prompt or a menu standing where the box was. `unknown` is a screen cmux\ncannot read as Claude Code's — a shell prompt, a process that ended. `waiting_on_human` is cmux's\nnote that the session last asked the person something — a permission prompt, a question — and\nit can stay `true` after an API error or an interrupt. None of these is a box to type into, and\nneither is an error or an answer without `state`.\n\n**Then do not type. Tell the person which tab holds what, and go on as if this skill were not\nhere.**\n\n## Label the tab\n\nWhen you send work (the supervisor's 3), you may write the worker and the work onto its tab.\n**Ask the person once per round** whether worker tabs should carry labels — unlike a pane option\nin tmux, a label replaces the tab's name where they look, a name they gave it included. On a yes:\n\n    cmux rpc tab.action '{\"surface_id\":\"<surface>\",\"action\":\"rename\",\"title\":\"<worker> <id>\"}'\n\n`<id>` is the backlog or epic you sent. Go through `rpc`, not `rename-tab`: the CLI's tab words\nadd your own workspace to the call, and cmux then cannot find a worker tab that stands in\nanother workspace. A name given this way stays over the title Claude Code keeps writing\n(`✳ <topic>`) until it is taken off. Take it off when that work's report is checked (the\nsupervisor's 5):\n\n... [11 lines truncated] ...\n\ntab after your label, and `clear_name` would erase it. Rename no workspace: the names in the\nsidebar are the person's.\n\n## Clear a worker's window\n\nBefore you send a worker its next work, you may clear its window (`/clear`) yourself — all of\nthese first:\n\n1. **Its report is checked** — the supervisor's 5 held all three checks and the\n   `Report-checked:` note is written\n2. **It reads `idle`** — in `ListAgents` and in its row of the session map\n3. **Its input box is empty** (above)\n\nThen:\n\n    cmux send --surface <surface> -- '/clear\\n'\n\nTo `send`, `\\n` is the Enter key: this types `/clear` and presses it, in one call. Then, as a\nseparate call, look once: the session map reads `idle` for it and\n\n    cmux read-screen --surface <surface> --lines 20\n\nshows the cleared screen — the conversation gone, an empty box. Then send with `SendMessage`\nas the supervisor's 3 says. **If any condition fails, cmux refuses to type, or the look does not\nshow it cleared, do not type again** — do what the supervisor's 5 says without cmux: ask the\nperson, or send to another idle worker. When it was the look that failed, tell the person that\n`/clear` may stand typed in that tab's box: pressed later, it would erase the next message\nsent there.\n\n## When a message does not arrive\n\nWhen `SendMessage` to a worker fails — an error, no such session — and that worker has a surface\nwhose input box is empty (above), you may put the message into the box yourself. **A message\nheld for the person's approval is not one that failed:** that hold is the person's gate, like\na permission prompt, and the held message still arrives once they approve it — pasting it too\nskips their gate and hands the worker the same work twice. Tell the person it waits for them\ninstead. Typed keys submit at every newline, so paste it as one block:\n\n1. Write the message to a file in your scratchpad, with one line at the end naming you — a\n   pasted message carries no sender, and the worker reports to the message's `from`. The\n   first line stays the message's own, which names the work and the step to start from:\n   `from: <your ListAgents name>`\n2. Paste and submit it — the lone `-` reads the file from stdin; after a `--` it would be pasted\n   as the text itself:\n\n       cmux paste --surface <surface> --submit - < <file>\n\n   It goes in as one paste, and cmux presses the key that submits it. If cmux refuses —\n   someone's words or a dialog in the box — do not try again. {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 1270,1300p src/cmd/merge_driver.rs; sed -n 2005,2030p src/cmd/init.rs","description":"Read budget note near 1280 and init's driver planting call"},"toolOutput":"///\n/// **딸린 파일을 손으로 읽지 않는다.** 규칙은 `.gitattributes` 하나에만 있는 것이 아니다 —\n/// `.git/info/attributes` 와 위 디렉터리의 파일, 그리고 패턴끼리의 우선순위까지 git 의 규칙이다.\n/// 그것을 여기 다시 적으면 git 이 실제로 무엇을 쓰는지와 이 판정이 갈리고, 갈리는 쪽은 늘\n/// 이쪽이다. `check-attr` 에게 물으면 git 이 제 규칙으로 답한다.\n///\n/// `-z` 로 받는다 — 맨 출력은 `<경로>: merge: <값>` 이라 경로에 `: ` 가 들면 자를 자리가 갈린다.\n/// 못 물어봤으면(저장소 밖이다, git 이 없다, 한도 안에 못 들었다) **거짓이다**: 모르면 입을 다문다.\n///\n/// **한도는 부르는 쪽이 준다**(리뷰 moai-59k3.4c3) — 알림([`notice_at`])만 주고, `moai init` 이 심을지\n/// 가르는 자리([`plant_for_init`])와 `init --check`([`state_at`])는 끝까지 기다린다. 한 한도를 셋이\n/// 함께 쓰던 때는 `check-attr` 가 2초를 넘긴 저장소에서 `init` 이 드라이버를 말없이 안 심었고\n/// `--check` 는 `off` 를 냈다 — 거기서 \"모른다\" 는 \"안 걸었다\" 가 아니다.\nfn declared(root: &Path, budget: Option<std::time::Duration>) -> bool {\n    let Some(Ok(out)) = crate::git::run_within(root, &[\"check-attr\", \"-z\", \"merge\", \"--\", SNAPSHOT], budget) else {\n        return false;\n    };\n    let mut f = out.split('\\0');\n    f.next() == Some(SNAPSHOT) && f.next() == Some(\"merge\") && f.next() == Some(DRIVER)\n}\n\n/// 심어 둔 줄에서 **실제로 부르는 명령**을 떼어 낸다. 모양이 이 도구가 지은 것이 아니면 `None`.\n///\n/// **표식은 `\" {SUB} %O %A %B\"` 다** — 이 도구가 지은 줄은 명령 바로 뒤에 그것이 선다. 앞에 무엇이 붙든\n/// (지금은 `cp %A %A.ours; if `, 옛 판은 아무것도 없다) 그 자리 앞의 낱말 하나가 명령이다.\n/// 재는 쪽이 앞머리를 세지 않으니 [`driver_command`] 를 고쳐도 여기가 안 따라 낡는다.\n///\n/// **표식이 없으면 재지 않는다**(리뷰 moai-h6aq.cx8). 앞 판은 낱말 하나만 떼어, 사람이 손으로\n/// 적은 `python3 tools/merge.py %O %A %B` 를 `python3` 으로 읽고 그것이 이 프로세스의 PATH 에\n/// 없으면 \"썩었다\" 고 불렀다 — 남의 줄을 덮으라는 힌트가 함께 서는데 걷을 길이 없다.\n///\n                let _ = match before {\n                    None => std::fs::remove_file(&d.path),\n                    Some(n) => std::fs::OpenOptions::new().write(true).open(&d.path).and_then(|f| f.set_len(n)),\n                };\n            }\n            return Err(fail);\n        }\n    }\n\n    let attrs = attributes.map_or(Added::Already, &write);\n    // 이 클론에만 둘 자리를 못 찾으면(`ignored` 가 없으면) 위의 거절(git 저장소가 아니다)이 이미 막았다.\n    let ignore = early.unwrap_or_else(|| ignored.map_or(Added::Already, &write));\n    // **선언을 쓴 바로 뒤에 그 이름이 가리키는 명령을 심는다**(moai-08bo, 2026-09-21 사용자 결정).\n    // 앞 판은 이름만 쓰고 명령은 사람에게 치라고 했다 — 도구가 제 손으로 안 도는 절반이었다.\n    // 무엇을 하고 안 하는지는 [`crate::cmd::merge_driver::plant_for_init`] 가 쥔다: 선언이 없는\n    // 저장소와 git 저장소가 아닌 자리에는 안 심고, 이미 같은 줄이면 아무것도 안 쓴다.\n    let planting = if no_driver { None } else { Some(crate::cmd::merge_driver::plant_for_init(&root)) };\n    // 못 건드린 자리 — 이름과 까닭과 **손으로 더할 줄**을 함께 든다(moai-gq1c, moai-0dwc). 줄을 안\n    // 대면 사람은 도구가 무엇을 넣으려 했는지 모른 채 파일만 고치게 된다. 못 읽은 것과 못 쓴 것을\n    // 가르는 것은 **말뿐이다** — 사람이 할 일이 인코딩과 권한으로 갈린다. 링크는 줄 대신 고칠 말을 댄다\n    // ([`Added::Linked`]).\n    let untouched: Vec<(&str, &Added, &str)> = attributes\n        .map(|d| (d.name, &attrs, d.block.as_str()))\n        .into_iter()\n        .chain(ignored.map(|d| (d.name, &ignore, d.block.as_str())))\n        .filter(|(_, done, _)| done.trouble().is_some())","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

없고, 남의\n/// 프로세스 환경을 읽는 일은 자동 모드의 분류기가 비밀 뒤지기로 막았다(2026-10-11) — tty 와 시작 시각은 환경을 안\n/// 읽는다. 죽은 줄과 `$TMUX` 없이 부른 판은 기록의 칸을 그대로 낸다. 죽은 줄의 칸은 아무도 겨누지 않는다 —\n/// 되살리기(moai-uqf7)는 제가 연 칸에만 친다. 파이썬은 3.6 에서도 돈다 — `subprocess.run` 의 `capture_output`·`text` 는\n/// 3.7 의 것이라 RHEL 8 의 `python3` 에서 잡히지 않는 `TypeError` 로 줄 중간에 죽는다.\n///\n/// **산 줄이 하나도 없으면 아무 줄도 내지 않고 1 로 끝난다**(리뷰 moai-p5sz.tkn). 짝을 부르는 것은 살아 있는 Claude\n/// Code 세션이라 제 기록 하나는 늘 `alive` 여야 한다 — 그것까지 `dead` 면 이 셸이 시작 시각을 못 읽는 것이다(macOS 의\n/// Bash 샌드박스가 `ps` 에게 남의 프로세스를 안 보이고, 리눅스의 샌드박스는 제 pid 이름공간만 본다). 그 판의 `dead` 를\n/// 믿으면 되살리기가 산 세션을 `claude --resume` 으로 한 번 더 띄워 한 대화를 두 창이 잇는다.\n///\n/// **cmux 안에서 부르면 같은 칸에 surface 의 UUID 가 선다**(moai-p5sz.7q3) — 부르는 셸에 `$TMUX` 는 없고\n/// `CMUX_SURFACE_ID` 가 서 있을 때다. `moai-cmux` 의 명령은 모두 `--surface <UUID>` 로 겨누니 칸 하나가 둘 다 받는다.\n/// 다리는 `cmux --json --id-format both top --all` 의 surface 별 `cmux_process_pids` 다(사람 결정 2026-10-10) — 그\n/// surface 의 `CMUX_SURFACE_ID` 를 환경에 든 프로세스를 cmux 가 스스로 센 것이라, 짝은 남의 환경을 안 읽는다.\n/// `--id-format both` 가 없으면 cmux 가 JSON 에서 UUID(`id`)를 지운다. 이렇게 정한 까닭이 셋이다.\n///\n/// - **tty 는 못 쓴다** — `tree` 가 surface 마다 대는 `tty` 에 낡은 값이 섞여(2026-10-11 Mac 에서 `ttys023` 을 두\n///   surface 가 함께 댔고 실제 주인은 하나였다) 엉뚱한 surface 에 칠 수 있다\n/// - **tmux 가 이긴다** — tmux 를 cmux 안에서 돌리면 둘 다 서는데, 그 셸에서 친 것은 tmux 칸으로 가니 tmux 의 짝을\n///   낸다. 거꾸로 cmux 쪽에서는 기록에 `tmux` 가 선 산 세션을 `-` 로 낸다 — tmux 서버가 cmux 안에서 섰다면 그\n///   환경의 `CMUX_SURFACE_ID` 는 tmux 를 띄운 surface 의 것이라, 거기 치면 그 세션이 아니라 tmux 의 지금 칸에 간다\n/// - **`/tmp/cmux-` 로 여는 `$TMUX` 는 tmux 가 아니다**(사람 결정 2026-10-11, moai-xpa8.1vt) — `cmux claude-teams`\n///   (그리고 `omo`·`omx`·`omc`)가 Claude 의 agent teams 에 주는 가짜다(`/tmp/cmux-claude-teams/<워크스페이스>,<창>,<칸>`,\n///   v0.65.0 의 `configureTmuxCompatEnvironment`). 그 가 그 꼴을 바꾸면 옛\n///   쓸모없는 쪽으로 돌아갈 뿐이다. 그렇게 띄운 일꾼의 기록에는 그 가짜에서 온 `tmux` 가 서서 아래 갈래로 `-` 다 —\n///   감독이 여는 일꾼은 맨 `claude` 라 거기 안 걸린다\n/// - **cmux 가 `top` 을 모르면 칸이 모두 `-` 다** — `top` 은 v0.64.0, [90 lines truncated] ...\n\nPY\"##;\n\n/// **빈 입력 칸의 잣대는 이 글 하나다.** `moai-tmux` 와 `moai-recover` 가 `format!` 으로 같은 글을 싣는다 —\n/// 되살리기는 모두에게 심기고 `moai-tmux` 는 고른 사람에게만 서니(moai-3r7l), 되살리기가 `moai-tmux` 의 절을 가리키면\n/// 그것이 없는 자리에서 없는 글을 댄다(moai-o9je). 둘째 잣대를 적으면 Claude Code 의 입력 칸 꼴이 바뀌는 날 한쪽만\n/// 고쳐진다. 비었을 때 무엇을 하는가(안 친다·사람에게 말한다)는 스킬마다 제 글이 잇는다.\n///\n/// **화면만으로는 빈 칸이 아니다**(moai-xpa8.p56) — 짝([`SESSIONS`])을 새로 봐 그 세션이 그 칸에 `alive` 일 때만이다.\n/// 죽임을 당한 Claude 는 마지막 화면(칸까지)을 `exec bash` 의 셸 위에 남겨, 닿지 않은 메시지(세션이 죽어 `SendMessage` 가\n/// 실패하는 흔한 자리다)가 셸에 스크립트로 쳐진다. cmux 쪽이 리뷰(moai-p5sz.tkn 2번)에서 받은 고침을 tmux 로 옮긴\n/// 것이고, 2026-10-11 cmux 실기에서 `kill -9` 한 탭이 마지막 화면을 남기는 것을 봤다.\npub const EMPTY_BOX: &str = \"    tmux display -p -t <pane> '#{pane_in_mode}'\n    tmux capture-pane -p -e -t <pane>\n\nThe first line prints `1` while the person is scrolling the pane (copy mode) — keys you send\nthen go to tmux's copy mode, not to Claude Code, so a pane in a mode is theirs: do not type.\nClaude Code's input box is the line that starts with `❯`, under the conversation, between two\n`─` rules. **Empty** is `❯` followed by nothing, or by Claude Code's dim placeholder — `-e`\nkeeps the colours, and the placeholder is drawn dim (SGR `2`, or a grey foreground) where the\nperson's text is not. Anything else — a word, a pasted block, a half-typed command — is the\nperson's, and if you cannot tell the placeholder from their draft, it is theirs. A pane with\nno `❯` box at all (a shell prompt, a dialog) is not a box to type into either. **Even an empty\nbox counts only while the session map, run again just before, still reads that session\n`alive` in that pane** — the screen alone cannot tell: a pane whose Claude Code was killed keeps\nits last frame, box and all, above the shell `exec bash` started, and the keys go to that\nshell.\";\n\n/// 선택 스킬 `moai-tmux` 의 SKILL.md — tmux 안에서 도는 감독의 손이다(2026-10-10 사용자 결정, moai-u99i). 고른 사람에게만\n/// 심는다(`skill::OPTIONAL`, moai-3r7l).\n///\n/// **moai-obxm 의 두 결정을 tmux 쓰는 사람에게만 뒤집는다.** \"창을 비우는 것은 사람의 몫 — 감독은 칸에 아무것도 치지\n/// 않는다\" 와 \"감독도 에이전트를 띄우지 않는다\" 였다. 이제 `$TMUX` 가 서 있으면 감독이 칸을 비우고, 닿지 않은\n/// 메시지를 붙이고, 사람이 그러라고 한 뒤에 새 일꾼 칸을 연다. 참인 쪽은 그대로다 — **바이너리는 아무것도 띄우거나\n/// 몰지 않고**(이 글은 스킬의 말일 뿐 새 명령이 없다), 헤드리스·`-p`·`--dangerously-*`·권한 모드 바꾸기는 없다.\n///\n/// **치기 전의 잣대는 하나다 — 입력 칸에 무엇이든 있으면 안 친다.** 옛 5-1 은 사람이 쓰던 초안을 건지느라 480줄이\n/// 되었다. 초안인지 자리글(placeholder)인지 못 가르면 있는 것으로 읽고 사람에게 말한다.\n///\n/// **칸은 언제나 짝([`SESSIONS`])에서 찾은 `%id` 로 겨눈다.** 사람의 tmux 서버라, 맨 `kill-*` 하나가 그 서버의 모든\n/// 세션을 죽인다(2026-09-18). 감독 제 칸·다른 저장소의 칸·시험 서버의 칸에는 치지 않는다.\n///\n/// **칸 이름표는 칸 사용자 옵션 `@moai` 다.** Claude Code 가 `pane_title` 을 제 화제로 덮어 써서 제목은 못 쓴다.\n/// 보일지는 바퀴마다 사람에게 묻고, 그렇다고 하면 **도는 서버의** `pane-border-format` 앞에 붙인다 — 사람의 설정\n/// 파일은 안 고친다.\n///\n/// Claude Code 에만 심는다([`crate::skill::Skill::claude_only`]) — 감독 스킬과 같은 까닭이다.\npub fn tmux() -> String {\n    format!(\n        r#\"---\nname: moai-tmux","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

사람과\n/// 시계만 주고 색을 안 줘, 다른 자리들과 다른 환경에서 돌고 있었다.\n///\n/// 더 줄 것이 있으면 돌려받아 이어 붙인다(`env`·`current_dir`). 걷어야 할 것은\n/// [`isolated`] 가 이미 걷었다.\nfn staged(args: &[&str]) -> Command {\n    let mut cmd = {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 1825,1870p src/guide.rs","description":"Read the supervisor tmux/cmux selection text"},"toolOutput":"**One supervisor per repository.** A supervisor waiting for reports reads `idle` in\n`ListAgents` like any worker, so a second one sends it backlog, and the two keep separate\nbooks of what was sent — one backlog, or one worker, gets two jobs. Before the first round,\nask the person whether another window here runs `moai-supervise`; if one does, stop. A\nsession that refuses work because it is a supervisor comes out of the candidates. **You\nrefuse too:** a message that hands you backlog to work on came from another supervisor — do\nnothing of it, reply to its `from` that you are a supervisor, and tell the person.\n\nFive things about the messaging, one line each:\n\n- A session in a different permission mode holds an incoming message for its person's\n  approval — a worker that stays idle after you sent may be waiting on that\n- `notify_when_idle` answers only for a session on this machine — one reason a worker is a\n  session on this machine (2)\n- A subagent sends under its parent session's address — a message can come from a session\n  that did not write it itself\n- `@path` in a message attaches nothing — a file the worker has to read is named by its\n  absolute path, and the worker reads it itself (3)\n- Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop — the report comes to you (4)\n\n**Inside tmux, load `moai-tmux` too.** When `$TMUX` is set in your shell, the skill\n`moai-tmux` gives you hands on the workers' panes, at five points of the round: offer new\nworker panes when no worker is idle (2), label the pane you send to and deliver a message\n`SendMessage` could not (3), read a stalled worker's pane (4), and clear a reported worker's\nwindow before its next work (5). It finds each worker's pane from its `ListAgents` name, and\nnever types into a box that holds anything. **Without `$TMUX` nothing of it applies** — every\nstep below goes through messages and the person, as written, unless you are inside cmux (the\nnext paragraph). `moai-tmux` is an optional skill:\nit stands only where it was chosen (`moai skill install --with moai-tmux`, or its row in `moai\ninit`). Inside tmux without it, tell the person that one line plants it, and carry on as if\noutside tmux.\n\n**Inside cmux, load `moai-cmux` instead.** When `CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set in your shell and\n`$TMUX` is not, `moai-cmux` gives you the same hands on the workers' cmux tabs, at the same\nfive points, and reads the same session map. It needs cmux 0.65.0 or later and says so itself.\n**A `$TMUX` that starts with `/tmp/cmux-` is cmux's own stand-in**, not a tmux server —\n`cmux claude-teams` sets it for Claude Code's agent teams, and the `tmux` on its `PATH` is cmux\nin disguise — so with it you are inside cmux: `moai-cmux`. When both are set otherwise you run in\ntmux inside a cmux tab — what you type goes to tmux, so it is\n`moai-tmux`. **With neither, nothing of either applies.** `moai-cmux` is optional the same\nway (`moai skill install --with moai-cmux`); inside cmux without it, tell the person that one\nline plants it, and carry on as if outside cmux.\n\n**When sessions died** — a restart or an OOM kill took the workers or a supervisor down —\nand the person asks to bring them back, load `moai-recover`, inside tmux or not.","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 795,840p CHANGELOG.md; grep -rn \"codex_trust\" i18n/*.toml 2>/dev/null | head; ls i18n 2>/dev/null | head","description":"Read CHANGELOG notes about Codex trust"},"toolOutput":"  `--scope` stays Claude's registration; given without Claude, one line says\n  so. `--json` adds `agents`, `found`, `agents_dir`, `agents_files` and\n  `hooks`, and Claude's keys stand only when Claude is among the agents.\n- **The hooks stand in Codex and Antigravity too.** `moai skill install --agent\n  codex` plants `.codex/hooks.json` and `--agent antigravity` plants\n  `.agents/hooks.json` — commit them with the skills. They call `moai hook\n  <event> --dialect codex|antigravity`: the five rules, the board and the\n  letters are the same, only the shapes in and out are each agent's. Codex\n  runs project hooks once a person trusts them in `/hooks`, and sends them only\n  for its shell, `apply_patch` and MCP calls; a patch — through the\n  `apply_patch` tool or typed as `apply_patch <<'EOF'` in its shell — is\n  judged file by file. Each Codex hook carries only what its event takes, so\n  `/hooks` has no configuration warning for the file: `additionalContextLimit`\n  stands on `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit` and `PreToolUse`, the events\n  that can add context, and `Interrupt` and `SessionEnd` get 3 seconds, the\n  most Codex gives them. The letters a Codex turn's end holds the turn with\n  stay within 8,000 bytes, because Codex keeps that text to its default of\n  about 2,500 tokens and no setting raises it — a longer letter is cut there,\n  naming `moai inbox <id> --from <n>` for the rest, where Codex would have\n  moved its middle into a file. The question a turn's end asks while work is\n  still held fits the same room: open reviews tied to the held work, and held\n  rows that would close their epic if deferred, get the room first; the other\n  held rows fill what is left from the top, those that do not fit are left out\n  whole, and one more line counts them and names `moai prime`. Antigravity has no prompt\n  event, so its first model call of a turn loads the board and the letters; a\n  turn is held with `decision: continue`. Both carry the same 10,000\n  characters as Claude Code —\n  measured whole on agy 1.2.16 and 1.2.17, up to a letter written entirely in\n  Korean (28 KB). A hooks file moai did not write is left as it is, with\n  one line saying so — for Antigravity that includes moai's group with a\n  handler of your own in it, or turned off. `moai skill status` judges each\n  file by the moai it calls. Codex runs its hooks from a daemon its sessions\n  share, so a Codex session's presence row follows its session id, records no\n  pid or tmux pane, and goes when the session ends; `moai agents` cannot sweep\n  it by its process.\n- **The AGENTS block says where no hook stands** — an agent without them, Codex\n  before the trust, a tool call that sends none — the rules are words only,\n  rules 4 and 5 most of all. `moai init` writes the new block.\n- **One text for every agent.** The three trees get the same skills; the steps\n  only one agent has — entering a worktree, asking the person, calling the\n  review, changing the model, clearing the window (`/clear`, `/new`), calling a\n  skill, waking a session, stopping what a review left running — sit in a\n  \"Words per agent\" table in the `moai`, `moai-supervise` and `moai-work`\n  skills, one column per agent, and the steps name them in italics. A step an\n  agent does not have reads `—`: tell the person and go on.\n- **`moai skill status` shows `.agents/skills/`** — not planted, current, or\n(eval):1: no matches found: i18n/*.toml\nen.json\nes.json\nja.json\nko.json\nREADME.md\nzh.json","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 178,190p docs/agents.md; echo ----; sed -n 428,490p docs/agents.md","description":"Read docs/agents.md sections on tmux/cmux detection"},"toolOutput":"- **Nothing writes the choice down.** A skill planted in the tree is the answer.\n  So a plain `moai skill install` refreshes the optional skills already planted\n  and plants no new one, and a first install plants none\n- **The first `moai init` in a terminal offers a row per optional skill** under\n  the hooks and skills row. A row starts checked when the skill is already\n  planted, or when your shell says you use it (`$TMUX` set, for `moai-tmux`;\n  `$CMUX_SURFACE_ID` set, for `moai-cmux`).\n  Where nothing is asked — a script, an agent, `--yes` — only what `--with`\n  names is planted, never what the shell suggests\n- **`uninstall --only` keeps the registration.** It removes that skill's\n  directory (only while it holds nothing but moai's files) and brings Claude's\n  registration up to the new version where it already stands; where none stands\n----\nand stops at anything that cannot be undone.\n\n### In tmux\n\nWhen the supervisor runs inside tmux (`$TMUX` is set) and the `moai-tmux`\nskill is planted ([optional skills](#optional-skills) — `moai skill install\n--with moai-tmux`), it also loads that skill and works on the workers' panes of\nyour own tmux server (moai-u99i). Without tmux, or without the skill, nothing of\nthis happens.\n\n- **Which pane is which worker.** Claude Code keeps a record per process under\n  `~/.claude/sessions/`; the skill reads the live ones (the pid alive and its\n  start time matching) and pairs each `ListAgents` name with its pane `%N`.\n  Every tmux call names that pane\n- **A label on the pane.** When it sends work, it writes `<worker> <id>` into the\n  pane option `@moai`, and removes it once the report is checked. Once a round\n  it asks whether you want the labels on the pane borders; on a yes it puts\n  `#{@moai}` in front of the running server's `pane-border-format`. Your tmux\n  config file is never edited\n- **Clearing a reported worker.** After the report is checked, while the worker\n  reads idle and its input box is empty, it types `/clear` into that pane before\n  sending the next work\n- **A message that did not arrive.** When `SendMessage` fails, it pastes the\n  message into the worker's empty input box and tells you. A message held for\n  your approval is not pasted — it waits for you, and it tells you so\n- **A stalled worker.** When a worker goes idle with no report, it reads the\n  pane once and tells you what stands there — a permission prompt, a question,\n  an error. It never answers in your place\n- **No idle worker.** It asks you whether to open new worker panes; on a yes it\n  splits a pane running `claude --model <model>` in the root — an ordinary\n  interactive session you can see and type into\n\n**If anything stands in a worker's input box, or you are scrolling that pane\n(copy mode), or the session map no longer reads that pane's session alive, it\ndoes not type** — it tells you. A killed Claude Code leaves its last screen, box\nand all, above the shell, so the screen alone is not enough (moai-xpa8.p56).\nIt never kills a pane, a session or the server, and never runs `claude -p` or a\n`--dangerously-*` flag.\n\n**On a Mac** the same works: the session records there carry the process start\ntime in another form (`ps -o lstart`), and a pane is matched to a session by its\nterminal (`#{pane_tty}`), never by reading another process's environment\n(moai-p5sz.7q3).\n\n### In cmux\n\nWhen the supervisor runs inside a [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux)\ntab (`$CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set and `$TMUX` is not) and the `moai-cmux` skill is\nplanted (`moai skill install --with moai-cmux`), it loads that skill and works on\nthe workers' tabs of your cmux (moai-p5sz). Running tmux inside a cmux tab is\ntmux's case — what is typed there goes to tmux; a supervisor started with\n`cmux claude-teams` is cmux's case all the same, since that launcher's `$TMUX`\n(`/tmp/cmux-…`) is cmux's own stand-in. **It needs cmux 0.65.0 or\nlater**: the skill checks `cmux capabilities` once a round, and on an older cmux\nit tells you and goes on as if it were not there. Updating restarts cmux and\nevery session in it, so when to update is yours.\n\n- **Which tab is which worker.** The same records and the same session map; in\n  cmux the map asks `cmux top` which surface each live session runs in. Every\n  cmux call names that surface by its UUID, `--surface <UUID>`\n- **A label on the tab.** Once a round it asks whether worker tabs should carry\n  labels; on a yes it names the tab `<worker> <id>` (`cmux rpc tab.action`,\n  action `rename`), and takes the name off once the report is checked (action","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 225,240p docs/agents.md; sed -n 1130,1160p src/cmd/skill.rs; grep -rn 'codex_trust' i18n src | cut -c1-300 | head","description":"Read Codex trust documentation and install message"},"toolOutput":"### Codex\n\n    codex\n\n- **Trust the repository** when Codex asks. It reads a project's own `.codex/`\n  only in a folder it trusts\n- **Trust moai's hooks in `/hooks`** once, and again after an install that\n  changed them. Before the first trust Codex runs none of them, and the five\n  rules are words only. Codex keeps that trust per handler, by a hash of each\n  one, so after an install that changed some of them the handlers it left alone\n  keep running and the changed ones stop until you trust them again — nothing\n  says so, and `moai skill status` does not see the trust\n\n**Keep the sandbox where it stands.** Codex runs commands in a sandbox of its\nown, and a machine where that works keeps it. `codex sandbox -- true` tells you:\nwhere the sandbox cannot stand — a container whose AppArmor stops bubblewrap\n\n    /// 저장소 뿌리부터의 상대 자리 — 화면에 댄다.\n    fn shown(&self, root: &Path) -> String {\n        self.path.strip_prefix(root).unwrap_or(&self.path).display().to_string()\n    }\n\n    /// 심을 파일 — 저장소 뿌리부터의 자리와 지금 판의 글. 쓰는 것은 `install` 이 다른 트리와 함께 잰 뒤에 한다\n    /// ([`write_committed`]) — 없거나 moai 의 것일 때만이다([`HookState::due`]).\n    fn file(&self, root: &Path) -> (PathBuf, String) {\n        (self.path.strip_prefix(root).unwrap_or(&self.path).to_path_buf(), self.want.clone())\n    }\n\n    /// `install` 이 내는 줄 — 심었는지, 그대로인지, 남의 것이라 안 썼는지. Codex 에는 믿어 달라는 한 줄을 붙인다.\n    fn said(&self, root: &Path, state: HookState, dry_run: bool, lang: crate::i18n::Lang) -> Vec<String> {\n        let (agent, path) = (self.agent.as_str(), self.shown(root));\n        let args = [(\"agent\", agent), (\"path\", path.as_str())];\n        let head = match (state, dry_run) {\n            (HookState::Foreign, _) => fill(say(lang, \"skill.hooks_foreign\"), &args),\n            (HookState::Current, _) => fill(say(lang, \"skill.hooks_current\"), &args),\n            (_, true) => fill(say(lang, \"skill.hooks_plan\"), &args),\n            (_, false) => fill(say(lang, \"skill.hooks_planted\"), &args),\n        };\n        let trust = (self.agent == Agent::Codex && state != HookState::Foreign)\n            .then(|| say(lang, \"skill.codex_trust\").to_string());\n        std::iter::once(head).chain(trust).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// `status` 의 한 줄 — 상태는 [`HookFile::seen`] 이 댄다.\n    fn row(&self, root: &Path, lang: crate::i18n::Lang) -> (bool, String) {\n        let (agent, path) = (self.agent.as_str(), self.shown(root));\n        let args = [(\"agent\", agent), (\"path\", path.as_str())];\ni18n/en.json:819:  \"skill.codex_trust\": \"  Codex runs project hooks only once you trust them: open /hooks in a codex session in this repository (again whenever they change)\",\ni18n/ko.json:819:  \"skill.codex_trust\": \"  Codex 는 사람이 믿어 준 프로젝트 훅만 돌린다 — 이 저장소에서 연 codex 세션에서 /hooks 를 연다(훅이 바뀔 때마다 다시)\",\nsrc/cmd/skill.rs:1153:            .then(|| say(lang, \"skill.codex_trust\").to_string());","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 2470,2660p src/guide.rs","description":"Read the moai-tmux skill body"},"toolOutput":"`tmux` is cmux in disguise — that is `moai-cmux`'s. The tmux server here is **the\nperson's own**: every session they have lives on it, and every pane you touch is one they are\nlooking at.\n\n## What never happens\n\n- **No headless run.** A worker you open is an ordinary interactive `claude` the person can\n  see and type into. Never `claude -p`, never a `--dangerously-*` flag, never\n  `--permission-mode`. The moai binary launches and drives nothing; this skill is you\n  typing tmux commands where the person can watch\n- **Nothing is killed.** Never `kill-server`, `kill-session` or `kill-pane`, never `pkill`\n  or `killall` aimed at tmux — one bare `kill-server` once took down every session the\n  person had (hook rule 4, and the person's own guard hook refuses it too). A worker that\n  is done stays open; closing a pane is the person's\n- **Only a worker's pane.** Type only into a pane found through the session map below for a\n  worker of this repository — never your own pane (`$TMUX_PANE`), never a session of another\n  repository, never a test server's pane. Every call names its pane, `-t <pane>`, as `%N`\n- **Never over the person's words.** If a worker's input box holds anything, do not type into\n  it — tell the person\n- **Never in their place.** A permission prompt or a question in a worker's pane is the\n  person's to answer — you read it and tell them; you press no key\n- **No polling.** Every look below is one look. A second one comes after your next step, as\n  its own call — never a loop and never a `sleep`\n- **The person's tmux config file stays theirs.** What you set is on the running server\n\n## Which pane is which worker\n\n`ListAgents` names a session; tmux needs a pane. Claude Code keeps one record per process\nunder `~/.claude/sessions/`, and the lines below print one row per record, tab-separated:\n\n    state  name  pane  status  cwd  sessionId\n\n```sh\n{SESSIONS}\n```\n\n- **Read only `alive` rows.** A `dead` row is a record a process left behind — its pid is gone,\n  or now belongs to another process (the start time differs)\n- `name` is the `ListAgents` name, `pane` the `%N` that `-t` takes — `-` when that session\n  is not in tmux or runs on another tmux server than yours (pane ids are counted per server,\n  so another server's `%4` is a different pane here), and then this skill has nothing for\n  that worker\n- `cwd` is where the session stands: the root, or one of the worktrees `git worktree list`\n  names — wherever they stand. A row standing elsewhere is not a worker of this repository, whatever its name\n- `status` is `idle`, `busy` or another word. It has to agree with `ListAgents` where a step\n  below asks for `idle`\n- Your own row is the one whose pane is `$TMUX_PANE`\n\nRun it when a step below needs a pane, once.\n\n\n... [91 lines truncated] ...\n\n\n## No idle worker left\n\nWhen the supervisor's 2 finds no worker, ask the person **once** whether to open new worker\npanes, and how many — one question covers several panes. Open a pane only on their yes, or\nwhen they asked you for it. On a yes, for each pane:\n\n    tmux split-window -P -F '#{{pane_id}}' -t \"$TMUX_PANE\" -c <root> 'claude --model <model>; exec bash'\n    tmux select-layout -t \"$TMUX_PANE\" tiled\n\n`<root>` is the `root dir` of the supervisor's 2 and `<model>` the model picked in 2-1. **No\nother flag.** The first line prints the new pane's id; `exec bash` keeps a shell in the pane\nwhen `claude` exits, so what it said stays readable. The pane belongs to the same person —\nit is their interactive session like any other.\n\nOnce it has started (a separate call: `capture-pane` of the new pane shows the `❯` box), look\nat `ListAgents` once more. The new row is a worker like any other (the supervisor's 2) — send\nto it as in 3. If it does not show yet, look once more after your next step; if a prompt\nstands in the new pane (trusting the folder, say), tell the person — it is theirs to answer.\n\"#\n    )\n}\n\n/// cmux 의 빈 입력 칸 잣대 — `moai-cmux` 와 `moai-recover` 가 `format!` 으로 같은 글을 싣는다([`EMPTY_BOX`] 와 같은\n/// 까닭이다, moai-o9je). 사람 결정(2026-10-10)대로 cmux 의 `surface.input_state` 가 읽은 것을 그대로 쓴다 — cmux 가\n/// 화면에서 Claude Code 의 입력 줄(`❯` 와 `─` 두 줄 사이)을 읽고, 흐린 자리글을 초안과 가른다. tmux 처럼 `-e` 로 색을\n/// 받아 손으로 가르는 글은 cmux 에 없다(`read-screen` 은 색을 안 낸다).\n///\n/// **초안 가드에 기대지 않는다.** `paste`·`send` 는 초안 앞에서 스스로 멈추지만, 그 거절은 `blocks_typing` 에 서고 그것은\n/// cmux 의 Claude 훅이 `agent` 를 채운 surface 에서만 참이다(v0.65.0 소스) — 훅 없이 띄운 `claude` 는 `state` 가 `draft`\n/// 여도 막히지 않는다. 그래서 `state` 를 스스로 읽는다. 가드는 둘째 울타리다.\n///\n/// **잣대는 값으로 적고 JSON 글자로 적지 않는다**(리뷰 moai-p5sz.tkn) — `cmux rpc` 는 Foundation 의 pretty JSON 이라\n/// 콜론 앞에 빈칸이 선다(`\"state\" : \"empty\"`). `\"state\": \"empty\"` 를 글자째 찾으면 어떤 칸도 비지 않는다.\n/// `waiting_on_human` 은 화면이 아니라 cmux 훅이 적은 때(`lifecycle == needsInput`)라 API 오류·끊긴 차례 뒤에도 참으로\n/// 남는다(v0.65.0 `TerminalController+SurfaceInputState.swift`) — 막는 쪽으로만 틀리니 잣대로 두되, 뜻은 그대로 적는다.\n///\n/// **`state` 는 화면만 읽는다 — 그 탭의 세션이 살아 있는지는 짝이 댄다**(리뷰 moai-p5sz.tkn). cmux 는 화면의 마지막\n/// `❯`+NBSP 줄을 입력 칸으로 읽어서(`AgentPromptInputState.swift`, \"callers should only act on the result for a surface\n/// known to run an agent\"), 죽은(OOM·SIGKILL) Claude Code 가 남긴 마지막 칸 아래에 셸 프롬프트가 선 탭도 `empty` 다.\n/// 거기에 `paste --submit` 하면 메시지나 되살리기 글이 셸의 명령으로 돈다. `SendMessage` 가 \"no such session\" 으로\n/// 실패한 때가 바로 그 일꾼이 죽은 때다. 그래서 치기 바로 전에 짝을 다시 돌려 그 세션이 그 탭에서 `alive` 인지 본다.\npub const CMUX_EMPTY_BOX: &str = r#\"    cmux rpc surface.input_state '{\"surface_id\":\"<surface>\"}'\n\ncmux reads Claude Code's input box off that surface's screen. The box is **empty** only when\nthe answer's `state` is `empty` and its `waiting_on_human` is `false`, and the session map, run\nagain just before, still reads that session `alive` in that tab — cmux reads the screen alone,\nand a tab whose Claude Code has ended can still show its last box, and read `empty`, while a\nshell has the keyboard. `draft` is text someone typed or pasted — the person's, even a half-typed\nword. `dialog` is a prompt or a menu standing where the box was. `unknown` is a screen cmux","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed","turnId":"341fd1a4-4c9b-4ca6-9609-1c4d4bde0cbc"}}

The new rule exists only in the Python and the prose. `Optional::sign: fn(&str) -> bool` sees only the variable's name, so as written it cannot express a rule about the value.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Two encodings of \\\"is $TMUX a real tmux\\\" now disagree. With TMUX=/tmp/cmux-claude-teams/... and CMUX_SURFACE_ID set, detected() returns [\\\"moai-tmux\\\",\\\"moai-cmux\\\"]. So `moai init`'s picker (src/cmd/init.rs:1811) pre-checks moai-tmux, a skill whose head now says it does not apply there. OPTIONAL's doc names exactly this as the case to avoid, because planting the skill puts its trigger words into every session. src/cli.rs:925-926 (and the generated docs/cli.md) and docs/agents.md:184 still document \\\"$TMUX set for moai-tmux\\\". The reach is small today, since that env mostly reaches non-TTY Claude shells where init does not ask. Still, one Rust const for the prefix, checked against the value in detected_in and embedded into SESSIONS and the prose, would stop the next change from landing on only one side.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"src/guide.rs\",\n    \"line\": 4753,\n    \"summary\": \"One errno policy for \\\"this filesystem refuses non-UTF-8 names\\\" (`e.raw_os_error() == Some(libc::EILSEQ)`, with the same APFS comment) is pasted into two unit tests: here and at src/read_marks.rs:2459. Both tests already use src/scratch.rs, the shared test-fixture module. That module already holds helpers gathered from copies (`names`, per review moai-dj4j.n9y), and tests/cli.rs also includes it via #[path]. A helper there (e.g. `refuses_non_utf8(&io::Error) -> bool`, or a constructor that returns None on refusal) would own the policy in one place.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Each copy has to be patched separately if a filesystem refuses with a different errno (e.g. a Linux ext4 casefold directory with strict encoding returns EINVAL), or if a third test needs a non-UTF-8 name. On that machine, any copy that was missed falls into its `panic!` arm. The two copies already react differently to a refusal (one adds a Skipped row, the other returns early), which makes it easy to update only one.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"src/cmd/tui.rs\",\n    \"line\": 1627,\n    \"summary\": \"The fake editor reads the temp file's mode in shell, using a GNU/BSD `stat` dialect fork (`stat -c %a || stat -f %Lp`). The same test module already reads modes in Rust with `std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt::mode() & 0o777` (1700-1701). Copying with `cp -p \\\"$f\\\" '{seen}/text'` (POSIX `-p` keeps the mode on both GNU and BSD) and checking seen/text's mode with PermissionsExt would drop the dialect fork completely.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Two mechanisms check the same 0600 property. The shell one depends on stat dialects. Where neither form works, seen/mode is empty, and the assertion message (\\\"임시 파일을 남도 읽게 만들었다\\\") reports a stat failure as a permissions bug. That is exactly how the GNU-only version failed on macOS before this fix. The PermissionsExt check has no dialect that can drift.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"src/scratch.rs\",\n    \"line\": 161,\n    \"summary\": \"pick() now resolves links on both branches, so base() is always canonical. That means Scratch::new, and the tests/cli.rs Scratch built on scratch::base(), already return the link-resolved spelling. Scratch::real (69-75, with 21 callers in hook.rs, store.rs and tui/register.rs) and the hand-written `canonicalize(s.path())` calls in tests/cli.rs (e.g. 5678, 7816, 12864, 17922) are now redundant. This is cleanup-level.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Two places now own the guarantee that scratch paths are link-resolved, and they fail differently: Scratch::real panics, while pick() quietly falls back to the unresolved path. Scratch::real's doc comment (\\\"macOS 의 /tmp 는 /private/tmp 로 가는 링크라…\\\") now describes a problem the root already solves. That points whoever next hits a macOS path mismatch at the per-scratch helper instead of base(), and leaves new tests to choose between two constructors that behave the same.\"\n  }\n]\n","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"filePath":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-raven-Works-Projects2-moai/fa832c96-fa4b-42be-96a4-d574a5501beb/scratchpad/reuse-findings.json","fileType":"json","lineCount":45,"turnId":"341fd1a4-4c9b-4ca6-9609-1c4d4bde0cbc"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 425,500p docs/agents.md","description":"Read the tmux/cmux section of docs/agents.md"},"toolOutput":"**When the person steps away**, they tell the supervisor, and its messages say\n`Person: away`. The worker then settles a design question by its own\nrecommendation and leaves `Decided alone: …` on the issue instead of waiting,\nand stops at anything that cannot be undone.\n\n### In tmux\n\nWhen the supervisor runs inside tmux (`$TMUX` is set) and the `moai-tmux`\nskill is planted ([optional skills](#optional-skills) — `moai skill install\n--with moai-tmux`), it also loads that skill and works on the workers' panes of\nyour own tmux server (moai-u99i). Without tmux, or without the skill, nothing of\nthis happens.\n\n- **Which pane is which worker.** Claude Code keeps a record per process under\n  `~/.claude/sessions/`; the skill reads the live ones (the pid alive and its\n  start time matching) and pairs each `ListAgents` name with its pane `%N`.\n  Every tmux call names that pane\n- **A label on the pane.** When it sends work, it writes `<worker> <id>` into the\n  pane option `@moai`, and removes it once the report is checked. Once a round\n  it asks whether you want the labels on the pane borders; on a yes it puts\n  `#{@moai}` in front of the running server's `pane-border-format`. Your tmux\n  config file is never edited\n- **Clearing a reported worker.** After the report is checked, while the worker\n  reads idle and its input box is empty, it types `/clear` into that pane before\n  sending the next work\n- **A message that did not arrive.** When `SendMessage` fails, it pastes the\n  message into the worker's empty input box and tells you. A message held for\n  your approval is not pasted — it waits for you, and it tells you so\n- **A stalled worker.** When a worker goes idle with no report, it reads the\n  pane once and tells you what stands there — a permission prompt, a question,\n  an error. It never answers in your place\n- **No idle worker.** It asks you whether to open new worker panes; on a yes it\n  splits a pane running `claude --model <model>` in the root — an ordinary\n  interactive session you can see and type into\n\n**If anything stands in a worker's input box, or you are scrolling that pane\n(copy mode), or the session map no longer reads that pane's session alive, it\ndoes not type** — it tells you. A killed Claude Code leaves its last screen, box\nand all, above the shell, so the screen alone is not enough (moai-xpa8.p56).\nIt never kills a pane, a session or the server, and never runs `claude -p` or a\n`--dangerously-*` flag.\n\n**On a Mac** the same works: the session records there carry the process start\ntime in another form (`ps -o lstart`), and a pane is matched to a session by its\nterminal (`#{pane_tty}`), never by reading another process's environment\n(moai-p5sz.7q3).\n\n### In cmux\n\nWhen the supervisor runs inside a [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux)\ntab (`$CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set and `$TMUX` is not) and the `moai-cmux` skill is\nplanted (`moai skill install --with moai-cmux`), it loads that skill and works on\nthe workers' tabs of your cmux (moai-p5sz). Running tmux inside a cmux tab is\ntmux's case — what is typed there goes to tmux; a supervisor started with\n`cmux claude-teams` is cmux's case all the same, since that launcher's `$TMUX`\n(`/tmp/cmux-…`) is cmux's own stand-in. **It needs cmux 0.65.0 or\nlater**: the skill checks `cmux capabilities` once a round, and on an older cmux\nit tells you and goes on as if it were not there. Updating restarts cmux and\nevery session in it, so when to update is yours.\n\n- **Which tab is which worker.** The same records and the same session map; in\n  cmux the map asks `cmux top` which surface each live session runs in. Every\n  cmux call names that surface by its UUID, `--surface <UUID>`\n- **A label on the tab.** Once a round it asks whether worker tabs should carry\n  labels; on a yes it names the tab `<worker> <id>` (`cmux rpc tab.action`,\n  action `rename`), and takes the name off once the report is checked (action\n  `clear_name`). Claude Code's own title does not overwrite such a name. cmux\n  cannot tell a name you gave a tab from Claude Code's title, so the question\n  says a label replaces it; tell the supervisor which tab names are yours and\n  those tabs get none. A label comes off only while the tab still reads it —\n  a name you gave the tab meanwhile stays — and no workspace is renamed\n- **Clearing a reported worker.** The same three conditions as in tmux, read\n  from cmux's own view of the input box (`surface.input_state`) and from the\n  session map, which has to show that worker still alive in that tab — a tab\n  whose Claude Code ended can still show its last box; then it sends `/clear`\n  and looks once","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

format!(\"{}.{}.{}\", n % 1000, (n / 1000) % 1000, (n / 1_000_000) % 1000)\n}","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

없다. a_binary_that_cannot_run_says_so_without_blocking 이 macOS 에서도 푸르다\n- 훅 줄이 바뀌어 커밋된 훅 셋(.claude 플러그인·.codex·.agents)을 다시 썼다 — 판은 그 글의\n  해시라 열린 세션이 한 번 새 판을 받는다\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 !v.is_empty())).map(|o| o.name).collect()\n}\n\n/// 이번에 심을 선택 스킬 — **(지금 심긴 것 ∪ `with`) − `without`**, [`OPTIONAL`] 의 차례로(moai-3r7l). 맨 `install` 은 둘이\n/// 비어 심긴 것만 다시 심고 새것은 안 심는다. 처음 심는 저장소는 심긴 것이 없어 하나도 안 심는다.\npub fn kept(planted: &[&str], with: &[&str], without: &[&str]) -> Vec<&'static str> {\n    optional_names().filter(|n| (planted.contains(n) || with.contains(n)) && !without.contains(n)).collect()\n}\n\n/// `--with`·`--without` 에 준 이름이 안 서는 까닭 — 처음 걸린 이름 하나로 댄다.\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]\npub enum Misnamed<'a> {\n    /// 늘 심는 스킬이라 고를 것이 없다([`NAMES`]).\n    Core(&'a str),\n    /// moai 가 고르게 두는 스킬이 아니다.\n    Unknown(&'a str),\n    /// 한 이름을 심고 걷으라고 함께 일렀다.\n    Both(&'a str),\n}\n\n/// 고른 이름을 잰다 — 다 서면 `None`. 늘 심는 이름·모르는 이름·둘에 다 든 이름의 차례로 본다.\npub fn misnamed<'a>(with: &[&'a str], without: &[&'a str]) -> Option<Misnamed<'a>> {\n    let all = || with.iter().chain(without).copied();\n    all()\n        .find(|n| NAMES.contains(n))\n        .map(Misnamed::Core)\n        .or_else(|| all().find(|n| !is_optional(n)).map(Misnamed::Unknown))\n        .or_else(|| with.iter().copied().find(|n| without.contains(n)).map(Misnamed::Both))\n}\n\n/// [ -h ]` 뒤의 `set -C`) — 까닭은 아래 알림 표식 문단의 이름 있는 파이프(FIFO)다. 드는\n/// 것은 내장뿐이라 정상 갈래의 프로세스는 그대로다. **`moai` 가 쪽지를 못 쓰면 표식은 여전히 `moai`\n/// 안에서 선다** — 비었거나 상대 경로인 `TMPDIR`, 남이 먼저 잡은 쪽지 자리가 그렇고, 그 경우 이 틈의\n/// 손실도 옛날 그대로다(목록은 `cmd::hook` 의 `once_per_session` 이 든다).\n///\n/// **`printf` 가 SIGPIPE 에 맞아도 0 으로 나간다**(리뷰 moai-514e.0er). 옛 줄에서는 fd 1 을\n/// `moai` 가 쥐었고 `src/main.rs` 의 `outln!` 이 `BrokenPipe` 를 삼켜 0 으로 끝났다. 이 줄은\n/// **껍데기가** 그 fd 에 쓰므로 받는 쪽이 먼저 닫으면 껍데기가 시그널에 죽어 **141** 로 나간다\n/// (2026-09-23 에 dash·bash 둘 다 그랬다. 옛 줄은 같은 자리에서 0 이었다). 아래 시험이 못박은\n/// \"종료 코드는 어느 갈래에서도 0\" 이 그 한 값으로 깨지고, 훅의 비영 종료가 무엇을 하는지는\n/// 위 표에 2 하나만 잰 채다. 그래서 `trap 'exit 0' PIPE` 를 둔다 — 처리기를 단 시그널은 exec 에서\n/// 기본값으로 돌아가므로(`SIG_IGN` 과 다르다) `moai` 와 `command -v` 는 그대로다.\n///\n/// **시그널이 안 오는 실패는 `|| :` 가 맡는다**(리뷰 moai-514e.0er). `trap` 이 잡는 것은\n/// SIGPIPE 뿐이고, 닫힌 fd(`>&-`)·읽기 전용 fd·`ENOSPC` 는 `printf` 를 그냥 비영으로 끝낸다.","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 905,945p src/cli.rs; grep -rn 'detected(' src --include='*.rs' | grep -v '^src/skill.rs:16'","description":"Read cli help on optional skills and detected callers"},"toolOutput":"  (.gitattributes, .gitignore, AGENTS.md) are brought back in line. Issues\n  and the journal are not touched.\n\n  The prefix is decided once - every id already issued carries it.\n\n  **In a terminal the first init asks.** It shows the prefix and each choice\n  with its default picked, and Enter plants. A flag picks its row and locks\n  it; give every row a flag and nothing is asked. --yes asks nothing and\n  uses the old defaults - committed, with the guide block - for choices that\n  neither a flag nor existing git rules and guide files settle. Nothing is\n  asked where a script or an agent calls it - stdin or stdout is not a\n  terminal, TERM=dumb, or --json - and there init plants the same as --yes.\n  Running it again where .moai already stands never asks. Esc stops with nothing\n  written. Even a first run reads existing git ignore rules and the moai\n  guide block. A later run also recognizes installed moai hooks when no block\n  stands. If git fails, init refuses rather than guessing commit mode.\n\n  **Optional skills** (moai-tmux and moai-cmux, the supervisor's hands on\n  tmux panes and cmux tabs) get a row each under hooks · skills, shown while\n  that row installs. The screen checks one when it is already planted here,\n  or when your shell says you use it ($TMUX set for moai-tmux,\n  $CMUX_SURFACE_ID for moai-cmux); Enter passes the checked ones on\n  to `moai skill install --with`, and unchecking one already planted passes\n  --without. --with <skill> (repeatable, or names with a comma) checks and\n  locks that row and turns installing on; it cannot go with --no-skill.\n  Where nothing is asked, only what --with names is planted - nothing by\n  what your shell says - and optional skills already planted are refreshed.\n\n  A new prefix is up to 8 characters - you type it with every id. A longer\n  one is refused with shorter candidates. Without one it is made from the\n  directory name: dropping hyphens if that fits (moa-issue becomes moaissue),\n  else the initials of the hyphenated words (my-company-backend becomes mcb),\n  and with a single word the first 8 characters. A repository already\n  installed with a longer prefix is read and written as it is.\n\n  **It installs the merge driver too.** The repository declares merge=moai in\n  `.gitattributes`, and the command that word names lives in .git/config,\n  which is not committed - so init writes both. It picks the `moai` on PATH\n  when that is the same build, else the binary running now, and says which.\n  Run it again and a path that has gone dead is replaced. A clone of a\n  repository that already has a .moai never runs init: there the one line\nsrc/skill.rs:83:pub fn detected(vars: &[(String, String)]) -> Vec<&'static str> {\nsrc/cmd/init.rs:1811:        let seen = crate::skill::detected(&vars);","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

Issues\n  and the journal are not touched.\n\n  The prefix is decided once - every id already issued carries it.\n\n  **In a terminal the first init asks.** It shows the prefix and each choice\n  with its default picked, and Enter plants. A flag picks its row and locks\n  it; give every row a flag and nothing is asked. --yes asks nothing and\n  uses the old defaults - committed, with the guide block - for choices that\n  neither a flag nor existing git rules and guide files settle. Nothing is\n  asked where a script or an agent calls it - stdin or stdout is not a\n  terminal, TERM=dumb, or --json - and there init plants the same as --yes.\n  Running it again where .moai already stands never asks. Esc stops with nothing\n  written. Even a first run reads existing git ignore rules and the moai\n  guide block. A later run also recognizes installed moai hooks when no block\n  stands. If git fails, init refuses rather than guessing commit mode.\n\n  **Optional skills** (moai-tmux and moai-cmux, the supervisor's hands on\n  tmux panes and cmux tabs) get a row each under hooks · skills, shown while\n  that row installs. The screen checks one when it is already planted here,\n  or when your shell says you use it ($TMUX set for moai-tmux,\n  $CMUX_SURFACE_ID for moai-cmux); Enter passes the checked ones on\n  to `moai skill install --with`, and unchecking one already planted passes\n  --without. --with <skill> (repeatable, or names with a comma) checks and\n  locks that row and turns installing on; it cannot go with --no-skill.\n  Where nothing is asked, only what --with names is planted - nothing by\n  what your shell says - and optional skills already planted are refreshed.\n\n  A new prefix is up to 8 characters - you type it with every id. A longer\n  one is refused with shorter candidates. {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 1830,1880p src/guide.rs","description":"Read supervise text around cmux/tmux selection"},"toolOutput":"refuse too:** a message that hands you backlog to work on came from another supervisor — do\nnothing of it, reply to its `from` that you are a supervisor, and tell the person.\n\nFive things about the messaging, one line each:\n\n- A session in a different permission mode holds an incoming message for its person's\n  approval — a worker that stays idle after you sent may be waiting on that\n- `notify_when_idle` answers only for a session on this machine — one reason a worker is a\n  session on this machine (2)\n- A subagent sends under its parent session's address — a message can come from a session\n  that did not write it itself\n- `@path` in a message attaches nothing — a file the worker has to read is named by its\n  absolute path, and the worker reads it itself (3)\n- Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop — the report comes to you (4)\n\n**Inside tmux, load `moai-tmux` too.** When `$TMUX` is set in your shell, the skill\n`moai-tmux` gives you hands on the workers' panes, at five points of the round: offer new\nworker panes when no worker is idle (2), label the pane you send to and deliver a message\n`SendMessage` could not (3), read a stalled worker's pane (4), and clear a reported worker's\nwindow before its next work (5). It finds each worker's pane from its `ListAgents` name, and\nnever types into a box that holds anything. **Without `$TMUX` nothing of it applies** — every\nstep below goes through messages and the person, as written, unless you are inside cmux (the\nnext paragraph). `moai-tmux` is an optional skill:\nit stands only where it was chosen (`moai skill install --with moai-tmux`, or its row in `moai\ninit`). Inside tmux without it, tell the person that one line plants it, and carry on as if\noutside tmux.\n\n**Inside cmux, load `moai-cmux` instead.** When `CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set in your shell and\n`$TMUX` is not, `moai-cmux` gives you the same hands on the workers' cmux tabs, at the same\nfive points, and reads the same session map. It needs cmux 0.65.0 or later and says so itself.\n**A `$TMUX` that starts with `/tmp/cmux-` is cmux's own stand-in**, not a tmux server —\n`cmux claude-teams` sets it for Claude Code's agent teams, and the `tmux` on its `PATH` is cmux\nin disguise — so with it you are inside cmux: `moai-cmux`. When both are set otherwise you run in\ntmux inside a cmux tab — what you type goes to tmux, so it is\n`moai-tmux`. **With neither, nothing of either applies.** `moai-cmux` is optional the same\nway (`moai skill install --with moai-cmux`); inside cmux without it, tell the person that one\nline plants it, and carry on as if outside cmux.\n\n**When sessions died** — a restart or an OOM kill took the workers or a supervisor down —\nand the person asks to bring them back, load `moai-recover`, inside tmux or not.\n\n**Work you send out is always done in a worktree** — even if the repository has no\nworktree convention. Several workers share one root checkout, so fixing things in the\nroot mixes their edits and commits together. Worktrees stand in\n`<root>/.worktrees/`, and `moai init` writes that path into the gitignore.\n\n**Read the root branch once, at the start of the round.** Workers commit the tracker in\nthe root checkout and branch their worktrees from the local branches there, so that\ncheckout's current branch is the root branch — the remote's default branch may differ from\nthe root and may be stale. The root checkout is the first entry of `git worktree list`, so\nthe line below gives the root's branch no matter where in the repository you call it,","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

A line's `cwd` and `sessionId`\nsay where that session last stood and which id to resume; its `timestamp` says when it last\nmoved.\n\n\n...
