The box is **empty** only when\nthe answer's `state` is `empty` and its `waiting_on_human` is `false`, and the session map, run\nagain just before, still reads that session `alive` in that tab — cmux reads the screen alone,\nand a tab whose Claude Code has ended can still show its last box, and read `empty`, while a\nshell has the keyboard. `draft` is text someone typed or pasted — the person's, even a half-typed\nword. `dialog` is a prompt or a menu standing where the box was. `unknown` is a screen cmux\ncannot read as Claude Code's — a shell prompt, a process that ended. `waiting_on_human` is cmux's\nnote that the session last asked the person something — a permission prompt, a question — and\nit can stay `true` after an API error or an interrupt. None of these is a box to type into, and\nneither is an error or an answer without `state`.\"#;\n\n/// 선택 스킬 `moai-cmux` 의 SKILL.md — cmux 안에서 도는 감독의 손이다(2026-10-10 사용자 결정, moai-p5sz). `moai-tmux`\n/// ([`tmux`])의 cmux 짝이라 그 글과 결정을 그대로 옮긴다 — 칸을 비우고, 닿지 않은 메시지를 붙이고, 사람이 그러라고 한\n/// 뒤에 새 일꾼 칸을 연다. 바이너리는 아무것도 띄우거나 몰지 않고(새 명령이 없다), 헤드리스·`-p`·`--dangerously-*`·\n/// 권한 모드 바꾸기는 없다. 고른 사람에게만 심는다(`skill::OPTIONAL`, 표식 `CMUX_SURFACE_ID`).\n///\n/// **cmux 0.65.0 이 바닥이다**(2026-10-11 사용자 결정). 사람이 고른 길 — 짝의 `top`, 붙이기의 `paste --submit`, 빈 칸\n/// 판정의 `surface.input_state` — 이 모두 그 판에서 처음 섰다(v0.63.2·v0.65.0·main 소스를 견줌, moai-p5sz.6uv 노트).","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 1835,1875p src/guide.rs","description":"Read supervise tmux/cmux paragraphs"},"toolOutput":"- A session in a different permission mode holds an incoming message for its person's\n  approval — a worker that stays idle after you sent may be waiting on that\n- `notify_when_idle` answers only for a session on this machine — one reason a worker is a\n  session on this machine (2)\n- A subagent sends under its parent session's address — a message can come from a session\n  that did not write it itself\n- `@path` in a message attaches nothing — a file the worker has to read is named by its\n  absolute path, and the worker reads it itself (3)\n- Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop — the report comes to you (4)\n\n**Inside tmux, load `moai-tmux` too.** When `$TMUX` is set in your shell, the skill\n`moai-tmux` gives you hands on the workers' panes, at five points of the round: offer new\nworker panes when no worker is idle (2), label the pane you send to and deliver a message\n`SendMessage` could not (3), read a stalled worker's pane (4), and clear a reported worker's\nwindow before its next work (5). It finds each worker's pane from its `ListAgents` name, and\nnever types into a box that holds anything. **Without `$TMUX` nothing of it applies** — every\nstep below goes through messages and the person, as written, unless you are inside cmux (the\nnext paragraph). `moai-tmux` is an optional skill:\nit stands only where it was chosen (`moai skill install --with moai-tmux`, or its row in `moai\ninit`). Inside tmux without it, tell the person that one line plants it, and carry on as if\noutside tmux.\n\n**Inside cmux, load `moai-cmux` instead.** When `CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set in your shell and\n`$TMUX` is not, `moai-cmux` gives you the same hands on the workers' cmux tabs, at the same\nfive points, and reads the same session map. It needs cmux 0.65.0 or later and says so itself.\n**A `$TMUX` that starts with `/tmp/cmux-` is cmux's own stand-in**, not a tmux server —\n`cmux claude-teams` sets it for Claude Code's agent teams, and the `tmux` on its `PATH` is cmux\nin disguise — so with it you are inside cmux: `moai-cmux`. When both are set otherwise you run in\ntmux inside a cmux tab — what you type goes to tmux, so it is\n`moai-tmux`. **With neither, nothing of either applies.** `moai-cmux` is optional the same\nway (`moai skill install --with moai-cmux`); inside cmux without it, tell the person that one\nline plants it, and carry on as if outside cmux.\n\n**When sessions died** — a restart or an OOM kill took the workers or a supervisor down —\nand the person asks to bring them back, load `moai-recover`, inside tmux or not.\n\n**Work you send out is always done in a worktree** — even if the repository has no\nworktree convention. Several workers share one root checkout, so fixing things in the\nroot mixes their edits and commits together. Worktrees stand in\n`<root>/.worktrees/`, and `moai init` writes that path into the gitignore.","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 430,500p docs/agents.md","description":"Read docs/agents.md tmux/cmux sections"},"toolOutput":"### In tmux\n\nWhen the supervisor runs inside tmux (`$TMUX` is set) and the `moai-tmux`\nskill is planted ([optional skills](#optional-skills) — `moai skill install\n--with moai-tmux`), it also loads that skill and works on the workers' panes of\nyour own tmux server (moai-u99i). Without tmux, or without the skill, nothing of\nthis happens.\n\n- **Which pane is which worker.** Claude Code keeps a record per process under\n  `~/.claude/sessions/`; the skill reads the live ones (the pid alive and its\n  start time matching) and pairs each `ListAgents` name with its pane `%N`.\n  Every tmux call names that pane\n- **A label on the pane.** When it sends work, it writes `<worker> <id>` into the\n  pane option `@moai`, and removes it once the report is checked. Once a round\n  it asks whether you want the labels on the pane borders; on a yes it puts\n  `#{@moai}` in front of the running server's `pane-border-format`. Your tmux\n  config file is never edited\n- **Clearing a reported worker.** After the report is checked, while the worker\n  reads idle and its input box is empty, it types `/clear` into that pane before\n  sending the next work\n- **A message that did not arrive.** When `SendMessage` fails, it pastes the\n  message into the worker's empty input box and tells you. A message held for\n  your approval is not pasted — it waits for you, and it tells you so\n- **A stalled worker.** When a worker goes idle with no report, it reads the\n  pane once and tells you what stands there — a permission prompt, a question,\n  an error. It never answers in your place\n- **No idle worker.** It asks you whether to open new worker panes; on a yes it\n  splits a pane running `claude --model <model>` in the root — an ordinary\n  interactive session you can see and type into\n\n**If anything stands in a worker's input box, or you are scrolling that pane\n(copy mode), or the session map no longer reads that pane's session alive, it\ndoes not type** — it tells you. A killed Claude Code leaves its last screen, box\nand all, above the shell, so the screen alone is not enough (moai-xpa8.p56).\nIt never kills a pane, a session or the server, and never runs `claude -p` or a\n`--dangerously-*` flag.\n\n**On a Mac** the same works: the session records there carry the process start\ntime in another form (`ps -o lstart`), and a pane is matched to a session by its\nterminal (`#{pane_tty}`), never by reading another process's environment\n(moai-p5sz.7q3).\n\n### In cmux\n\nWhen the supervisor runs inside a [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux)\ntab (`$CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set and `$TMUX` is not) and the `moai-cmux` skill is\nplanted (`moai skill install --with moai-cmux`), it loads that skill and works on\nthe workers' tabs of your cmux (moai-p5sz). Running tmux inside a cmux tab is\ntmux's case — what is typed there goes to tmux; a supervisor started with\n`cmux claude-teams` is cmux's case all the same, since that launcher's `$TMUX`\n(`/tmp/cmux-…`) is cmux's own stand-in. **It needs cmux 0.65.0 or\nlater**: the skill checks `cmux capabilities` once a round, and on an older cmux\nit tells you and goes on as if it were not there. Updating restarts cmux and\nevery session in it, so when to update is yours.\n\n- **Which tab is which worker.** The same records and the same session map; in\n  cmux the map asks `cmux top` which surface each live session runs in. Every\n  cmux call names that surface by its UUID, `--surface <UUID>`\n- **A label on the tab.** Once a round it asks whether worker tabs should carry\n  labels; on a yes it names the tab `<worker> <id>` (`cmux rpc tab.action`,\n  action `rename`), and takes the name off once the report is checked (action\n  `clear_name`). Claude Code's own title does not overwrite such a name. cmux\n  cannot tell a name you gave a tab from Claude Code's title, so the question\n  says a label replaces it; tell the supervisor which tab names are yours and\n  those tabs get none. Claude Code writes its own topic into the pane title,\nso the label lives in the pane option `@moai`. Remove it when that work's report is checked\n(the supervisor's 5):\n\n    tmux set-option -p -u -t <pane> @moai\n\n**Showing it is the person's choice, asked once per round.** Ask whether the labels should\nshow on the pane borders. On a yes, read the running server's two settings:\n\n    tmux show -gv pane-border-format\n    tmux show -gv pane-border-status\n\nand put the label in front of the format you read:\n\n    tmux set -g pane-border-format '#{{?@moai,#{{@moai}} ,}}<the value you read>'\n    tmux set -g pane-border-status top\n\nSet `pane-border-status` only when it read `off`. If the format you read already starts with\n`#{{?@moai,`, it is shown already — leave it. If that value holds a single quote, do not build\nthe line; tell the person what to add. Never write the person's tmux config file.\n\n## Clear a worker's window\n\nBefore you send a worker its next work, you may clear its window (`/clear`) yourself — all of\nthese first:\n\n1. **Its report is checked** — the supervisor's 5 held all three checks and the\n   `Report-checked:` note is written\n2. **It reads `idle`** — in `ListAgents` and in its row of the session map\n3. **Its input box is empty** (above)\n\nThen:\n\n    tmux send-keys -t <pane> /clear Enter\n\nand, as a separate call, look once: the session map reads `idle` for it and `capture-pane`\nshows the cleared screen — the conversation gone, an empty box. Then send with `SendMessage`\nas the supervisor's 3 says. **If any condition fails, or the look does not show it cleared,\ndo not type again** — do what the supervisor's 5 says without tmux: ask the person, or send\nto another idle worker. When it was the look that failed, tell the person that `/clear` may\nstand typed in that pane's box: pressed later, it would erase the next message sent there.\n\n## When a message does not arrive\n\nWhen `SendMessage` to a worker fails — an error, no such session — and that worker has a pane\nwhose input box is empty (above), you may put the message into the box yourself. **A message\nheld for the person's approval is not one that failed:** that hold is the person's gate, like\na permission prompt, and the held message still arrives once they approve it — pasting it too\n\n... [10 lines truncated] ...\n\n       tmux paste-buffer -p -d -b moai-send -t <pane>\n       tmux send-keys -t <pane> Enter\n\n3. **Tell the person** you did, and into which pane\n\nThe worker still answers with `SendMessage`. A worker that answered your message by refusing\nthe work is not a delivery that failed — it comes out of the candidates (the supervisor's 2).\n\n## When a worker stalls\n\nWhen a `notify_when_idle` notice comes with no report, or the person asks about a worker that\nhas read `busy` far longer than its work should take, look at its pane once:\n\n    tmux capture-pane -p -t <pane> -S -40\n\nand read why it stopped — a permission prompt, a question (`AskUserQuestion`), an API or\nrate-limit error, or a process that ended (a shell prompt where the box was). **Tell the\nperson** what the pane shows and which pane it is. Do not answer the prompt, do not press a\nkey, and do not look again in a loop. A process that ended is a dead session: bringing it\nback is `moai-recover`, once the person asks for it.\n\n## No idle worker left\n\nWhen the supervisor's 2 finds no worker, ask the person **once** whether to open new worker\npanes, and how many — one question covers several panes. Open a pane only on their yes, or\nwhen they asked you for it. On a yes, for each pane:\n\n    tmux split-window -P -F '#{{pane_id}}' -t \"$TMUX_PANE\" -c <root> 'claude --model <model>; exec bash'\n    tmux select-layout -t \"$TMUX_PANE\" tiled\n\n`<root>` is the `root dir` of the supervisor's 2 and `<model>` the model picked in 2-1. **No\nother flag.** The first line prints the new pane's id; `exec bash` keeps a shell in the pane\nwhen `claude` exits, so what it said stays readable. The pane belongs to the same person —\nit is their interactive session like any other.\n\nOnce it has started (a separate call: `capture-pane` of the new pane shows the `❯` box), look\nat `ListAgents` once more. The new row is a worker like any other (the supervisor's 2) — send\nto it as in 3. If it does not show yet, look once more after your next step; if a prompt\nstands in the new pane (trusting the folder, say), tell the person — it is theirs to answer.\n\"#\n    )\n}\n\n/// cmux 의 빈 입력 칸 잣대 — `moai-cmux` 와 `moai-recover` 가 `format!` 으로 같은 글을 싣는다([`EMPTY_BOX`] 와 같은\n/// 까닭이다, moai-o9je). 사람 결정(2026-10-10)대로 cmux 의 `surface.input_state` 가 읽은 것을 그대로 쓴다 — cmux 가\n/// 화면에서 Claude Code 의 입력 줄(`❯` 와 `─` 두 줄 사이)을 읽고, 흐린 자리글을 초안과 가른다. tmux 처럼 `-e` 로 색을\n/// 받아 손으로 가르는 글은 cmux 에 없다(`read-screen` 은 색을 안 낸다).\n///\n/// **초안 가드에 기대지 않는다.** `paste`·`send` 는 초안 앞에서 스스로 멈추지만, 그 거절은 `blocks_typing` 에 서고 그것은\n/// cmux 의 Claude 훅이 `agent` 를 채운 surface 에서만 참이다(v0.65.0 소스) — 훅 없이 띄운 `claude` 는 `state` 가 `draft`","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed","turnId":"8069921a-80de-477b-8468-c8f893a9af67"}}

Every call names its pane, `-t <pane>`, as `%N`\n- **Never over the person's words.** If a worker's input box holds anything, do not type into\n  it — tell the person\n- **Never in their place.** A permission prompt or a question in a worker's pane is the\n\n... It is `-` when that session is not\n  in a cmux tab of yours — another terminal, or tmux, tmux inside a cmux tab included — when it\n  shares its tab with another live session, or when cmux gave no answer (a line on its own says\n  so), and then this skill has nothing for that worker\n- **No row at all, and a line saying no record reads alive:** this shell cannot tell live from\n  dead — act on no row, and tell the person what it said\n- `cwd` is where the session stands: the root, or one of the worktrees `git worktree list`\n  names — wherever they stand. Then, as a\nseparate call, look once: the session map reads `idle` for it and\n\n    cmux read-screen --surface <surface> --lines 20\n\nshows the cleared screen — the conversation gone, an empty box. Then send with `SendMessage`\nas the supervisor's 3 says. **If any condition fails, cmux refuses to type, or the look does not\nshow it cleared, do not type again** — do what the supervisor's 5 says without cmux: ask the\nperson, or send to another idle worker. Triggers on \"worker surface\", \"worker tab\", \"open a worker\", \"clear the worker\", \"일꾼 탭\", \"일꾼 창 열어\", \"탭 비워\".\n---\n\n# moai-cmux — the supervisor's hands on the workers' surfaces\n\nThis is the supervisor's (`moai-supervise`) companion **when it runs inside cmux** —\n`CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set in its shell and `$TMUX` is not. A `$TMUX` that starts with\n`/tmp/cmux-` counts as not set: it is cmux's own stand-in, which cmux's `claude-teams` sets for\nClaude Code's agent teams, and the `tmux` on that `PATH` is cmux in disguise — it passes\n`set-option` by and refuses `load-buffer`. Inside a real tmux — one running in a cmux tab\nincluded — what you type goes to tmux: that is `moai-tmux`, and none of this applies.\nOutside both tmux and cmux none of this applies either: the supervisor works through messages\nand the person alone. The cmux app here is **the person's own**: every workspace they have lives\nin it, and every surface you touch is a tab they are looking at.\n\ncmux's words: a window holds workspaces (the rows of its sidebar), a workspace holds panes (its\nsplits), and a pane holds surfaces (the tabs of that split). A surface is one terminal — what you\nread and what you type into.\n\n## First, the version\n\nThis needs cmux 0.65.0 or later. Look once, at the start of the round:\n\n    cmux capabilities\n\nIf its `methods` do not list `surface.input_state`, the cmux here is older: tell the person once\nthat `moai-cmux` needs cmux 0.65.0 or later, and go on as if this skill were not here. Updating\nrestarts cmux, and with it every session inside — yours too — so when is theirs to choose. If it\nprints an error instead of a `methods` list — a socket it cannot reach, a sandbox — that says\nnothing about the version: tell the person what it said, and go on as if this skill were not here.\n\n## What never happens\n\n- **No headless run.** A worker you open is an ordinary interactive `claude` the person can\n  see and type into. Never `claude -p`, never a `--dangerously-*` flag, never\n  `--permission-mode`. The moai binary launches and drives nothing; this skill is you\n  typing cmux commands where the person can watch\n- **Nothing is closed.** Never `close-surface`, `close-workspace` or `close-window`, never\n  `respawn-pane`, never `pkill` or `killall` aimed at cmux. A worker that is done stays open;\n  closing a tab is the person's\n- **Never `--force`.** cmux refuses to type into a Claude Code box that holds someone's words or a\n  dialog — but only for a session its own Claude hook knows, which is why you read the box\n\n... [129 lines truncated] ...\n\n\nThe worker still answers with `SendMessage`. A worker that answered your message by refusing\nthe work is not a delivery that failed — it comes out of the candidates (the supervisor's 2).\n\n## When a worker stalls\n\nWhen a `notify_when_idle` notice comes with no report, or the person asks about a worker that\nhas read `busy` far longer than its work should take, look at its tab once:\n\n    cmux read-screen --surface <surface> --lines 40\n\nand read why it stopped — a permission prompt, a question (`AskUserQuestion`), an API or\nrate-limit error, or a process that ended (a shell prompt where the box was, or under its last\nbox). The input box check above gives a hint when you have it: `waiting_on_human` says the\nsession last asked the person something — it can outlast an API error, so the screen decides —\nand `unknown` is a screen that is no longer Claude Code's; whether the session is still alive,\nthe session map says. **Tell the person** what the tab\nshows and which tab it is. Do not answer the prompt, do not press a key, and do not look again\nin a loop. A process that ended is a dead session: bringing it back is `moai-recover`, once\nthe person asks for it.\n\n## No idle worker left\n\nWhen the supervisor's 2 finds no worker, ask the person **once** whether to open new worker\ntabs, and how many — one question covers several. Open one only on their yes, or when they\nasked you for it. On a yes, for each:\n\n    cmux --id-format both new-split right --surface \"$CMUX_SURFACE_ID\" --command 'cd <root> && claude --model <model>'\n\n`<root>` is the `root dir` of the supervisor's 2 and `<model>` the model picked in 2-1. **No\nother flag** on `claude`. It prints `OK surface:<n> (<UUID>) workspace:<n> (<UUID>)` — the first\nUUID is the new surface, the second your workspace. `--command` is typed into the new tab's\nshell, so the shell stays when `claude` exits and what it said stays readable, and the split\ndoes not take focus. **If cmux refuses the split** — no space for a new pane, as every split\nlands in your row, or it cannot find your tab in the workspace this session started in — open\nno more: tell the person how many opened and what it said. When all are open, even the splits\nout once:\n\n    cmux rpc workspace.equalize_splits '{{\"workspace_id\":\"<workspace UUID>\"}}'\n\nThe tab belongs to the same person — it is their interactive session like any other.\n\nOnce it has started (a separate call: the input box check above reads `empty` for the new\nsurface), look at `ListAgents` once more. The new row is a worker like any other (the\nsupervisor's 2) — send to it as in 3. If it does not show yet, look once more after your next\nstep; if a prompt stands in the new tab (trusting the folder, say), tell the person — it is\ntheirs to answer.\n\"#\n    )\n}","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 175,195p docs/agents.md; echo ----; sed -n 425,490p docs/agents.md","description":"Read docs/agents.md around the tmux/cmux sections"},"toolOutput":"    moai skill uninstall --only moai-tmux     the same, under the uninstall name\n    moai init --with moai-tmux                plant it with the rest on the first init\n    moai skill install --with moai-cmux       the cmux one, the same way\n\n- **Nothing writes the choice down.** A skill planted in the tree is the answer.\n  So a plain `moai skill install` refreshes the optional skills already planted\n  and plants no new one, and a first install plants none\n- **The first `moai init` in a terminal offers a row per optional skill** under\n  the hooks and skills row. A row starts checked when the skill is already\n  planted, or when your shell says you use it (`$TMUX` set, for `moai-tmux`;\n  `$CMUX_SURFACE_ID` set, for `moai-cmux`).\n  Where nothing is asked — a script, an agent, `--yes` — only what `--with`\n  names is planted, never what the shell suggests\n- **`uninstall --only` keeps the registration.** It removes that skill's\n  directory (only while it holds nothing but moai's files) and brings Claude's\n  registration up to the new version where it already stands; where none stands\n  it changes the files and registers nothing. A tree moai has not planted\n  stays as it is — no plugin, no `.agents/skills/`, no hooks file is made\n- **A skill you left out is not drift.** The notice that the planted skills\n  differ from this moai's does not count an optional skill you did not plant\n\n----\n**When the person steps away**, they tell the supervisor, and its messages say\n`Person: away`. The worker then settles a design question by its own\nrecommendation and leaves `Decided alone: …` on the issue instead of waiting,\nand stops at anything that cannot be undone.\n\n### In tmux\n\nWhen the supervisor runs inside tmux (`$TMUX` is set) and the `moai-tmux`\nskill is planted ([optional skills](#optional-skills) — `moai skill install\n--with moai-tmux`), it also loads that skill and works on the workers' panes of\nyour own tmux server (moai-u99i). Without tmux, or without the skill, nothing of\nthis happens.\n\n- **Which pane is which worker.** Claude Code keeps a record per process under\n  `~/.claude/sessions/`; the skill reads the live ones (the pid alive and its\n  start time matching) and pairs each `ListAgents` name with its pane `%N`.\n  Every tmux call names that pane\n- **A label on the pane.** When it sends work, it writes `<worker> <id>` into the\n  pane option `@moai`, and removes it once the report is checked. Once a round\n  it asks whether you want the labels on the pane borders; on a yes it puts\n  `#{@moai}` in front of the running server's `pane-border-format`. Your tmux\n  config file is never edited\n- **Clearing a reported worker.** After the report is checked, while the worker\n  reads idle and its input box is empty, it types `/clear` into that pane before\n  sending the next work\n- **A message that did not arrive.** When `SendMessage` fails, it pastes the\n  message into the worker's empty input box and tells you. A message held for\n  your approval is not pasted — it waits for you, and it tells you so\n- **A stalled worker.** When a worker goes idle with no report, it reads the\n  pane once and tells you what stands there — a permission prompt, a question,\n  an error. It never answers in your place\n- **No idle worker.** It asks you whether to open new worker panes; on a yes it\n  splits a pane running `claude --model <model>` in the root — an ordinary\n  interactive session you can see and type into\n\n**If anything stands in a worker's input box, or you are scrolling that pane\n(copy mode), or the session map no longer reads that pane's session alive, it\ndoes not type** — it tells you. A killed Claude Code leaves its last screen, box\nand all, above the shell, so the screen alone is not enough (moai-xpa8.p56).\nIt never kills a pane, a session or the server, and never runs `claude -p` or a\n`--dangerously-*` flag.\n\n**On a Mac** the same works: the session records there carry the process start\ntime in another form (`ps -o lstart`), and a pane is matched to a session by its\nterminal (`#{pane_tty}`), never by reading another process's environment\n(moai-p5sz.7q3).\n\n### In cmux\n\nWhen the supervisor runs inside a [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux)\ntab (`$CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set and `$TMUX` is not) and the `moai-cmux` skill is\nplanted (`moai skill install --with moai-cmux`), it loads that skill and works on\nthe workers' tabs of your cmux (moai-p5sz). Running tmux inside a cmux tab is\ntmux's case — what is typed there goes to tmux; a supervisor started with\n`cmux claude-teams` is cmux's case all the same, since that launcher's `$TMUX`\n(`/tmp/cmux-…`) is cmux's own stand-in. **It needs cmux 0.65.0 or\nlater**: the skill checks `cmux capabilities` once a round, and on an older cmux\nit tells you and goes on as if it were not there. Updating restarts cmux and\nevery session in it, so when to update is yours.\n\n- **Which tab is which worker.** The same records and the same session map; in\n  cmux the map asks `cmux top` which surface each live session runs in. Every\n  cmux call names that surface by its UUID, `--surface <UUID>`\n- **A label on the tab.** Once a round it asks whether worker tabs should carry\n  labels; on a yes it names the tab `<worker> <id>` (`cmux rpc tab.action`,\n  action `rename`), and takes the name off once the report is checked (action","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 425,560p docs/agents.md","description":"Read docs/agents.md supervisor tmux/cmux sections"},"toolOutput":"**When the person steps away**, they tell the supervisor, and its messages say\n`Person: away`. The worker then settles a design question by its own\nrecommendation and leaves `Decided alone: …` on the issue instead of waiting,\nand stops at anything that cannot be undone.\n\n### In tmux\n\nWhen the supervisor runs inside tmux (`$TMUX` is set) and the `moai-tmux`\nskill is planted ([optional skills](#optional-skills) — `moai skill install\n--with moai-tmux`), it also loads that skill and works on the workers' panes of\nyour own tmux server (moai-u99i). Without tmux, or without the skill, nothing of\nthis happens.\n\n- **Which pane is which worker.** Claude Code keeps a record per process under\n  `~/.claude/sessions/`; the skill reads the live ones (the pid alive and its\n  start time matching) and pairs each `ListAgents` name with its pane `%N`.\n  Every tmux call names that pane\n- **A label on the pane.** When it sends work, it writes `<worker> <id>` into the\n  pane option `@moai`, and removes it once the report is checked. Once a round\n  it asks whether you want the labels on the pane borders; on a yes it puts\n  `#{@moai}` in front of the running server's `pane-border-format`. Your tmux\n  config file is never edited\n- **Clearing a reported worker.** After the report is checked, while the worker\n  reads idle and its input box is empty, it types `/clear` into that pane before\n  sending the next work\n- **A message that did not arrive.** When `SendMessage` fails, it pastes the\n  message into the worker's empty input box and tells you. A message held for\n  your approval is not pasted — it waits for you, and it tells you so\n- **A stalled worker.** When a worker goes idle with no report, it reads the\n  pane once and tells you what stands there — a permission prompt, a question,\n  an error. It never answers in your place\n- **No idle worker.** It asks you whether to open new worker panes; on a yes it\n  splits a pane running `claude --model <model>` in the root — an ordinary\n  interactive session you can see and type into\n\n**If anything stands in a worker's input box, or you are scrolling that pane\n(copy mode), or the session map no longer reads that pane's session alive, it\ndoes not type** — it tells you. A killed Claude Code leaves its last screen, box\nand all, above the shell, so the screen alone is not enough (moai-xpa8.p56).\nIt never kills a pane, a session or the server, and never runs `claude -p` or a\n`--dangerously-*` flag.\n\n**On a Mac** the same works: the session records there carry the process start\ntime in another form (`ps -o lstart`), and a pane is matched to a session by its\nterminal (`#{pane_tty}`), never by reading another process's environment\n(moai-p5sz.7q3).\n\n### In cmux\n\nWhen the supervisor runs inside a [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux)\n\n... [36 lines truncated] ...\n\nIt never closes a tab, a workspace or a window, never moves focus, and never\npasses `--force`.\n\n### Bring back sessions that died\n\nWhen the supervisor and its workers died together — the machine restarted, the\ncontainer was OOM-killed — open one Claude Code session in the root and ask it\nto bring them back (\"recover the sessions\", \"되살려\"). It loads `moai-recover`\n(moai-uqf7); your asking is the yes.\n\n- **Which died.** It reads the same records under `~/.claude/sessions/` and\n  takes the dead ones standing in the root or a worktree, leaving out any that\n  is already back and older crashes you did not name. When several stand in one\n  directory it asks you once which to bring back\n- **What each was doing.** From each session's transcript under\n  `~/.claude/projects/` it reads its role (supervisor or worker), the issue it\n  held and what it was waiting for, adds the uncommitted files and the issue's\n  `Next:` note, and shows you one table\n- **What died with it.** A background subagent or command that never reported\n  back, and a `target` link whose `/tmp/cargo-target/<name>` was wiped — it\n  makes that directory again; the build output is gone, so the session rebuilds\n- **Bringing them back, workers first and the supervisor last.** Inside tmux it\n  splits a pane per session running `claude --resume <id>` and pastes a short\n  note on what happened once the input box is empty; the supervisor is told its\n  workers' names may have changed. Inside cmux (0.65.0 or later) it does the\n  same with a split tab per session, and when cmux has no room for another pane\n  the sessions left get the lines to type. Outside both it prints, per session,\n  `cd <dir> && claude --resume <id>` and the note to paste\n\nIt changes nothing in the sessions' work — no commit, no build, no `moai` write.\n\n## Work the queue from a session\n\nEvery command takes `--json`. Three are enough for a session to take its next row:\n\n- `moai ready --json` — `ready` is yours to pick up, `others` is ready work that\n  belongs to someone else or nobody (ask first), `held` is what is deferred or\n  blocked and where to pick it up again\n- `moai mv <id> in_progress --from todo` — picks up one id only if it still\n  stands where you saw it. A session that lost the race gets `stale` and a\n  non-zero exit, and moves on to the next row. Pass one id per call\n- `moai prime` — what this session holds and what is next, short enough to load\n  into a prompt\n\nThe moai binary never launches a session or runs one headless. A person opens\neach one — or, inside tmux or cmux, says yes to the supervisor opening one — and the\nsession reads these the way that person would.\n\n**Name the AI that did the work** before closing an issue — one note, the\n[model line](glossary.md#model-line), one line per issue, read back as `work` in","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

4] = [\"moai\", \"moai-supervise\", \"moai-wiki\", \"moai-recover\"];\n\n/// **고른 사람에게만 심는** 스킬과, 그것을 쓰는 사람인지 알아보는 표식(2026-10-10 사용자 결정, moai-3r7l) — [`NAMES`]\n/// 곁의 둘째 목록이다. tmux 를 안 쓰는 사람에게 칸을 만지는 스킬을 심으면 그 발동어가 그 사람의 모든 세션에 실린다.\n///\n/// - **고른 것은 저장하지 않는다.** 설정 키도 파일도 없고, \"그 트리에 지금 심겼는가\" 가 답이다(`cmd::skill::optional_in`)\n///   — 따로 적으면 심긴 디렉터리와 그 값 둘이 진실을 다툰다(규약의 \"파생값은 저장하지 않는다\")\n/// - **표식은 `moai init` 의 고르는 상자가 미리 고를 때만 쓴다**([`detected`]). 사람 없이 도는 `init`·`skill install` 은\n///   표식으로 심지 않는다 — 심는 것은 `--with` 와 이미 심긴 것뿐이다([`kept`])\n///\n/// 하나를 더하는 것은 이 목록의 한 줄과 [`skills`] 의 글 한 칸이다. 둘째 `moai-cmux`(moai-p5sz.lz0)의 표식은\n/// `CMUX_SURFACE_ID` 다 — cmux 는 제 탭의 셸마다 `CMUX_*` 여럿을 세우는데, 그 가운데 스킬이 실제로 기대는 것이 이것이다\n/// (그 탭을 겨누는 이름). 머리(`CMUX_`)로 재면 cmux 가 깔아 둔 `CMUX_BUNDLED_CLI_PATH` 따위가 cmux 밖의 셸에 새어도\n/// 쓰는 사람으로 읽는다. tmux 를 cmux 탭 안에서 돌리는 사람에게는 둘 다 켜진다 — 둘 다 그 사람의 것이다.\npub const OPTIONAL: [Optional; 2] = [\n    Optional { name: \"moai-tmux\", sign: |var| var == \"TMUX\" },\n    Optional { name: \"moai-cmux\", sign: |var| var == \"CMUX_SURFACE_ID\" },\n];\n\n/// 고를 수 있는 스킬 하나 — 이름과 표식.\npub struct Optional {\n    pub name: &'static str,\n    /// 그 스킬을 쓰는 사람이라는 환경 변수의 이름인가 — 그 이름의 변수가 **비지 않게** 하나라도 서면 쓰는 사람이다\n    /// ([`detected`]). tmux 는 제 안에서 도는 셸에 `$TMUX` 를 세운다.\n    pub sign: fn(&str) -> bool,\n}\n\n/// `name` 이 고를 수 있는 스킬인가([`OPTIONAL`]).\npub fn is_optional(name: &str) -> bool {\n    OPTIONAL.iter().any(|o| o.name == name)\n}\n\n83:pub fn detected(vars: &[(String, String)]) -> Vec<&'static str> {\n89:fn detected_in(list: &[Optional], vars: &[(String, String)]) -> Vec<&'static str> {\n    OPTIONAL.iter().any(|o| o.name == name)\n}\n\n/// 고를 수 있는 스킬의 이름 — [`OPTIONAL`] 의 차례로.\npub fn optional_names() -> impl Iterator<Item = &'static str> {\n    OPTIONAL.iter().map(|o| o.name)\n}\n\n/// 환경 `vars` 가 쓰는 사람이라고 이르는 선택 스킬 — [`OPTIONAL`] 의 차례로. **환경을 받기만 한다** — 이 모듈은 글만\n/// 짓고, 환경을 읽는 것은 부르는 쪽이다(`init` 의 고르는 상자).\npub fn detected(vars: &[(String, String)]) -> Vec<&'static str> {\n    detected_in(&OPTIONAL, vars)\n}\n\n/// [`detected`] 의 몸통 — 목록을 받아, 목록에 없는 꼴의 표식(이름의 머리로 재는 것)도 시험이 잰다. cmux 는 그 꼴로\n/// 재려다 탭을 겨누는 이름 하나(`CMUX_SURFACE_ID`)로 섰다([`OPTIONAL`]).\nfn detected_in(list: &[Optional], vars: &[(String, String)]) -> Vec<&'static str> {\n    list.iter().filter(|o| vars.iter().any(|(k, v)| (o.sign)(k) && !v.is_empty())).map(|o| o.name).collect()\n}\n\n/// 이번에 심을 선택 스킬 — **(지금 심긴 것 ∪ `with`) − `without`**, [`OPTIONAL`] 의 차례로(moai-3r7l). 맨 `install` 은 둘이\n/// 비어 심긴 것만 다시 심고 새것은 안 심는다. 처음 심는 저장소는 심긴 것이 없어 하나도 안 심는다.\npub fn kept(planted: &[&str], with: &[&str], without: &[&str]) -> Vec<&'static str> {\n    optional_names().filter(|n| (planted.contains(n) || with.contains(n)) && !without.contains(n)).collect()\n}","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

`<체크아웃>/.claude/moai-plugin/skills/<이름>` 이다.\n/// `claude plugin install`·`update` 는 제 캐시에 사본을 뜨고 설치 장부의 판을 올리지만, 세션은 그 사본의 스킬을\n/// 안 읽는다 — 판이 정하는 것은 `plugin update` 가 새 판을 알아보는 때다. 손으로 세는 판은 반드시 어긋난다 —\n/// 내용이 같으면 판도 같아 헛 업데이트가 없고, 한 글자라도 다르면 반드시 달라진다.\n///\n/// 판이 **내려가도** 괜찮은 까닭은 [`version_of`] 에 있다. 두 자리에 나눠 적으면\n/// 한쪽만 고쳐져 갈라진다 — 실제로 여기 적혀 있던 까닭이 틀린 채로 남아 있었다.\npub fn tree(prefix: &str, root: &Path, exe: &str, skills: &[Skill]) -> Vec<(PathBuf, String)> {\n    tree_named(&market(prefix, root), exe, skills)\n}\n\n/// `tree` 의 몸통. 저장소 자리는 마켓플레이스 이름으로만 들어오므로, 이름을\n/// 받아 두면 **커밋된 트리를 그 트리가 적힌 자리 그대로** 다시 낼 수 있다 —\n/// 다른 체크아웃(워크트리)에서 부른 시험이 남의 자리를 안 섞는다.\nfn tree_named(market: &str, exe: &str, skills: &[Skill]) -> Vec<(PathBuf, String)> {\n    let mut files: Vec<(PathBuf, String)> =\n        skill_files(skills).map(|(p, b)| (Path::new(\"skills\").join(p), b)).collect();\n    let market = (PathBuf::from(\".claude-plugin/marketplace.json\"), marketplace_json(market));\n    // 판은 **매니페스트를 뺀 트리 전부와 판 자리를 비운 매니페스트**에서 나온다.\n    // 매니페스트 자신은 그 판을 담고 있으므로 그대로는 셈에 넣을 수 없다 —\n    // 넣으면 해시가 제 꼬리를 문다. 그렇다고 매니페스트를 통째로 빼면 그 틀\n    // (`timeout`·`description`)만 바꾼 판이 옛 판과 같아 `claude` 가 옛 복사를\n    // 계속 쓴다. 훅 명령·실행 파일·이름표는 그 틀과 `marketplace.json` 에 이미\n    // 들어 있어 따로 셈하지 않는다 — 따로 적은 목록은 틀이 자랄 때마다 어긋난다.\n    let version = version_of(&[files.as_slice(), std::slice::from_ref(&market)].concat(), &plugin_json(exe, \"\"));\n    files.push((PathBuf::from(\".claude-plugin/plugin.json\"), plugin_json(exe, &version)));\n    files.push(market);\n    files\n}\n\n/// 트리의 내용 해시를 판으로 낸다. **오르내린다** — 해시라 다음 판이 더 낮을 수 있다\n/// (실제로 `968.33.712` 다음이 `59.172.404` 이었다).\n///\n/// 괜찮은 까닭을 확인했다(moai-70ip, 2026-09-15). `claude` 의 플러그인 갱신은 판을 semver\n/// 로 견주지 않고 **달라졌는가**만 본다 — 판 글자를 안 바꾸면 갱신이 안 가고, 바꾸면 간다\n/// (plugin-marketplaces·plugins-reference 문서). moai 쪽 신선도(`cmd/skill.rs`)도 같은지만\n/// 본다. 그래서 내려가는 판이 갱신을 건너뛰게 하지 않는다 — `1.0.1 → 0.0.5` 로 실제로 재 봤다.\n///\n/// 판이 semver 여야 한다거나 올라야 한다는 요구는 문서에 없다. 그래도 **모양은 semver 로\n/// 맞춰 둔다** — 판을 그렇게 읽는 자리가 나중에 생겨도 값이 형식에서 먼저 걸리지는 않는다.\n/// 갱신 판정이 semver 비교로 바뀌는 날에는 해시를 버리지 말고 앞자리에 오르는 셈을 붙인다.\nfn version_of(files: &[(PathBuf, String)], template: &str) -> String {\n    let mut all = String::new();\n    for (path, body) in files {\n        all.push_str(&path.to_string_lossy());\n        all.push('\\u{1}');\n        all.push_str(body);\n        all.push('\\u{2}');\n    }\n    all.push_str(template);\n    // semver 세 자리에 나눠 담는다 — 위 주석의 까닭이다.\n    let n = stable(all.as_bytes());\n    format!(\"{}.{}.{}\", n % 1000, (n / 1000) % 1000, (n / 1_000_000) % 1000)\n}","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

 Dialect::Codex => top.get(\"description\").and_then(|d| d.as_str()) == Some(CODEX_DESCRIPTION),\n        Dialect::Antigravity => {\n            let Some(serde_json::Value::Object(group)) = top.get(ANTIGRAVITY_GROUP).filter(|_| top.len() == 1) else {\n                return false;\n            };\n            group.iter().all(|(key, value)| match key.as_str() {\n                \"enabled\" => value.as_bool() == Some(true),\n                _ => value.is_null() || moai_handlers(value),\n            })\n        }\n        Dialect::Claude => false,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Antigravity 의 이벤트 하나에 선 처리기들이 **모두 moai 의 것**인가 — 처리기를 바로 두거나 `matcher` 무리의 `hooks`\n/// 로 한 번 싼 꼴([`antigravity_hooks`])이고, 하나도 없으면 아니다.\nfn moai_handlers(handlers: &serde_json::Value) -> bool {\n    fn ours(handler: &serde_json::Value) -> bool {\n        handler\n            .get(\"command\")\n            .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)\n            .is_some_and(|c| c.contains(\" hook \") && c.contains(\" --dialect antigravity\"))\n    }\n    fn every(list: &[serde_json::Value], each: fn(&serde_json::Value) -> bool) -> bool {\n        !list.is_empty() && list.iter().all(each)\n    }\n    fn entry(e: &serde_json::Value) -> bool {\n        match e.get(\"hooks\").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array) {\n            Some(inner) => every(inner, ours),\n            None => ours(e),\n        }\n    }\n    handlers.as_array().is_some_and(|list| every(list, entry))\n}\n\n/// 두 훅 파일이 **뜻으로** 같은가 — 꼴(빈칸·키 차례)과 값이 `null` 인 키는 안 본다(리뷰 moai-u5wr.e74). agy 는 이 파일을\n/// 제 꼴로 다시 쓰며 아는 이벤트를 `null` 로      match v {\n            serde_json::Value::Object(m) => serde_json::Value::Object(\n                m.into_iter().filter(|(_, v)| !v.is_null()).map(|(k, v)| (k, bare(v))).collect(),\n            ),\n            serde_json::Value::Array(list) => serde_json::Value::Array(list.into_iter().map(bare).collect()),\n            other => other,\n        }\n    }\n    let read = |text: &str| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(text).ok().map(bare);\n    matches!((read(a), read(b)), (Some(x), Some(y)) if x == y)\n}\n\n/// 심긴 훅 파일(`.codex/hooks.json`·`.agents/hooks.json`)이 부르는 실행 파일 — 첫 `command` 의 머리(`command -v -- \"`)에서\n/// 꺼낸다([`hook_exe`] 와 같은 자). Codex 의 줄은 `sh -c '…'` 로 싸여 있어 그 껍질을 먼저 벗긴다. `moai skill status` 가\n/// 그 파일을 **그 파일이 부르는 moai 로** 견주는 데 쓴다 — Claude 의 줄이 설치본의 훅이 부르는 파일로 견주는 것과 같은\n\n/// [`command`] 를 그 에이전트의 말씨로(moai-u5wr). **Claude 의 줄은 글자 하나 안 바뀐다** — 판이 그 글의 해시라\n/// ([`version_of`]) 바뀌면 열린 세션마다 헛 갱신이 선다. 갈리는 것은 셋이다.\n///\n/// - **`moai` 에 `--dialect` 를 붙인다** — Claude 는 안 붙인다(기본값이다)\n/// - **세션을 가르는 환경 변수가 다르다** — Antigravity 는 `ANTIGRAVITY_CONVERSATION_ID` 를 세운다(2026-10-04\n///   실측). Codex 는 세션을 대는 변수가 없고 훅을 띄운 데몬의 환경을 물려줘, 거기 선 `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` 는\n///   **남의 세션 것**이다(moai-sile) — 그래서 Codex 의 표식은 `$PPID` 하나로 가른다. 그 값은 Codex 세션들이 함께\n///   쓰는 데몬이라 알림이 데몬마다 한 번이 되는데, 남의 세션 id 로 가르는 것보다 낫다\n/// - **Antigravity 에는 알림(`systemMessage`)을 안 낸다** — 그 꼴은 맨 윗단 `decision` 이라 모르는 키를 어떻게\n///   읽는지 재지 않았다. 못 도는 판은 빈 출력이다(빈 출력은 지나간다고 쟀다)\n///\n/// **Codex 의 줄은 `sh -c` 로 싼다.** Codex 가 훅 명령을 어느 셸로 푸는지는 문서에 없고, 기록한 훅의 부모가 곧\n/// 데몬이라(사이에 셸이 안 보였다) 사람의 로그인 셸(`fish` 일 수도 있다)로 풀릴 수 있다. 이 줄은 POSIX 셸의\n/// 글이라 감싸면 어느 쪽이든 선다 — 셸로 풀면 바깥 셸이 따옴표를 벗기고, 낱말로 쪼개도 작은따옴표 안은 한 낱말이다.\nfn command_for(exe: &str, event: &str, dialect: Dialect) -> String {\n    let line = shell_line(exe, event, dialect);\n    match dialect {\n        Dialect::Codex => format!(\"sh -c {}\", crate::text::single_quoted(&line)),\n        Dialect::Claude | Dialect::Antigravity => line,\n    }\n}\n\n/// [`command_for`] 의 몸통 — 셸에 넘길 한 줄이다.\nfn shell_line(exe: &str, event: &str, dialect: Dialect) -> String {","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

It runs on that epic's branch — in its worktree, where it has\none — after the review and the CHANGELOG line and before the merge.\n\n1. Read four things: `moai show <epic> --json` (the body and the notes say why it was\n   decided), the CHANGELOG line the epic wrote if the repository keeps one, the\n   `--help` of each command the epic touched, and `moai wiki ls --json`\n2. Ask once: **did this epic change what a person does** —\n   a key, a command, a flag, a file, a format, a procedure. A refactor\n   inside, or a fix that left the behaviour as it was, changed nothing a person\n   does. If nothing changed, stop — write nothing\n3. Change the page that teaches it — find it in `moai wiki ls`, or grep `dir` for the\n   command or the key. If no page covers it, write one from the template below. A\n   page ends with one `Decided in:` line naming the epics whose decisions it carries;\n   put this epic's id on it\n4. Commit on that branch, before the merge — the pages then ride the same merge, and\n   the merge diff is where they get read\n\n       git add -- <wiki dir>\n       git commit -m \"docs(wiki): <what changed> (<epic>)\" -- <wiki dir>\n\n   `<wiki dir>` is `dir` from `moai wiki ls --json`. **Do not skip the `add`**: with a\n   path, `git commit` leaves out a file git does not know yet, so a new page stays\n   behind without a word\n5. Name the pages you changed in your report, or say that none changed\n\n## When a person asks you to sweep\n\nA person calls this skill to catch the wiki up — before a release, or after work\nmerged without touching it.\n\n1. Find when the last release went out — `git tag --sort=-creatordate` lists the tags\n   newest first; take the newest release tag, and `git log -1 --format=%cs <tag>`\n-----\n\n    git commit -m \"docs(changelog): <what this epic changed> (<epic>)\" -- CHANGELOG.md\n   This window is the only one that knows what the epic did, and it is the only one that\n   knows what was taken out as well as what went in — a section filled in later from commit\n   subjects shows what was added and misses what was removed, because a removal stands under\n   a revert subject of its own. The release notes are that section as it stands, so a\n   missing line reads to whoever receives them as a change that never shipped.\n   **Nothing checks this** — a check here would be a gate, and an empty section must not\n   stop a release\n\n7-4. **If the repository keeps a wiki** (`moai wiki ls` lists pages), ask once whether this\n   epic changed what a person does — a key, a command, a flag, a file, a format, a procedure.\n   If it did, follow the `moai-wiki` skill and commit what it wrote for the same reason as\n   7-3 — here, in the worktree, before the merge. `<wiki dir>` is `dir` in `moai wiki ls --json`\n\n    git add -- <wiki dir>\n    git commit -m \"docs(wiki): <what changed> (<epic>)\" -- <wiki dir>\n   If it did not, write nothing. **Nothing checks this**\n\n8. Come back to the root with `ExitWorktree(keep)` — remove the worktree from inside it and\n   this window stands in a directory that is gone.\n   Before merging outside a milestone, check that the root stands on <root branch> — if it\n   does not, do not merge: tell the supervisor\n\n       git symbolic-ref -q HEAD                  it has to be refs/heads/<root branch>\n   **Inside a milestone you merge in the milestone's worktree, not in the root** — check that","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

`COLUMNS` — clap 이 도움말을 접을 때 읽는 폭. 지금은 접기를 꺼 안 읽지만(moai-opjn),\n///   그것이 돌아오는 날을 지키는 `narrow_terminals_keep_heredoc_openers_whole` 는 폭 하나만\n///   바꿔 기준과 견준다. 기준이 돌리는 사람의 창 폭을 물려받으면 좁은 셸에서는 훑기가 접힌\n///   `Commands:` 줄을 명령 이름으로 읽어, 접힘을 대는 대신 엉뚱한 이름으로 넘어진다\n///\n/// 시험이 제 값을 주려면 이 뒤에 `.env` 로 덮는다. `PATH` 는 두고 간다 — moai 가\n/// git 을 부르고, `claude` 가 없는 자리가 필요한 시험은 `Claude` 가 따로 만든다.\nfn isolated(program: impl AsRef<std::ffi::OsStr>) -> Command {\n    // 빈 집 하나를 모든 시험이 함께 쓴다. moai 도 git 도 `HOME` 에 쓰지 않으니\n    // 비어 있는 채로 남고, `target/` 밑이라 기계에 부스러기를 흘리지 않는다.\n    let home = Path::new(env!(\"CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR\")).join(\"moai-cli-home\");\n    std::fs::create_dir_all(&home).unwrap();\n    let mut cmd = Command::new(program);\n    // **걷기가 먼저다.** `Command` 의 환경은 이름마다 마지막에 부른 것이 이긴다 —\n    // 아래 `.env` 보다 뒤에 두면, 목록에 `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` 같은 이름이 느는 날\n    // 이 루프가 방금 세운 격리를 도로 지운다. `git::isolated` 도 같은 차례다.\n    // 그날 `the_fake_claude_command_starts_from_the_isolated_one` 도 같이 고친다 —\n    // 그쪽은 목록의 **모든** 이름이 걷혔는지 보므로, 여기서 덮어 준 이름에 걸린다.\n    // 차례를 되돌려 달래지 않는다. 그게 이 차례가 막는 바로 그 덫이다.\n    for var in git_leaks::swept(true) {\n        cmd.env_remove(var);\n    }\n    cmd.env(\"HOME\", &home)\n        .env_remove(\"CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR\")\n        .env_remove(\"CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR\")\n        .env(\"GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL\", \"/dev/null\")\n        .env(\"GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM\", \"/dev/null\")\n        .env(\"GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM\", \"1\")\n        .env_remove(\"MOAI_ACTOR\")\n        .env_remove(\"MOAI_NOW\")","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 265,300p docs/agents.md; echo \"-----\"; sed -n 560,600p docs/agents.md","description":"Read hooks section and troubleshooting in docs/agents.md"},"toolOutput":"## What the hooks do\n\nThe hooks catch the same few places in each agent's session. Each calls\n`moai hook`, which nobody runs by hand.\n\n| When | What happens |\n|---|---|\n| The session starts | A baseline of the warnings is written. After a compaction, what the session was holding is loaded back into it |\n| A person sends a prompt | The `moai status` board is loaded, once per session |\n| Before a tool call | The five rules below are checked |\n| The turn ends | If the session still holds work, the turn is held once and asks for a [`Next:` note](glossary.md#next-note) for whoever comes after; it is also held when the [warnings](glossary.md#warning) grew. That question has a fixed room: open reviews tied to the held work, and held rows that would close their epic if deferred, get it first; the other held rows fill what is left from the top, those that do not fit are left out whole, and one more line counts them and names `moai prime`, which lists everything held |\n\n**The hook never fails the session.** Whatever goes wrong inside it, it exits 0,\nand the only thing it refuses is the one tool call that broke a rule. A person\ntyping `moai` in a terminal never passes through it.\n\n**Each agent has its own shapes, the rules are one.** The hooks tell `moai hook`\nwhose they are (`--dialect`), and what differs is only what goes in and out:\n\n- **Codex** sends hooks only for its shell, `apply_patch` and MCP calls — a\n  patch is checked file by file, whether it came through the `apply_patch` tool\n  or was typed as `apply_patch <<'EOF'` in the shell, and one file that breaks a\n  rule refuses the patch\n- **Antigravity** has no prompt event, so the first model call of each turn\n  loads the board; it has no session start either, so the baseline is written\n  there too. A line the rules only add to a tool call — fork 1's second\n  question, say — has nowhere to stand in its answer and is not shown\n\n**Where no hook stands, the rules are words only** — an agent without them,\nCodex before the trust in `/hooks`, a tool call that sends none. Nothing is\nrefused there; the `AGENTS.md` block asks the agent to keep the five itself,\nrules 4 and 5 most of all.\n\n## The five rules\n\nA refusal opens with the rule's number and name, and hands over the command that\n-----\n[model line](glossary.md#model-line), one line per issue, read back as `work` in\n`--json` and summed by `moai stats`:\n\n    moai note <id> 'model: anthropic/opus-5 tokens=182000 (high — the write path)'\n\nLeave `tokens=` out when the count is unknown; never write 0 or a guess.\n\n## When it goes wrong\n\n- **A tool call was refused.** Read the first line — `Rule N — …` — and run the\n  command the refusal hands over. Do not stop to ask a person unless it is rule 5\n- **The rules do not seem to stand.** `moai skill status` says whether the plugin\n  is registered and whether the binary the hook calls still runs. A session opened\n  before the install keeps the old hook until it is reopened\n- **Codex runs none of moai's hooks.** Codex has not been told to trust them —\n  open `/hooks` in a codex session in the repository and trust them. An install\n  that changed them asks for that trust again\n- **`moai status` says the planted skills or hooks differ from this moai's.**\n  An older moai planted them — most often after upgrading. Run the line the\n  notice names (`moai skill install`, with `--agent codex` or `antigravity`\n  where those trees stand); it also removes what this moai no longer plants\n- **`skill install` says a hooks file is not moai's.** It holds hooks someone\n  else wrote, and moai will not overwrite them. Merge moai's entries into it by\n  hand, or move it aside and install again\n- **`skill install` printed two `claude plugin` lines and failed.** The\n  registration did not go through — most often `claude` is not on `PATH`; run\n  those lines where it is\n- **`skill install` refused a path that \"points at … outside\", \"is not a\n  regular file\" or \"is not a directory\".** A file or directory under\n  `.claude/moai-plugin/`, `.agents/skills/` or a hooks file is a link that leaves\n  the checkout (or lands in `.git`), a FIFO or device stands where a file goes,\n  or a file or a dangling link stands where a directory has to be made (a\n  `.codex` that is a file, say). moai checks every place before the first write,\n  so nothing was written — not the other agents' files either — and `claude` was\n  not asked to register. `--dry-run` stops with the same line. Replace the link\n  with a real file or directory, or move aside what stands there, and install\n  again\n- **`init` or `skill install` refused a path that points into `.moai`.** A\n  committed link (`AGENTS.md -> .moai/issues.jsonl`, a `SKILL.md`, a hooks file,\n  or a directory such as `.agents -> .moai`) would land the write in the\n  tracker. {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 1,90p CHANGELOG.md","description":"Read the CHANGELOG header and recent sections"},"toolOutput":"# Changelog\n\nAll notable changes to this project are documented here. The format follows\n[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and this project uses\n[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).\n\n`scripts/bump-version.sh auto` moves whatever has accumulated under\n`[Unreleased]` into a new release section and leaves `[Unreleased]` empty for the\nnext one. The headings pick the version: before 1.0, `Fixed` and `Security` alone\nmake a patch release and anything else a minor one. It does not commit and it\ndoes not tag — see `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\n## [Unreleased]\n\n### Fixed\n\n- **`moai-tmux` and `moai-recover` could read a dead pane as an empty input\n  box.** A pane whose Claude Code was killed keeps its last frame, box and all,\n  above the shell, so a message `SendMessage` could not deliver — a dead session\n  is the usual reason it fails — could be pasted into that shell. The box now\n  counts as empty only while the session map, run again just before, still\n  reads that session alive in that pane, as `moai-cmux` already does.\n  (moai-xpa8.p56)\n- **A hook whose `moai` could not run said nothing on a Mac when the hook ran\n  under `sh -e`.** macOS's `/bin/sh` (bash 3.2) reports a file without its\n  execute bit as exit 1 inside a command substitution under `set -e`, which the\n  hook line read as `moai` ending by itself. The hook line now turns `-e` off\n  inside that substitution, so the notice that the five rules are not standing\n  shows again. Reinstall with `moai skill install` to pick it up. (moai-xpa8.q9x)\n- **A supervisor started with `cmux claude-teams` had no hands on the workers.**\n  That launcher sets a stand-in `$TMUX` (`/tmp/cmux-…`) whose `tmux` is cmux in\n  disguise, so the supervisor took `moai-tmux`'s way, its labels went nowhere\n  and the session map found no pane. A `$TMUX` that starts with `/tmp/cmux-` now\n  counts as cmux, and the supervisor uses `moai-cmux`. (moai-xpa8.1vt)\n\n## [0.14.0] - 2026-10-11\n\n### Added\n\n- **A second optional Claude Code skill, `moai-cmux`, for a supervisor running\n  inside [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux).** It is `moai-tmux` for\n  cmux tabs: it finds each worker's surface (`cmux top` says which surface a\n  session runs in), labels its tab once you say labels are wanted, clears a\n  reported worker's window, pastes a message `SendMessage` could not deliver\n  (`cmux paste --submit`), reads why a worker stalled, and — only after asking —\n  opens new worker splits running an ordinary interactive `claude`. It reads the\n  input box through cmux's own `surface.input_state` and never types over\n  anything in it, never closes a tab, never moves focus and never passes\n  `--force`. **It needs cmux 0.65.0 or later** and checks that itself; on an\n  older cmux it says so and does nothing. Running tmux inside a cmux tab stays\n  `moai-tmux`'s case. Plant it with `moai skill install --with moai-cmux`, or\n  its row in the first `moai init` (checked when `$CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set).\n  (moai-p5sz)\n\n### Changed\n\n- **`moai-recover` opens a tab per session inside cmux 0.65.0 or later**, the\n  way it opens a pane per session inside tmux, and pastes its note once the\n  tab's input box reads empty. It is planted everywhere, so this reaches every\n  cmux user, `moai-cmux` or not; outside tmux and cmux it still prints the line\n  to type. (moai-p5sz.kfi)\n\n### Fixed\n\n- **`moai-tmux` and `moai-recover` found no session on a Mac.** Their session\n  map read the process start time from `/proc`, which macOS does not have, so\n  every session read as dead. It now compares the start time Claude Code writes\n  on a Mac (`ps -o lstart`), and matches a session to a tmux pane by its\n  terminal (`#{pane_tty}`) instead of reading the process's environment — which\n  also no longer trips Claude Code's auto-mode guard against reading other\n  processes' environments. (moai-p5sz.7q3)\n\n## [0.13.0] - 2026-10-10\n\n### Added\n\n- **A fourth Claude Code skill, `moai-tmux`, planted only where you choose it.**\n  When the supervisor runs inside tmux it finds each worker's pane from\n  `~/.claude/sessions/`, labels it (pane option `@moai`), clears a reported\n  worker's window, pastes a message `SendMessage` could not deliver, reads why a\n  worker stalled and tells the person, and — only after asking — opens new\n  worker panes running an ordinary interactive `claude`. It never types over a\n  non-empty input box and never kills anything. Without `$TMUX` nothing\n  changes. It is the first *optional* skill: a plain `moai skill install`\n  plants it nowhere new, and only refreshes it where it is already planted.\n  (moai-u99i, moai-3r7l)\n- **Optional skills are chosen per repository.** `moai skill install --with\n  <skill>` plants one and `--without <skill>` removes it (both repeat, and take\n  names separated by commas); `moai skill uninstall --only <skill>` is the same\n  removal under the uninstall name, and brings up only the registrations that","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

53%). **여기 적는 것은 든\n# 값이지 지금 크기가 아니다** — 절대 수는 커밋마다 움직여, 읽는 사람이 무엇과 견줄지 모른다.\n# 지금 크기는 `ls -l target/release/moai` 가 댄다. 위의 표와 다른 것은 기능을 깎아서다: `gzip` 을\n# 끄면 `flate2` 가 안 따라오고, 답이 JSON 몇 KB 라 푸는 값도 {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 1,240p src/scratch.rs","description":"Read scratch.rs temp dir picker"},"toolOutput":"//! 시험이 쓰는 임시 디렉터리 한 벌(moai-shgx). **시험에서만 선다.**\n//!\n//! ## 왜 한 벌인가\n//!\n//! 같은 것이 다섯 벌 있었다 — `tui/register.rs`·`tui/layer.rs`·`tui/mod.rs`·\n//! `user_config.rs` 와 통합 시험의 것. 앞의 넷과 `cmd/tui.rs` 의 편집기 시험 자리는\n//! 이것으로 모았다. **통합 시험(`tests/cli.rs`)의 `Scratch` 는 아직 따로다** — 따로 된\n//! 크레이트라 `use` 로는 못 가져가고, 뿌리([`base`])만 `#[path]` 로 이 파일을\n//! 읽어 함께 쓴다. 울타리는 안 쓴다(moai-izeo 뒤로 그쪽에서 [`fence`] 를 부르지 않는다).\n//! 그래서 **이 파일의 단위 시험은 그쪽에서도 컴파일돼 돈다** — 여기 더하는 시험은 `crate::` 의\n//! 다른 모듈을 쓰지 못한다(그쪽 크레이트에는 없다). 그리고 **모으지 않은 자리**(`git.rs`·\n//! `store.rs`·`worktree.rs`)는 끝에서 `remove_dir_all` 을 부르는 식이라, 시험이\n//! 패닉하면 그 줄에 닿지 못해 `/tmp/moai-git-<pid>` 가 그대로 남는다. 이름에 pid 가\n//! 들어 다음 판이 그것을 치우지도 않는다 — 이 기계에 죽은 pid 의 것 셋이 남아 있었다.\n//!\n//! `Drop` 은 패닉으로 풀릴 때도 돈다. 그래서 치우는 일은 **놓을 때** 한다.\n//!\n//! ## 자리\n//!\n//! `std::env::temp_dir()` 다 — **그것이 어느 체크아웃 안이면 밖으로 옮긴다**([`base`], moai-izeo).\n//! **`CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` 은 여기서 못 쓴다** — cargo 는\n//! 그것을 통합 시험·벤치 타깃에만 주고, 이 모듈은 바이너리 타깃의 단위 시험으로\n//! 컴파일되므로 `option_env!` 가 늘 `None` 이었다(`tests/cli.rs` 는 통합 시험이라\n//! `env!` 로 그것을 곧바로 읽는다). 있는 척하는 갈래는 걷어냈다.\n//!\n//! 일부러 저장소 안(`target/` 밑)으로 옮기지는 않는다 — 위의 `.git` 이 꼭대기로 잡혀 moai-46xz 가\n//! 통째로 돌아오고, 위의 `.moai` 는 그보다 나쁘다(moai-izeo: 시험이 바깥 트래커에 실제로 썼다).\n//! **지금 그 자리에 서는\n/// 것은 흘려보내기와 표식 세우기를 묶은 `{ … }` 전체다**(리뷰 moai-45hf.nab) — `printf` 가 지거나\n/// 표식이 못 서면(그 디렉터리가 없다) 그 묶음이 비영이고, `|| :` 를 걷으면 dash 는 `-ec` 에서\n/// 2 로 나간다. 그 2 가 곧 게이트다. 알림의 `printf` 에도 do f=\\\"$a\\\"; done\\nprintf '%s\\\\n' \\\"$@\\\" > '{seen}/args'\\n{{ stat -c %a \\\"$f\\\" 2>/dev/null || stat -f %Lp \\\"$f\\\"; }} > '{seen}/mode'\\ncp \\\"$f\\\" '{seen}/text'\\n{script}\\n\",\n                    seen = seen.display()\n                ),\n            )\n            .unwrap();\n            std::fs::create_dir_all(&seen).unwrap();\n            // 인자가 붙은 편집기(`code --wait`)와 같은 모양 — 셸 규칙으로 쪼개져야 선다.\n            format!(\"sh '{}' --wait\", path.display())\n        }\n\n        fn seen(&self, what: &str) -> String {\n            std::fs::read_to_string(self.0.join(\"seen\").join(what)).unwrap_or_default()\n        }\n\n... {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 1838,1870p src/guide.rs","description":"Read supervisor tmux/cmux section"},"toolOutput":"  session on this machine (2)\n- A subagent sends under its parent session's address — a message can come from a session\n  that did not write it itself\n- `@path` in a message attaches nothing — a file the worker has to read is named by its\n  absolute path, and the worker reads it itself (3)\n- Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop — the report comes to you (4)\n\n**Inside tmux, load `moai-tmux` too.** When `$TMUX` is set in your shell, the skill\n`moai-tmux` gives you hands on the workers' panes, at five points of the round: offer new\nworker panes when no worker is idle (2), label the pane you send to and deliver a message\n`SendMessage` could not (3), read a stalled worker's pane (4), and clear a reported worker's\nwindow before its next work (5). It finds each worker's pane from its `ListAgents` name, and\nnever types into a box that holds anything. **Without `$TMUX` nothing of it applies** — every\nstep below goes through messages and the person, as written, unless you are inside cmux (the\nnext paragraph). `moai-tmux` is an optional skill:\nit stands only where it was chosen (`moai skill install --with moai-tmux`, or its row in `moai\ninit`). Inside tmux without it, tell the person that one line plants it, and carry on as if\noutside tmux.\n\n**Inside cmux, load `moai-cmux` instead.** When `CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set in your shell and\n`$TMUX` is not, `moai-cmux` gives you the same hands on the workers' cmux tabs, at the same\nfive points, and reads the same session map. It needs cmux 0.65.0 or later and says so itself.\n**A `$TMUX` that starts with `/tmp/cmux-` is cmux's own stand-in**, not a tmux server —\n`cmux claude-teams` sets it for Claude Code's agent teams, and the `tmux` on its `PATH` is cmux\nin disguise — so with it you are inside cmux: `moai-cmux`. When both are set otherwise you run in\ntmux inside a cmux tab — what you type goes to tmux, so it is\n`moai-tmux`. **With neither, nothing of either applies.** `moai-cmux` is optional the same\nway (`moai skill install --with moai-cmux`); inside cmux without it, tell the person that one\nline plants it, and carry on as if outside cmux.\n\n**When sessions died** — a restart or an OOM kill took the workers or a supervisor down —\nand the person asks to bring them back, load `moai-recover`, inside tmux or not.","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

[4 lines truncated] ...\n\npub fn recover() -> String {\n    format!(\n        r#\"---\nname: moai-recover\ndescription: Use in Claude Code when the person asks to bring back the sessions of this repository that died — after a restart, an OOM kill or a crash — so the supervisor and its workers carry on where they stopped. Finds the dead sessions, draws the state each was in, points out background work that never returned and broken target links, and resumes each one in a new tmux pane or cmux tab, or prints the command to type. Triggers on \"recover the sessions\", \"bring the sessions back\", \"resume the dead sessions\", \"되살려\", \"세션 복구\", \"이어 가게 해\".\n---\n\n# moai-recover — bring back the sessions that died\n\nUse this when the person asks for it: the sessions of this repository — a supervisor, its\nworkers — died together, after a restart, an OOM kill or a crash, and the person wants them\nto carry on. **Their asking is the yes:** inside tmux or cmux you open the panes without asking\nagain.\nNone of this is a moai command; it is you reading Claude Code's own records and typing where\nthe person can watch.\n\n## What never happens\n\n- **No headless run.** A session you bring back is an ordinary interactive `claude --resume`\n  the person can see and type into. Never `claude -p`, never a `--dangerously-*` flag, never\n  `--permission-mode`\n- **Nothing is killed.** Never `kill-server`, `kill-session` or `kill-pane`, never `pkill`\n  or `killall` aimed at tmux (hook rule 4); inside cmux never `close-surface`, `close-workspace`\n  or `close-window`, and never `--force`. A session that is alive is left alone\n- **Only the panes you opened.** Type only into a pane this skill opened, by the `%N` that\n  `split-window` printed — every call names it, `-t <pane>`. Inside cmux it is the surface UUID\n  `new-split` printed, `--surface <surface>`\n- **Never over the person's words.** Paste only into an empty input box (\"Is the input box\n  empty\" below); otherwise tell the person\n- **No polling.** Every look is one look; the next comes after your next step, as its own\n  call — never a loop, never a `sleep`\n- **Their work stays as it is.** No commit, no checkout, no stash, no build, no `moai` write —\n  what a dead session left is for that session to pick up\n\n## Is the input box empty\n\nInside tmux:\n\n{EMPTY_BOX}\n\nInside cmux:\n\n{CMUX_EMPTY_BOX}\n\n**When it is not empty, do not paste.** Tell the person which pane holds what — the words in it\nare theirs.\n\n## 1. v.sort();\n    v\n}\n\n/// [`crate::path::real`] 과 같은 자 — **여기만 제 몸으로 든다.**\n///\n/// 이 파일은 `tests/cli.rs` 가 `#[path]` 로 함께 들어(dev-dependency 0개, CLAUDE.md \"테스트\"),\n/// 그쪽에서는 `crate` 가 시험 크레이트라 {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 1835,1870p src/guide.rs","description":"Read supervisor tmux/cmux paragraphs"},"toolOutput":"- A session in a different permission mode holds an incoming message for its person's\n  approval — a worker that stays idle after you sent may be waiting on that\n- `notify_when_idle` answers only for a session on this machine — one reason a worker is a\n  session on this machine (2)\n- A subagent sends under its parent session's address — a message can come from a session\n  that did not write it itself\n- `@path` in a message attaches nothing — a file the worker has to read is named by its\n  absolute path, and the worker reads it itself (3)\n- Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop — the report comes to you (4)\n\n**Inside tmux, load `moai-tmux` too.** When `$TMUX` is set in your shell, the skill\n`moai-tmux` gives you hands on the workers' panes, at five points of the round: offer new\nworker panes when no worker is idle (2), label the pane you send to and deliver a message\n`SendMessage` could not (3), read a stalled worker's pane (4), and clear a reported worker's\nwindow before its next work (5). It finds each worker's pane from its `ListAgents` name, and\nnever types into a box that holds anything. **Without `$TMUX` nothing of it applies** — every\nstep below goes through messages and the person, as written, unless you are inside cmux (the\nnext paragraph). `moai-tmux` is an optional skill:\nit stands only where it was chosen (`moai skill install --with moai-tmux`, or its row in `moai\ninit`). Inside tmux without it, tell the person that one line plants it, and carry on as if\noutside tmux.\n\n**Inside cmux, load `moai-cmux` instead.** When `CMUX_SURFACE_ID` is set in your shell and\n`$TMUX` is not, `moai-cmux` gives you the same hands on the workers' cmux tabs, at the same\nfive points, and reads the same session map. It needs cmux 0.65.0 or later and says so itself.\n**A `$TMUX` that starts with `/tmp/cmux-` is cmux's own stand-in**, not a tmux server —\n`cmux claude-teams` sets it for Claude Code's agent teams, and the `tmux` on its `PATH` is cmux\nin disguise — so with it you are inside cmux: `moai-cmux`. When both are set otherwise you run in\ntmux inside a cmux tab — what you type goes to tmux, so it is\n`moai-tmux`. **With neither, nothing of either applies.** `moai-cmux` is optional the same\nway (`moai skill install --with moai-cmux`); inside cmux without it, tell the person that one\nline plants it, and carry on as if outside cmux.\n\n**When sessions died** — a restart or an OOM kill took the workers or a supervisor down —\nand the person asks to bring them back, load `moai-recover`, inside tmux or not.","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

tty 와 같은 장치(`st_rdev`)일 때만 칸을 내고 아니면 `-` 다. 같은 tty\n/// 면 그 칸에서 도는 프로세스라는 뜻이라, 서버가 같은지보다 한 걸음 더 잰다. 프로세스의 tty 는 리눅스에서\n/// `/proc/<pid>/stat` 의 7번째 칸(`tty_nr` — 커널이 `st_rdev` 와 같은 꼴로 적는다), macOS 에서 {"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 2455,2632p src/guide.rs","description":"Read moai-tmux skill body"},"toolOutput":"///\n/// Claude Code 에만 심는다([`crate::skill::Skill::claude_only`]) — 감독 스킬과 같은 까닭이다.\npub fn tmux() -> String {\n    format!(\n        r#\"---\nname: moai-tmux\ndescription: Use in Claude Code together with moai-supervise when the supervisor runs inside tmux ($TMUX is set) — to find a worker's pane from its ListAgents name, label it, clear a reported worker's window, deliver a message SendMessage could not, read why a worker stalled, and open new worker panes once the person says yes. Triggers on \"worker pane\", \"open a worker\", \"clear the worker\", \"일꾼 칸\", \"일꾼 창 열어\", \"칸 비워\".\n---\n\n# moai-tmux — the supervisor's hands on the workers' panes\n\nThis is the supervisor's (`moai-supervise`) companion **when it runs inside tmux** — `$TMUX`\nis set in its shell. Without `$TMUX` none of this applies: the supervisor works through\nmessages and the person — or, inside cmux, through `moai-cmux`. Nor does it apply when `$TMUX`\nstarts with `/tmp/cmux-`: that is cmux's own stand-in (`cmux claude-teams` sets it), and its\n`tmux` is cmux in disguise — that is `moai-cmux`'s. The tmux server here is **the\nperson's own**: every session they have lives on it, and every pane you touch is one they are\nlooking at.\n\n## What never happens\n\n- **No headless run.** A worker you open is an ordinary interactive `claude` the person can\n  see and type into. Never `claude -p`, never a `--dangerously-*` flag, never\n  `--permission-mode`. The moai binary launches and drives nothing; this skill is you\n  typing tmux commands where the person can watch\n- **Nothing is killed.** Never `kill-server`, `kill-session` or `kill-pane`, never `pkill`\n  or `killall` aimed at tmux — one bare `kill-server` once took down every session the\n  person had (hook rule 4, and the person's own guard hook refuses it too). A worker that\n  is done stays open; closing a pane is the person's\n- **Only a worker's pane.** Type only into a pane found through the session map below for a\n  worker of this repository — never your own pane (`$TMUX_PANE`), never a session of another\n  repository, never a test server's pane. Every call names its pane, `-t <pane>`, as `%N`\n- **Never over the person's words.** If a worker's input box holds anything, do not type into\n  it — tell the person\n- **Never in their place.** A permission prompt or a question in a worker's pane is the\n  person's to answer — you read it and tell them; you press no key\n- **No polling.** Every look below is one look. A second one comes after your next step, as\n  its own call — never a loop and never a `sleep`\n- **The person's tmux config file stays theirs.** What you set is on the running server\n\n## Which pane is which worker\n\n`ListAgents` names a session; tmux needs a pane. Claude Code keeps one record per process\nunder `~/.claude/sessions/`, and the lines below print one row per record, tab-separated:\n\n    state  name  pane  status  cwd  sessionId\n\n```sh\n{SESSIONS}\n```\n\n... [78 lines truncated] ...\n\n\n1. Write the message to a file in your scratchpad, with one line at the end naming you — a\n   pasted message carries no sender, and the worker reports to the message's `from`. The\n   first line stays the message's own, which names the work and the step to start from:\n   `from: <your ListAgents name>`\n2. Paste and submit it:\n\n       tmux load-buffer -b moai-send <file>\n       tmux paste-buffer -p -d -b moai-send -t <pane>\n       tmux send-keys -t <pane> Enter\n\n3. **Tell the person** you did, and into which pane\n\nThe worker still answers with `SendMessage`. A worker that answered your message by refusing\nthe work is not a delivery that failed — it comes out of the candidates (the supervisor's 2).\n\n## When a worker stalls\n\nWhen a `notify_when_idle` notice comes with no report, or the person asks about a worker that\nhas read `busy` far longer than its work should take, look at its pane once:\n\n    tmux capture-pane -p -t <pane> -S -40\n\nand read why it stopped — a permission prompt, a question (`AskUserQuestion`), an API or\nrate-limit error, or a process that ended (a shell prompt where the box was). **Tell the\nperson** what the pane shows and which pane it is. Do not answer the prompt, do not press a\nkey, and do not look again in a loop. A process that ended is a dead session: bringing it\nback is `moai-recover`, once the person asks for it.\n\n## No idle worker left\n\nWhen the supervisor's 2 finds no worker, ask the person **once** whether to open new worker\npanes, and how many — one question covers several panes. Open a pane only on their yes, or\nwhen they asked you for it. On a yes, for each pane:\n\n    tmux split-window -P -F '#{{pane_id}}' -t \"$TMUX_PANE\" -c <root> 'claude --model <model>; exec bash'\n    tmux select-layout -t \"$TMUX_PANE\" tiled\n\n`<root>` is the `root dir` of the supervisor's 2 and `<model>` the model picked in 2-1. **No\nother flag.** The first line prints the new pane's id; `exec bash` keeps a shell in the pane\nwhen `claude` exits, so what it said stays readable. The pane belongs to the same person —\nit is their interactive session like any other.\n\nOnce it has started (a separate call: `capture-pane` of the new pane shows the `❯` box), look\nat `ListAgents` once more. The new row is a worker like any other (the supervisor's 2) — send\nto it as in 3. If it does not show yet, look once more after your next step; if a prompt\nstands in the new pane (trusting the folder, say), tell the person — it is theirs to answer.\n\"#\n    )\n}","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}

{"toolName":"Bash","toolInput":{"command":"sed -n 2420,2450p src/skill.rs","description":"Read skill.rs test around the handoff marker name parsing"},"toolOutput":"    }\n\n    /// **표식 이름에 바이너리 철자와 이벤트가 든다**(moai-f7up). 한 세션이 저장소 둘을 오가는\n    /// 것은 드물지 않은데, 이름만 같으면 첫 저장소의 표식이 둘째의 입을 막는다 — 저마다 제\n    /// 바이너리가 못 돌 수 있으니 둘 다 제 알림을 내야 한다. 이벤트도 같은 까닭이다\n    /// (`session-start` 의 알림은 사람에게 안 들린다, 리뷰 moai-514e.hgz).\n    ///\n    /// **이름을 다시 지어내지 않는다** — `tests/cli.rs` 의 `baseline` 이 적어 둔 규칙이다.\n    /// 표식 이름은 `s=` 가 적은 그 값을 그대로 떼어 본다: 너비를 넓혀도 접두어를 바꿔도\n    /// 이 시험이 엉뚱한 까닭으로 붉어지거나 푸르러지지 않는다.\n    #[test]\n    fn two_repos_do_not_share_the_notice_mark() {\n        let mark = |exe: &str, event: &str| {\n            // `s=\"…\"` 가 적은 값을 통째로 뗀다([`notice_mark`]). 경로가 아니라 그 대입에서 찾는 까닭은\n            // 경로에 `moai-hook-` 이 들면 `find` 가 그쪽을 먼저 집기 때문이고, 끝은 그 대입을 닫는\n            // 따옴표다 — 너비도 접두어도 안 박는다.\n            let name = notice_mark(&command(exe, event)).to_string();\n            assert!(name.contains(\"${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID\"), \"세션이 표식에 안 든다 — {name}\");\n            name\n        };\n        let a = \"/repo/a/target/release/moai\";\n        let b = \"/repo/b/target/release/moai\";\n        assert_ne!(mark(a, \"stop\"), mark(b, \"stop\"), \"바이너리 둘이 표식을 나눠 쓴다\");\n        assert_ne!(mark(a, \"session-start\"), mark(a, \"pre-tool-use\"), \"이벤트 둘이 표식을 나눠 쓴다\");\n        // **같은 철자·같은 이벤트가 같은 표식인 것은 안 잰다** — `command` 는 인자만 보는 순수\n        // 함수라 제 자신과 견주는 줄이 된다(리뷰 moai-514e.hgz). 세션 안에서 한 번만 서는지는\n        // `the_notice_stands_once_a_session` 이 껍데기로 실제로 두 번 돌려 잰다.\n        // 이벤트도 종료 값도 이름에 선다 — `$c` 는 껍데기가 풀 자리라 글자 그대로 남는다.\n        assert!(mark(a, \"stop\").ends_with(\".stop.$c.said\"), \"이벤트·종료 값이 표식에 안 선다 — {}\", mark(a, \"stop\"));\n    }","durationMs":0,"success":true,"metadata":{"command":"sed"}}
